articles.title: Underdetected peripheral artery disease in people with hypertension: A narrative review of risk-stratified case-finding, diagnostic pathways, and equity in care.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is common but often underrecognized in people with hypertension because symptoms are frequently absent or atypical and access to physiologic testing is uneven. This narrative review examines how hypertension care can support risk-stratified PAD recognition while keeping targeted case-finding distinct from universal screening.

METHODS: We conducted a structured narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE from inception through 31 July 2026, supplemented by citation searching and review of major US and European guidelines and relevant US policy and coverage sources. Evidence was interpreted according to the question it could answer: association/prognosis, diagnostic accuracy, treatment effect, implementation, or policy status.

RESULTS: Hypertension and PAD share age-related, metabolic, renal, and tobacco-related determinants, while pressure-related vascular injury provides biological plausibility for their association. Resting ankle-brachial index (ABI) is the initial physiologic test for appropriately selected people; toe-brachial index with waveforms is preferred for noncompressible ankle arteries, exercise ABI for persistent exertional symptoms despite normal or borderline resting values, and duplex ultrasound when anatomic definition will change management. Guideline-supported risk-based testing differs from universal screening of unselected asymptomatic adults, for which outcome benefit remains unproven. Detection is clinically meaningful only when linked to appropriate prevention, symptom management, foot protection, and referral.

CONCLUSION: This narrative review supports a risk-stratified, treatment-linked approach to PAD recognition in hypertension care, but the proposed case-finding pathway itself has not been proven to improve clinical outcomes. Pragmatic trials of the complete care pathway are needed.

articles.title: Severity-Based Triage for Direct Transportation to Nearest Comprehensive Stroke Center: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The efficacy of endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (LVO) is time dependent. Patients initially transported to a primary stroke center (PSC) may require secondary transfer, potentially delaying EVT. For severely affected patients, bypassing the PSC for direct transport to a comprehensive stroke center may expedite EVT but risks delaying IV thrombolysis. Effects of prehospital bypass strategies on functional outcomes are thus uncertain.

METHODS: For this systematic review and meta-analysis, PubMed and Web of Science were searched until December 2025. Randomized and nonrandomized studies comparing transport to the nearest stroke center with transport to a more distant comprehensive stroke center in patients with suspected stroke were included. Two investigators independently screened records, selected eligible studies, extracted summary data, and assessed risk of bias. Random-effects meta-analysis was used to quantify associations between prehospital bypass, endovascular therapy, and functional outcomes.

RESULTS: Literature search identified 1,991 distinct reports. Of 18 eligible studies, 2 were randomized controlled trials (RCTs, n = 1,540 patients), 11 before-after studies (n = 11,837), and 5 cross-sectional studies (n = 1,139), comprising a total of 14,516 patients (52% men/48% women). Risk of bias was high in nonrandomized studies. Patients undergoing prehospital bypass and control patients had similar likelihoods of receiving EVT (odds ratio [OR] 1.52, 95% CI 0.98-2.35) or thrombolysis (OR 1.12, 0.92-1.35). Prehospital bypass was associated with earlier groin puncture (median difference -63.9 minutes, 95% CI -84.1 to -43.7). Time to needle in bypass patients was longer than in control patients in RCTs (median delay 34 minutes, 23.1-44.9 minutes), but similar in nonrandomized studies. Functional independence (modified Rankin Scale 0-2) at 90 days was more frequent in bypass patients (OR 1.23, 1.04-1.45). In patients with intracerebral hemorrhage, bypass was associated with increased mortality (risk ratio 1.30, 1.02-1.64).

DISCUSSION: For patients with LVO stroke, benefits of expedited thrombectomy may outweigh possible risks associated with longer prehospital transport times. However, evidence is insufficient to recommend the routine implementation of prehospital bypass protocols. Further research is needed to determine circumstances under which direct access to comprehensive stroke centers should be prioritized for patients with severe stroke symptoms.

articles.title: Association of Prethrombectomy Hemorrhagic Infarction on MRI With Further Transformation and Functional Outcomes: A Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) is the standard of care for acute ischemic stroke from large vessel occlusion (LVO). Although postprocedural parenchymal hematoma (PH) predicts poor outcomes, pretreatment hemorrhagic infarction (HI), defined as petechial bleeding within infarcted tissue, is traditionally viewed as a benign radiologic finding. Its significance on sensitive preintervention MRI remains underexplored. We evaluated whether pretreatment MRI HI is associated with 90-day functional dependence, post-MT PH, and symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage (SICH).

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with anterior circulation LVO undergoing MT at 2 stroke centers (2015-2022). Patients required pre-MT T2*-weighted MRI. HI was graded (types I/II) per European Cooperative Acute Stroke Study III criteria in blinded fashion. The primary outcome was 90-day functional dependence (modified Rankin Scale 3-6). Secondary outcomes were post-MT ipsilateral PH and SICH. We used multivariable Bayesian and frequentist logistic regression to adjust for age, sex, NIH Stroke Scale, baseline disability, comorbidities, infarct volume, and procedural factors.

RESULTS: Among 479 patients (median age 72 years; 46% female; 50% received IV thrombolysis), pretreatment HI was identified in 25 (5.2%), with excellent inter-rater agreement (Cohen κ = 0.9). Functional dependence at 90 days occurred in 47% of the total cohort, ipsilateral PH in 9.4%, and SICH in 3.1%. In multivariable analysis, pre-MT HI was independently associated with 90-day functional dependence (Bayesian adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 6.66, 95% credible interval [CrI] 2.15-24.28, Pr[OR > 1] = 1.00; frequentist aOR 5.95, 95% CI 1.91-18.52, p = 0.002). Pre-MT HI also demonstrated a high posterior probability of association with post-MT ipsilateral PH (Bayesian aOR 2.76, 95% CrI 0.73-9.26, Pr[OR > 1] = 0.94; frequentist aOR 2.84, 95% CI 0.84-9.58, p = 0.091) and SICH (Bayesian aOR 5.59, 95% CrI 0.63-34.92, Pr[OR > 1] = 0.95; frequentist aOR 6.02, 95% CI 1.00-36.11, p = 0.049).

DISCUSSION: HI detected on pretreatment MRI is an independent predictor of poor long-term functional outcomes and correlates with post-MT PH/SICH. Pre-MT HI may reflect significant blood-brain barrier disruption and microvascular fragility, serving as a marker of reperfusion vulnerability. Limitations include the retrospective design and the relatively low frequency of HI, PH, and SICH, which were addressed using Bayesian modeling to quantify uncertainty. Although not a contraindication to MT, identifying HI may aid in periprocedural risk stratification and serve as a candidate marker for future neuroprotective trials.

articles.title: Sex Differences in Blood Pressure Dynamics and Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Optimal blood pressure (BP) management after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) remains controversial, and whether early BP dynamics differentially affect outcomes among female and male participants is unclear.

METHODS: This was an exploratory secondary analysis of ENCHANTED2/MT, a multicenter, open-label, blinded-end point randomized trial conducted in 44 tertiary hospitals in China. Eligible adults had AIS due to large-vessel occlusion, successful reperfusion after EVT, and persistent elevated systolic BP (SBP) within 3 hours after reperfusion. Serial BP measurements obtained during the first 72 hours after randomization were used to estimate patient-specific mean BP trajectories and short-term BP variability with a location-scale mixed-effects modeling approach. Associations of mean BP, BP variability, and randomized intensive vs standard BP lowering strategy with clinical outcomes were examined, with sex being evaluated as an effect modifier. The primary outcome was the 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS).

RESULTS: Among 816 patients (mean age 67.6 ± 12.0 years; 38% female), intensive BP management was associated with worse 90-day ordinal mRS outcome among male participants (adjusted common odds ratio [acOR] 1.91; 95% CI 1.29-2.83), whereas the corresponding estimate among female participants was closer to null (acOR 0.94; 95% CI 0.56-1.57; ratio of acORs 0.49; 95% CI 0.26-0.94). In separate postrandomization BP exposure models, each 5 mm Hg higher mean SBP was associated with worse 90-day mRS outcome among male participants (acOR 1.11; 95% CI 1.03-1.20), whereas no clear adverse association was observed among female participants (acOR 0.95; 95% CI 0.85-1.05; ratio of acORs 0.85; 95% CI 0.75-0.97). SBP variability showed weaker and less consistent sex differential associations. Findings across secondary outcomes were directionally similar but exploratory.

DISCUSSION: In this exploratory secondary analysis of ENCHANTED2/MT, randomized BP management strategy and early post-thrombectomy BP dynamics showed sex-stratified associations with outcomes. These associations may reflect biological sex and sex-related differences in baseline clinical and vascular characteristics. These findings are hypothesis generating and should be confirmed in prospectively designed studies before informing sex-specific BP management after EVT.

TRIAL REGISTRATION INFORMATION: ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04140110; the Registration Date, October 22, 2019.

articles.title: Pearls & Oy-sters: Trace Visualization of the Central Retinal Artery: A Favorable Sign for Late-Window Endovascular Therapy in Central Retinal Artery Occlusion.
articles.abstract: In acute central retinal artery occlusion (CRAO), vessel stenosis and hemodynamic impairment significantly affect visual prognosis. We report a 69-year-old man who presented with 18 hours of acute, severe right eye blurred vision. Fundus examination and optical coherence tomography confirmed central retinal artery (CRA) occlusion with inner retinal edema. Digital subtraction angiography revealed an aortic arch variation and severe C1 segment stenosis of the right internal carotid artery (ICA), accompanied by delayed ophthalmic artery filling and faint visualization of the CRA. After multidisciplinary consultation, the patient underwent ICA stenting. Postoperative imaging showed resolved stenosis and improved retinal perfusion; the patient's vision subsequently improved and stabilized. This case suggests that revascularization can facilitate visual recovery even beyond the traditional window. Furthermore, faint CRA visualization on digital subtraction angiography indicates residual flow, providing a potential rationale for recanalization therapy.

articles.title: Increased risk of arteriovenous fistula thrombosis in haemodialysis patients with ANCA-associated vasculitis: a retrospective comparative study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the occurrence and timing of arteriovenous fistula (AVF) thrombosis in patients undergoing maintenance haemodialysis (HD) due to ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV) and those with non-vasculitic causes of end-stage kidney disease (ESKD).

METHODS: This single-centre retrospective study included patients receiving maintenance HD for AAV-related ESKD and a control group with ESKD attributed to diabetic nephropathy or hypertensive nephrosclerosis. The AVF thrombosis analysis was restricted to patients with an AVF during follow-up. Cox proportional hazards regression was used to evaluate the association between AAV and AVF thrombosis.

RESULTS: The study included 31 patients with AAV (mean age 71.3 ± 13.6 years; 58% male) and 102 controls (mean age 55.8 ± 17.9 years; 56% male). Among patients with an AVF, thrombosis occurred in 9 of 18 patients (50%) in the AAV group and 6 of 51 patients (11.8%) in the control group (p = .002). In the unadjusted Cox regression analysis, AAV was associated with a higher hazard of AVF thrombosis (HR 4.14, 95% CI 1.43-11.97; p = .009). This association remained statistically significant after adjustment for age (HR 4.46, 95% CI 1.39-14.26; p = .012).

CONCLUSION: AAV was associated with a higher hazard of AVF thrombosis in patients undergoing maintenance HD compared with non-vasculitic ESKD, even after adjustment for age. However, the limited number of thrombotic events and potential residual confounding warrant cautious interpretation. Larger studies are needed to confirm these findings and clarify their implications for vascular access management.

METHODS: This single-centre retrospective study included patients receiving maintenance HD for AAV-related ESKD and a control group with ESKD attributed to diabetic nephropathy or hypertensive nephrosclerosis. The AVF thrombosis analysis was restricted to patients with an AVF during follow-up.

articles.title: In-Hospital Outcomes and Mortality After Revascularization for Chronic Mesenteric Ischemia by Maintenance Dialysis Status: A National Inpatient Sample Analysis, 2006-2020.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Evidence on in-hospital outcomes after chronic mesenteric ischemia (CMI) revascularization in patients receiving maintenance dialysis is limited.

METHODS: We analyzed adult CMI-coded hospitalizations undergoing endovascular or open revascularization in the 2006-2020 National Inpatient Sample. Hospitalizations with and without maintenance dialysis were compared using 1:2 propensity score matching and survey-weighted multivariable regression.

RESULTS: Of 7,962 eligible hospitalizations, 411 (5.2% of the unweighted sample) involved maintenance dialysis. Maintenance dialysis was associated with higher adjusted odds of in-hospital mortality (aOR 1.96), non-routine discharge (aOR 1.46), prolonged hospitalization (aOR 1.41), transfusion (aOR 1.43), sepsis (aOR 1.88), pneumonia (aOR 1.69), multiorgan failure or shock (aOR 1.80), and venous thromboembolism (aOR 2.06). Hospital charges were also higher (adjusted beta USD 17,497), whereas urinary tract infection odds were lower (aOR 0.68).

DISCUSSION: Maintenance dialysis was associated with greater in-hospital morbidity and mortality among CMI-coded revascularization hospitalizations. The inability to distinguish stable from acute-on-chronic CMI limits interpretation as an elective cohort. Findings support individualized perioperative assessment without establishing causation or optimal treatment timing.
articles.englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Evidence on in-hospital outcomes after chronic mesenteric ischemia (CMI) revascularization in patients receiving maintenance dialysis is limited. METHODS: We analyzed adult CMI-coded hospitalizations undergoing endovascular or open revascularization in the 2006-2020 National Inpatient Sample. Hospitalizations with and without maintenance dialysis were compared using 1:2 propensity score matching and survey-weighted multivariable regression.

articles.title: T-cell states in aortic dissection: from molecular immune profiling toward causal and translational validation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND/OBJECTIVES: Single-cell RNA sequencing and T-cell receptor profiling reveal substantial T-cell heterogeneity in aortic dissection (AD), but whether these responses contribute to vascular injury or reflect post-onset immune activation remains uncertain. This review evaluates human and experimental evidence by disease stage, tissue compartment, functional validation, T-cell specificity, and intervention timing, distinguishing descriptive profiling from evidence supporting causal and translational inference.

DISCUSSION: Human studies identify Th1/Th17-associated, CD8+ cytotoxicity-associated, and regulatory T-cell alterations, with stage-related differences in T-cell composition and clonality. Most evidence is cross-sectional and obtained after clinical onset. Antigen specificity, direct aortic-wall cytotoxicity, impaired Treg suppression, and T-cell-mediated aortic-wall injury remain unproven. Single-cell and TCR profiling identify candidate T-cell states and clonotypes for spatial and functional validation, not causal proof. Among candidate pathways, the IL-6-STAT3-IL-17 axis currently has the strongest AD-specific preclinical rationale, but existing interventions are largely non-T-cell-restricted and initiated before or during disease induction. Stronger causal attribution requires convergent human evidence, post-lesion T-cell-restricted perturbation, disease-progression endpoints, and rescue or target-engagement studies. The subacute phase after anatomical and haemodynamic stabilisation may offer a window to study persistent injury-amplifying T-cell responses, whereas early acute and perioperative immunomodulation remains unsupported.

CONCLUSIONS: Current evidence supports altered T-cell states after AD onset but does not establish an initiating role. Near-term priorities should be prospective biomarker validation and post-lesion mechanistic studies rather than T-cell-directed immuno-modulation during the early acute and perioperative phases. Clinical translation should await reproducible associations linked to stage-specific causal mechanisms and acceptable safety.

articles.title: Association between neuromuscular electrical stimulation and intermittent pneumatic compression for the prevention of deep venous thrombosis among neurosurgery patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Deep vein thrombosis (DVT) considerably affects the incidence and mortality rates in patients undergoing neurosurgery. Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) and intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) are frequently used as adjunct treatments to prevent DVT; however, their effects remain unclear. This study was conducted to compare the association of NMES and IPC as two mechanical prophylaxis strategies in neurosurgical patients who were ineligible for pharmacological prophylaxis.

METHODS: Postoperative neurosurgical patients were retrospectively enrolled from a single centre between January 2020 and December 2021. These patients were assessed to have a high bleeding risk and received either NMES or IPC as mechanical prophylaxis. Univariable analysis was used to explore the risk factors for DVT, and multivariable logistic regression analysis was used to determine the independent associations between DVT and potential variables after adjusting for confounding factors.

RESULTS: Among 232 patients who underwent neurosurgery, 131 received IPC and 101 received NMES, with no overlap between the two groups. DVT was diagnosed in 62 patients (11 received NMES and 51 received IPC). After controlling for sex, age, operation duration and length of hospital stay, NMES use was associated with a lower incidence of DVT (OR = 0.268, 95% CI = 0.125-0.576, p = .001). Moreover, men were less likely to have DVT than women (OR = 0.469, 95% CI = 0.242-0.910, p = .025), older age was associated with higher odds of DVT (OR = 3.419, 95% CI = 1.594-7.334, p = .002), and a longer operation duration was associated with higher odds of DVT (OR = 2.180, 95% CI = 1.042-4.560, p = .039).

CONCLUSION: This study found an association between NMES and reduced odds of DVT compared with IPC in neurosurgery patients. Although NMES may be more widely adopted in neurosurgery to decrease the incidence of DVT, further evidence is required to determine its effectiveness in clinical practice.

Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) and intermittent pneumatic compression (IPC) are frequently used as adjunct treatments to prevent DVT; however, their effects remain unclear. This study was conducted to compare the association of NMES and IPC as two mechanical prophylaxis strategies in neurosurgical patients who were ineligible for pharmacological prophylaxis.

articles.title: Neutrophil extracellular traps drive immunoinflammatory remodeling in abdominal aortic aneurysm: from inflammatory amplification to precision therapy.
articles.abstract: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a chronic vascular disorder characterized by progressive aortic wall dilation, extracellular matrix degradation, and an increased risk of catastrophic rupture. Currently, no effective pharmacological therapy is available to prevent or slow AAA progression. Neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) have emerged as a critical pathological platform linking dysregulated innate immunity to vascular structural deterioration. In the AAA microenvironment, local inflammation, oxidative stress, metabolic disturbances, altered mechanical forces, and platelet activation collectively contribute to the induction of NETosis. Persistent NET formation promotes immunoinflammatory remodeling of the aortic wall by activating inflammatory sensing pathways, including TLR9, cGAS-STING, and NLRP3, modulating macrophage responses, inducing vascular smooth muscle cell ferroptosis and phenotypic switching, and exacerbating proteolytic degradation, oxidative injury, and immunothrombotic responses. During disease progression, NETs may transition from early drivers of inflammatory amplification to sustained regulators of vascular remodeling, while in advanced AAA they may synergize with intraluminal thrombus formation and structural destabilization to accelerate disease progression. Circulating NET-associated biomarkers represent promising candidates for complementing conventional imaging-based risk assessment; however, their specificity and predictive value require further validation. Therapeutic strategies targeting PAD4-mediated NET formation, the oxidative metabolic environment, NET-associated effector molecules, DNase I-mediated NET degradation, and nucleic acid sensing pathways have demonstrated potential in preclinical studies. This review systematically summarizes the emerging roles of NETs in AAA pathogenesis and discusses future precision strategies integrating biomarkers, multi-omics profiling, and imaging-based risk stratification with stage-specific therapeutic interventions.

articles.title: Cross-elbow stent placement for refractory arteriovenous fistula stenosis and chronic total occlusion in hemodialysis patients: a single-center retrospective cohort of 42 cases.
articles.abstract: Cross-elbow stent placement in hemodialysis arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) has been avoided due to risks of fracture, kinking, deformation, migration, and infection. However, elbow lesions may be refractory to angioplasty and progress to chronic total occlusion (CTO). We evaluated the safety, feasibility, and patency of cross-elbow stenting for AVF salvage. Consecutive adult hemodialysis patients who received cross-elbow stents for clinically significant AVF stenosis or CTO (September 2021 - March 2026) at a single center were retrospectively analyzed. Primary outcomes were target lesion primary patency (TLPP), access circuit primary patency (ACPP), access circuit secondary patency, and access circuit assisted primary patency, estimated by Kaplan-Meier. Technical and clinical success and complications were recorded. Forty-two patients were included; 45.2% had CTO and 57.1% had prior PTA. Eluvia-based stents were used in 83.3%. Technical and clinical success were both 100%. Mean access flow increased from 407 ± 267 to 839 ± 188 mL/min. TLPP at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months was 90.1%, 84.4%, 76.9%, and 76.9%, respectively. No stent fracture, migration, kinking, or infection occurred. Cross-elbow stenting was technically feasible and provided favorable short- to mid-term patency without device-related complications, supporting its use as a salvage option for selected refractory AVF lesions and CTOs.

However, elbow lesions may be refractory to angioplasty and progress to chronic total occlusion (CTO). We evaluated the safety, feasibility, and patency of cross-elbow stenting for AVF salvage.

articles.title: Trends in incident hemodialysis access and mortality in China: results from China Renal Data System 2000-2024.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUNDS: Large‑scale multicenter data on vascular access among Chinese incident hemodialysis (HD) patients are limited. We explored temporal trends of initial vascular access and its relationship with all‑cause mortality.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted using the China Renal Data System, enrolling incident HD patients from January 2000 to April 2024. Vascular access trends and distribution at HD initiation were analyzed.

RESULTS: 16,717 patients were enrolled (mean age 55.62 ± 10.93 years; 61.54% male; mean follow‑up 64.41 months). At HD initiation, 29.17% of patients used arteriovenous fistula/graft (AVF/AVG), while 70.83% used central venous catheter (CVC), comprising 60.78% with a maturing AVF/AVG and 10.06% with CVC alone. AVF/AVG use increased from 26.24% in 2015 to 35.77% in 2024, while CVC-only use decreased from 16.16% to 8.27%. Mortality rates per 100 person-years were 4.15 (95% confidence interval [CI] 3.93 - 4.38), 7.24 (95% CI 7.00 - 7.49), and 15.08 (95% CI 14.07 - 16.15) in the AVF/AVG, CVC with maturing AVF/AVG, and CVC-only groups, respectively. In the adjusted Cox model, patients using CVC with a maturing AVF/AVG or CVC alone exhibited 36% and 91% higher all-cause mortality risks, respectively, compared with those using AVF/AVG.

CONCLUSIONS: Over the 25-year period, initial vascular access among Chinese incident HD patients gradually shifted from CVC to AVF/AVG, reflecting ongoing and considerable improvements in vascular access practice in China. CVC use at HD initiation was associated with higher all-cause mortality compared with AVF/AVG. These findings support early AVF/AVG creation in end-stage kidney disease patients to avoid CVC use at HD initiation.

We explored temporal trends of initial vascular access and its relationship with all‑cause mortality. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study was conducted using the China Renal Data System, enrolling incident HD patients from January 2000 to April 2024.

articles.title: Variation and temporal trends in Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group billing for carotid endarterectomy across Vascular Quality Initiative centers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hospitals use Medicare Severity Diagnosis Related Group (MS-DRG) coding to bill for each admission, with higher payment provided for those with complications or comorbidities (CCs) or major CCs (MCCs). We analyzed variation in MS-DRG coding for carotid endarterectomy (CEA) across Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) centers to identify opportunities for improvement.

METHODS: We matched CEA cases in the VQI registry with Medicare claims data from 2013 through 2023. A multivariable stepwise logistic regression model was created to identify variables associated with CC or MCC billing (with odds ratios [ORs]). We examined variations in CC or MCC billing percentages among centers and applied a multivariable model to compare observed-to-expected (O:E) CC or MCC billing rates to adjust for patient differences. Billing trends over time were analyzed using linear regression.

RESULTS: Among 75,064 primary CEA admissions for Medicare beneficiaries, 39.5% were billed with CCs or MCCs (31.1% CCs, 8.4% MCCs) and 60.5% without. Eleven VQI clinical variables that indicated CCs were significantly associated with CC or MCC billing: dialysis dependence (OR, 22.30), postoperative neurological events (OR, 5.25), length of stay >2 days (OR, 4.98), pre-existing heart failure (OR, 4.08), any postoperative complication (OR, 3.70), reoperation (OR, 3.65), preoperative neurological event (OR, 1.70), higher American Society of Anesthesiologists class (OR, 1.50), urgent/emergent procedure (OR, 1.28), postoperative intravenous blood pressure management (OR, 1.27), and institutional transfer (OR, 1.16). Across 371 VQI centers, CC or MCC billing rates varied 5.6-fold, ranging from 15% to 84% of admissions. After risk adjustment, observed-to-expected ratios still demonstrated 4.2-fold variation, from 0.45 to 1.90 across centers. The observed rate of CC or MCC billing increased over time, from 35.5% in 2015 to 46.1% in 2023 (P < .001). In contrast, the expected adjusted rates predicted by the model remained stable (P = .269). A discrete inflection point was identified between 2016 and 2017, after which higher billing rates persisted (P < .001).

CONCLUSIONS: Substantial variation exists for MS-DRG billing for CEA across VQI centers. Billing rates for CCs or MCCs increased from 2013 through 2023. These findings suggest potential underbilling at some centers and overbilling at others. Leveraging Medicare-linked VQI registry data and the proposed model could help to improve coding and billing accuracy, optimize reimbursement, and reduce Medicare audit risk.

We analyzed variation in MS-DRG coding for carotid endarterectomy (CEA) across Vascular Quality Initiative (VQI) centers to identify opportunities for improvement. METHODS: We matched CEA cases in the VQI registry with Medicare claims data from 2013 through 2023.

articles.title: Maternal and Fetal Safety Outcomes of Thrombolytics for Ischemic Stroke in Pregnancy: A Systematic Review and Aggregated Case Series.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: The safety of intravenous thrombolytics for ischemic stroke in pregnancy is largely unknown. We performed a systematic review to identify published use of thrombolytics for stroke during pregnancy, with the aim of assessing maternal and fetal safety outcomes. To provide additional safety data, we included cases of thrombolysis for deep vein thrombosis, mechanical valve thrombosis, and pulmonary embolism in pregnancy.

METHODS: We used the PRISMA and MOOSE guidelines to conduct the review. We searched 3 databases (OVID Medline, EMBASE, Scopus) for studies published up to October 2025. We analyzed outcomes in a Bayesian aggregated case series to compare rates of adverse outcomes in our cohort with those in the general population. Elective termination and spontaneous abortion were grouped together, given that it was often difficult to determine whether complications of thrombolysis may have played a role in the decision for termination.

RESULTS: We included 123 studies of 216 patients (median age 31 years) treated with thrombolytics during pregnancy, of whom 85 had ischemic stroke. Six of the 32 total fetal deaths were deemed likely to be causally related to thrombolytics (3 in stroke). The risk of miscarriage in our thrombolysis population was 12.4% higher (95% credible interval [CrI]: 2.6%, 23.2%) than published general pregnant population rates, and the risk of stillbirth was 5.9% higher (95% CrI: 1.6%, 12.7%). The proportion of pregnant patients with symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage was similar between our pregnant cohort and young, nonpregnant patients receiving thrombolytics (risk difference -0.4%; 95% CrI: -0.8%, 2.7%).

DISCUSSION: Thrombolytics were likely causally associated with a small minority of published cases of fetal death after thrombolysis in pregnancy. There was no signal of increased harm from thrombolysis to the mother, including similar rates of symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage. In many cases, it was difficult to discern effects of thrombolytics on fetal outcomes from the effects of the disease itself; hence, our results should be interpreted with caution. Nonetheless, our findings broadly support the use of thrombolytics in otherwise-eligible pregnant patients but underscore the importance of the risk-benefit assessment in such patients.

TRIAL REGISTRATION INFORMATION: The study protocol was pre-registered on PROSPERO (registration number: CRD42024605043).

We performed a systematic review to identify published use of thrombolytics for stroke during pregnancy, with the aim of assessing maternal and fetal safety outcomes. To provide additional safety data, we included cases of thrombolysis for deep vein thrombosis, mechanical valve thrombosis, and pulmonary embolism in pregnancy.

articles.title: Low Ventricular Chamber Stiffness Identifies a High-Risk Eccentric Remodeling Phenotype in the Fontan Circulation: A FORCE Registry Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Rising end-diastolic pressure in patients with a Fontan circulation has led to the hypothesis that circulatory failure is driven by progressive ventricular stiffening. However, end-diastolic pressure is influenced by loading conditions and extracardiac constraint and may not accurately reflect chamber stiffness. We aimed to characterize ventricular chamber stiffness using the end-diastolic pressure-volume relationship and examine its clinical and prognostic significance in patients with a Fontan circulation.

METHODS: In the FORCE registry (Fontan Outcomes Registry Using Clinical Examinations), chamber stiffness was quantified with the exponential coefficient β derived from single-beat end-diastolic pressure-volume relationship reconstruction using paired catheterization and cardiovascular magnetic resonance data. The β values were standardized as body surface area- and sex-based Z scores and related to clinical characteristics, ventricular remodeling, and a composite adverse outcome (death, transplantation listing, sustained atrial or ventricular arrhythmias, protein-losing enteropathy, or plastic bronchitis).

RESULTS: Among 814 patients (median age, 14.7 years), median β was 0.034 mL-1 (0.025-0.046). Lower β Z score was associated with dominant right ventricle, eccentric remodeling with reduced ejection fraction, increased collateral flow and intracardiac recirculation, greater symptom burden, and higher arrhythmia prevalence, despite similar filling pressures. Over a median follow-up of 2.7 years (0.9-6.1 years), lower β Z score independently predicted adverse outcomes (adjusted hazard ratio, 1.30 per 1-SD decrease [95% CI 1.04-1.61]). A β Z score <-0.71, β<0.025 mL-1, or body surface area-indexed end-diastolic volume >103 mL/m2 showed similarly modest discrimination for adverse outcomes overall (area under the curve, 0.59), with greater discrimination in dominant right ventricles.

CONCLUSIONS: Contrary to prevailing assumptions, lower rather than higher chamber stiffness was associated with adverse Fontan outcomes, identifying a high-compliance phenotype characterized by ventricular dilation and eccentric remodeling. These findings suggest that, in the contemporary FORCE cohort, Fontan failure might be more closely associated with this remodeling phenotype than with progressive stiffening.
articles.englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Rising end-diastolic pressure in patients with a Fontan circulation has led to the hypothesis that circulatory failure is driven by progressive ventricular stiffening. However, end-diastolic pressure is influenced by loading conditions and extracardiac constraint and may not accurately reflect chamber stiffness. We aimed to characterize ventricular chamber stiffness using the end-diastolic pressure-volume relationship and examine its clinical and prognostic significance in patients with a Fontan circulation.

articles.title: Systematic Review of Patient Priorities and Shared Decision Making in Lower Extremity Peripheral Artery Disease Treatment Decisions.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this review was to synthesise evidence on patient priorities, preferences for treatment, and shared decision making experiences in lower extremity peripheral artery disease (PAD) treatment decisions across intermittent claudication, chronic limb threatening ischaemia, and amputation level contexts.

DATA SOURCES: Key databases including MEDLINE and Embase.

REVIEW METHODS: This was a systematic review (PROSPERO ID: CRD420251106155). Key databases including MEDLINE and Embase were searched for English language studies published from 1 January 2000 to 17 December 2025. Eligible studies included adults with symptomatic PAD, reporting experiences, information needs, priorities, or decision making related to PAD treatment. Two reviewers independently screened studies, resolving disagreements by consensus with a third reviewer. Study quality was assessed using design appropriate tools. Qualitative and quantitative findings were integrated using a structured thematic narrative approach.

RESULTS: Thirty-four studies were included in the systematic review, comprising qualitative, mixed methods, observational registry or cohort, and stated preference studies, and one stepped wedge cluster randomised trial. Most qualitative and cohort studies were rated moderate to high quality. Participant reporting in the 34 studies was limited: seven studies (21%) did not report sex, two (6%) recruited men only, and most mixed sex studies recruited predominantly men; and 18 (53%) did not report ethnicity and, where reported, participants were predominantly White. Across heterogeneous studies, recurring patient valued domains included pain relief, walking ability, independence, emotional wellbeing, function, quality of life, treatment burden, risk, and uncertainty. Decision making processes were shaped by preferred involvement, trust, communication, clarity of options, and continuity of care. Studies identified a mismatch between patients' preferred and experienced decisional roles, with reported involvement lower than desired. Stated preference evidence showed heterogeneity in risk tolerance and treatment trade offs. Trial evidence reported improvements in shared decision making measures and patient knowledge after structured decision support and clinician training.

CONCLUSION: Patient valued outcomes and treatment trade offs vary across lower extremity PAD contexts and individuals. Shared decision making may help incorporate these priorities into treatment decisions, supported by tailored information, continuity of care, clinician training, and decision support tools.
articles.englishSummary: OBJECTIVES: The aim of this review was to synthesise evidence on patient priorities, preferences for treatment, and shared decision making experiences in lower extremity peripheral artery disease (PAD) treatment decisions across intermittent claudication, chronic limb threatening ischaemia, and amputation level contexts. DATA SOURCES: Key databases including MEDLINE and Embase. REVIEW METHODS: This was a systematic review (PROSPERO ID: CRD420251106155).

articles.title: Predicting Morbidity, Mortality, Revision, and Ambulation in Patients Undergoing Major Lower Limb Amputation for Peripheral Arterial Disease or Diabetes Mellitus: The Case for Regional Level Clinical Prediction Models.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Several outcome prediction tools exist to support decision making for patients undergoing major lower limb amputation (MLLA). However, most predict a single outcome, are derived from registry level data, and lack external validation. The present study aimed to develop clinically focussed, multi-outcome prediction tools using granular regional data with immediate external validation on an international database.

METHODS: This study involved development, and internal and external validation of multivariable binomial and multinomial regression prediction models. All patients undergoing MLLA for ischaemic or diabetic indications between 1 January 2013 and 1 July 2023 at a single regional vascular hub were used for model development. Clinically focussed logistic multivariable binomial and multinomial regression models were developed predicting 30 day and 1 year mortality and revision, 30 day major morbidity or mortality, and best mobility achieved (binary and 3 category). Model complexity, crossvalidated receiver operating curve (ROC) discrimination and calibration were assessed and optimised, with the best performing models undergoing external validation on PERCEIVE study data. External validity was assessed using discrimination and calibration statistics, with one revision attempt permitted.

RESULTS: The development dataset included 609 patients (75.2% men, median age 69 years). Internal crossvalidated ROC values were 0.774 for 30 day mortality, 0.752 for 1 year mortality, 0.679 for 30 day revision, 0.707 for 1 year revision, 0.699 for 30 day major morbidity or mortality, 0.876 for binary best ambulation, and 0.752 for 3 category best ambulation predictions. All models were well calibrated. On external validation the ROC values were 0.616, 0.722, 0.617, 0.488, 0.697, 0.643, and 0.602, respectively.

CONCLUSION: The prediction models performed well for internal "regional" patient outcomes, especially for mortality and ambulation. On external validation, like other models externally validated on the PERCEIVE data, they failed to generalise to the wider population undergoing MLLA, except for 1 year mortality. Predicting patient outcomes from pre-operative variables remains challenging; however, regional level modelling may provide better performance over more general prediction tools.
articles.englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Several outcome prediction tools exist to support decision making for patients undergoing major lower limb amputation (MLLA). However, most predict a single outcome, are derived from registry level data, and lack external validation. The present study aimed to develop clinically focussed, multi-outcome prediction tools using granular regional data with immediate external validation on an international database.

articles.title: Patients Educating Patients: A Scalable Patient-Led Webinar Model Integrating Patient and Clinician Expertise in Venous Thromboembolism Care.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Individuals with venous thromboembolism (VTE) face knowledge gaps about diagnosis, treatment, and management. We report the implementation of the National Blood Clot Alliance's (NBCA) Patients Educating Patients (PEP) Talks webinar series as a novel educational model for VTE survivors.

METHODS: PEP Talks is a virtual, monthly educational webinar series hosted by NBCA and moderated by two patient leaders and a clinical expert. Sessions featured patient-identified VTE topics with structured discussion and live interactive components, with recordings available for on-demand viewing. Program evaluation included registration volume, live attendance, and recording views. Participant engagement was measured by number of reactions and questions submitted during sessions. We assessed impact with pre- and post-webinar questions.

RESULTS: Twelve sessions were held between October 2024-January 2026. Eleven were recorded and uploaded online. A total of 5,731 individuals registered for the series. Across 12 sessions, 713 unique individuals attended at least one live session, with 1,600 total live attendances. Recordings accumulated 7,657 total views. Among attendees, the majority were VTE survivors (72%), followed by caregivers/relatives (6%) and healthcare professionals (7%). Individuals from 35 countries participated, with most from the US (78%). The majority (58% - 81%) viewed more than 75% of each session. Participant engagement was high, with 2,024 participant-generated questions and 269 positive audience reactions. Pre- and post-session polling demonstrated high levels of patient satisfaction and self-reported understanding of VTE-related concepts.

CONCLUSION: PEP Talks demonstrates the feasibility of a scalable, patient-centered educational webinar model for VTE survivors, achieving high engagement and favorable participant-reported educational outcomes.
articles.englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Individuals with venous thromboembolism (VTE) face knowledge gaps about diagnosis, treatment, and management. We report the implementation of the National Blood Clot Alliance's (NBCA) Patients Educating Patients (PEP) Talks webinar series as a novel educational model for VTE survivors. METHODS: PEP Talks is a virtual, monthly educational webinar series hosted by NBCA and moderated by two patient leaders and a clinical expert.

articles.title: Feasibility and Restenosis Predictors of Optical Frequency Domain Imaging-Guided Drug-Coated Balloon Treatment for Femoropopliteal Lesions.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The clinical utility of optical frequency domain imaging (OFDI) for guiding endovascular therapy in femoropopliteal lesions has not been established. Additionally, the prognostic value of OFDI findings during drug-coated balloon (DCB) treatment for femoropopliteal lesions has never been evaluated.

OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to clarify the feasibility of OFDI-guided DCB treatment and investigate the OFDI findings associated with restenosis after DCB treatment in femoropopliteal lesions.

METHODS: This multicenter, prospective, observational study included patients with symptomatic, nonseverely calcified femoropopliteal lesions who underwent DCB treatment under OFDI guidance. Procedural success was defined as residual stenosis of less than 30% without flow compromise and without any procedural complications. The primary outcome was restenosis of the target lesion, defined as a peak systolic velocity ratio of ≥2.5, as measured by duplex ultrasound at rest or target lesion revascularization.

RESULTS: A total of 202 lesions were initially enrolled, of which 35 (17.3%) were excluded primarily because of severe calcification or inadequate OFDI data. Among the 167 analyzable lesions included in the present analysis, the procedural success rate and 1-year freedom from restenosis were 91.6% and 85.5%, respectively. In the procedural OFDI findings, a calcified nodule in the target lesion (subdistribution hazard ratio: 3.25; 95% CI: 1.01-10.42; P = 0.048) was associated with restenosis.

CONCLUSIONS: OFDI-guided DCB treatment is feasible in selected femoropopliteal lesions. An OFDI-detected calcified nodule is associated with an increased risk of restenosis after DCB treatment for femoropopliteal lesions.
articles.englishSummary: BACKGROUND: The clinical utility of optical frequency domain imaging (OFDI) for guiding endovascular therapy in femoropopliteal lesions has not been established. Additionally, the prognostic value of OFDI findings during drug-coated balloon (DCB) treatment for femoropopliteal lesions has never been evaluated. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to clarify the feasibility of OFDI-guided DCB treatment and investigate the OFDI findings associated with restenosis after DCB treatment in femoropopliteal lesions.

articles.title: Real-World 30-day Outcomes Following Commercial Adoption of the GORE EXCLUDER Thoracoabdominal Branch Endoprosthesis: A National Medicare Analysis.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The Thoracoabdominal Branch Endoprosthesis (TAMBE) recently received FDA approval as the first off-the-shelf endovascular device for complex aneurysmal disease involving the visceral aorta. Prior to formal FDA approval, a pivotal pre-approval analysis demonstrated high procedural success, low perioperative morbidity, and no perioperative mortality. Using Medicare Fee-for-Service (FFS) data, we sought to evaluate real-world adoption patterns and 30-day outcomes following TAMBE implementation nationwide.

METHODS: Medicare Fee-for-Service beneficiaries undergoing TAMBE between October 2024 and December 2025 were identified using the TAMBE-specific ICD-10-PCS code (X2VE3SA). Outcomes were compared to a contemporaneous cohort undergoing ≥4-vessel F/BEVAR in 2023, the year preceding TAMBE approval. Primary outcomes included 30-day mortality, stroke, myocardial infarction (MI), acute kidney injury (AKI), spinal cord ischemia (SCI), bowel ischemia, and reintervention, and were analyzed using Fine-Gray competing-risk regressions with adjustment for demographic, clinical, and procedural characteristics. Pre-specified sub-analyses examined outcomes by aortic indication, hospital procedure volume, and adoption period. Consistent with CMS small-cell suppression policy, any outcome frequencies <11 events were masked and not reported.

RESULTS: The primary cohort consisted of 869 patients treated at 351 hospitals, compared with 678 patients undergoing 4-vessel F/BEVAR. TAMBE was associated with significantly higher unadjusted 30-day mortality (6.7% vs. 4.0%; P=.02), though this difference did not persist after adjustment (adjusted HR 1.37 [0.85-2.21]). No differences were observed in stroke (<1.3% vs. <1.6%), MI (2.0% vs. <1.6%), AKI (7.2% vs. 6.9%) or SCI (5.0% vs. 4.1%) (all P>.05). The majority of implanting hospitals (N=195; 56%) performed a single TAMBE during the study period, and 30-day outcomes did not differ significantly by hospital volume after adjustment. A sensitivity analysis restricted to unambiguously coded, elective TAMBE cases compared with elective F/BEVAR showed similarly elevated 30-day mortality (6.8% vs. 4.0%), albeit not statistically different following adjustment (aHR 1.46 [0.75-2.84]).

CONCLUSION: In this national analysis of Medicare FFS beneficiaries, real-world 30-day outcomes following TAMBE in the first year-plus of commercial availability were notably worse than those reported in the pivotal trial and early single-institution post-market series, with a nearly 7% 30-day mortality rate that persisted across indications, hospital volumes, and time periods. The rapid dissemination of TAMBE to over 351 hospitals, most performing only a single procedure, highlights a fundamental tension between the device's off-the-shelf accessibility and the institutional readiness required for safe deployment, underscoring the need for ongoing post-market surveillance, structured proctorship programs, and a more deliberate approach to patient and operator selection as TAMBE adoption continues.

Prior to formal FDA approval, a pivotal pre-approval analysis demonstrated high procedural success, low perioperative morbidity, and no perioperative mortality. Using Medicare Fee-for-Service (FFS) data, we sought to evaluate real-world adoption patterns and 30-day outcomes following TAMBE implementation nationwide.

articles.title: Risk and Outcomes of Acute Aortic Events in Patients With Polycystic Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study evaluated whether polycystic kidney disease (PKD) is associated with an increased risk of life-threatening acute aortic events (AAEs) and adverse clinical outcomes.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This retrospective cohort study used the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD) from 2000 to 2022. Patients with PKD were propensity score-matched 1 : 10 to controls from an age- and sex-matched control pool. The mean follow-up was 9.5 years. The primary outcome was the incidence of AAE, defined as aortic rupture, aortic dissection, or death due to aortic disease. Secondary outcomes were in-hospital and post-discharge complications. The matched cohort comprised 3,655 patients with PKD and 36,550 controls. PKD was associated with significantly increased risks of aortic rupture (hazard ratio [HR] 4.20; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.74-10.16), aortic dissection (HR 2.31; 95% CI 1.50-3.54), and death due to aortic disease (HR 3.82; 95% CI 2.02-7.23). Among 40,995 admissions for AAEs, patients with PKD had a higher risk of new-onset dialysis (odds ratio 2.59; 95% CI 1.13-5.91). After discharge, patients with PKD also had higher risks of stroke, readmission, and new-onset maintenance dialysis than controls.

CONCLUSIONS: PKD was associated with increased risks of life-threatening AAEs and subsequent adverse outcomes. These findings support heightened clinical awareness and risk-based cardiovascular assessment in select high-risk patients.
articles.englishSummary: BACKGROUND: This study evaluated whether polycystic kidney disease (PKD) is associated with an increased risk of life-threatening acute aortic events (AAEs) and adverse clinical outcomes. METHODS AND RESULTS: This retrospective cohort study used the Taiwan National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD) from 2000 to 2022. Patients with PKD were propensity score-matched 1 : 10 to controls from an age- and sex-matched control pool.

articles.title: Transcarotid Artery Revascularization in Patients with Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis Demonstrates Excellent Outcomes: A Decade Review of Three Stroke Centers.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) represents an alternative to carotid endarterectomy (CEA) for high-grade carotid artery stenosis treatment. We compared perioperative safety, long-term neurologic and cardiovascular outcomes, and durability after TCAR and CEA across three stroke centers.

DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

METHODS: We analyzed CEA and TCAR procedures for asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis from January 2017 through February 2026 across three institutions. One-to-one nearest-neighbor propensity score matching was performed without replacement. Thirty-day outcomes were compared using the exact McNemar test. Long-term outcomes were evaluated using Cox regression with robust variance estimates. Fine-Gray regression was used to treat death as a competing event for nonfatal outcomes.

RESULTS: The final cohort included 889 procedures, 750 CEAs and 139 TCARs. Matching yielded 136 balanced pairs. No ipsilateral stroke, transient ischemic attack (TIA), myocardial infarction (MI), or death occurred within 30 days after TCAR, and no 30-day outcome differed significantly between matched groups. In adjusted analyses of the full cohort, TCAR was associated with mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR], 1.57; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.07-2.31), stroke or death (aHR, 1.64; 95% CI, 1.13-2.36), and the composite of TIA, stroke, MI, or death (aHR, 1.57; 95% CI, 1.11-2.24). After matching, these associations did not reach statistical significance. Median follow-up in the matched cohort was 4.0 years. Long-term neurologic outcomes also did not differ significantly. Restenosis did not differ significantly (subdistribution HR, 1.43; 95% CI, 0.62-3.30; P = 0.399), and one reintervention occurred in each matched group.

CONCLUSION: Among selected asymptomatic patients, TCAR had low perioperative event rates. After matching, no significant differences from CEA were detected in long-term neurologic outcomes, mortality, composite outcomes, restenosis, or reintervention, while late MI remained higher after TCAR. These findings support TCAR as an attractive revascularization option when CEA is less suitable.
articles.englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) represents an alternative to carotid endarterectomy (CEA) for high-grade carotid artery stenosis treatment. We compared perioperative safety, long-term neurologic and cardiovascular outcomes, and durability after TCAR and CEA across three stroke centers. DESIGN: Retrospective cohort study.

articles.title: Association between the stress hyperglycemia ratio and restenosis at 12 months after first percutaneous transluminal angioplasty in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether preoperative stress hyperglycemia ratio (SHR) is associated with 12-month target lesion restenosis after first percutaneous transluminal angioplasty (PTA) of autologous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) stenosis in patients on maintenance hemodialysis (MHD).

METHODS: We retrospectively included 158 MHD patients undergoing first PTA for autologous AVF stenosis at Shaoxing Second Hospital between January 2023 and December 2024. SHR was calculated from preoperative venous glucose and glycated hemoglobin A1c, and patients were grouped by quartiles. The primary endpoint was target lesion restenosis within 12 months, with all patients retained and follow-up administratively censored at 12 months. Cause-specific Cox models were fitted: Model 0 was unadjusted; Model 1 adjusted for age, sex, BMI, smoking, diabetes, hypertension, statin use and antiplatelet therapy; Model 2 further adjusted for dialysis vintage, access site, dialysis modality, pre-procedure stenosis severity, Ln(C-reactive protein), lesion length and vascular calcification. Kaplan-Meier analysis, restricted cubic splines, subgroup analyses of 13 categorical factors, a Fine-Gray competing-risk model, exploratory mediation analysis and discrimination analysis were also performed.

RESULTS: During follow-up, 104 patients (65.8%) developed restenosis, 11 (7.0%) died before restenosis and 43 (27.2%) were censored at 12 months. Restenosis incidence from Q1 to Q4 was 25.6% (10/39), 50.0% (20/40), 94.9% (37/39) and 92.5% (37/40) (log-rank P < 0.001). Compared with Q1, fully adjusted Model 2 HRs for Q2-Q4 were 2.29 (95% CI 1.04-5.04; P = 0.039), 4.30 (2.08-8.87; P < 0.001) and 5.51 (2.52-12.07; P < 0.001). Each 1-SD increase in SHR was associated with an HR of 1.57 (1.25-1.96) in Model 2 (P < 0.001), and restricted cubic splines showed a nonlinear association (P < 0.001). Ln(CRP) was independently associated with restenosis (HR 1.62, 1.06-2.48; P = 0.027). Subgroup and competing-risk analyses were consistent; the exploratory indirect effect through Ln(CRP) was 0.090 (bootstrap 95% CI 0.000-0.199).

CONCLUSION: Preoperative SHR was independently associated with 12-month restenosis after first autologous AVF PTA in MHD patients, showing a nonlinear relationship. As it derives from routine laboratory tests, SHR may aid preoperative risk stratification; causality and clinical utility require prospective multicenter validation.

METHODS: We retrospectively included 158 MHD patients undergoing first PTA for autologous AVF stenosis at Shaoxing Second Hospital between January 2023 and December 2024. articles.title: Clinical, histological, and transcriptomic clustering capture distinct clinically relevant aspects of carotid atherosclerosis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Patients with carotid atherosclerosis exhibit substantial heterogeneity in clinical presentation, plaque characteristics, and future cardiovascular risk, which do not always align. Clinical variables, plaque morphology, and molecular profiles are all used for patient stratification, yet it remains unclear which aspects of disease these data types capture and how they relate to clinically relevant outcomes. We therefore aimed to determine how clustering based on clinical, histological, and transcriptomic data relates to current cerebrovascular symptoms, plaque biology, and future cardiovascular risk.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We analysed 1075 patients undergoing carotid endarterectomy with matched clinical, histological, and transcriptomic data. Unsupervised clustering was applied separately to each data modality, and resulting clusters were evaluated for overlap and association with current symptom status and 3-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Clusters derived from different modalities showed limited overlap, but distinct associations with clinical outcomes. Clinical clusters were most strongly associated with 3-year MACE, whereas histological and transcriptomic clusters were more closely related to current cerebrovascular symptoms. Transcriptomic clusters further delineated molecular pathways and plaque biology. Integration of modalities provided modest improvement in outcome stratification, indicating that these data types capture complementary rather than redundant information.

CONCLUSION: Clinical, histological, and transcriptomic data capture distinct but complementary aspects of carotid atherosclerosis, reflecting systemic cardiovascular risk, local plaque phenotype, and underlying biology, with differing relevance to current cerebrovascular symptoms and future cardiovascular risk. The choice of data modality should therefore be guided by the intended clinical or biological question, rather than assuming a single approach can capture the full disease spectrum.

Clinical variables, plaque morphology, and molecular profiles are all used for patient stratification, yet it remains unclear which aspects of disease these data types capture and how they relate to clinically relevant outcomes. We therefore aimed to determine how clustering based on clinical, histological, and transcriptomic data relates to current cerebrovascular symptoms, plaque biology, and future cardiovascular risk.

articles.title: How far are vision-free medical robots from achieving trustworthy embodied intelligence?
articles.abstract: Embodied Intelligence (EI) is rapidly reshaping the field of robotic surgery, enabling unprecedented levels of clinical precision while liberating surgeons from excessive cognitive and physical burdens. However, for "vision-free" surgical robots incapable of integrating direct visual sensing-such as endovascular robots and untethered swarms-their persistent reliance on external medical imaging fundamentally impedes their evolution toward safe and trustworthy EI-surgery.

articles.title: Streamlined 2D multimodal fusion framework predicts 90 day functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Functional outcome prediction after endovascular therapy can support early risk stratification in acute ischemic stroke. We developed a 2D multimodal fusion framework using multicenter data from 405 patients with post-interventional cerebral hyperdensity on immediate non-contrast CT. Radiomic and deep transfer learning features were extracted from the single CT slice showing the largest hyperdensity area and combined with clinical variables using an Extra Trees classifier. In the external test cohort, the fusion model predicted unfavorable 90-day outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score greater than 2, with an AUC of 0.803, specificity of 88.0%, positive predictive value of 93.3%, and sensitivity of 60.9%. SHAP analysis identified malignant cerebral edema, age, baseline NIHSS, reperfusion status, and imaging intensity descriptors as influential factors. By reducing dependence on 3D segmentation, this framework provides an early phase (within 5 days) prognostic assessment tool for individualized in-hospital risk stratification after thrombectomy.

articles.title: Outcomes of Endovascular Repair for Stanford Type B Aortic Dissection with Concurrent Retrograde Intramural Hematoma Involving the Aortic Arch and/or Ascending Aorta (Zone 0-2) in a Chinese Population: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the outcomes of thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) for type B aortic dissection (TBAD) with concurrent retrograde intramural hematoma (RTIMH) involving the aortic arch, with or without further extension into the ascending aorta.

METHODS: A systematic search of MEDLINE and EMBASE to June 2026 was performed. Studies reporting TEVAR outcomes in adults with TBAD-associated RTIMH, defined as a primary intimal tear at or distal to Ishimaru zone 3 with retrograde intramural hematoma extension into zones 0-2, were included. Co-primary outcomes were technical success and post-TEVAR retrograde type A aortic dissection (RTAD), defined as the new development of a communicating dissection flap within the previously non-flow intramural hematoma. Secondary outcomes included early mortality, stroke, type I endoleak, reintervention, survival, aortic rupture, and aortic remodelling. Proportions were pooled using single-arm random-effects meta-analysis following logit transformation; remaining findings were synthesised narratively.

RESULTS: Seven retrospective cohort studies comprising 342 patients, all from mainland Chinese institutions, were included. The pooled technical success rate was 99% (95% CI 97-99%; I2 = 0.0%). The pooled post-TEVAR RTAD rate was 3% (95% CI 1-8%; I2 = 7.6%), with all events preceded by proximal stent-graft-induced new entry. Secondary outcomes included pooled 30-day mortality of 2% (95% CI 1-4%; I2 = 0.0%), aortic rupture of 2% (95% CI 1-4%; I2 = 0.0%), reintervention of 7% (95% CI 5-11%; I2 = 0.0%), late all-cause mortality of 4% (95% CI 3-6%; I2 = 0.0%), and type I endoleak of 4% (95% CI 2-7%; I2 = 0.0%). All studies reporting pre- and post-procedural imaging demonstrated reductions in ascending aortic diameter and hematoma thickness, with complete ascending IMH resolution in 52.5-100% of patients.

CONCLUSIONS: TEVAR is technically feasible with low perioperative mortality and consistent aortic remodelling in selected patients with TBAD-associated RTIMH. Post-TEVAR RTAD and type I endoleak represent the principal procedure-specific risks. Contemporary evidence remains limited to small retrospective cohorts from a single geographic region.

articles.title: One-Year Outcomes of Surgical Versus Endovascular Revascularization for Acute Limb Ischemia in the SAPLING-ALI Registry.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Despite the increasing use of endovascular therapy as an alternative to surgery for acute limb ischemia, individualized treatment selection remains challenging. We compared outcomes of endovascular therapy versus surgery and sought to identify patient characteristics favoring either strategy.

METHODS: This multicenter retrospective study included consecutive patients with acute limb ischemia (Rutherford category 1-2b) who underwent revascularization at 13 Japanese institutions between July 2011 and March 2025; patients with thrombosed popliteal artery aneurysm were excluded. The primary outcome was amputation-free survival, defined as freedom from major amputation or death from any cause. The primary analysis was a Cox model adjusted for 13 baseline covariates with hospital as a categorical covariate; propensity score weighting was used as a sensitivity analysis. Subgroup analyses were performed to identify characteristics favoring either strategy.

RESULTS: Of 978 patients (endovascular therapy, n = 607; surgery, n = 371), those treated with endovascular therapy more often had diabetes, hemodialysis, dementia, and non-ambulatory status. Unadjusted 1-year amputation-free survival was lower with endovascular therapy than with surgery (68.7% vs 76.3%; log-rank P = .001), but the adjusted hazard ratio for death or major amputation was 1.03 (95% confidence interval, 0.77-1.38; P = .84). Results were consistent with overlap weighting (hazard ratio 1.15; 95% confidence interval, 0.93-1.42) and across other sensitivity analyses. Thirty-day mortality was 13.1% after endovascular therapy and 8.9% after surgery (P = .05), and the difference was attenuated after weighting. No subgroup favoring either strategy was identified (all P for interaction ≥ .18).

CONCLUSIONS: Unadjusted amputation-free survival was lower after endovascular therapy than after surgery, but the difference disappeared after adjustment for patient characteristics and hospital, and no subgroup favoring either strategy was identified. Endovascular therapy, being less invasive, may be a reasonable alternative to surgery for acute limb ischemia.

articles.title: A standardised ultrasound strategy safely excludes recurrent deep-vein thrombosis without prior imaging.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Diagnosing recurrent ipsilateral deep-vein thrombosis (DVT) is challenging because current diagnostic strategies often require comparison with prior imaging, which is frequently unavailable in clinical practice.

OBJECTIVE: To assess whether a sequential diagnostic strategy using colour duplex ultrasound with newly developed standardised criteria, and D-dimer testing could safely exclude recurrent DVT without previous imaging.

METHODS: In this multicentre diagnostic outcome study, we enrolled 466 consecutive outpatients with suspected recurrent ipsilateral lower-limb DVT at 27 centres in France. Ultrasound classified findings as acute occlusive/sub-occlusive thrombosis (absence of vein compressibility and flow, or flow outlining the thrombus, no reflux), chronic post-thrombotic changes (partial obstruction, partial compressibility and filling, reflux), or normal. Patients with non-diagnostic (i.e., inconclusive) ultrasound underwent D-dimer testing and, if positive (≥500 ng/mL FEU), repeat ultrasound at day 7±2. Anticoagulation was withheld after a negative strategy result. The primary outcome was the 3-month cumulative incidence of adjudicated symptomatic venous thromboembolism in untreated patients.

RESULTS: Baseline ultrasound was negative in 280 (60.1%), positive in 176 (37.8%), and non-diagnostic in 10 (2.1%). Five patients with non-diagnostic ultrasound had a negative D-dimer and five had a positive D-dimer but unchanged repeat ultrasound. Two patients (0.4%) were lost to follow-up. Among untreated patients with a negative strategy result, symptomatic venous thromboembolism occurred in three patients (1.1%; 95% CI 0.0-2.2).

CONCLUSIONS: The absence of venous occlusion or sub-occlusion on ultrasound safely excluded recurrent ipsilateral DVT without requiring comparison with prior imaging. This approach could simplify diagnostic pathways and overcome a major limitation of current strategies.
articles.englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Diagnosing recurrent ipsilateral deep-vein thrombosis (DVT) is challenging because current diagnostic strategies often require comparison with prior imaging, which is frequently unavailable in clinical practice. OBJECTIVE: To assess whether a sequential diagnostic strategy using colour duplex ultrasound with newly developed standardised criteria, and D-dimer testing could safely exclude recurrent DVT without previous imaging. METHODS: In this multicentre diagnostic outcome study, we enrolled 466 consecutive outpatients with suspected recurrent ipsilateral lower-limb DVT at 27 centres in France.

articles.title: Association Between Post-procedural Mean Arterial Pressure and Functional Outcomes in Patients Undergoing Mechanical Thrombectomy: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Large-vessel occlusion (LVO) strokes carry high morbidity despite advances in endovascular thrombectomy (EVT). Optimal post-EVT blood pressure (BP) management remains unclear, with current guidelines recommending uniform targets. We investigated the association between post-EVT mean arterial pressure (MAP) and functional outcomes.

METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed patients with LVO stroke at Emory University Hospital (2016-2024) who underwent EVT. BP readings up to 48 h postprocedure were extracted and summarized in sequential time windows. Maximum MAP deviation from postprocedural baseline served as the primary exposure, specified a priori. Outcomes included modified Rankin Scale (mRS) grade at discharge as the primary measure dichotomized as favorable (mRS grades 0-2) versus unfavorable (mRS grades 3-6). Associations were examined using restricted cubic spline logistic regression with a likelihood-ratio test for nonlinearity. Patients were stratified by baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS).

RESULTS: Among 632 patients (median age 66 years, 53.0% male), successful recanalization (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction [mTICI] grade 2b-3) was achieved in 93.7%. Despite this, only 23.7% achieved favorable outcomes at discharge. Larger deviations in either direction from the individual baseline tended to accompany higher discharge mRS grade, but the shape of this association varied with the time window examined and with the summary metric used to define the exposure. It also differed by baseline stroke severity: severe strokes (NIHSS ≥ 16) showed comparatively flat associations, whereas in milder strokes (NIHSS ≤ 5) larger deviations tended to accompany higher mRS grades.

CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory, single-center analysis, the association between early post-EVT MAP deviation and functional outcome differed across multiple conditions varying with the time window examined, the summary metric used, and baseline stroke severity. These findings suggest that post-EVT hemodynamic variability may be relevant in a patient-specific way, challenging the adequacy of uniform BP targets and supporting further investigation of individualized management strategies.

articles.title: Comparative Early Outcomes of Total Transfemoral vs. Upper Extremity Access for Thoracoabdominal Multibranch Endoprosthesis (TAMBE) Implantation.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Early experience with the Thoracoabdominal Multibranch Endoprosthesis (TAMBE) device relied on routine upper extremity access (UEA), but total transfemoral approaches have emerged to minimise aortic arch manipulations and the risk of neurological complications. The aim of this study was to evaluate outcomes following total transfemoral access (TFA) vs. UEA for TAMBE implantation.

METHODS: A retrospective review of consecutive patients undergoing TAMBE implantation at a single centre between April 2020 and January 2026 was performed. Patients were stratified by access strategy into TFA and UEA. The primary outcomes were thirty day mortality and major adverse events (MAEs).

RESULTS: One hundred patients underwent TAMBE implantation during the study period, of whom 32 underwent TFA and 68 UEA. The majority of aneurysms treated were thoraco-abdominal aortic aneurysms (61%), and 45% of patients had a prior endovascular intervention with no significant difference between groups (all p > .050). Mean operative time (232.8 ± 92.4 minutes vs. 250.8 ± 77.3 minutes; p = .18) and fluoroscopy time (59.2 ± 28.4 minutes vs. 48.3 ± 21.6 minutes; p = .066) were not statistically different between groups. Technical success was 91% in the TFA group compared with 99% in the UEA group (p = .095). Thirty day mortality (3% vs. 3%; p = 1.0) and MAEs (16% vs. 13%; p = .76) were not statistically different between TFA and UEA groups. Spinal cord ischaemia rates were 16% for the TFA group and 7% for the UEA group (p = .16), with most cases mild and resolved by discharge (80%). No stroke events occurred in either group. At 6 months, overall branch patency was 92% (78 of 85 branches from 22 patients), including 83% (15 of 18 branches from five patients) in the TFA group and 94% (63 of 67 branches from 17 patients) in the UEA group (p = .16).

CONCLUSION: In this single centre experience, total transfemoral TAMBE implantation was performed in selected patients, and no statistically significant differences were detected in thirty day mortality, MAEs, and technical success between access strategies. Larger studies are needed to determine whether clinically meaningful differences exist.
articles.englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Early experience with the Thoracoabdominal Multibranch Endoprosthesis (TAMBE) device relied on routine upper extremity access (UEA), but total transfemoral approaches have emerged to minimise aortic arch manipulations and the risk of neurological complications. The aim of this study was to evaluate outcomes following total transfemoral access (TFA) vs. UEA for TAMBE implantation.

articles.title: Longitudinal Trends of Intact and Ruptured Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Repairs in the United States: A Cross-Sectional Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted access to elective procedures and routine care. Given the risk of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) rupture, understanding repair trends is important to assess the impact of the pandemic on vascular outcomes.

METHODS: This repeated cross-sectional analysis used the TriNetX network, a multicenter US electronic health records database. We included 423 874 patients diagnosed with AAA from 2016 to 2024. Patients were categorized by clinical presentation-intact AAA and ruptured AAA-and stratified by surgical approach: endovascular aneurysm repair or open aneurysm repair. Annual trends in AAA repair rates were assessed using joinpoint regression to calculate annual percentage change.

RESULTS: Among 19 330 AAA repairs, 3791 (19.6%) were open aneurysm repair, and 15 539 (80.4%) were endovascular aneurysm repair. From 2018 to 2024, 1623 repairs (9.9%) were for ruptured AAA and 14 835 (90.1%) were for intact AAA. The rate of intact AAA repairs initially remained stable from 2018 to 2022 but significantly decreased after the pandemic from 2022 to 2024 (annual percentage change, -2.87% [95% CI, -10.95 to -1.00]). In contrast, ruptured AAA repairs rates shifted sharply during the pandemic, with an established prepandemic decline in ruptured repairs from 2018 to 2020 (annual percentage change, -11.48%) reversed, with an increase from 2020 to 2022 (annual percentage change +12.01%), before declining from 2022 to 2024 (annual percentage change, -11.00%).

CONCLUSIONS: In this retrospective cross-sectional study, repairs for intact AAA declined, while repairs for ruptured AAA increased during the pandemic period. These trends suggest that potential delays in routine surveillance and elective surgery during the pandemic may have increased acute presentations.

Given the risk of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) rupture, understanding repair trends is important to assess the impact of the pandemic on vascular outcomes. METHODS: This repeated cross-sectional analysis used the TriNetX network, a multicenter US electronic health records database.

articles.title: Lipoprotein(a) and incident peripheral artery disease in the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an atherogenic, prothrombotic lipoprotein linked to atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, but prospective data on its association with peripheral artery disease (PAD) in large, diverse U.S. cohorts are limited. We characterized the association of Lp(a) with long-term incident PAD risk in a diverse, community-based U.S.

METHODS: We included Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities (ARIC) Study participants attending Visit 4 (1996-98) with measured Lp(a) and no prevalent PAD. Lp(a) was natural logarithm (ln)-transformed and categorized as <30, 30-50, and >50 mg/dL. Incident PAD was identified from hospitalization and procedure codes through 2019. Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox models adjusted for confounders; Fine-Gray models and cumulative incidence functions accounted for competing mortality.

RESULTS: Among 9727 participants (mean age 63.1 years, 53.9% women, 20.4% Black), 825 incident PAD events occurred over a median 22.5 years of follow-up. Lp(a) was <30 mg/dL in 69.7%, 30-50 in 11.7%, and >50 in 18.6%. Fully adjusted HRs were 1.27 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.03-1.57) for 30-50 mg/dL and 1.32 (95% CI, 1.11-1.57) for >50 mg/dL versus <30 mg/dL; each unit increase in ln(Lp(a)) was associated with an HR of 1.14 (95% CI, 1.07-1.20). Estimates were similar accounting for competing mortality, and cumulative incidence differed across categories (p < 0.001). The association did not differ by baseline statin use.

CONCLUSIONS: Higher Lp(a) was independently associated with greater long-term PAD risk in a community-based cohort, supporting Lp(a) as a risk factor for lower-extremity atherosclerotic disease and its value for risk stratification.
