articles.title: Branched Endovascular Aortic Repair as a Salvage Strategy after Failed Chimney Endovascular Aortic Repair: An International Multicentre Cohort.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Chimney endovascular aortic repair (chEVAR) failures, often manifesting as late type Ia endoleaks or sac expansion, present a formidable surgical challenge. Due to the variable upward orientation of pre-existing chimney stents, fenestrated solutions are frequently technically precluded. This study aimed to evaluate the outcomes of branched endovascular aortic repair (BEVAR) as a salvage strategy for late chEVAR failure within a multicentre international cohort.

METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 29 consecutive patients (median age 81.0 years, interquartile range [IQR] 66.0, 83.0) treated across 13 European centres (2013 - 2025) for failed chEVAR using branched endografts. The primary endpoints were technical success, thirty day clinical success, and procedure related complications. Secondary endpoints included overall survival, freedom from re-intervention, and target visceral vessel (TVV) patency.

RESULTS: The median interval from index chEVAR to BEVAR re-intervention was 48.5 months (IQR 30.0, 80.8). Acute urgent or emergent procedures accounted for 17% of cases (n = 5), while 31% (n = 9) underwent expedited repair for large aneurysms. Off the shelf devices were utilised in 41% of cases. A total of 106 TVVs were incorporated through branches, with a mean of 3.7 vessels per patient. Technical success was achieved in 97% (28 of 29). There was no peri-operative mortality or open surgical conversion. Significant complications included two cases (7%) of severe spinal cord ischaemia. The thirty day clinical success rate was 90%. At a median follow up of 19 months (IQR 9, 40), the Kaplan-Meier estimate for overall survival was 92% at 1 year. TVV patency was 100%, with only one renal artery re-intervention for in stent re-stenosis. Freedom from branch related re-intervention was 96% at 1 year.

CONCLUSION: Salvage of failed chEVAR using branched endografts is technically demanding but yields excellent early results. In experienced centres, BEVAR appears feasible and offers one potential salvage option in selected patients with suitable anatomy, particularly when an off the shelf solution is required.
articles.englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Chimney endovascular aortic repair (chEVAR) failures, often manifesting as late type Ia endoleaks or sac expansion, present a formidable surgical challenge. Due to the variable upward orientation of pre-existing chimney stents, fenestrated solutions are frequently technically precluded. This study aimed to evaluate the outcomes of branched endovascular aortic repair (BEVAR) as a salvage strategy for late chEVAR failure within a multicentre international cohort.

articles.title: Zero Iodine Contrast Endovascular Aortic Repair Using Carbon Dioxide Angiography is Associated with Lower Rates of Renal Deterioration: A Multicentre, Prospective, Propensity Matched Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This prospective, multicentre, non-randomised, observational cohort study evaluated the association between a carbon dioxide (CO2) only angiography strategy during endovascular aortic repair (EVAR) and midterm renal outcomes compared with procedures requiring adjunctive iodinated contrast media (ICM).

METHODS: Consecutive patients undergoing EVAR with a standardised CO2 only protocol were included. Patients were stratified according to intra-operative contrast use (CO2 only vs. CO2 + ICM). The primary endpoint was renal deterioration, defined as a persistent increase of one or more chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage(s) confirmed on two consecutive follow up assessments. Secondary endpoints included mortality, re-intervention, and aneurysm related outcomes. Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed to adjust for baseline differences. Multivariable regression and time to event analyses were conducted.

RESULTS: Of 291 patients (median age 78 years), 239 (82%) underwent CO2 only EVAR and 52 (18%) required adjunctive ICM. At midterm follow up (up to 24 months; mean follow up 18 months), renal deterioration was less frequent in the CO2 only group than in the CO2 + ICM group (5% vs. 23%; p < .001). Patients treated with CO2 only angiography had a significantly lower serum creatinine and higher estimated glomerular filtration rate at follow up (p < .001 for both). These findings were confirmed after PSM, with renal deterioration occurring in 6% vs. 23% of patients (p = .023). In the matched cohort, CO2 only angiography remained independently associated with lower odds of CKD stage progression (odds ratio 0.14, 95% confidence interval 0.03 - 0.45; p < .001). Thirty day and midterm mortality and endoleak rates were similar between groups, whereas re-interventions were more frequent in the CO2 + ICM group.

CONCLUSION: A zero iodine contrast, CO2 only angiography strategy during EVAR was associated with a lower rate of renal deterioration. Because patients requiring adjunctive ICM were identified intra-operatively rather than randomly allocated, residual confounding by indication cannot be excluded, despite propensity score matching. These findings support the feasibility of a CO2 first strategy and justify confirmation in randomised studies.

articles.title: Robotic pulmonary artery reconstruction during lung resection: technical strategies, patient selection and current evidence.
articles.abstract: Pulmonary artery (PA) reconstruction permits parenchyma-sparing resection in selected central lung cancers; its robotic application, however, requires control of a fragile vessel in a confined operative field. This narrative review examines published robot-assisted PA reconstruction, procedural configurations, haemorrhage management, patient selection and relevant video-assisted thoracoscopic (VATS) and open evidence. PubMed/MEDLINE and publisher sources were searched through 26 October 2026, with priority given to studies identifying actual PA repairs separately from bronchial sleeve operations. The early 30-patient uniportal robotic sleeve series contained four PA reconstructions, whereas a subsequent 134-patient sleeve cohort reported excellent overall margins without a separately extractable PA-specific denominator. In a contemporary series of 49 PA reconstructions after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy, 21 operations were open and 28 were reported jointly as VATS/RATS. Small robotic technical series demonstrate tangential repair, angioplasty and circumferential anastomosis, but do not establish comparative vascular safety or durable patency. A large registry found fewer overall conversions during robotic than VATS lobectomy, although robotic conversions were proportionally more often emergent or vascular. Robot-specific safety depends on preplanned proximal and distal occlusion, unobstructed bedside access, disciplined clamp and suture strategies, and immediate conversion capability. Lung autotransplantation remains a separate, highly selected alternative. Available evidence supports feasibility in experienced programmes, not superiority over VATS or thoracotomy. Multicentre, PA-specific reporting is needed to establish vascular outcomes and reproducibility.
articles.englishSummary: Pulmonary artery (PA) reconstruction permits parenchyma-sparing resection in selected central lung cancers; its robotic application, however, requires control of a fragile vessel in a confined operative field. This narrative review examines published robot-assisted PA reconstruction, procedural configurations, haemorrhage management, patient selection and relevant video-assisted thoracoscopic (VATS) and open evidence. PubMed/MEDLINE and publisher sources were searched through 26 October 2026, with priority given to studies identifying actual PA repairs separately from bronchial sleeve operations.

articles.title: Prediction of Stroke Outcome After Endovascular Thrombectomy From Clinical Characteristics: A Machine Learning Approach.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Predicting outcomes after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke is challenging. This study aimed to develop a machine learning model to predict outcomes after EVT using only clinical characteristics available shortly after hospital arrival, excluding imaging, laboratory, and angiographic data.

METHODS: We analyzed data from the JSDB (Japan Stroke Data Bank), a multicenter, prospective registry of patients with acute stroke. A total of 4353 patients who underwent EVT between 2016 and 2020 were included, with those from 2016 to 2019 assigned to the derivation cohort and those from 2020 to the validation cohort. The model was developed using 132 routinely collected clinical variables that can be rapidly obtained on patient arrival. Feature selection was performed using the Boruta algorithm, and the model was built using CatBoost. The primary outcome was a modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score of 0 to 2 at discharge.

RESULTS: Among 4353 patients treated with EVT, the derivation cohort included 2764 patients and the validation cohort, 1589 patients. In these cohorts, 973 (35.2%) and 547 (34.4%) achieved mRS 0 to 2, respectively. Boruta selected 47 predictors. CatBoost achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.744 (95% CI, 0.710-0.776) in the derivation test set and 0.781 (95% CI, 0.755-0.803) in the validation cohort. Validation areas under the receiver operating characteristic curves were 0.792 (95% CI, 0.765-0.815) for mRS 0 to 1, 0.766 (95% CI, 0.744-0.787) for mRS 0 to 3, and 0.680 (95% CI, 0.631-0.729) for mRS 6.

CONCLUSIONS: Our machine learning model predicted outcomes following EVT using only admission clinical data. This imaging-independent machine learning approach may support early prognostication and facilitate discussions of expected clinical courses.

This study aimed to develop a machine learning model to predict outcomes after EVT using only clinical characteristics available shortly after hospital arrival, excluding imaging, laboratory, and angiographic data. METHODS: We analyzed data from the JSDB (Japan Stroke Data Bank), a multicenter, prospective registry of patients with acute stroke.

articles.title: Predictors of Clinically Meaningful 1-Year Health Status Improvements Following Endovascular or Surgical Revascularization: Insights From the BEST-CLI Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite efforts to promote limb salvage in chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), the factors associated with meaningful health status improvement after revascularization remain poorly understood. We examined predictors of meaningful 1-year health status improvement following revascularization for CLTI.

METHODS: We pooled endovascular and surgical arms from the BEST-CLI (Best Endovascular Versus Best Surgical Therapy in Patients With CLTI) randomized controlled trial, including patients with CLTI (150 international sites, 2014-2019). Health status was assessed at baseline and 1 year using the peripheral artery disease-specific Vascular Quality of Life questionnaire, the generic European Quality-of-Life 5 Dimensions, and the Short Form-12 Physical and Mental Component Summary. Distribution-based minimal clinically important difference thresholds were defined as 0.5 SD of baseline health status scores. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of no meaningful 1-year improvement (same/worsened versus improved).

RESULTS: Among 1017 patients (72.0% men, mean age 66.8±9.7 years), clinically meaningful improvements were reported by 76.5% for Vascular Quality of Life, 52.8% European Quality-of-Life 5 Dimensions, 56.7% for Short Form-12 Physical Component Summary, and 42.1% for Short Form-12 Mental Component Summary, regardless of revascularization type (surgical versus endovascular). Cardiometabolic risk factors and higher preprocedural health status increased the odds of no meaningful improvement. Revascularization type was not associated with Vascular Quality of Life improvement (odds ratio, 1.059 [95% CI, 0.91-1.23]; P=0.445; C statistic=0.77).

CONCLUSIONS: One-year postrevascularization, over three-fourths of individuals with CLTI perceived meaningful improvements in peripheral artery disease-specific health, and over half improved overall physical health, regardless of procedure type. Cardiometabolic risk factors and higher preprocedural health status predicted 1-year health status response. REGISTRATION: URL: https://clinicaltrials.gov; Unique identifier: NCT02060630.

articles.title: Comparison of Prosthetic Valve Deformation and Hemodynamic Performance Between Bicuspid and Tricuspid Aortic Valve Anatomy After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: This study compared prosthetic valve deformation and postprocedural hemodynamic performance between bicuspid and tricuspid aortic valve anatomy after transcatheter aortic valve replacement with the Venus-A prosthesis.

METHODS: We retrospectively evaluated patients who underwent transcatheter aortic valve replacement between 2012 and 2022 and underwent postoperative computed tomography within 1 year. Predischarge echocardiographic assessments included the mean transvalvular gradient and paravalvular leak. Computed tomography measurements included expansion ratio, ellipticity, implantation depth, asymmetric leaflet expansion, and hypoattenuated leaflet thickening. The leaflet inflow and valve waist were collectively defined as the functional valve portion.

RESULTS: Among 212 patients (106 bicuspid and 106 tricuspid), the mean age was 74.2±7.6 years, and 43.9% were women. Patients with bicuspid anatomy had a significantly lower oversizing ratio and underwent balloon predilation and postdilation more frequently than those with tricuspid anatomy. Residual transvalvular gradients were higher with bicuspid than tricuspid anatomy (12.0 [interquartile range, 8.2-17.0] versus 10.0 [7.2-14.0] mm Hg; P=0.014), whereas moderate to severe paravalvular leak did not differ significantly. Prosthetic ellipticity was greater in bicuspid anatomy, but expansion ratios, including those within the functional valve portion, did not differ significantly. Implantation depth, asymmetric leaflet expansion, and hypoattenuated leaflet thickening incidence also did not differ significantly.

CONCLUSIONS: Following Venus-A implantation, bicuspid anatomy was associated with greater prosthetic ellipticity and higher residual gradients, despite no significant difference in prosthetic expansion.

Predischarge echocardiographic assessments included the mean transvalvular gradient and paravalvular leak.

articles.title: Multidisciplinary Collaboration in the Performance of Aortic Surgery: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
articles.abstract: Intraoperative management of a patient undergoing cardiac surgery requires continuous and independent interventions by multiple healthcare professionals, including surgeons, anesthesiologists, and perfusionists, among others. Although each clinician performs tasks based on their training and accepted techniques, guidelines, and protocols, an action by one member of the team can have immediate consequences for other team members. Aortic surgery adds a level of complexity, with the need for interventions such as single-lung ventilation, systemic cooling (and subsequent rewarming), and myocardial, cerebral, and visceral protection. Much has been made of the utility of the multidisciplinary team. This scientific statement is intended to approach the patient undergoing aortic surgery from 3 different viewpoints: that of the surgeon, the anesthesiologist, and the perfusionist. This scientific statement is not intended to provide an exhaustive summary of approaches to aortic surgery but rather to illustrate the specific concerns that each member of the team may have.

articles.title: Anterior mitral leaflet modification to prevent left ventricular outflow tract obstruction during transcatheter mitral valve replacement: the PROTECT-LVOT registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction remains the major limitation of transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR). Anterior mitral leaflet (AML) modification has emerged as a key preventive strategy, yet real-world data remain limited and residual risk is still unknown.

AIMS: We sought to evaluate the outcomes of TMVR with concomitant AML modification across valve-in-mitral annular calcification (ViMAC), valve-in-ring (ViR), and valve-in-valve (ViV) substrates.

METHODS: We established a multicentre retrospective registry of consecutive patients undergoing TMVR with AML modification between 2017 and 2025. The co-primary in-hospital safety endpoint was a composite of cardiovascular death, stroke/transient ischaemic attack, and major bleeding.

RESULTS: A total of 55 patients were included (67% females). The median age was 78 years (interquartile range [IQR] 73-81); the median Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality was 6.7% (IQR 4.8-9.5). AML modification was performed in 65.5% of cases with the Laceration of the Anterior Mitral leaflet to Prevent Outflow ObstructioN technique and in 34.5% with the Balloon-Assisted Translocation of the Mitral Anterior Leaflet technique. AML modification was successful in 96.4% of cases. Despite successful AML modification, haemodynamically significant LVOT obstruction occurred in 12.7% of cases. The co-primary in-hospital safety endpoint occurred in 20.0% of patients, driven by cardiovascular death in 14.5% of patients. Overall in-hospital mortality was 16.4%. The ViMAC substrate was associated with the numerically highest LVOT obstruction rate (ViMAC 20.7%, ViR 0.0%, ViV 8.3%, odds ratio [OR] 4.72, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.89-47.86; p=0.070). The aortomitral angle showed a borderline association with LVOT obstruction (OR 1.22 per degree, 95% CI: 0.99-1.48; p=0.059).

CONCLUSIONS: AML modification enables TMVR in high-risk anatomies with high feasibility but does not eliminate LVOT obstruction. ViMAC represents the most challenging substrate.

Anterior mitral leaflet (AML) modification has emerged as a key preventive strategy, yet real-world data remain limited and residual risk is still unknown. AIMS: We sought to evaluate the outcomes of TMVR with concomitant AML modification across valve-in-mitral annular calcification (ViMAC), valve-in-ring (ViR), and valve-in-valve (ViV) substrates.

articles.title: Bioprosthetic valve performance of transcatheter aortic valves.
articles.abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation is used increasingly in younger patients with longer life expectancy, necessitating long-term effectiveness. Randomised clinical trials have demonstrated comparable or superior haemodynamic performance of transcatheter heart valves (THVs) to surgical aortic valve replacement over midterm follow-up. Within a lifetime management framework, haemodynamic performance and durability of THVs are central considerations in patients undergoing aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis. This review provides an overview of THV design and function along with contemporary clinical evidence, with a focus on current haemodynamic assessment considerations, challenges in cross-platform interpretation of valve performance, and limitations of randomised comparative evidence, as well as future directions in the evaluation of THV performance.

articles.title: Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative Contemporary Benchmarks: Thoracic Endovascular Aortic Repair.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To describe contemporary outcomes as well as temporal trends of in-hospital mortality and complication rates for patients undergoing thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) across indications and levels of urgency, establishing a benchmark for future analytic efforts.

METHODS: The VQI TEVAR and complex EVAR registry was queried for procedures performed between January 2014-December 2024. Primary outcomes included in-hospital mortality and major complications. Analyses were stratified by indication to include descending thoracic aortic aneurysms (DTAA), dissections, and trauma. Aneurysms involving the aortic arch (i.e. landing zone < 2) or extending to the visceral segment and distally (i.e. landing zone >5) were excluded. Linear regression and the Cochran Armitage test for trend were used to analyze yearly mortality and complication rates over time. Mortality and complication end-points were further analyzed using logistic regression with and without risk-adjustment.

RESULTS: Over the ten-year study period, 4,632 TEVARs were performed for DTAA, 6,701 for dissection, and 2,321 for trauma. For patients undergoing TEVAR for DTAA, in-hospital mortality declined significantly for both elective (2014, 3.9% versus 2024, 1.0%, -0.26 percentage points per year, p=0.01) and nonelective cases (2014, 16.7% versus 2024, 8.7%, -0.63 percentage points per year, p=0.04). There was also a decline in in-hospital mortality among elective dissection patients (2014, 3.7% versus 2024, 0.5%, -0.17 percentage points per year, p=0.03). Elective TEVAR overall is associated with a mortality rate of less than two percent per year. The in-hospital complication trends declined significantly for patients undergoing TEVAR for DTAA - elective patients experienced a decline in complication rates by -1.13 percentage points per year (2014, 24.8% versus 2024, 11.5% p<0.001) and non-elective patients experienced a decline in complication rates by -2.0 percentage points per year (2014, 40.5% versus 2024, 25.2%, p<0.001). Dissection patients undergoing elective repair had a decrease of -0.8 percentage points per year (2014, 16.9% versus 2024, 9.2%, p<0.001). Nonelective dissections repairs had a complication rate of 36.4% in 2014 vs 34.1% in 2024, p=0.874). Trauma patients tended toward higher complication rates over time, with a rate of 21.6% in 2014 and 32.2% in 2024, p=0.06) Trauma patients experienced an overall increase in in-hospital mortality of +0.38 percentage points per year (2014, 9.8% versus 2024, 9.4%, p=0.01).

CONCLUSION: Temporal trends within the VQI demonstrate improvements in mortality and complication rates for patients undergoing TEVAR for DTAA and elective dissection repair, with contemporary yearly mortality rates of less than two percent. Patients undergoing non-elective dissection repair and those with traumatic indications represent challenging and complex pathologies requiring further research to identify opportunities to improve outcomes.

articles.title: Final 5-year results of the Thoracic Branch Endoprosthesis Feasibility Trials for Treatment of Aortic Arch Aneurysms.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To report final 5-year outcomes from prospective multicenter feasibility studies of the GORE® TAG® Thoracic Branch Endoprosthesis (TBE) for aneurysms involving the proximal descending thoracic aorta and aortic arch (zones 0-2).

METHODS: Forty consecutive patients (23 male; mean age, 74±10 years) were enrolled at six sites in prospective, nonrandomized feasibility trials (2014-2016). Patients underwent TEVAR with proximal TBE in zone 0/1 (n=9; NCT02264977) or zone 2 (n=31; NCT02021812). A clinical events committee adjudicated aneurysm-related and all-cause mortality, major adverse events, and cerebrovascular events. Core laboratory analysis assessed endoleaks (types I-IV), aneurysm sac enlargement, device migration, and side branch patency. Five-year cumulative risk rates (2006 days) were estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis.

RESULTS: The median follow-up time among survivors was 60.2 months (range, 25.8 to 66.0), with 17 patients completing the required 5-year clinical and imaging follow-up across both studies. Eleven late deaths occurred; KM-estimated cumulative risk of 5-year all-cause mortality was 29% (95% CI: 17%-46%). One zone 2 death was adjudicated as aortic-related (2.5%; 95% CI: 0.4%-16%) due to ascending aortic rupture, with no ruptures occurring within treated aortic segments. Reintervention risk through 5 years was low (KM-estimated cumulative risk, 5.1%; 95% CI: 1.3%-19%), with two events, both in the zone 2 cohort. Five patients experienced stroke events through 5 years, corresponding to a KM cumulative risk of 19.0% ( 95% CI: 7.2%-43%), two in zone 2 and three in zone 0/1. Two patients had target vessel instability (5.0%, 95% CI: 0.6%-16.9%). Two side-branch patency events occurred in zone 2: one complete side-branch occlusion in the LSA associated with transient mild arm claudication and one asymptomatic partial occlusion, primary patency through 5-year follow-up was 94.8% (37/39 evaluable patients). Core laboratory identified endoleaks in 12 patients (30.8%; 95% CI: 15%-45%). Three patients (7.7%) had a type I or III endoleak by 5 years, all in the zone 2 arm; these included type IA in one patient (2.6%) and type III in two patients (5.1%). Additionally indeterminate (n=8, 20.5%) and type II (n=6, 15.4%) endoleaks were observed. Cumulative risk rate of aneurysm sac enlargement through 5-years was 15.0% for all patients (95% CI: 5.6%-30.3%), with events occurring in three zone 2 patients and one zone 0/1 patient.

CONCLUSIONS: At 5 years, the early feasibility studies demonstrated excellent side branch patency, a low incidence of type IA endoleak, low aortic-related mortality, and no rupture within the treated aortic segments. Larger studies are needed to better define zone-specific cerebrovascular risk and long-term durability.

articles.title: Peripheral Artery Disease in Acute Care Settings: Diagnosis and Management of Common Presentations and Emergencies: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
articles.abstract: People with peripheral artery disease (PAD) are often misdiagnosed or diagnosed late and, even after diagnosis, are undertreated with both pharmacologic and invasive therapies. The disease is associated with an increased risk of mortality, myocardial infarction, stroke, other vascular disease, limb loss, and reduced quality of life. Although the risks and long-term management of PAD are well documented, these risks are acutely magnified when PAD exists as a comorbidity in patients hospitalized for other cardiovascular or medical conditions. Procedures requiring vascular access for the treatment of acute myocardial infarction, cardiogenic shock, or valvular heart disease, as well as procedures for the treatment of the patient's underlying PAD, require special consideration in patients with PAD. Familiarity with the use and placement of mechanical circulatory support in patients with PAD, as well as the management of recent endovascular or surgical vascular interventions, is essential for providing appropriate care in the acute care setting.

articles.title: Impact of True and False Lumen Origins on Target Vessel Instability in Post-Dissection F/BEVAR.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the occurrence of target artery-related adverse events in post-dissection F/BEVAR patients, based upon artery origin from the true or false lumen.

METHODS: This is a multicenter, prospective, cohort study evaluating post-dissection patients treated with F/BEVAR, in the US Aortic Research Consortium. The primary endpoint was 5-year target vessel instability (TVI). Secondary endpoints included 5-year primary patency, freedom from secondary interventions (SIs), and type Ic and IIIc endoleaks. The analysis was performed on a per-vessel basis.

RESULTS: A total of 1052 target arteries were analyzed, primarily including the celiac, superior mesenteric, and renal arteries, with individual hepatic and splenic arteries occasionally incorporated in the repair. Of the 277 patients included, 75% were men, and 19% were black, with a mean age of 66.8 ± 10.3 years. The mean aneurysm sac diameter was 66.0 ± 11.4 mm, with extent II thoracoabdominal aneurysms being the most prevalent (72.6%) among this cohort. Technical success was obtained in 96% of the cases. As primary outcome, the incidence of target vessel instability (TVI) was significantly lower (P<0.001) among the true-lumen vessels (16.4%) compared to false-lumen (29.9%) and dual-lumen arteries (43.8%). As for the secondary outcomes, the incidence of type Ic endoleak was significantly higher (P=0.001) in false-lumen vessels (9.6%) and dual-lumen vessels (8.6%) compared to true-lumen vessels (3.3%). There was no significant difference in the incidence of type IIIc endoleak (p=0.241) or target vessel occlusion (P=0.458). Target artery stenosis was significantly more common among arteries originating from the false lumen compared to true lumen (2.6% vs 0.4%, P=0.009). Fenestrations were associated with a higher incidence (30.5%) of TVI when compared to branches (5.9% P=0.005), however, this was observed only among dual-lumen vessels. Arteries incorporated by a fenestration and that had a dual-lumen origin, were associated with a higher occurrence of secondary interventions (23.7%) compared to true-lumen vessels (8.6%, P=0.010). The same was not observed among the arteries incorporated by a branch configuration. The time-to-event analysis demonstrated a significantly higher 5-year freedom from TVI in true-lumen vessels compared to false and dual-lumen ones (True lumen: 83.6%; False=70.1 %; Dual=56.2 %; Log-rank P=0.0002). Freedom from secondary interventions at 5 years was significantly higher in true-lumen vessels compared to dual-lumen ones (Log-rank P=0.0104), but not to false-lumen arteries (Log-rank P=0.0847). The 5-year primary patency did not differ significantly among groups (True lumen: 98.3%; False = 92.6%; Dual=93.9%; Log-rank P=0.1368). On Cox proportional hazards analysis, dual-lumen (95% CI 1.24-3.28, p=0.005) and false-lumen (95% CI 1.04 - 2.60, p=0.0325) target arteries were associated with an increased hazard of TVI, when compared to true lumen arteries, having 2.02 (P=0.005) and 1.65 (P=0.0325) times more risk of presenting TVI than a true-lumen vessel CONCLUSIONS: In F/BEVAR for post-dissection aneurysms, target vessel instability and secondary intervention are significantly lower in target arteries originating from the true lumen, when compared to false-lumen or dual-lumen vessels. Device design, with use of fenestrations or branches may also play a role, with a significant difference only observed in dual-lumen target arteries.
articles.englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the occurrence of target artery-related adverse events in post-dissection F/BEVAR patients, based upon artery origin from the true or false lumen. METHODS: This is a multicenter, prospective, cohort study evaluating post-dissection patients treated with F/BEVAR, in the US Aortic Research Consortium. The primary endpoint was 5-year target vessel instability (TVI).

articles.title: Fenestrated Endografts Provide Superior Outcomes Compared to Branched Devices in Juxtarenal Aortic Repair.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Urgent endovascular juxtarenal aortic repair with custom-made fenestrated devices is not feasible due to its long elaboration time. Off-the-shelf branched devices can be used, however, durability of the target vessels, especially renal artery branches, is of concern. Our objective is to compare mid and long-term patency of target vessels (TV), especially renal arteries (RA) in juxtarenal fenestrated or branched aortic endovascular repair.

METHODS: Single-center retrospective study identifying all patients undergoing fenestrated or branched endovascular repair (f/bEVAR) for juxtarenal aortic aneurysms (JAA) between 2011-2022. A FEVAR group with use of fenestrations to incorporate target vessels (TV) and a BEVAR group, with use of branches were created. Clinical and anatomical characteristics as well as perioperative technical success and complications were compared. The primary endpoint was the assessment of RA primary patency, freedom from endoleaks and instability (endpoint including occlusion, endoleak or need for reintervention) at follow-up. Secondary endpoints were the assessment of CT-SMA patency rates, freedom from endoleak and instability at follow-up and the evaluation of the anatomical and clinical factors associated with renal artery bridging covered stent (BCS) occlusion.

RESULTS: From 2011-2022, FEVAR was performed in 212 patients and BEVAR in 57. There were no statistical differences in demographics. The BEVAR group presented more frequently as urgencies (61% vs 11% for FEVAR p <,001). 955 TV were incorporated, including 536 RA. Technical success was 99%. BEVAR patients experienced higher perioperative death rates (14% vs 3% in FEVAR; p 0,005) and major complications (53% vs 17% in FEVAR; p <,001). Primary patency of RA in FEVAR was 99% at 3 years vs 74% for BEVAR (p < ,001). Freedom from RA BCS endoleaks were 97% at 3 years for the FEVAR group vs 87% in the BEVAR group (p <,001). Freedom from RA instability at 3 years was 95% in the FEVAR group vs 63% for the BEVAR group (p <,001). For CT-SMA only freedom from instability showed significant better outcomes at 3 years in the FEVAR group (96% vs 88% for BEVAR ; p ,006). In the multivariate analysis, the use of branches was the only factor associated with loss of patency in the RA.

CONCLUSIONS: In complex aortic repair for JAA, fenestrated devices achieved high patency rates while branched devices, mostly done for urgencies, are associated with significantly worse RA outcomes.
articles.englishSummary: INTRODUCTION: Urgent endovascular juxtarenal aortic repair with custom-made fenestrated devices is not feasible due to its long elaboration time. Off-the-shelf branched devices can be used, however, durability of the target vessels, especially renal artery branches, is of concern. Our objective is to compare mid and long-term patency of target vessels (TV), especially renal arteries (RA) in juxtarenal fenestrated or branched aortic endovascular repair.

articles.title: Single vs. Dual Antiplatelet Therapy after Fenestrated and Branched Endovascular Aortic Repair: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare single vs. dual antiplatelet therapy after fenestrated or branched endovascular aortic repair (FBEVAR).

DATA SOURCES: PubMed, MEDLINE, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and ProQuest Dissertations & Theses Global were searched from inception to 12 July 2026, with a supplementary targeted PubMed search on 5 September 2026.

REVIEW METHODS: Comparative studies of post-operative antiplatelet therapy were included. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and certainty of evidence using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation approach. Outcomes were synthesised narratively when clinical and methodological differences precluded meaningful pooling; an additional quantitative summary of study defined bleeding outcomes was also reported.

RESULTS: Six retrospective cohorts comprising 3 623 patients were included, with 3 197 patients in separately extractable single or dual antiplatelet therapy groups. Several studies reported associations favouring dual antiplatelet therapy for target vessel patency. However, differences in outcome definitions, analytical units, and treatment classification precluded a common pooled estimate, and one association was attenuated after accounting for treatment changes. Evidence regarding ischaemic events, mortality, re-intervention, and endoleak was insufficient for reliable pooled comparisons. Five cohorts reported peri-operative bleeding using heterogeneous definitions and observation periods, of which a four study summary yielded an odds ratio of 1.30 (95% confidence interval 0.87 - 1.94) for dual vs. single antiplatelet therapy. Given the differences in outcome definitions, this does not estimate a common clinical effect.

CONCLUSION: The current evidence comparing single and dual antiplatelet therapy after FBEVAR is based on heterogeneous cohort studies, focuses largely on surrogate outcomes such as target vessel patency, and shows no clear benefit for dual antiplatelet therapy. Comparative bleeding risk as well as clinical outcomes of single vs. dual antiplatelet therapy after FBEVAR remain uncertain. Future prospective studies are needed to better delineate superiority of one regimen over the other.
articles.englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to compare single vs. dual antiplatelet therapy after fenestrated or branched endovascular aortic repair (FBEVAR). DATA SOURCES: PubMed, MEDLINE, Web of Science Core Collection, Scopus, and ProQuest Dissertations & Theses Global were searched from inception to 12 July 2026, with a supplementary targeted PubMed search on 5 September 2026.

articles.title: Prevention of Venous Thromboembolism after Total Hip or Knee Replacement.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Studies comparing aspirin with anticoagulants for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty have had conflicting results.

METHODS: In a comparative-effectiveness noninferiority trial, we randomly assigned patients undergoing elective hip or knee arthroplasty to receive aspirin (81 mg twice daily), warfarin (to a target international normalized ratio of 2.0), or rivaroxaban (10 mg daily) for 30 days. The composite primary effectiveness outcome (death from any cause or symptomatic VTE) and primary safety outcome (bleeding, reoperation for wound problems, or myocardial infarction) were evaluated through 6 months in a blinded fashion. The noninferiority margin for the risk difference was 0.69 percentage points.

RESULTS: Among 18,883 participants who had undergone randomization, 15,317 (7214 with hip arthroplasty and 8103 with knee arthroplasty) were included in the primary per-protocol analysis. A primary effectiveness outcome event occurred in 77 of 6090 participants (1.26%) in the aspirin group, in 52 of 4231 (1.23%) in the warfarin group, and in 47 of 4996 (0.94%) in the rivaroxaban group; a primary safety outcome event occurred in 177 (2.91%), 142 (3.36%), and 174 (3.48%), respectively. In pairwise comparisons, 6-month risks of a primary effectiveness outcome event were 1.24% and 0.94% for aspirin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.30 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.20 to 0.81); 1.24% and 1.01% for aspirin versus warfarin (difference, 0.23 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.34 to 0.81); and 1.13% and 1.10% for warfarin versus rivaroxaban (difference, 0.03 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.57 to 0.63). Risks of a primary safety outcome event were 3.70% and 3.02% for rivaroxaban versus aspirin (difference, 0.68 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.41); 3.65% and 2.88% for warfarin versus aspirin (difference, 0.77 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.04 to 1.58); and 3.59% and 3.61% for rivaroxaban versus warfarin (difference, -0.02 percentage points; 95% CI, -0.89 to 0.85). Intention-to-treat analyses yielded similar results.

CONCLUSIONS: Aspirin prophylaxis after total hip or knee arthroplasty was not noninferior to rivaroxaban or warfarin with respect to death or symptomatic VTE. Warfarin and rivaroxaban were not noninferior to aspirin for safety. (Funded by the Patient-Centered Outcomes Research Institute; PEPPER ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT02810704.).

articles.title: Rivaroxaban Then Aspirin vs. Aspirin Alone after Total Hip or Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aspirin after an initial short course of rivaroxaban has been shown to be safe and effective for the prevention of venous thromboembolism after total hip or total knee arthroplasty, but uncertainty remains about the use of aspirin alone.

METHODS: In this multicenter, double-blind, randomized, controlled trial, we assigned patients to receive once-daily thromboprophylaxis with either 81 mg of aspirin or 10 mg of oral rivaroxaban for the first 5 days after total hip or total knee arthroplasty. All the patients then received further thromboprophylaxis with 81 mg of aspirin daily for 9 additional days after knee arthroplasty and for 30 additional days after hip arthroplasty. Patients were followed for 90 days for symptomatic venous thromboembolism, which consisted of either proximal deep-vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism (primary effectiveness outcome), and for bleeding complications (primary safety outcome). The noninferiority margin for aspirin alone as compared with rivaroxaban-aspirin was 0.7 percentage points.

RESULTS: A total of 5429 patients underwent randomization. Venous thromboembolism developed in 13 of 2718 patients (0.48%) in the aspirin-alone group and in 12 of 2647 patients (0.45%) in the rivaroxaban-aspirin group (risk difference, 0.02 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -0.34 to 0.39; P<0.001 for noninferiority). Major bleeding or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding events occurred in 45 of 2718 patients (1.66%) in the aspirin-alone group and in 54 of 2647 patients (2.04%) in the rivaroxaban-aspirin group (risk difference, -0.38%; 95% CI, -1.11 to 0.34).

CONCLUSIONS: After total hip and total knee arthroplasty, the use of aspirin alone was not inferior to a strategy of using rivaroxaban followed by aspirin for the prevention of symptomatic venous thromboembolism, with no clinically relevant difference in bleeding events. (Funded by the Canadian Institutes of Health Research; EPCAT III ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04075240.).

articles.title: Elevated Lipoprotein(a) Is Associated With Heart Failure in Patients With Peripheral Artery Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The prognostic value of lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] in peripheral artery disease (PAD) remains uncertain.

METHODS AND RESULTS: We retrospectively studied 138 patients with intermittent claudication undergoing endovascular therapy. Patients were classified by Lp(a) level (≥30 vs. <30 mg/dL). The primary endpoint was major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Elevated Lp(a) was associated with a higher incidence of MACE (31.1% vs. 9.6%; P=0.002), predominantly driven by heart failure. It independently predicted MACE (HR 4.23) and heart failure (HR 5.12), but not cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction or stroke.

CONCLUSIONS: Elevated Lp(a) was associated with heart failure-driven MACE after endovascular therapy in patients with PAD.

articles.title: Training Structure and Satisfaction with Learning in European Vascular Surgery Training: Results from the European Vascular Surgery Training (EVaST) Surveys.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study describes the availability of modifiable structural training elements across European vascular surgery programmes to identify which of these elements are independently associated with trainees' satisfaction with learning and to contextualise them with trainer reported delivery constraints.

METHODS: The study comprised two parallel cross-sectional web based European Vascular Surgery Training (EVaST) surveys of trainees and trainers. The main outcome variable was satisfaction with learning (10 point Likert scale). Five modifiable structural elements were identified a priori: structured curriculum; training coordinator; dedicated or protected training time; assigned mentor; and simulation access. Associations were examined using an adjusted linear mixed effects model (LMM), with secondary models for coordinator resourcing and mentorship evaluations. Trainer data were analysed descriptively.

RESULTS: Of 420 trainee responses (32 countries), 273 entered the complete case main LMM. Availability was inconsistent: structured curriculum 56.4%; dedicated or protected training time 34.3%; and simulation access 32.3%. In the adjusted LMM, learning satisfaction was higher with a structured curriculum (= 0.79, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.21 - 1.38; p = .008) and dedicated training time (= 0.62, 95% CI 0.05 - 1.19; p = .035). In secondary models, coordinators with dedicated educational time showed the largest association (= 1.76, 95% CI 1.05 - 2.46; p < .001), and mentorship with regular evaluations was associated with higher satisfaction (= 0.98, 95% CI 0.36 - 1.59; p = .002). Among 659 trainers (37 countries), mentorship importance was rated 8.26 out of 10, yet only 43.4% had dedicated mentorship time; the dominant barrier was clinical workload (84.1%). Desired improvements were dedicated mentorship time (64.4%), formalised programmes (54.3%), and regular feedback sessions (51.6%).

CONCLUSION: A structured curriculum and dedicated training time were independently associated with higher trainee learning satisfaction across European vascular surgery programmes. Organisational roles such as training coordinators and mentors were associated with higher satisfaction in exploratory secondary analyses, suggesting these roles may be most beneficial when actively resourced with dedicated time and regular evaluations. Trainer constraints converged on protected time for training and mentorship.

METHODS: The study comprised two parallel cross-sectional web based European Vascular Surgery Training (EVaST) surveys of trainees and trainers. The main outcome variable was satisfaction with learning (10 point Likert scale).

articles.title: The IMA-PLUS Score for Predicting Type 2 Endoleak After Endovascular Repair: Development and External Validation in European and Japanese Cohorts.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Prophylactic embolisation of infrarenal branch vessels has been investigated to prevent type 2 endoleak (EL2) following endovascular repair (EVAR) of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA), but patient selection is poorly defined. In this study, a computed tomography angiography (CTA) based risk score was developed and validated to predict EL2 after EVAR.

METHODS: This multicentre, retrospective diagnostic study used prospectively collected data from the Zenith alpha for aneurysm Repair Registry (ZEPHYR) as the development cohort. Eligible patients underwent standard EVAR with pre-operative arterial phase CTA and at least one post-operative delayed phase CTA. The model was converted into a numerical score ("IMA-PLUS Score") and validated in two retrospective cohorts. Discrimination, calibration, and risk group thresholds were assessed. In validation cohorts, freedom from AAA expansion and EL2 associated reinterventions up to 5 years were analysed.

RESULTS: Data from 245 patients of the ZEPHYR registry were included. EL2 occurred in 96 patients (39.2%). The IMA-PLUS Score includes inferior mesenteric artery diameter, number of infrarenal renal pole arteries, number of patent lumbar arteries, and median sacral artery patency, achieving a crossvalidated area under the curve (AUC) of 0.78. Using prespecified thresholds (low < 128, medium 128 - 200, high > 200), observed EL2 incidences in ZEPHYR were 19%, 59%, and 74%. In the Heidelberg cohort (n = 134; EL2 44%), AUC was 0.77 (95% confidence intervals [CI] 0.69 - 0.85) with EL2 incidences of 24%, 60%, and 89% across risk groups with good calibration; interobserver agreement for total score was high (intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.95). In the Tokyo cohort (n = 123; EL2 52.8%) AUC was 0.75 (95% CI 0.67 - 0.84); EL2 incidences were 36%, 76%, and 80%, with higher observed incidence than predicted. In validation cohorts, the IMA-PLUS Score was associated with AAA expansion and reduced freedom from EL2 associated reinterventions.

CONCLUSION: The IMA-PLUS Score may support selection of patients for future studies on preventive management strategies.

In this study, a computed tomography angiography (CTA) based risk score was developed and validated to predict EL2 after EVAR. METHODS: This multicentre, retrospective diagnostic study used prospectively collected data from the Zenith alpha for aneurysm Repair Registry (ZEPHYR) as the development cohort.

articles.title: Fenestrated-Branched Endovascular versus Open Surgical Repair for Elective Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysms: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study compared outcomes between patients undergoing elective open surgical repair (OSR) and fenestrated branched endovascular aortic repair (FBEVAR) for thoraco-abdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAAs) through a systematic review and meta-analysis.

DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane.

REVIEW METHODS: A total of 5 980 articles were screened following the PRISMA protocol. Primary endpoints were thirty day or in hospital major adverse events (MAEs) and mortality, and late all cause mortality. Secondary endpoints were thirty day or in hospital permanent paraplegia, stroke, bowel ischaemia, and new onset dialysis, as well as late re-interventions. A DerSimonian-Laird random effects model was employed to calculate risk ratios (RRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for binary endpoints. Significance was defined as a p value of . Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I and evidence certainty with GRADE.

RESULTS: A total of 1 567 patients from five retrospective observational comparative studies were included. FBEVAR was used to treat TAAA in 824 patients (52.6%). Thirty day MAEs (RR 0.51, 95% CI 0.34 - 0.78; p = .002; I2 = 77.0%), mortality (RR 0.60, 95% CI 0.37 - 0.97; p = .040; I2 = 29.0%), and dialysis (RR 0.18, 95% CI 0.06 - 0.54; p = .002; I2 = 80.0%) were significantly less frequent among patients undergoing FBEVAR. Conversely, late aortic related re-interventions were significantly more common in the elective FBEVAR cohort (RR 1.80, 95% CI 1.04 - 3.13; p = .040; I2 = 18.0%). No statistically significant differences were observed between groups in thirty day or in hospital permanent paraplegia (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.51 - 1.91; p = .96; I2 = 39.0%), bowel ischaemia (RR 0.46, 95% CI 0.09 - 2.33; p = .35; I2 = 81.0%), and stroke (RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.37 - 2.06; p = .76; I2 = 0.0%), or late mortality (RR 1.29, 95% CI 0.87 - 1.92; p = .20; I2 = 57.0%). According to GRADE, certainty of evidence was low to very low across outcomes.

CONCLUSION: Elective FBEVAR was associated with a significantly lower incidence of thirty day MAEs, mortality, and acute kidney injury requiring dialysis compared with OSR. In contrast, elective OSR was associated with a significantly lower incidence of late aortic related re-interventions, whereas overall re-intervention rates were similar between groups.
articles.englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: This study compared outcomes between patients undergoing elective open surgical repair (OSR) and fenestrated branched endovascular aortic repair (FBEVAR) for thoraco-abdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAAs) through a systematic review and meta-analysis. DATA SOURCES: PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane. REVIEW METHODS: A total of 5 980 articles were screened following the PRISMA protocol.

articles.title: Feasibility of robotic-assisted surgery for nutcracker syndrome: a systematic review and single-arm meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Nutcracker syndrome (NCS) results from compression of the left renal vein, and refractory symptoms require surgical reconstruction. Robotic platforms provide magnified three-dimensional vision and articulated instruments that are theoretically advantageous for vascular dissection and anastomosis within the confined retroperitoneal space. However, the available evidence consists almost entirely of small single-arm case series, and whether robotic-assisted surgery represents a feasible treatment option for NCS has not been established quantitatively; previous systematic reviews were descriptive only, without quantitative pooling of proportional outcomes or stratification by reconstructive technique and age. To evaluate the feasibility of robotic-assisted surgery for NCS in terms of technical completion, conversion to open surgery, perioperative safety, postoperative recovery and symptom relief, and to explore whether heterogeneity was explained by reconstructive technique, age or sample size. Four electronic databases-PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, CENTRAL (Cochrane Library) and the Web of Science Core Collection-were searched from inception to 1 October 2026, and the reference lists of the retrieved articles and of earlier reviews on this topic were screened by hand. Eligible reports were original studies of robot-assisted NCS surgery from which quantitative data could be obtained, provided the series comprised at least three patients; studies of non-robotic procedures, non-NCS cohorts, asymptomatic nutcracker phenomenon, stent implantation by the endovascular route alone, narrative reviews, conference proceedings, single-patient reports and duplicate cohorts were not considered. Screening and data collection were carried out independently by two investigators, and study quality was appraised with the JBI checklist designed for case series. Stata 17.0 was used for the single-arm proportional meta-analyses: individual proportions underwent Freeman-Tukey double arcsine transformation before being combined under a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model, with the summary estimates then expressed on the original scale, while continuous variables were harmonised to mean ± SD following Wan et al. and Shi et al. Cochran's Q test and the I-squared statistic were used to quantify heterogeneity. Subgroup comparisons were restricted to outcomes with substantial heterogeneity and were interpreted as exploratory analyses of study-level variation rather than as tests of independent effects. Ten studies comprising 140 patients were included (China, 4; USA, 4; France, 2; 9 retrospective and 1 prospective). Reconstructive techniques were left renal vein (LRV) transposition (5 studies, 45 patients), extravascular renal vein stent placement (3 studies, 29 patients) and renal autotransplantation (2 studies, 66 patients). Completion and conversion status could be ascertained in 111 patients from eight studies: 110 (99.1%) completed the planned reconstruction robotically and 1 (0.9%) was converted to open surgery; status was not reported for 29 patients in two studies and these patients were not counted as zero events. The pooled symptom improvement rate was 96% (95% CI 85%-100%; I-squared = 46.66%; 6 studies, 87 patients) and the complete symptom resolution rate 69% (95% CI 34%-96%; I-squared = 77.83%; 4 studies, 35 patients). The pooled incidence of Clavien-Dindo < 3 complications was 17% (95% CI 5%-33%; I-squared = 60.86%) and that of Clavien-Dindo >= 3 complications was 5.5% (95% CI 2.3%-9.8%; I-squared = 0%; 8 studies, 6 events); lymphorrhea/chylous ascites occurred in 15% (95% CI 0%-43%; I-squared = 79.16%) and postoperative reintervention in 3% (95% CI 0%-10%; I-squared = 0%). Pooled operating time was 204.52 min (95% CI 157.47-251.57 min; I-squared = 99.1%), estimated blood loss 54.21 mL (95% CI 37.56-70.86 mL; I-squared = 96.2%) and postoperative length of stay 2.72 days (95% CI 1.60-3.85 days; I-squared = 96.2%). Exploratory technique-stratified analyses suggested lower estimated blood loss, shorter operating time and shorter length of stay after extravascular stent placement than after LRV transposition or renal autotransplantation; however, several strata contained only one or two studies and these differences are descriptive rather than evidence of comparative superiority. Robotic-assisted surgery for NCS was associated with a high rate of technical completion among patients with ascertainable status, favourable symptom improvement and a low frequency of major complications. The apparent ordering of perioperative burden across techniques is consistent with differences in procedural invasiveness but may also reflect confounding by indication, centre effects and case selection. Owing to the single-arm design, short and inconsistent follow-up, absent patency data and very low certainty, these findings should be regarded as a pooled feasibility benchmark rather than as evidence of comparative effectiveness.

articles.title: Acute aortic syndrome rule-out criteria: development and external validation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Acute aortic syndrome (AAS) is a rare but catastrophic event, presenting with non-specific symptoms that mimic common conditions, and carries a mortality approaching 80% when missed. Current clinical tools, including the Aortic Dissection Detection Risk Score (ADD-RS) and its refinement, the simplified AORTA score, achieve high sensitivity when combined with D-dimer but fail to identify a population at sufficiently low risk to safely avoid further testing. To address this gap, the Acute Aortic Syndrome Rule-Out Criteria (ARC) were developed and validated, a pragmatic bedside tool designed to safely exclude AAS in low-risk patients without additional testing.

METHODS: A retrospective multistep derivation and validation study was conducted. The derivation cohort included patients with confirmed AAS from the International Registry of Acute Aortic Dissection (IRAD). Starting from existing scores, candidate predictors were identified from the IRAD dataset and sequentially added to achieve sensitivity ≥ 99%. External validation was performed in patients with suspected AAS across three prospective multicentre cohorts (ADvISED, PROFUNDUS, and DAShED). Diagnostic accuracy was assessed using sensitivity and specificity with 95% confidence intervals (CIs).

RESULTS: The final seven-variable ARC included age >60 years, abrupt onset pain, severe pain, hypotension/shock, neurological deficit, pulse deficit, and known aortic disease. Patients were classified as positive if any ARC variable was present and negative only if all variables were absent. In the derivation cohort, ARC achieved a sensitivity of 99.2% (95% CI 99.1-99.3). In the ADvISED/PROFUNDUS cohort (4598 patients, 10.2% AAS prevalence), sensitivity was 100% (95% CI 99.2-100) with specificity 23.7% (95% CI 22.4-25.0). In the DAShED cohort (5346 patients, 0.3% prevalence), sensitivity was 100% (95% CI 76.8-100) and specificity 36.4% (95% CI 35.1-37.7), ruling out 36.3% of patients without missing any AAS cases.

CONCLUSIONS: ARC is an externally validated, pragmatic clinical rule demonstrating high diagnostic sensitivity in a large external validation cohort. When incorporated into existing diagnostic pathways, ARC has the potential to reduce unnecessary testing while maintaining diagnostic performance. Further prospective validation is required to confirm its clinical utility.

Current clinical tools, including the Aortic Dissection Detection Risk Score (ADD-RS) and its refinement, the simplified AORTA score, achieve high sensitivity when combined with D-dimer but fail to identify a population at sufficiently low risk to safely avoid further testing. To address this gap, the Acute Aortic Syndrome Rule-Out Criteria (ARC) were developed and validated, a pragmatic bedside tool designed to safely exclude AAS in low-risk patients without additional testing.

articles.title: Epigenome-Wide Association Study of Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Identifies Central Role for Inflammatory Pathways.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Epigenetic mechanisms underlying susceptibility to abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) remain poorly understood. Identifying causal DNA methylation markers for AAA can elucidate the regulatory processes that drive aneurysm formation and accelerate translational applications. We leveraged the Veterans Affairs (VA) Million Veteran Program to identify methylation biomarkers and delineate underlying pathways.

METHODS: We first conducted an epigenome-wide association study of incident AAA (1324 cases and 42 065 noncases), performed stratified analyses by population group and smoking status, and conducted Mendelian randomization to facilitate causal inference of the cytosine-phosphate-guanine (CpG)-AAA association. Chromatin state, island context, and transcription factor binding were implicated through functional annotation of identified CpGs. To identify genes impacted by change in methylation state, we aligned associations with transcriptional data obtained in blood, aorta, and liver. We performed expression quantitative trait methylation to capture CpG-gene-expression links across the genome. Network Mendelian randomization was used to test cardiometabolic and inflammatory mediation. Finally, we developed a methylation risk score for AAA using penalized regression and evaluated its performance against a clinical model in the Million Veteran Program and 2 external studies.

RESULTS: Epigenome-wide association study identified 1253 CpGs associated with incident AAA, and Mendelian randomization supported a putative causal role for 143 of these associations. Functional annotation pointed to predominantly distal, enhancer-centered regulation and enrichment of inflammatory transcription factor programs (eg, activator protein-1 and nuclear factor κB). This distal architecture was consistent with expression quantitative trait methylation results, which showed a larger number of trans associations. Among 143 CpGs associated with AAA in Mendelian randomization analyses, we identified 213 CpG-gene expression pairs with strong colocalization support, including AGER, C2, and DDR1. Multi-trait colocalization further prioritized 8 CpG-gene expression-AAA links with evidence of a shared genetic signal. Network Mendelian randomization identified 135 putative mediation pathways linking CpGs to AAA, including 58 via cardiometabolic traits and 77 via inflammation-related traits. Blood lipid traits mediated >40% of the associations between AAA risk and CpGs near LDLR (cg19305903) and TRIB1 (cg14128479). Among inflammation-related mediators, circulating DAG1, NEXN, MMP9, IL1RN, and MMP13 were prioritized as potential intermediates. Additionally, a CpG selection process was used to develop a methylation risk score for AAA, which strongly associated with disease in both the discovery cohort and 2 external validation cohorts, even after adjustment for a full suite of clinical covariates.

CONCLUSIONS: This study identified putative causal DNA methylation markers for AAA, and multi-omics analyses implicate activator protein-1-linked inflammatory transcriptional programs, blood lipids, and multiple inflammation-related proteins as key pathways underlying methylation-associated AAA risk.

Identifying causal DNA methylation markers for AAA can elucidate the regulatory processes that drive aneurysm formation and accelerate translational applications. We leveraged the Veterans Affairs (VA) Million Veteran Program to identify methylation biomarkers and delineate underlying pathways.

articles.title: The Association Between Hospital Comprehensive Stroke Center Designation Status and Stroke Rate Reporting in the Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapy Registry After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: Implications for Hospital Performance Assessment.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The Michigan Structural Heart Consortium showed that transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) stroke rates were associated with hospital Comprehensive Stroke Center (CSC) designation, suggesting that hospital structural factors affect stroke reporting. We sought to determine whether CSC designation is nationally associated with reported stroke rates and the potential impact on hospital performance and Transcatheter Valve Therapy National Data Registry (TVTR) public reporting.

METHODS: Consecutive TVTR cases from January 2016 through June 2023 were included, excluding sites reporting to the TVTR <1 year or performing <20 total TAVR procedures. The primary outcome was in-hospital stroke rate. Secondary outcomes were disabling stroke and 30-day stroke. Major bleeding, death, acute renal failure, and a composite end point were falsification end points to determine whether CSC status was uniquely associated with stroke. Multivariable hierarchical models were created starting with patient covariates and sequentially adding hospital variables to account for determinants of stroke. The impact of CSC status on hospital performance was estimated by correcting CSC hospital stroke rates in the validated TVTR 30-day composite model.

RESULTS: A total of 525 919 TAVRs at 800 sites were included, and 10 963 strokes (2.1%) were reported within 30 days: 8284 (1.6%) in-hospital and 2679 (0.5%) after discharge. A total of 4733 (0.9%) were disabling strokes. Multivariate analysis showed that CSC status and participation in TAVR trials were independent predictors of in-hospital stroke rate (P=0.033 and 0.012) and disabling stroke (P=0.033 and 0.007), but not falsification end points (P=NS). Participation in TAVR trials and operator volume were independent predictors of 30-day stroke (P=0.039 and P=0.041). The impact of CSC status on the 30-day composite model showed performance improvement for 8 of 153 CSC hospitals.

CONCLUSIONS: CSC hospital status and participation in TAVR trials are significant predictors unique for stroke. Correcting for the association of CSC status on stroke rate resulted in an estimated 8 of 153 hospitals improving their TVTR 30-day composite model performance. Further work is needed to account for potential ascertainment bias for stroke in public reporting.

articles.title: The complexity of provoked venous thromboembolism: one treatment plan does not fit all.
articles.abstract: The decision of whether to continue patients diagnosed with venous thromboembolism (VTE) on anticoagulation after the initial treatment period is often nuanced. Many patients will have ≥1 transient risk factor associated with a time-limited increased risk of VTE. Transient risk factors are further divided into major factors, such as joint replacement, or minor factors, such as prolonged travel, which determine the magnitude of risk for an initial VTE. In addition, major transient risk factors generally carry a lower risk of recurrent VTE than minor transient risk factors. However, many patients will also have ≥1 persistent VTE risk factor, which further increase the risk for recurrence. Some persistent risk factors, such as inflammatory bowel disease, are associated with a sufficiently high risk of recurrent VTE, for which guidelines recommend indefinite anticoagulation. There are multiple other persistent risk factors that carry a lower risk of recurrent VTE, such as chronic renal insufficiency and obesity. The HI-PRO (High-Risk Patients with Provoked Venous Thromboembolism) trial sought to assess the efficacy and safety of extended thromboprophylaxis for the prevention of recurrent VTE in patients with an initial provoked VTE and at least 1 persistent risk factor. The study found a lower risk of recurrent VTE in the thromboprophylaxis cohort, challenging the traditional time-limited treatment for provoked VTE, but heterogeneity of the study population and small sample size preclude identification of which subsets of patients could safely discontinue anticoagulation. We consider the conundrum of provoked VTE in this review.

articles.title: Feasibility of patient-specific 3D-printed fragment models for preoperative planning in bicondylar tibial plateau fractures: a retrospective case series.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE: Schatzker type V and VI tibial plateau fractures have complex three-dimensional patterns that complicate surgical planning and coronal alignment restoration. This study assessed the feasibility of patient-specific 3D-printed fragment models for planning combined medial and lateral approaches and described radiographic and functional outcomes.

METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 22 patients with Schatzker type V or VI fractures treated at Foshan Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine from January 2023 to July 2024. Preoperative CT data enabled fragment segmentation, color coding, virtual reduction, and fabrication of patient-specific physical models. Posterior tibial slope, medial proximal tibial angle, articular depression, and tibial plateau width were compared pre- and postoperatively. Rasmussen functional and radiological scores and Knee Society Scores were assessed at 3 and 6 months, 1 year, and final follow-up; complications were recorded.

RESULTS: All 22 patients completed follow-up (mean, 30.73 ± 3.20 months). A mean of 24.41 ± 2.26 tibial fragments were identified and segmented per patient. Mean articular depression decreased from 6.70 ± 3.07 to 1.74 ± 0.48 mm. Posterior tibial slope, medial proximal tibial angle, and tibial plateau width improved significantly after surgery (all P < 0.001). Mean postoperative coronal alignment was within the predefined normal range in both preoperative varus and valgus subgroups. All three scores differed significantly across follow-up (all P < 0.001). At final follow-up, mean Rasmussen functional and Knee Society Scores were 27.18 ± 1.84 and 87.55 ± 4.92, respectively, with excellent-or-good rates of 100% and 95.45%. Mild post-traumatic knee osteoarthritis, superficial infection, and deep-vein thrombosis occurred in 5, 1, and 2 patients, respectively. No secondary varus or valgus deformity was observed.

CONCLUSIONS: In complex bicondylar tibial plateau fractures, patient-specific 3D-printed fragment models provided a practical three-dimensional reference for fragment identification, reduction sequencing, and planning of combined medial and lateral approaches. Satisfactory articular reduction, maintenance of proximal tibial coronal alignment, and favorable functional outcomes at final follow-up were observed in this cohort. These findings support the feasibility of incorporating 3D-printed fragment models into preoperative planning for these fractures.

This study assessed the feasibility of patient-specific 3D-printed fragment models for planning combined medial and lateral approaches and described radiographic and functional outcomes. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 22 patients with Schatzker type V or VI fractures treated at Foshan Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine from January 2023 to July 2024.

articles.title: Association of Multimodal Collateral Profiles with Outcomes After Large Core Thrombectomy.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cerebral collateral circulation markers in large core thrombectomy and their impact on functional outcomes have not been extensively reported. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed health system medical records of large core (Alberta Stroke Program Early Computed Tomography Score <6 and/or computed tomography perfusion [CTP] cerebral blood flow <30% volume ≥50 milliliters [mL]) thrombectomy patients over a 19-month period. A good collateral profile (CCC+) was defined as the combination of computed tomography angiography Tan arterial score ≥2 and CTP cerebral blood volume index (CBVI) ≥0.8. A poor profile (CCC-) was defined as Tan <2 and CBVI <0.8. All others were categorized as having a mixed profile (CCC±). Multivariable Firth's penalized logistic regression was used to identify factors independently associated with the primary outcome, 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) 0-3. Results: 88 patients with median (interquartile range, IQR) age 65.5 (56.5-77.5) years and core volume 78 (55-116) mL were included. Forty-seven patients (53.4%) had poor collateral profiles, 31 (35.2%) were classified as CCC±, and 10 (11.4%) as CCC+. In the multivariable Firth's penalized logistic regression model, CCC+ patients had higher odds of achieving a 90-day mRS of 0-3 compared with CCC- patients, though the difference was not statistically significant (odds ratio [OR] 1.117, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.235-5.311, p = 0.889). No significant difference was observed between CCC± and CCC- patients (OR 0.869, 95% CI 0.293-2.577, p = 0.800). Glucose was the only factor independently associated with 90-day outcomes (OR 0.742, 95% CI 0.602-0.915, p = 0.005). Conclusions: No independent association was detected between favorable or mixed cerebral collateral circulation and 90-day mRS 0-3 after large core thrombectomy, though the study was underpowered for the CCC+ comparison. Presenting glucose may inform the likelihood of achieving independent ambulatory status at 90 days.

articles.title: Cross-Phenotype Genomics Reveals Heterogeneous Genetic Susceptibility Architecture Relevant to Menopause.
articles.abstract: Background: Menopause is accompanied by substantial interindividual variation in hormonal, metabolic, cardiovascular, skeletal, and thrombotic phenotypes. Although the genetics of reproductive ageing and individual menopause-associated traits are increasingly characterised, the cross-phenotype architecture of individual menopause-relevant germline variants remains less well defined. Methods: We performed a variant-centred genomic analysis of 31 prespecified menopause-relevant germline variants. Cross-trait evidence comprised 766 variant-trait records across 52 phenotypes and was integrated with a targeted Pan-UK Biobank phenome-wide association study (PheWAS; 1462 tests across 57 endpoints), clinically relevant outcome analyses, linkage disequilibrium assessment, FinnGen R12 venous thromboembolism (VTE) associations, regional fine-mapping, and molecular annotation. Association strength, between-study heterogeneity, phenotypic breadth and sharing, and locus resolution were evaluated as distinct evidence dimensions. Results: In total, 25 of 31 variants showed at least one cross-trait association at p < 1 × 10-5 and 21 reached genome-wide significance. Phenotypic breadth varied markedly, from restricted profiles to 16 associated phenotypes, and strong associations frequently coexisted with substantial between-study heterogeneity. In Pan-UK Biobank, 222 associations involving 25 variants met false-discovery-rate correction, spanning hormonal, reproductive, cardiometabolic, skeletal, nutritional, hepatic, and neurological phenotypes. Cross-phenotype reconstruction identified recurrent connectivity through sex hormone-binding globulin, testosterone, adiposity, lipid, and skeletal traits, while linkage disequilibrium analyses distinguished phenotypic sharing from genetic redundancy. Clinically, F5 rs6025 and F2 rs1799963 showed strong VTE associations in FinnGen (OR 2.387 and 1.921, respectively), but markedly different locus resolution: rs6025 had posterior inclusion probability (PIP) 0.979 and constituted a single-variant 95% credible set, whereas rs1799963 had PIP 0.596 within a four-variant credible set. Conclusions: Menopause-relevant germline variation exhibits heterogeneous cross-phenotype architectures in which association strength, phenotypic breadth, between-study consistency, genetic independence, and locus resolution are not interchangeable. This variant-centred framework provides a basis for evaluating inherited susceptibility relevant to menopause and hormone exposure, while prospective individual-level studies remain necessary before translation into risk prediction or treatment selection.

articles.title: Urgent Endovascular Treatment of a Pancreatitis-Related Pseudoaneurysm Identified on Follow-Up CT.
articles.abstract: Visceral artery pseudoaneurysm (VA-PSA) is an uncommon but life-threatening complication of acute-on-chronic pancreatitis, particularly in the presence of walled-off necrosis (WON). Early radiological recognition is essential because of the high risk of rupture. We present the case of a 51-year-old man with chronic pancreatitis who developed a pseudoaneurysm arising from the proper hepatic artery within a pancreatic head necrotic collection. Follow-up contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) demonstrated a new arterial-phase enhancing focus within the WON. Digital subtraction angiography (DSA) confirmed the pseudoaneurysm, which was successfully excluded with a covered stent placed via a right transfemoral approach. Post-procedural recovery was uneventful, and short-term follow-up CT showed persistent exclusion of the lesion.

articles.title: Development of a Quantitative Contrast CT-Based TAVR-Risk Score to Reliably Predict Deformation in Bicuspid Aortic Valves.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) calcification affects clinical outcomes by causing transcatheter heart valve (THV) deformation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). However, a computed tomography (CT)-based scoring system for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation has not been established.

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to develop a cardiac CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score for grading BAV calcification severity and predicting THV deformation.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients with BAV who underwent TAVR using contemporary balloon-expandable valves between January 2016 and December 2024 and who had preprocedural and postprocedural CT imaging. The BAV TAVR-risk score integrated calcification severity and distribution across valve leaflets, raphe, annulus, and left ventricular outflow tract, quantified using a fixed HU-850 threshold of detection on contrast-enhanced CT scans. Score thresholds were derived by receiver operating curve analysis with Youden index optimization. Patients were categorized into low-, intermediate-, and high-risk score groups.

RESULTS: Among 321 patients (median follow-up: 1,825 days; Q1-Q3: 765-1,825 days), 56 (17.4%) were classified into the high-risk score group. Both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV occurred in 49 of the 321 patients (15.3%) and were predominantly observed in the high-risk score group. However, in the low-risk score group, 149 of 155 patients (96.1%) demonstrated no underexpansion or eccentricity of the THV. A high BAV TAVR-risk score independently predicted both underexpansion and eccentricity of the THV (OR: 89.13; 95% CI: 35.02-226.83; P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: This CT-based BAV TAVR-risk score provides a systematic method to precisely quantify BAV severity which reliably predicts THV deformation for BAV patients with contemporary balloon-expandable valves and may help guide decision-making in this challenging population.
