articles.title: Safety and Effectiveness of the GORE VIABAHN FORTEGRA Venous Stent for the Treatment of Symptomatic Inferior Vena Cava Obstruction With or Without Combined Iliofemoral Obstruction.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This prospective, non-randomised, clinical investigational trial investigated the safety and effectiveness of the GORE VIABAHN FORTEGRA Venous Stent for treatment of symptomatic inferior vena cava obstruction, with or without combined iliofemoral obstruction.

METHODS: Subjects were enrolled at 17 sites across the USA, Europe, Australia, and New Zealand. The primary endpoint was a composite measure including primary patency and freedom from stent embolisation at 12 months, and 30 day freedom from pulmonary embolism and device or procedure related death, major bleeding, and vascular injury requiring surgical or endovascular intervention. The hypothesis driven secondary endpoint was change in revised venous clinical severity score (rVCSS) pain score from baseline to 12 months.

RESULTS: Eighty nine subjects were treated with an investigational iliocaval venous stent. Fifty nine (75%) of 79 evaluable subjects experienced freedom from a primary endpoint event, exceeding the performance goal of 58% at 12 months (90% confidence interval 66.6 - 82.7%) (p < .001). Of the 63 subjects reporting any pain at baseline, 51 (81%), saw an improvement in rVCSS pain score at 12 months, with a median difference of -2.0 (p < .001).

CONCLUSIONS: Endovascular treatment of symptomatic iliocaval obstruction with the purpose designed investigational venous stent is safe and effective. Results demonstrate robust primary patency rates, an acceptable safety profile, and reduced pain.

articles.title: Incidence and Risk Factors of Surgical Site Infections in Vascular Surgical Procedures in the Groin.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Vascular procedures in the groin are common and carry a high risk of surgical site infection (SSI). Several risk factors have been established but others are less clear, not least due to the heterogeneity of studies. This study aimed to provide generalisable data on SSI and associated factors after open vascular procedures in the groin.

METHODS: This was a retrospective, dual centre cohort study including all patients undergoing open vascular surgery in the groin during a twelve year period at two centres. The primary endpoints were SSI rates at thirty and ninety days. Secondary endpoints were mortality at thirty days and 1 year.

RESULTS: After exclusion of 165 early peri-operative deaths (5.6%) from the original 2 968 patients, 2 803 were analysed of which 1 424 (50.8%) included a bypass and 1 130 (40.4%) an endarterectomy, while 570 patients (20.3%) underwent minor procedures. The incidence of SSI was 6.3% (176 of 2 803) at thirty days and 8.2% (170 of 2 087) at ninety days. Of these, 40.1% (n = 83) were superficial, 32.8% (n = 68) involved the fascial layer, and 27.1% (n = 56) involved the vessels. All cause mortality was 6.6% (197 of 2 968) at thirty days and 14.1% (418 of 2 968) at 1 year, the latter significantly associated with SSI at thirty days (hazard ratio 2.23, 95% confidence interval 1.32 - 3.75; p = .003). On multivariable regression analysis, higher body mass index (odds ratio [OR] 1.08; p < .001), previous percutaneous interventions on the index vessels (OR 1.47; p = .030), use of a bovine pericardium patch (OR 1.98; p = .007), and creation of a supra-inguinal bypass (OR 1.91; p = .008) were associated with increased odds of SSI. Furthermore, lymphatic complications were strongly associated with subsequent SSI on univariable analysis (OR 3.766; p < .001).

CONCLUSION: The odds of experiencing SSI depend on several patient and procedure related factors. Lymphatic complications were strongly associated with subsequent SSI. Therefore, future prospective studies should investigate whether strategies to reduce lymphatic complications also reduce SSIs.
articles.englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Vascular procedures in the groin are common and carry a high risk of surgical site infection (SSI). Several risk factors have been established but others are less clear, not least due to the heterogeneity of studies. This study aimed to provide generalisable data on SSI and associated factors after open vascular procedures in the groin.

articles.title: Immunothrombosis Biomarkers and Multi-Omics Profiles After Successful Recanalization in Patients Receiving Ischemic Postconditioning: An Exploratory Analysis of the INSPIRE Trial.
articles.abstract: Successful recanalization after endovascular thrombectomy does not always restore microvascular perfusion, highlighting the need for adjunctive strategies. Ischemic postconditioning (IPostC) involves brief, controlled​ cycles of flow interruption and restoration at the onset of reperfusion to attenuate ischemia-reperfusion injury. In the parent INSPIRE trial, IPostC, delivered in situ as four cycles of 2-minute balloon inflation followed by 2-minute deflation at the previously occluded arterial segment immediately after successful recanalization, reduced infarct growth from baseline to 48 h. This exploratory secondary analysis included all 60 randomized patients. We investigated whether IPostC was associated with early changes in immunothrombosis, coagulation, and microvascular transit and explored associated plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiles. Arterial blood obtained approximately 15 min after successful recanalization was analyzed using flow cytometry and thromboelastography. Quantitative digital subtraction angiography-derived microcirculation time was analyzed in 55 patients, and plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiling was performed in 29 patients. Compared with controls, patients receiving IPostC had lower neutrophil CD11b expression (median, 52.15 versus 64.27 mean fluorescence intensity ×10²; P = 0.011), a lower thromboelastography α-angle (65.15° versus 67.95°; P = 0.037), and shorter microcirculation time (2.11 versus 3.03 s; P = 0.020). Longer microcirculation time was associated with greater infarct growth (r = 0.533; P < 0.001). Proteomic and metabolomic analyses identified signals involving blood-brain barrier and extracellular-matrix organization and mitochondrial bioenergetics. Biomarker comparisons were not adjusted for multiple comparisons; in the omics analyses, no protein and 17 metabolites remained significant after false discovery rate correction. In summary, IPostC was associated with lower neutrophil activation, slower clot propagation, and faster microvascular transit after recanalization, and multi-omics profiling pointed to blood-brain barrier integrity and mitochondrial bioenergetics as candidate pathways. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger studies. Trial registration: NCT06545734, registered 9 August 2024.

In the parent INSPIRE trial, IPostC, delivered in situ as four cycles of 2-minute balloon inflation followed by 2-minute deflation at the previously occluded arterial segment immediately after successful recanalization, reduced infarct growth from baseline to 48 h.

articles.title: Impact of Balloon-Expandable Valve Asymmetry on Heart Failure Post Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fluoroscopic assessment enables immediate evaluation of transcatheter heart valve expansion during transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Whether fluoroscopic asymmetric expansion of balloon-expandable valves is associated with post-TAVR heart failure (HF) remains uncertain.

METHODS: Among 607 consecutive patients undergoing balloon-expandable valve-TAVR in a prospective registry, 589 were analyzed. Valve asymmetry was quantified using a fluoroscopic asymmetry index (%), defined as [(longest/shortest balloon-expandable valve height)-1]×100. The primary end point was 2-year HF hospitalization.

RESULTS: During follow-up, 99 patients (17%) experienced HF hospitalization. As a continuous variable, asymmetry index (%) was not independently associated with 2-year HF (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] per 1% increase, 1.02 [95% CI, 0.98-1.06]). Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated no significant linear or nonlinear association (overall P=0.71; P for nonlinearity=0.89), although the risk curve suggested increased HF risk beyond moderate valve asymmetry. Exploratory threshold analysis identified an asymmetry index cutoff of 7.48%. Patients above this threshold had a higher incidence of HF hospitalization than those below it (23.6% versus 15.8%; log-rank P=0.043), despite comparable rates of impaired valve performance at discharge. Valve asymmetry >7.48% remained independently associated with late HF occurring beyond 30 days after TAVR (adjusted HR, 1.69 [95% CI, 1.10-2.60]).

CONCLUSIONS: Fluoroscopic assessment of balloon-expandable valve expansion identified patients with marked valve asymmetry at increased risk of late HF after TAVR, despite preserved early valve performance. These findings support the potential value of intraprocedural valve geometry assessment for long-term risk stratification and warrant further investigation.
articles.englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Fluoroscopic assessment enables immediate evaluation of transcatheter heart valve expansion during transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Whether fluoroscopic asymmetric expansion of balloon-expandable valves is associated with post-TAVR heart failure (HF) remains uncertain. METHODS: Among 607 consecutive patients undergoing balloon-expandable valve-TAVR in a prospective registry, 589 were analyzed.

articles.title: PASCAL Precision System Outcomes by Implant Location and Lesion Location in Degenerative Mitral Regurgitation Patients From the STS/ACC TVT Registry.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair can be more challenging in noncentral regions of the valve and in anterior or bileaflet lesions. We assess effect of implant location and leaflet lesion location on safety and effectiveness of PASCAL Precision system in degenerative mitral regurgitation (MR).

METHODS: Mitral valve transcatheter edge-to-edge repair outcomes in patients with degenerative MR treated with PASCAL Precision system (September 2022-October 2024), from the US STS/ACC TVT (Society of Thoracic Surgeons/American College of Cardiology Transcatheter Valve Therapy) Registry, were analyzed by implant location (A2P2/non-A2P2) and leaflet lesion location (anterior/posterior/bileaflet). Procedural, clinical, and echocardiographic outcomes to 30 days were assessed.

RESULTS: At 30 days, both A2P2 (n=1526) and non-A2P2 (n=299) groups had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 1.1% versus 1.0%, mitral valve reintervention: 0.4% versus 0.0% and single leaflet device attachment: 0.5% versus 0.3%; all P>0.05) and demonstrated significant MR reduction (P<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference between groups (P=0.750) (MR ≤2+: 93.4% versus 95.4%; MR ≤1+: 72.0% versus 73.3%). Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores improved significantly in both groups (∆19.3, ∆17.7 points; P=0.741). The anterior (n=250), posterior (n=902), and bileaflet (n=192) disease groups also had low event rates (cardiovascular mortality: 0.4%, 1.1%, 0.0%; mitral valve reintervention: 0.8%, 0.1%, 0.5%; and single leaflet device attachment: 0.8%, 0.2%, 0.5%; all P>0.05), and demonstrated significant MR reduction (P<0.001 versus baseline) with no significant difference across groups (P=0.459) (MR ≤2+: 94.1%, 93.1%, and 94.5%; MR ≤1+: 79.0%, 69.2%, and 72.4%). All groups experienced significant improvement in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire Overall Summary scores (∆21.4, ∆18.8, ∆12.0 points; P=0.087).

CONCLUSION: In real-world patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation, treatment with the PASCAL Precision system was associated with favorable safety and effectiveness at 30 days, regardless of implant location or leaflet lesion location.

articles.title: Impact of Undertreated Antithrombotic Therapy on Adverse Patient Outcomes: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association.
articles.abstract: Antithrombotic therapy undertreatment includes omission, nonadherence, underdosing, and clinical circumstances that result in subtherapeutic antithrombotic levels. Antithrombotic undertreatment has profound implications for patient safety, public health, and healthcare costs. Due to deviation from evidence-based clinical practice, misperceptions of bleeding versus thrombotic risk, and inequities in healthcare access, many patients with atrial fibrillation, venous thromboembolism, or peripheral artery disease remain untreated or receive suboptimal anticoagulant dosing. Antithrombotic undertreatment has been shown to increase rates of ischemic stroke, systemic embolism, recurrent thrombosis, and mortality. Real-world data continue to highlight substantial gaps in care, which appear to be magnified in patients with inequity in social determinants of health. The emergence of antithrombotic stewardship, in concert with growing bodies of literature on antithrombotic agent underdosing, represents a transformative opportunity to address these gaps through structured, interprofessional, and evidence-based approaches. Through interdisciplinary collaboration, healthcare professionals are well positioned to enhance patient health and safety by recognizing and recommitting to reducing antithrombotic undertreatment.
articles.englishSummary: Antithrombotic therapy undertreatment includes omission, nonadherence, underdosing, and clinical circumstances that result in subtherapeutic antithrombotic levels. Antithrombotic undertreatment has profound implications for patient safety, public health, and healthcare costs. Due to deviation from evidence-based clinical practice, misperceptions of bleeding versus thrombotic risk, and inequities in healthcare access, many patients with atrial fibrillation, venous thromboembolism, or peripheral artery disease remain untreated or receive suboptimal anticoagulant dosing.

articles.title: Modified Hybrid Repair with Open Reconstruction of Infrarenal Aortoiliac Segment for Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysms Without Custom Distal Landing Zone: A Single-Center Case Series.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Inadequate distal landing zones can limit hybrid repair of thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysm (TAAA). We evaluated a modified strategy combining prosthetic distal landing-zone reconstruction, retrograde visceral and renal revascularization, and thoracic stent-graft exclusion. Methods: This retrospective single-center case series included all nine consecutive patients with inadequate native distal landing zones who underwent single-stage modified hybrid repair in 2025. Open aneurysm excision and aortoiliac reconstruction provided the distal sealing segment and inflow for visceral and renal bypasses. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included postoperative length of hospital stay, 30-day major complication rate, 30-day paraplegia rate, 1-year reintervention rate, 30-day readmission rate, and technical success rate. Results: Five patients had Crawford extent II aneurysms and four had extent III aneurysms. Technical success was achieved in all nine patients. Median operative time, estimated blood loss, and intensive care unit stay were 724 min, 2500 mL, and 8 days, respectively. Thirty-day all-cause mortality was 0% (0/9). No spinal cord ischemia or mesenteric ischemia occurred within 30 days. Acute kidney injury occurred in six patients (66.7%), including one who received continuous renal replacement therapy. One patient required early covered stent-graft repair of a right iliac anastomotic leak. At a median follow-up of 9 months (IQR, 6-12), all reconstructed visceral and renal bypasses were patent, no new endoleak was detected, and all patients were alive. No additional reintervention was required. Conclusions: Modified hybrid repair with prosthetic distal landing-zone reconstruction was technically feasible in selected TAAA patients with inadequate distal sealing anatomy. Larger studies with longer follow-up are needed to evaluate durability and refine indications.

articles.title: Age-specific associations of endovascular therapy and reperfusion delay with outcomes after large vessel occlusion: a regional registry study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: The benefit of endovascular therapy (EVT) in very elderly patients with large vessel occlusion (LVO) remains uncertain, and sensitivity to reperfusion delay may differ by age. We evaluated age-specific associations of treatment and reperfusion time with functional outcomes.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: We analysed 1,280 patients with acute LVO in an emergency medical service-based registry, divided into groups aged 85 years or older and younger than 85 years. The primary outcome was an ordinal shift towards a better 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score. Secondary outcomes were dichotomized functional measures incorporating prestroke status.

RESULTS: Among 837 patients younger than 85 years, EVT was associated with a favourable mRS shift (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.47; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.07-2.01). Among 443 patients aged 85 years or older, the estimate was favourable but not statistically significant (aOR, 1.29; 95% CI, 0.87-1.92). No significant age-by-treatment interaction was observed for functional outcomes. Among patients treated with successful reperfusion by EVT, favourable outcomes declined more steeply with increasing onset-to-reperfusion time in those aged 85 years or older.

DISCUSSION: The association of EVT with functional outcomes was not significantly modified by age but estimates in very elderly patients were less precise. Very elderly patients appeared more vulnerable to reperfusion delay.

CONCLUSION: Treatment selection should integrate prestroke function, stroke severity, imaging findings, procedural feasibility, and the likelihood of rapid reperfusion rather than age alone.

articles.title: 3-Year Comparison of Sirolimus- Versus Paclitaxel-Coated Balloon Angioplasty in Femoropopliteal Artery Disease: The SIRONA Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sirolimus-coated balloons (SCBs) have emerged as alternatives to paclitaxel-coated balloons (PCBs), but randomized comparative data beyond 2 years are lacking.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to compare patient-reported outcomes, effectiveness, and safety through 3 years in symptomatic femoropopliteal artery disease.

METHODS: SIRONA was a prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trial comparing SCB angioplasty with a PCB strategy. Patients were randomized 1:1 after successful predilation. Prespecified 3-year outcomes included walking capacity, health-related quality of life, clinically driven target lesion/vessel revascularization (cdTLR/cdTVR), mortality, major amputation, and amputation-free survival.

RESULTS: Among 482 randomized patients (SCB, n = 238; PCB, n = 244), 96.3% had intermittent claudication; 3-year follow-up was completed by 76.5% and 79.6%, respectively. Changes in patient-reported walking distances did not differ between-groups. Three-year freedom from cdTLR was 88.2% (95% CI: 83.1%-91.9%) versus 80.2% (95% CI: 74.1%-85.0%; HR: 0.60, 95% CI: 0.36-0.97; nominal log-rank P = 0.03). Post-hoc analysis suggested time-varying treatment effects (treatment-by-period interaction P = 0.006), with separation after the first year. Freedom from cdTVR (HR: 0.78, 95% CI: 0.50-1.21; nominal P = 0.27) and amputation-free survival (HR: 1.09, 95% CI 0.57-2.09; nominal P = 0.79) did not differ.

CONCLUSIONS: Through 3 years, no between-group differences were observed in walking capacity and health-related quality of life or clinical safety outcomes between SCB angioplasty and the PCB strategy. Three-year freedom from cdTLR was higher with SCB angioplasty, with treatment effect that varied over time. Given the exploratory, nonmultiplicity-adjusted 3-year analysis, the cdTLR difference requires confirmation.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to compare patient-reported outcomes, effectiveness, and safety through 3 years in symptomatic femoropopliteal artery disease. METHODS: SIRONA was a prospective, multicenter, randomized controlled trial comparing SCB angioplasty with a PCB strategy.

articles.title: Functional outcomes and quality of life after endovascular thrombectomy in large and extensive infarcts (ASPECTS 0-5): a multicentre registry study.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) is established for large infarcts, but remains cautiously applied in extensive infarcts with an Alberta Stroke Program Early CT Score (ASPECTS) of 0-2. Real-life outcome data remain limited.

PATIENTS AND METHODS: Retrospective analysis of the German Stroke Registry-Endovascular Treatment comparing extensive (ASPECTS 0-2) and large infarcts (ASPECTS 3-5) in patients with anterior-circulation occlusion and EVT. The primary outcome was the ordinal 90-day mRS distribution; secondary outcomes were mRS 0-3, survival, quality of life (3-level European Quality of Life-5 Dimensions) and living condition.

RESULTS: Of 18,069 screened patients, 889 were analysed (ASPECTS 1-2, n = 89; ASPECTS 3-5, n = 800); none had ASPECTS 0. With ASPECTS 1-2, 20.2% achieved mRS 0-3 and 55.1% died within 90 days. In the model including successful reperfusion, no statistically significant association was detected between infarct group and the 90-day mRS distribution (common odds ratio [cOR] 0.80; 95% CI, 0.53-1.23) or mRS 0-3 (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 0.89; 95% CI, 0.64-1.25), whereas successful reperfusion was associated with both (cOR 3.68; 95% CI, 2.31-5.85 and aOR 4.10; 95% CI, 2.45-6.86). Among survivors, median European Quality of Life-5 Dimensions utility index was 0.445 vs 0.541 (n = 27/324), and 51.5% vs 50.9% lived at home (n = 33/411).

DISCUSSION: An extensive infarct carried a challenging prognosis, yet acceptable outcome and non-institutional living remained achievable in a relevant minority. An independent association of infarct group with outcome was not detected.

CONCLUSION: An acceptable outcome remained attainable in selected patients with extensive infarction, particularly after successful reperfusion. Lacking a medically managed comparator, these data describe prognosis rather than treatment effect.

Real-life outcome data remain limited. articles.title: Situs Inversus Totalis with Mirror-Image Dextrocardia and Acute Type A Aortic Dissection Treated by Ascending Aorta Replacement Plus Total Arch Replacement and Frozen Elephant Trunk Using an Inverted Four-Branched Graft: A Case Report.
articles.abstract: Situs inversus totalis (SIT) is a rare congenital condition characterized by a complete mirror-image reversal of the thoracic and abdominal viscera, usually accompanied by dextrocardia. Acute type A aortic dissection (AAD) is a highly lethal cardiovascular emergency, and its coexistence with SIT is exceedingly rare. To the best of our knowledge, apart from a recently reported pregnant patient, no case of AAD in a non-pregnant adult with SIT has been treated with ascending aorta replacement combined with total arch replacement (TAR) and frozen elephant trunk (FET) implantation. In this report, we present such a case and share our surgical experience, particularly the inverted four-branched graft technique used to resolve the mismatch between the commercially available graft and the mirrored anatomy. The postoperative course was complicated by right renal malperfusion and stage 2 acute kidney injury. Overall renal function recovered with conservative management, although the right kidney subsequently became atrophic; otherwise, recovery was satisfactory. Computed tomographic angiography (CTA) at 10 months showed the graft and all reconstructed branches patent and the FET in position without endoleak, and the patient remained in good condition at the telephone follow-up approximately 3 years after surgery.

articles.title: Lipid control in a cohort of patients with cardiorenal disease (LIPID-REN): a subanalysis of the CARDIOREN registry.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD) confers a very high cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk, requiring comprehensive risk factor assessment. However, real-world data on current practices in patients with cardiorenal disease remain limited. We aimed to evaluate the control of cardiovascular risk factors, with a focus on lipid management, in a contemporary cardiorenal cohort.

METHODS: This cross-sectional analysis was conducted within the CARDIOREN Registry, which enrolled patients with chronic heart failure from 13 tertiary hospitals in Spain (2021-2022). Of 1107 patients, 885 with complete data on low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C), albuminuria, and atherosclerotic CVD (ASCVD) were eligible. The present analysis was restricted to the patients who met the definition of advanced CKD, defined as estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) <30 ml/min/1.73 m² or eGFR 30-45 ml/min/1.73 m² with albuminuria >30 mg/g. ASCVD was defined as prior ischemic heart disease, stroke, or peripheral arterial disease. The proportion of patients with LDL-C <55 mg/dl was assessed. Multivariable logistic regression models, including a parsimonious primary model and sensitivity analyses, were used to identify factors associated with lower LDL-C levels.

RESULTS: Advanced CKD was present in 221 patients (25%); median age was 79 years, 58.8% were male, and 52.9% had ASCVD. Median LDL-C was 73 mg/dl, and only 22.6% achieved an LDL-C <55 mg/dl. Achievement of LDL-C <55 mg/dl was significantly lower in patients without ASCVD compared with those with ASCVD (13.4% vs. 30.7%; P = .002). In multivariable analysis, ASCVD was independently associated with a higher likelihood of achieving LDL-C <55 mg/dl, whereas female sex was independently associated with a lower likelihood of achieving this level.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with advanced CKD, lipid control was below cardiology guideline recommendations for patients at very high CVD risk, particularly among those without ASCVD and in women.

articles.title: Knowledge, Attitudes and Self-Reported Practices of Emergency and Intensive Care Nurses in Managing Traumatic Brain Injury.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a leading cause of mortality and disability worldwide, with a growing burden in low- and middle-income countries. Nurses in emergency and intensive care units (ICUs) play a critical role in TBI management, yet little is known about their competencies in Palestine.

AIMS: This study aimed to assess the knowledge, attitudes and self-reported practices of emergency and intensive care unit nurses regarding traumatic brain injury management and to identify factors associated with these outcomes.

STUDY DESIGN: A descriptive cross-sectional survey using stratified random sampling was conducted in governmental and private hospitals in the northern West Bank, Palestine. Data were collected in January 2025 using a validated Arabic questionnaire. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation coefficients and multiple linear regression analyses were performed, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05.

RESULTS: A total of 151 nurses participated, yielding a response rate of 61.4% (151/246). Nurses demonstrated generally good foundational knowledge, particularly in Glasgow Coma Scale interpretation and recognition of neurological responses, although gaps remained in advanced monitoring. Attitudes were predominantly positive, with strong support for specialised training. Self-reported practices included maintaining adequate blood pressure and initiating deep vein thrombosis (DVT) prophylaxis. Knowledge correlated significantly with attitude and self-reported practice, and attitude correlated strongly with self-reported practice. Previous TBI training, higher educational level and longer clinical experience were associated with better outcomes.

CONCLUSIONS: Emergency and intensive care unit nurses demonstrated adequate foundational knowledge and positive attitudes towards traumatic brain injury management, although gaps remained in advanced monitoring and selected self-reported practices. Structured continuing professional development, standardised protocols and organisational support are needed to strengthen neurotrauma nursing care.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: The findings support context-sensitive continuing education, simulation, standardised protocols and organisational measures that enable nurses to translate knowledge into consistent neurotrauma care in resource-constrained settings.

articles.title: Snare-Assisted Traction Technique for Renal Artery Reconstruction in Endovascular Repair of Complex Thoracoabdominal Aortic Aneurysms.
articles.abstract: Renal artery (RA) reconstruction during complex endovascular aortic repair often fails in hostile anatomy because of inadequate guidewire support. We describe snare-assisted traction (SAT), a novel endovascular bailout technique using conventional off-the-shelf devices. By combining distal snare traction with a long femoral sheath, SAT shifts target vessel reconstruction from simple wire guidance to sheath-based structural support. This provides robust stability for wire exchange and stent delivery without requiring specialized, unavailable tools or high-morbidity open conversion. Among 12 patients with severe RA angulation, ostial stenosis, or sac origin, SAT achieved 100% technical success without procedural complications. At median 6-month follow-up, all reconstructed RAs remained patent with stable renal function. SAT offers a safe, reproducible, and universally accessible solution for hostile target vessel access, significantly enhancing the feasibility and clinical safety of complex endovascular repair.

articles.title: A comparison of the efficacy and safety of direct oral anticoagulants with low molecular weight heparin for venous thromboembolism prophylaxis after total hip arthroplasty : a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: To evaluate differences in the efficacy and safety of low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) used for venous thromboembolism (VTE) prophylaxis after elective total hip arthroplasty (THA).

METHODS: This systematic review and meta-analysis reviewed MEDLINE, Embase, and CENTRAL from conception to 13 December 2025, for any randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing the efficacy (VTE risk) and safety (bleeding risk) of LMWH and DOACs after elective THA. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) of VTE, bleeding, reoperation, and mortality risks were assessed.

RESULTS: A total of 22 RCTs involving 28,112 participants were included. The risk of VTE in the DOAC group was lower compared with the LMWH group (OR 0.62 (95% CI 0.47 to 0.82); p = 0.002), driven by a reduction in deep vein thrombosis (DVT) risk (OR 0.60 (95% CI 0.42 to 0.86); p = 0.008). The findings remained consistent in the subgroup analysis restricted to anticoagulants and dosages licensed for use in the UK. Overall bleeding risk was higher in the DOAC group (OR 1.19 (95% CI 1.03 to 1.38); p = 0.023), but no difference was seen when comparing only UK-licensed anticoagulants and doses (OR 1.06 (95% CI 0.95 to 1.18); p = 0.279). Reoperation risk (OR 1.21 (95% CI 0.75 to 1.93); p = 0.351) and mortality (OR 1.03 (95% CI 0.46 to 2.33); p = 0.937) did not differ between groups.

CONCLUSION: DOACs reduce the risk of VTE and DVT following elective THA compared with LMWH without increasing bleeding risk, for UK-licensed agents and doses. Switching to DOACs could save the NHS £8.6 million per year. New clinical trials are needed to compare the safety and efficacy of UK-licensed DOACs and LWMH with modern postoperative rehabilitation protocols.

articles.title: Effectiveness of Tomazoni Measurement Method for Central Catheter Tip Positioning in Neonates: A Randomised Controlled Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Accurate peripherally inserted central catheter (PICC) tip positioning in neonates remains challenging, with high rates of malposition reported using traditional measurement methods.

AIM: To evaluate the effectiveness of the Tomazoni method for PICC positioning in neonates compared with the traditional method.

STUDY DESIGN: Pragmatic, parallel-group randomised clinical trial with stratified block randomisation, conducted in a neonatal intensive care unit in Brazil between June 2024 and April 2025.

RESULTS: Of 62 randomised procedures, 55 were evaluable (27 in the experimental group, 28 in the control group). Central positioning was achieved in 21 of 27 procedures (77.8%) in the experimental group versus 5 of 28 (17.9%) in the control group (p < 0.001). PICC insertion procedures assessed using the Tomazoni method were 4.36 times more likely to achieve central tip placement (RR = 4.36; 95% CI: 1.91-9.88). Catheter withdrawal was required in 3 of 27 procedures (11.1%) in the experimental group versus 16 of 28 (57.1%) in the control group (p = 0.001; RR = 0.19; 95% CI: 0.06-0.59).

CONCLUSIONS: The Tomazoni measurement method was associated with substantially higher rates of central PICC tip positioning and reduced need for catheter withdrawal compared with the traditional method.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: The Tomazoni method offers a reproducible, low-cost measurement strategy that can be implemented in neonatal intensive care units to improve catheter positioning accuracy and reduce procedure-related manipulations, with potential implications for patient safety. The trial, titled 'Comparison between measurements of peripherally inserted central catheters in children and newborns', was registered in the Brazilian Clinical Trials Registry under the identifier RBR-55zwb45.

TRIAL REGISTRATION: This trial is registered in the Brazilian Clinical Trials Registry (ReBEC) under the identifier RBR-55zwb45.

articles.title: Reducing Central Line-Associated Bloodstream Infections in ICUs: A Systematic Review of Barriers and Facilitators and Intervention Measures.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite established guidelines, central line-associated bloodstream infection (CLABSI) remains a severe ICU complication due to cognitive and resource barriers hindering healthcare worker compliance. A systematic evaluation of these barriers and facilitators is currently lacking but is important for informing targeted implementation strategies for CLABSI prevention.

AIMS: To explore the barriers and facilitators to implementing CLABSI prevention in ICUs using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR) to provide evidence-based strategies for improvement.

STUDY DESIGN: A PRISMA-guided systematic review was performed using PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, CNKI, VIP, Wan fang, and CBM databases, up to August 2026. Eligible studies included qualitative, quantitative, or mixed-methods research on the barriers and facilitators to CLABSI prevention implementation among ICU healthcare workers. Two researchers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed quality using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Data synthesis and intervention development were guided by the CFIR, with targeted strategies mapped using the CFIR-ERIC (Expert Recommendations for Implementing Change) matching tool.

RESULTS: The literature search identified 1,780 records, of which 28 studies were ultimately included. The review identified 28 barriers and facilitators, which were synthesized into four major themes and mapped to 16 CFIR constructs across the catheter-care continuum. The most prominent barriers involved staff knowledge gaps, inconsistent adherence to recommended practices, limited resources, and insufficient leadership support. CFIR-ERIC mapping identified 11 Level 1 expert-endorsed implementation strategies, of which four were represented in the included literature and seven were identified as potential implementation gaps.

CONCLUSIONS: CLABSI prevention in ICUs is influenced by multilevel implementation determinants spanning individual, organizational, and practice-related factors. A structured implementation-science approach may help healthcare organizations identify context-specific barriers and prioritize targeted strategies to support more consistent implementation of evidence-based CLABSI prevention practices.

RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: Improving CLABSI prevention may require multilevel strategies that combine targeted education and training, adequate resource allocation, leadership engagement, standardized clinical procedures, and ongoing audit and feedback. These strategies may help strengthen adherence to evidence-based practices, improve quality of care, and enhance patient safety in ICUs.

articles.title: Association between elevated lipoprotein (a) and venous thromboembolism: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is an established cardiovascular risk factor linked to atherogenesis, inflammation, and thrombosis; however, its association with venous thromboembolism (VTE) remains uncertain, with inconsistent findings across observational studies.

AIMS: To systematically evaluate the association between elevated Lp(a) levels and VTE risk and to examine differences by study design.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception through January 2026 for observational studies assessing Lp(a) and VTE. Effect estimates (odds ratios [ORs] or hazard ratios [HRs]) were pooled using DerSimonian-Laird random-effects models with Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Heterogeneity was assessed using I2 and τ2. Risk of bias was evaluated with ROBINS-E, publication bias with funnel plots, Egger's and Begg's tests, and certainty of evidence using GRADE. The primary outcome was VTE; secondary outcomes included deep vein thrombosis (DVT), pulmonary embolism (PE), and recurrent VTE.

RESULTS: Eleven studies (6 case-control, 5 cohort; 63,325 participants; 3581 VTE events) were included. Elevated Lp(a) was associated with a borderline increased VTE risk (pooled OR/HR 1.34 [95% CI 1.00-1.80]; P = 0.049), with high heterogeneity (I2 = 77.8%) and a wide prediction interval (0.56-3.21). In stratified analyses, case-control studies showed a significant association (OR 1.88 [1.25-2.81]; I2 = 57.2%), whereas cohort studies showed no association (HR 0.99 [0.85-1.15]; I2 = 0%), with significant between-group differences (p < 0.0001).

CONCLUSIONS: The association between elevated Lp(a) and VTE appears limited to case-control studies and is not supported by prospective cohort data, suggesting potential bias or residual confounding. Further large-scale and genetic studies are warranted to clarify this relationship.

METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, and Cochrane Library were searched from inception through January 2026 for observational studies assessing Lp(a) and VTE.

articles.title: Antiphospholipid syndrome: epidemiology and outcomes in the evolving criteria era.
articles.abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is a heterogeneous autoimmune thrombo-inflammatory disorder characterized by thrombosis, pregnancy morbidity and an expanding spectrum of microvascular, cardiac, haematological and other systemic manifestations. Although research has provided considerable insights into the pathogenesis and clinical phenotypes of APS, its epidemiology remains difficult to define because estimates depend on case definitions, antibody testing, repeat-testing requirements, testing practices and data sources. Population-based studies suggest that APS is rare, and catastrophic APS is rarer and best understood through registry data. Antiphospholipid antibody positivity alone does not establish APS; transient or low-level positivity can occur without disease, whereas persistent antibodies must be interpreted alongside compatible clinical manifestations. Despite its rarity, APS causes substantial morbidity through recurrent thrombosis, organ damage and adverse pregnancy outcomes, supporting targeted evaluation in unprovoked or recurrent venous thromboembolism, stroke in younger adults and selected pregnancy complications. Apparent differences among populations can reflect ascertainment, access to testing, study design and biological variation. Standardized case definitions, antibody testing and laboratory reporting, together with longitudinal population-based research in ancestry-diverse, paediatric and low-income and middle-income populations, are needed to refine estimates of APS burden and define its clinical spectrum.

Although research has provided considerable insights into the pathogenesis and clinical phenotypes of APS, its epidemiology remains difficult to define because estimates depend on case definitions, antibody testing, repeat-testing requirements, testing practices and data sources. Population-based studies suggest that APS is rare, and catastrophic APS is rarer and best understood through registry data.

articles.title: Use of smart glasses for ultrasound-guided central venous catheterization in adults: a randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Head-mounted displays can be integrated with ultrasonography to overlay the image in the operator's field of view, improving hand-eye coordination during invasive procedures. The clinical efficacy of smart glasses for central venous catheterization (CVC) remains uncertain. This study aimed to evaluate whether using smart glasses can improve efficiency compared to conventional ultrasound-guided CVC.

METHODS: This prospective, single-blinded, controlled study enrolled adult patients who underwent elective surgery requiring CVC. Patients were assigned to either the ultrasound screen (control) or smart glasses group using stratified randomization according to operator qualification. The primary outcome was the overall CVC procedural time. Secondary outcomes included ultrasound scanning and venous access time, number of needle redirections and probe repositionings, procedural success and complication rates.

RESULTS: In total, 124 patients were analyzed. The overall procedural time was significantly reduced in the smart glasses group compared to that in the control group (158 [140, 189] s vs. 134 [117,150] s; median difference, 26.0 s; 95% CI, [16.0-37.0] s, P < 0.001). Specifically, the ultrasound scanning time (median difference, 3.0 s, P = 0.004), venous access time (median difference, 2.0 s, P = 0.013), number of needle redirections (median difference, 1.0, P = 0.003) and probe repositionings (median difference, 0.0, P = 0.005) were significantly reduced in the smart glasses group compared to those in the control group. However, the success and complication rates were comparable between groups.

CONCLUSIONS: Smart glasses modestly improved procedural efficiency in ultrasound-guided CVC, potientially for novices, without improving success or complication rates. Larger-sample studies with more diverse operators and patients are warranted.

articles.title: Beyond the Threshold: Continuous Creatinine Change and Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy for Acute Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) worsens outcomes in acute ischemic stroke, but threshold-based definitions do not capture prognostic information from subthreshold changes. We tested whether early creatinine change within 48 hours of EVT conveys graded prognostic information beyond dichotomous CA-AKI.

METHODS: We performed a secondary analysis of the CAN-REST registry (Contrast-Associated Nephropathy After Endovascular Stroke Treatment), a retrospective multicenter observational cohort study of 6638 EVT-treated adults with acute ischemic stroke enrolled at 73 centers in 16 countries between January 1 and December 31, 2023. Early creatinine change was quantified as the natural logarithm ratio of 48-hour creatinine to baseline creatinine (ln[48-hour/baseline creatinine]), with CA-AKI defined per Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes criteria (≥0.3 mg/dL or ≥1.5× baseline rise within 48 hours). Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for prespecified baseline and periprocedural covariates examined associations with 90-day modified Rankin Scale shift and in-hospital mortality; linear versus restricted cubic spline specification was selected by likelihood ratio testing, and contrasts were estimated at ±10%, ±25%, and ±50%.

RESULTS: Greater creatinine worsening within 48 hours of EVT was independently associated with an unfavorable 90-day modified Rankin Scale shift (adjusted common odds ratio per 1-unit log-ratio increase, 1.48 [95% CI, 1.07-2.04]; linear) and in-hospital mortality (nonlinear dose-response, of larger magnitude). A 10% increase in creatinine at 48 hours-well below Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes threshold-was associated with worse functional outcome (adjusted common odds ratio, 1.04 [95% CI, 1.01-1.07]) and death (adjusted odds ratio, 1.22 [95% CI, 1.13-1.32]); a 10% decrease in creatinine at 48 hours was associated with lower odds of both outcomes (adjusted common odds ratio, 0.96 [95% CI, 0.93-0.99]; adjusted odds ratio, 0.74 [95% CI, 0.65-0.86]). The functional-outcome association concentrated at upper modified Rankin Scale cut-points (severe disability, death); effect modification by baseline renal function was not significant.

CONCLUSIONS: Early creatinine change after EVT conveys graded, outcome-specific prognostic information extending below formal CA-AKI thresholds, with a dose-response detectable at changes as modest as ±10%, complementing binary CA-AKI as a framework for post-EVT renal risk assessment.

articles.title: Deterioration of Peri-Infarct Microvascular Hemodynamics Following Successful Reperfusion in Acute Ischemic Stroke Predicts Infarct Growth.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Microvascular hemodynamic deterioration is a proposed mechanism underlying the no-reflow phenomenon in acute ischemic stroke. Experimental studies suggested that relative heterogeneity of capillary transit time (RTH) is a potential imaging biomarker of microvascular impairment. We investigated the relationship between peri-infarct RTH and infarct growth, measured on immediate post-thrombectomy (PT) perfusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and functional outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke with successful reperfusion.

METHODS: In this retrospective case-control study from the University of California, Los Angeles, patients with acute ischemic stroke from 2015 to 2020 were included if they had excellent reperfusion (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction score ≥2c) and diffusion- and perfusion-weighted MRIs at baseline, immediately PT, and 24 to 48 hours after thrombectomy. Peri-infarct regions were defined as time to maximum ≥6-second regions on baseline MRI that were not infarcted on immediate PT MRI. Following image coregistration, quantitative values of perfusion parameters, including RTH, were obtained from peri-infarct regions on immediate PT MRI. Two primary outcomes were assessed: (1) infarct growth ≥10 mL and (2) poor functional outcome (90-day modified Rankin Scale score >2). Associations between clinical and imaging parameters and outcomes were evaluated using univariate analysis. Age, sex, and covariates that were significant in univariate analysis were included in logistic regression analyses.

RESULTS: Among 47 patients included in the analysis (62% women; mean age, 72±13 years; median National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score, 14), 20 (43%) patients had substantial infarct growth and poor functional outcome. Peri-infarct RTH was significantly (P=0.005) higher in patients with infarct growth >10 mL than those without and remained as an independent predictor (odds ratio, 1.4 per 10% increase [95% CI, 1.0-2.0]; P=0.04). Similarly, the peri-infarct RTH was significantly higher (P<0.001) in patients with poor functional outcomes than those with good functional outcomes and remained as a significant predictor of poor functional outcome (odds ratio, 1.4 per 10% increase [95% CI, 1.0-1.9]; P=0.03).

CONCLUSIONS: Increased peri-infarct RTH on immediate PT MRI predicts substantial infarct growth and poor functional outcomes in successfully reperfused patients with acute ischemic stroke. Results highlight the role of microvascular dysfunction depicted by elevated RTH as a potential marker of no-reflow phenomenon despite excellent macrovascular reperfusion.

articles.title: Lysosomal dysfunction in vascular smooth muscle cells: Mechanisms and therapeutic targets in vascular disease.
articles.abstract: Vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) dysfunction is a common feature of atherosclerosis, aortic aneurysms, vascular calcification, and other vascular diseases. In VSMCs, lysosomes play an essential role in autophagic degradation, endocytic cargo processing, intracellular recycling, and cellular stress responses. Under pathological conditions, lysosomal dysfunction promotes foam cell formation, osteogenic differentiation, and extracellular matrix remodeling in VSMCs, thereby contributing to vascular diseases. This review summarizes current evidence on the role of lysosomal dysfunction in VSMC biology, its contribution to vascular diseases, and the molecular mechanisms involved. We also discuss strategies to restore lysosomal function and the challenges of targeting lysosomal pathways in VSMCs. A better understanding of VSMC-specific lysosomal regulation may facilitate the development of therapeutic strategies for vascular diseases.

articles.title: Transcarotid Artery Revascularization Versus Carotid Artery Stenting for Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The CREST-2 trial (Carotid Revascularization and Medical Management for Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis Trial) demonstrated superiority of carotid artery stenting (CAS) over intensive medical management for asymptomatic carotid stenosis, but it did not evaluate transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR). Herein, we compared ischemic stroke outcomes between TCAR and CAS among patients with asymptomatic carotid stenosis in contemporary real-world practice.

METHODS: We identified adults with asymptomatic carotid stenosis undergoing TCAR versus CAS using the 2016 to 2024 TriNetX database, which is a multicenter federated database of electronic health records. Propensity score matching was performed for demographics, laboratory values, risk factors, comorbidities, and medications. The primary outcome was ischemic stroke within 4 years.

RESULTS: Among 7303 identified patients, 2207 patients remained in each group after matching. TCAR did not demonstrate a significantly different stroke risk compared with CAS (hazard ratio, 0.68 [95% CI, 0.44-1.06]). The absolute risk difference was numerically but nonsignificantly lower for patients with TCAR throughout the follow-up period, progressively widening over time: 0.35% at 6 months (0.61% versus 0.96%; P=0.18) to 1.55% at 4 years (3.26% versus 4.81%; P=0.086).

CONCLUSIONS: TCAR did not significantly lower stroke risk compared with CAS for asymptomatic carotid stenosis. Although nonsignificant trends towards lower stroke risk were observed for TCAR, the widening of absolute risk differences over time suggests residual confounding rather than potential procedural benefit.

Herein, we compared ischemic stroke outcomes between TCAR and CAS among patients with asymptomatic carotid stenosis in contemporary real-world practice. METHODS: We identified adults with asymptomatic carotid stenosis undergoing TCAR versus CAS using the 2016 to 2024 TriNetX database, which is a multicenter federated database of electronic health records.

articles.title: Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitor Use and Functional Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy in Diabetic Stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although preclinical studies and limited clinical evidence suggest potential benefits of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) after acute ischemic stroke, their effects in patients with moderate-to-severe acute ischemic stroke requiring endovascular thrombectomy remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate whether SGLT2i use after endovascular thrombectomy is associated with improved 3-month functional outcomes in diabetic patients with acute ischemic stroke.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study analyzed prospectively collected data from January 2020 to March 2025 across 4 comprehensive stroke centers in Korea, Italy, and Switzerland. Consecutive adult patients with diabetes were grouped according to whether SGLT2i was used after their endovascular thrombectomy. Propensity score-based methods-including overlap weighting, inverse probability of treatment weighting, and 1:1 propensity score matching-were applied. Outcomes included the shift in 3-month modified Rankin Scale score, favorable (modified Rankin Scale score 0-2), and excellent outcomes (modified Rankin Scale score 0-1) at 3 months. Ordinal and binary logistic regression analyses were performed.

RESULTS: Of 429 eligible patients (mean [SD] age, 73.5 [11.1] years; 249 [58.0%] men; median [interquartile range] initial National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score, 12 [6-18]), 51 (11.9%) received SGLT2i poststroke. Successful recanalization was achieved in 85.3%. In the overlap weighting model (weighted n=37 per group), SGLT2i use was associated with improved 3-month modified Rankin Scale score distribution (common odds ratio, 2.31; [95% CI, 1.30-4.10]) and higher odds of a favorable outcome (odds ratio, 2.26; [95% CI, 1.15-4.43]). Results were consistent across inverse probability of treatment weighting and propensity score matching models, with inverse probability of treatment weighting analyses additionally demonstrating significant associations with excellent outcomes. No significant effect modification was observed across key clinical subgroups.

CONCLUSIONS: Poststroke SGLT2i therapy after endovascular thrombectomy was associated with improved 3-month functional outcomes in this multicenter retrospective analysis of diabetic patients. These findings suggest a potential therapeutic role for SGLT2i in poststroke diabetes management and support future prospective trials.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study analyzed prospectively collected data from January 2020 to March 2025 across 4 comprehensive stroke centers in Korea, Italy, and Switzerland.

articles.title: High-Resolution Disconnectome Predicts Outcome and Response to Thrombectomy in Basilar Artery Occlusion.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute basilar artery occlusion causes devastating strokes. Despite the benefit of endovascular treatment, the optimal management remains controversial in specific subgroups, particularly patients with mild deficits, and would benefit from robust prognostic tools. Given the dense white matter networks within the posterior fossa, we tested whether quantifying disconnections from acute diffusion-weighted imaging could improve outcome prediction and identify responders to recanalization compared with conventional metrics.

METHODS: We conducted a secondary analysis of a prospective multicenter stroke registry in France, including consecutive patients (2017-2024) with basilar artery occlusion and admission magnetic resonance imaging. Ultra-high-resolution diffusion magnetic resonance imaging was acquired in 2 healthy participants to build normative tractograms with optimized posterior fossa quality. Patient infarcts delineated on diffusion-weighted imaging were projected onto these tractograms to estimate disconnected fiber volume. The primary outcome was 90-day modified Rankin Scale score (0-3 versus 4-6). Predictive performance of disconnected fiber volume was compared with baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale (NIHSS), infarct volume, and posterior circulation Alberta Stroke Program Early Computed Tomography Score using logistic regressions and area under the receiver operating characteristic curves. Ordinal regressions tested associations between dichotomized disconnection status and the full modified Rankin Scale spectrum, stratified by recanalization status. Analyses were repeated in patients with an NIHSS score ≤10.

RESULTS: Among 201 patients (median age, 70; NIHSS score, 10), 97 (48.3%) had a poor outcome. Despite a small median infarct volume (4.75 mL), disconnected fiber volume was substantial (median 25.15 mL). Disconnected fiber volume achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curves of 0.84, outperforming NIHSS score (0.67; P<0.0001), infarct volume (0.75; P=0.00059), and posterior circulation Alberta Stroke Program Early Computed Tomography Score (0.76; P=0.0127). Patients without significant disconnection had better outcomes across the full modified Rankin Scale spectrum (odds ratio, 0.12 [95% CI, 0.065-0.204]) and derived greater benefit from successful recanalization (odds ratio, 0.33 [95% CI, 0.15-0.70]). In patients with an NIHSS score ≤10 (n=102), disconnected fiber volume remained the strongest predictor (area under the receiver operating characteristic curves of 0.83).

CONCLUSIONS: Disconnected fiber volume derived indirectly is a robust prognostic marker of basilar artery occlusion outcomes that outperforms conventional predictors and may support future treatment decisions after prospective validation.

articles.title: Early Recanalization After Tenecteplase or Alteplase in Distal and Medium Vessel Occlusion Strokes: An Observational Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intravenous thrombolysis remains the standard treatment for distal and medium vessel occlusion (DMVO) strokes. However, unlike large vessel occlusions, whether tenecteplase achieves higher early successful recanalization rates than alteplase in DMVO strokes remains uncertain.

METHODS: This single-center observational cohort study included consecutive patients with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-confirmed DMVO stroke treated at Centre Hospitalier Sud-Francilien, France, according to an institutional thrombolysis protocol specifying alteplase (0.9 mg/kg, 2016-2018) or tenecteplase (0.25 mg/kg, 2018-2023), with follow-up MRI 1 to 2 hours after intravenous thrombolysis. Patients intended for endovascular thrombectomy or without diagnostic-quality follow-up MRI were excluded. Recanalization was blindly assessed using a modified Arterial Occlusion Lesion scale designed for MRI and DMVO. Early successful recanalization was defined as ≥50% recanalization on early follow-up MRI (grade ≥2b), and substantial early infarct growth, assessed using a semiautomatic segmentation technique, was defined as a ≥0.5 mL and ≥20% increase in lesion volume. Propensity-score weighting accounted for baseline imbalances, including age, sex, vascular risk factors, baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score, occlusion site, and time period (2020-2023 versus 2016-2019).

RESULTS: Of the 319 included patients, 159 were treated with tenecteplase and 160 with alteplase. Median baseline National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale was 3 (1-7) in the tenecteplase group versus 4 (1-7.5) in the alteplase group, while M2 occlusions accounted for 54.1% versus 43.8% of cases. Early successful recanalization, assessed at a median postintravenous thrombolysis time of 80 (70-94) minutes, occurred in 72 (45.3%) and 53 (33.1%) patients treated with tenecteplase and alteplase, respectively (propensity-score weighting-odds ratio, 1.59 [95% CI, 1.15-2.20]; P=0.005). Substantial early infarct growth was observed in 42 (26.8%) and 64 (40.5%) patients, respectively (propensity-score weighting-odds ratio, 0.49 [95% CI, 0.35-0.69]; P<0.0001).

CONCLUSIONS: Compared with alteplase, tenecteplase-treated patients with DMVO had higher early successful recanalization and a lower risk of substantial early infarct growth, supporting its preferential use in this setting.

articles.title: Clinical Outcomes of Upper-Extremity Deep Vein Thrombosis According to Cancer Status and Catheter Association: A RIETE (Registro Informatizado de la Enfermedad TromboEmbólica) Registry Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Upper-extremity deep vein thrombosis (UEDVT) is increasingly diagnosed because of the widespread use of venous catheters, particularly in patients with cancer. However, its clinical course and the optimal duration of anticoagulant therapy remain uncertain.

METHODS: We analyzed 4979 patients with symptomatic isolated UEDVT enrolled in the Registro Informatizado de la Enfermedad TromboEmbólica, including 1383 patients with cancer and catheter-associated UEDVT, 599 with cancer and noncatheter-associated UEDVT, 921 without cancer and catheter-associated UEDVT, and 2076 without cancer and noncatheter-associated UEDVT. Outcomes included recurrent deep vein thrombosis, symptomatic pulmonary embolism, major bleeding, and all-cause mortality during anticoagulation and after treatment discontinuation. Competing-risk regression was used for thrombotic and bleeding outcomes, and Cox regression for mortality.

RESULTS: Catheter-associated UEDVT was more frequent among patients with cancer than among those without cancer (70% vs 35%). Among patients with cancer, catheter-associated UEDVT was associated with lower all-cause mortality than noncatheter-associated UEDVT (22.6 vs 55.9 deaths per 100 patient-years; adjusted hazard ratio 0.39; 95% CI 0.31-0.49) and lower recurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE) rates (6.27 vs 9.60 per 100 patient-years). Among patients without cancer, catheter-associated UEDVT was associated with higher mortality (10.7 vs 4.32 deaths per 100 patient-years) and major bleeding (2.49 vs 0.61 per 100 patient-years), whereas recurrent VTE rates were similar irrespective of catheter status. Across all 4 groups, recurrent VTE remained infrequent after anticoagulation discontinuation.

CONCLUSIONS: Clinical outcomes of UEDVT differ according to both cancer status and catheter association. The persistently low recurrence rates after anticoagulation discontinuation, particularly in catheter-associated UEDVT, support an individualized approach to anticoagulation duration.

articles.title: Association of limb fat distribution and plasma metabolites with the risk of venous thromboembolism.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a potentially life-threatening cardiovascular condition. However, the role of limb-specific fat distribution and its associated metabolomic signatures in VTE remains unclear.

OBJECTIVES: To assess associations between upper- and lower-limb fat distribution and VTE risk and to evaluate whether circulating metabolites mediate these relationships.

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study analyzed UK Biobank data, in which arm and leg fat mass were measured by bioelectrical impedance. Cox proportional hazards models and restricted cubic splines assessed sex-specific associations with incident VTE, deep vein thrombosis, and pulmonary embolism. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression was used to identify metabolites associated with arm-to-leg fat mass percentage, followed by mediation analyses.

RESULTS: Over a median follow-up of 13.6 years, 14 593 VTE events occurred among 458 651 participants. A higher arm-to-leg fat mass percentage was associated with increased VTE risk, with hazard ratios of 1.81 (95% CI, 1.63-2.00) in women and 1.55 (95% CI, 1.47-1.64) in men when comparing the highest tertile with the lowest. A total of 138 metabolites in women and 38 in men were associated with arm-to-leg fat distribution. In women, the metabolomic signature mediated 15.2% (95% CI, 6.8%-21.9%) of the association between arm-to-leg fat and VTE and 21.1% (95% CI, 12.8%-28.4%) of the corresponding association with pulmonary embolism; no significant mediation was observed in men.

CONCLUSION: Predominant upper peripheral fat distribution is associated with a high risk of VTE. Sex-specific metabolomic signatures partially mediate these associations in women, underscoring the importance of integrating limb fat distribution with metabolomics to improve VTE risk assessment.

OBJECTIVES: To assess associations between upper- and lower-limb fat distribution and VTE risk and to evaluate whether circulating metabolites mediate these relationships.

articles.title: Association of visit-to-visit blood pressure variability with kidney disease progression and cardiovascular outcomes in the chronic renal insufficiency cohort (CRIC).
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Visit-to-visit variability (VVV) of blood pressure (BP) has been linked to adverse cardiovascular and kidney outcomes in various populations, but results in those with chronic kidney disease (CKD) have been inconsistent.

METHODS: We evaluated VVV in Chronic Renal Insufficiency Cohort (CRIC) participants, using the coefficient of variation (CoV = standard deviation of SBP/mean SBP) calculated from BP measurements obtained at baseline visit through year 5 of the study. Cox proportional hazards models were used to assess the association of CoV with a composite cardiovascular outcome (myocardial infarction, stroke, peripheral artery disease, heart failure) and a composite kidney outcome (50% reduction in estimated glomerular filtration rate or end-stage kidney disease).

RESULTS: Among 3891 participants (44% women, mean age 63 ± 10 years, mean CoV 10.3 ± 5.2%), 757 cardiovascular and 920 kidney events occurred during a median follow-up of 5.4 and 4.5 years, respectively. In unadjusted analyses, the upper tertile of CoV was associated with increased risk of both cardiovascular [hazard ratio 2.04, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.70-2.43] and kidney outcomes (hazard ratio 1.62, 95% CI 1.38-1.89) compared to the lowest tertile. However, after adjustment for clinical and sociodemographic factors, higher CoV was significantly associated with cardiovascular outcomes (adjusted hazard ratio 1.25, 95% CI 1.04-1.52) but not kidney outcomes (adjusted hazard ratio 0.95, 95% CI 0.80-1.15).

CONCLUSION: In this large CKD cohort, higher visit-to-visit BP variability was independently linked to adverse cardiovascular, but not kidney, outcomes.

articles.title: Pretest direct oral anticoagulant removal is highly effective in lupus anticoagulant testing while on direct oral anticoagulants: a real-life experience.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) may cause false-positive lupus anticoagulant (LA) results by interfering with phospholipid-dependent coagulation assays. Current guidelines discourage LA testing during DOAC therapy unless anticoagulant interference is removed.

OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the real-life efficacy of routine pretest DOAC removal in LA testing.

METHODS: Consecutive DOAC-treated patients screened for LA at a tertiary center between August 2020 and December 2024 were analyzed. Blood samples were collected between 1 and 24 hours after the last DOAC dose. LA testing was performed after the DOAC-Stop (Haematex Research) treatment. Positive LA results were repeated within 1 month (≥24 hours after the last DOAC dose), and if still positive, after ≥3 months. Antiphospholipid antibodies were determined by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay.

RESULTS: Among 701 patients (51.4% women; median age 49 years [40.0-60.0]), mostly with venous thromboembolism (n = 548, 78.2%), 56 (8.0%) had positive LA screening and 31 (4.4%) had positive confirmatory tests after DOAC removal. Baseline characteristics were comparable, except for a higher proportion of women among screening-positive patients. Within 1 month, 26 of 31 patients available for retesting remained LA-positive. Persistent antiphospholipid antibody positivity after ≥12 weeks was confirmed in all 26 patients, including 19 with triple-positive antiphospholipid syndrome (APS), 4 double-positive APS, and 3 single-positive APS (isolated LA).

CONCLUSIONS: Pretest DOAC removal followed by 3-step LA testing using dilute Russell's viper venom time and activated partial thromboplastin time-based assays enabled reliable LA assessment in routine practice, with positive results observed exclusively in patients fulfilling APS criteria.
articles.englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) may cause false-positive lupus anticoagulant (LA) results by interfering with phospholipid-dependent coagulation assays. Current guidelines discourage LA testing during DOAC therapy unless anticoagulant interference is removed. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the real-life efficacy of routine pretest DOAC removal in LA testing.

articles.title: The role of antifactor Xa monitoring in the dosing and administration of low-molecular-weight heparins in pregnancy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low-molecular-weight heparins (LMWHs) are widely used in pregnancy for prevention and treatment of venous thromboembolism (VTE) and in individuals with mechanical heart valves (MHVs).

OBJECTIVES: Our aim was to determine the risk of thromboembolic complications (TECs) and major bleeding with weight-based, fixed, and anti-Xa-monitored dosing of LMWHs during pregnancy.

METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and searched 6 databases for articles published before August 2024 that reported on LMWH dosing and monitoring during pregnancy. We calculated event rates and 95% confidence intervals (95% CIs) for maternal death, TECs, and major bleeding using a random-effects meta-analysis. We assessed risk of bias using the Quality In Prognosis Studies tool and evaluated the certainty of evidence (CoE) using the Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation approach.

RESULTS: We identified 5007 studies, of which 94 (53 case series, 30 cohort studies, and 11 randomized trials) were eligible. For thromboprophylaxis and VTE treatment, fixed, weight-based, and anti-Xa-monitored LMWH doses had overlapping pooled event rates and 95% CIs for TECs and major bleeding. For MHVs, the risk of maternal death, TECs, and major bleeding was 2.7% (95% CI, 0.3%-6.5%), 7.9% (95% CI, 2.8%-14.6%), and 8.4% (95% CI, 2.0%-17.2%), respectively with overlapping pooled single-arm event rates and 95% CIs across different anti-Xa-monitored LMWH dosing regimens. The CoE for all estimates was low to very low, mainly due to imprecision, risk of bias, and publication bias.

CONCLUSION: Pooled single-arm event rates and 95% CIs for the main outcomes overlapped across LMWH dosing regimens currently used in pregnancy for thromboprophylaxis, VTE treatment, and anticoagulation in individuals with MHVs. These findings should be interpreted in light of small sample sizes, wide 95% CIs, and low CoE; and not as evidence of comparable effectiveness or safety.
articles.englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Low-molecular-weight heparins (LMWHs) are widely used in pregnancy for prevention and treatment of venous thromboembolism (VTE) and in individuals with mechanical heart valves (MHVs). OBJECTIVES: Our aim was to determine the risk of thromboembolic complications (TECs) and major bleeding with weight-based, fixed, and anti-Xa-monitored dosing of LMWHs during pregnancy. METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and searched 6 databases for articles published before August 2024 that reported on LMWH dosing and monitoring during pregnancy.

articles.title: Characterization of pulmonary embolism events in patients with suspected pneumonia.
articles.abstract: Pneumonia and pulmonary embolism (PE) share similar clinical presentations, posing a significant diagnostic challenge. We investigated whether available diagnostic modalities could identify distinct characteristics in patients suspected of pneumonia later diagnosed with PE. Patients who underwent a CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA) scan on admission were retrospectively screened for suspected pneumonia, defined as a chest X-ray infiltrate accompanied by clinical or laboratory evidence of infection. Patients with COVID-19, pregnancy, and thrombophilia were excluded. Comorbidities, clinical presentation, electrocardiograms, laboratory tests, and outcomes were compared between patients with and without PE. Among 5,522 CTPA scans, 846 patients had suspected pneumonia. 106 (12.5%) had PE. Patients with PE had a higher rate of prior venous thromboembolism (14.2% vs. 7.7%, P = 0.03). However, other risk factors and baseline anticoagulation therapy were comparable between groups. Most clinical and laboratory parameters, including CRP and D-dimer levels, were similar, as were the Wells criteria and Geneva scores. New-onset atrial fibrillation was more frequent in PE patients (11.1% vs. 5.4%, P = 0.009). Prolonged expiration and wheezing were more common in those without PE (17.9% vs. 5.7%, P = 0.0015) and remained the only discriminative parameter in a multivariate analysis (OR = 0.29, 95%CI: 0.09-0.74, P = 0.021). Notably, the presence of PE did not impact mortality rates. PE is prevalent in patients with suspected pneumonia undergoing CTPA. Clinical presentation, laboratory findings, and commonly used diagnostic tools, including the Wells criteria and the Geneva score, perform poorly in this setting. These findings underscore the need for new diagnostic approaches.
articles.englishSummary: Pneumonia and pulmonary embolism (PE) share similar clinical presentations, posing a significant diagnostic challenge. We investigated whether available diagnostic modalities could identify distinct characteristics in patients suspected of pneumonia later diagnosed with PE. Patients who underwent a CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA) scan on admission were retrospectively screened for suspected pneumonia, defined as a chest X-ray infiltrate accompanied by clinical or laboratory evidence of infection.

articles.title: Electronic Chip-Mimetic Medical Implants for Controllable Sonothermal Treatments.
articles.abstract: The sterility and controllable biological functionalities of implantable medical devices determine their lifespan, safety, and therapeutic efficacy. Inspired by the thermal effect of working electronic chips, which consist of various heterostructures, we have developed an electronic chip-mimetic sonothermal platform through constructing metal-semiconductor heterogeneous interface. Through magnetron sputtering on the surface of the sandblasted/acid-etched pretreated titanium (pTi), we find that semiconductor coatings (TiO2, Si, ZnO, and Te) endow pTi with different in situ sonothermal effects (ΔT > 18°C, 15 min) under ultrasound (US) irradiation, whereas conductor coatings do not. The sonothermal mechanism of pTi-semiconductor is associated with US-activated electron and phonon transport within the heterogeneous interface of implants, which is determined by the electrical and phonon characteristics of pTi-semiconductor, including their matching degree, thermal conductivity, defected structure, and type of semiconductor. Clinical titanium screws were introduced with defected structure in oxygen layer (TiO2-x) and bone-derived whitlockite, which shows great sonothermal/sonodynamic effects for efficient elimination of biofilm infection and improved osseointegration. In addition, the prepared NiTi-TiO2-x guidewire enables rapid thrombolysis (30 min) in the deep vein thrombosis of beagles after 10 min of sonothermal/urokinase treatment. The electronic chip-mimetic sonothermal platform provides a promising and widespread clinical application prospect.

articles.title: Socioeconomic status and its association with venous thromboembolism during pregnancy and postpartum: results from a Dutch population-based study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a leading cause of maternal morbidity and mortality. While socioeconomic status (SES) is associated with adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes, its association with pregnancy-related VTE has not been studied.

OBJECTIVES: This study aims to quantify the association between SES and pregnancy-related VTE in the Netherlands.

METHODS: We conducted a retrospective nationwide cohort study, including all pregnancies resulting in births (>16 weeks' gestation) in 2014-2015 from the Dutch Perinatal Registry (Perined). These records were anonymously linked to healthcare and sociodemographic data from Statistics Netherlands. VTE events were identified using diagnostic and International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision (ICD-10) codes. SES was assessed by equivalized disposable household income (quintiles) and maternal education levels (low, middle, and high). Associations were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier analyses and multivariable Cox regressions, adjusting for demographic, clinical, and obstetric factors.

RESULTS: Among the 334 828 included pregnancies, an absolute VTE risk of 0.31% (95% CI, 0.29-0.33) was observed. Compared with women in the highest income quintile (Q5) (0.22%, 95% CI, 0.18-0.26), those in the three lowest quintiles had higher VTE risks (Q1: 0.37%, 95% CI, 0.32-0.42, adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] 1.70, 95% CI, 1.33-2.18; Q2: 0.36%, 95% CI, 0.31-0.41, aHR 1.69, 95% CI, 1.33-2.15; Q3: 0.33%, 95% CI, 0.29-0.37, aHR 1.51, 95% CI, 1.20-1.90). Low and middle education levels were also associated with higher VTE risks (low: 0.42%, 95% CI, 0.35-0.48, aHR 1.83, 95% CI, 1.48-2.26; middle: 0.36%, 95% CI, 0.33-0.40, aHR 1.61, 95% CI, 1.37-1.89). Modeling both SES indicators concurrently and sensitivity analyses yielded similar results.

CONCLUSION: Low SES is associated with higher VTE risk during pregnancy and postpartum, highlighting persistent maternal health inequalities. Further research is needed to determine whether SES indicators improve VTE risk prediction and stratification in obstetric populations.
articles.englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a leading cause of maternal morbidity and mortality. While socioeconomic status (SES) is associated with adverse maternal and perinatal outcomes, its association with pregnancy-related VTE has not been studied. OBJECTIVES: This study aims to quantify the association between SES and pregnancy-related VTE in the Netherlands.
