articles.title: Stick or Switch: Diminishing Returns of Repeated Peripheral IV Access Attempts in Hypotensive Trauma Patients.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Peripheral IV (PIV) access is the first-line approach to vascular access in trauma patients. There is no evidence to guide clinicians on when to abandon PIV attempts in favor of alternative access. We sought to characterize PIV success rates, identify factors associated with success, and determine the marginal yield of sequential PIV attempts in hypotensive trauma patients.

STUDY DESIGN: We analyzed data from audiovisual recordings of trauma resuscitations from a multicenter, prospective study of vascular access in hypotensive (SBP <90 mmHg) patients. The primary outcome was the PIV attempt success rate. Secondary outcomes included attempt duration and cumulative patient-level success across sequential attempts. Generalized estimating equations with exchangeable correlation structure were used to account for clustering of attempts within patients.

RESULTS: A total of 886 PIV attempts occurred in 471 patients across 18 centers. The overall PIV success rate was 67.1%. Male patient sex (adjusted odds ratio 1.92, 95% CI 1.22 to 3.03, p = 0.005) and the presence of a measurable initial systolic blood pressure (adjusted odds ratio 1.84, 95% CI 1.06 to 3.20, p = 0.03) were independently associated with PIV success. The first PIV attempt was successful in 70% of patients, and cumulative success reached 83% by the second attempt. The marginal success rate among patients without earlier success dropped from 70% on the first attempt to 54% on the second and 39% on the third attempt.

CONCLUSIONS: PIV access in hypotensive trauma patients succeeds approximately two-thirds of the time. The marginal yield of sequential PIV attempts declines substantially after 2 failed attempts. These findings support the practice in which alternate vascular access, such as intraosseous access, is actively considered after a single failed PIV attempt in patients without a measurable blood pressure.
articles.englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Peripheral IV (PIV) access is the first-line approach to vascular access in trauma patients. There is no evidence to guide clinicians on when to abandon PIV attempts in favor of alternative access. We sought to characterize PIV success rates, identify factors associated with success, and determine the marginal yield of sequential PIV attempts in hypotensive trauma patients.

articles.title: Biological sex differences in the United States CTEPH Registry.
articles.abstract:
RATIONALE: Biological sex underpins phenotypic differences in many cardiopulmonary conditions. In pulmonary hypertension, most studies have focused on the "sex paradox" in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), where females are more susceptible to PAH but have better right ventricular function, better response to PAH medications, and better survival than males. Sex differences have also been observed in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) but are less well characterized.

OBJECTIVES: To investigate sex differences in males and females diagnosed with CTEPH in the United States.

METHODS: Using the multicenter United States CTEPH Registry, we explored sex differences in a CTEPH population at baseline and follow-up. We collected data every 6 months for a total of 48 months. Sex was determined from self-reported "male," "female," or "transgender" categories recorded on case report forms. We report descriptive analyses comparing male and female characteristics. We examined prespecified variables of interest using regression modeling, including adjustment for age, body mass index (BMI), and interaction terms (sex vs age, sex vs BMI). Survival analysis was performed with Cox proportional hazards modeling.

RESULTS: Females (n = 367, 49.1%) had greater BMI than males (median [IQR] F: 32 kg/m2 [26.6, 38.8] vs M: 28.7 kg/m2 [25.5, 33.8]). Males were more likely to have a recognized history of acute deep vein thrombosis (OR 2.6; CI 1.9-3.5). Males had better baseline PH-specific health-related quality of life (HRQoL) by EmPHasis10 (-3.3; CI -5.0- (-1.7), World Health Organization functional class (FC III/IV OR 0.52, CI 0.37-0.74) and longer 6-minute walk distance (+82.3 m, CI 56.4-108.2). Males were less likely to have distally located disease (OR 0.53, CI 0.35-0.78) and were less likely to have inoperable CTEPH (OR 0.62, CI 0.40-0.96). Post-PTE, females had persistently worse HRQoL and function, with increased need for adjunctive therapies. There was no difference in overall survival between males and females (HR 1.11; CI 0.71-1.75).

CONCLUSIONS: Males and females may have distinct CTEPH phenotypes, which impact access to and feasibility of PTE. There are sex-associated disparities in the experience of CTEPH as a disease state, and differential impacts on HRQoL that warrant further investigation.
articles.englishSummary: RATIONALE: Biological sex underpins phenotypic differences in many cardiopulmonary conditions. In pulmonary hypertension, most studies have focused on the "sex paradox" in pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), where females are more susceptible to PAH but have better right ventricular function, better response to PAH medications, and better survival than males. Sex differences have also been observed in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) but are less well characterized.

articles.title: Predictors of Delayed Ischaemic Stroke following Thoracic Endovascular Aortic Repair for Blunt Thoracic Aortic Injury.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Delayed ischaemic stroke (DIS) remains a feared complication following thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) for blunt thoracic aortic injury (BTAI), particularly when the left subclavian artery (LSCA) is covered. This study aimed to understand the impact of LSCA revascularisation and other peri-operative factors on delayed stroke risk.

METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study querying the Aortic Trauma Foundation registry to identify patients with BTAI undergoing TEVAR from 2014 to 2025. Patients with DIS after TEVAR were identified, and patient level factors, intra-operative data, and post-operative course variables were analysed.

RESULTS: Six hundred and twenty TEVARs for BTAI were identified. The overall DIS rate was 3.1% (19 of 620). LSCA coverage occurred in 32.6% (202 of 620) and was associated with a significantly higher rate of DIS (5.4% vs. 1.9%; p = .017). Adjunctive LSCA revascularisation during or after TEVAR was undertaken in 11.4% (23 of 202) of patients. Among patients requiring LSCA coverage (n = 202), there was no significant difference in the incidence of DIS between those who underwent adjunctive revascularisation (one of 23; 4.3%) and those who did not (10 of 179; 5.6%) (p = .81). Factors associated with DIS included the need for any intra-operative transfusion, mechanical ventilation > 48 hours, and initial post-TEVAR pressor requirement. Traumatic brain injury related factors, age, sex, and TEVAR timing were not identified as being associated with an increased DIS risk.

CONCLUSION: LSCA coverage during TEVAR for BTAI is associated with a significant increase in DIS rates. These data do not, however, demonstrate that LSCA revascularisation procedures mitigate the risk of these events in this setting. These findings may be limited by the small number of revascularised patients. Peri-operative physiological indicators emerge as the most reliable predictors of DIS in acute trauma, supporting an individualised approach where global trauma burden is considered a primary driver of neurological outcomes.
articles.englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Delayed ischaemic stroke (DIS) remains a feared complication following thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) for blunt thoracic aortic injury (BTAI), particularly when the left subclavian artery (LSCA) is covered. This study aimed to understand the impact of LSCA revascularisation and other peri-operative factors on delayed stroke risk. METHODS: This was a retrospective cohort study querying the Aortic Trauma Foundation registry to identify patients with BTAI undergoing TEVAR from 2014 to 2025.

articles.title: Long Term Risk of Clinical Recurrence following Endovenous Laser Ablation of the Great Saphenous Vein with 810 nm Laser Bare Tip Fibre: An Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Varicose veins are highly prevalent and most patients present with great saphenous vein (GSV) reflux. Treatment of truncal venous reflux is the cornerstone in the management of C2 disease. Endovenous laser ablation (EVLA) is widely accepted as the preferred treatment. This study aimed to estimate the long term risk of clinical recurrence in the treated leg after successful EVLA of the GSV.

METHODS: This single centre, observational study included patients with C2 varicose veins in whom refluxing GSV was diagnosed. EVLA was performed from 10 - 15 cm below the knee and occlusion was confirmed with duplex after three months. Additional treatment after EVLA was always in a staged approach. Clinical recurrence was defined as a patient actively seeking re-treatment at least six months after EVLA for symptoms due to varicose veins in the treated leg. Recurrence was identified through electronic health records or, when not documented, by telephonic survey.

RESULTS: The study included 543 patients with a median follow up of 6.0 (interquartile range 1.3, 10.3) years. The mean age at treatment was 52.8 ± 13.3 years and 79.2% were women. Clinical recurrence occurred in 210 patients, with an estimated ten year recurrence rate of 47.6% (95% confidence interval 42.5 - 52.1%). Additional therapy within six months following EVLA was associated with a hazard ratio of 1.31 (95% confidence 0.99 - 1.72; p = .055), adjusted for age and sex.

CONCLUSION: Clinical recurrence after EVLA of the GSV occurred in approximately half of patients within ten years of the procedure, exceeding rates reported with concomitant additional treatment and EVLA of the entire refluxing GSV. The association between early additional therapy and a higher recurrence rate suggests that it may indicate an unmet therapeutic need.
articles.englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Varicose veins are highly prevalent and most patients present with great saphenous vein (GSV) reflux. Treatment of truncal venous reflux is the cornerstone in the management of C2 disease. Endovenous laser ablation (EVLA) is widely accepted as the preferred treatment.

articles.title: Survival assessment of warfarin and international normalized ratio exposure in cancer-associated venous thromboembolism: Veterans Affairs healthcare systembased analysis.
articles.abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a common complication among patients with cancer. While randomized clinical trials have established the safety and efficacy of direct oral anticoagulants (DOAC) and low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) relative to warfarin for the treatment of cancer-associated thrombosis, emerging evidence suggests that warfarin may be associated with improved overall survival in patients with malignancy. We evaluated survival outcomes among patients with cancer and VTE treated with warfarin compared with other anticoagulants within the Veterans Affairs (VA) Healthcare System and analyzed the association of international normalized ratio (INR) exposure and overall survival. Among 12,298 propensity-matched patients (mean age 69 years; 97% men), warfarin use was associated with a 16% lower risk of mortality compared with other anticoagulants (hazard ratio [HR]=0.84; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.80-0.88; P <0 .001). Median survival was 1,457 days in the warfarin group versus 1,045 days in the non-warfarin group. Survival benefits were consistent across subgroups defined by tumor type, stage, and demographic characteristics. In landmark analyses, the greatest benefit was observed with extended periods in the INR range of 2.5 to 3.0 (HR=0.81; 95% CI: 0.75-0.87). In this population-based cohort study of patients with cancer and VTE, warfarin use was associated with improved survival compared with other anticoagulants. The greatest benefit was observed among patients who maintained an INR between 2.5 and 3.0.
articles.englishSummary: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a common complication among patients with cancer. While randomized clinical trials have established the safety and efficacy of direct oral anticoagulants (DOAC) and low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) relative to warfarin for the treatment of cancer-associated thrombosis, emerging evidence suggests that warfarin may be associated with improved overall survival in patients with malignancy. We evaluated survival outcomes among patients with cancer and VTE treated with warfarin compared with other anticoagulants within the Veterans Affairs (VA) Healthcare System and analyzed the association of international normalized ratio (INR) exposure and overall survival.

articles.title: Ultrasound Strain Patterns are Associated with Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm Growth.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Surveillance of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs) traditionally relies on diameter measurements, yet up to 10% of ruptures occur below repair thresholds. The relationship between localised wall strain and future AAA growth remains unexplored. This study aimed to examine localised AAA wall strain patterns and their association with aneurysm growth.

METHODS: This was a prospective study of patients with an infrarenal AAA under surveillance with conventional ultrasound. In a standard examination, ten second ultrasound videos (cineloops) were acquired in transverse plane with the curved array transducer at the maximum anteroposterior diameter during breath hold. From these cineloops, strain patterns were extracted and analysed via functional data analysis to assess changes over time and associations with annual AAA diameter growth.

RESULTS: Two hundred and seventy-eight patients (median age 73 years; 238 men) across 1 117 clinic visits were included, with a median follow up of 2.3 years. Progressive vessel wall stiffening and increasingly homogeneous strain patterns were observed over time (p < .001). Baseline strain patterns were statistically significantly associated with future AAA growth (p = .006), especially in specific regions. In the posterior left and right vessel wall, a 5% point increase in strain corresponded to a 31.9% and 6.7% higher annual growth rate, respectively. Conversely, the same increase at the anterior middle wall was linked to a 33.3% reduction in annual growth rate. These associations remained statistically significant after adjusting for baseline diameter, age, sex, smoking, hypertension, and diabetes (p = .041).

CONCLUSION: Ultrasound strain mapping identified biomechanical regions linked to AAA progression. Strain patterns were associated with future growth independently of diameter, supporting their potential utility in complementing diameter in AAA monitoring and risk stratification.
articles.englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Surveillance of abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAAs) traditionally relies on diameter measurements, yet up to 10% of ruptures occur below repair thresholds. The relationship between localised wall strain and future AAA growth remains unexplored. This study aimed to examine localised AAA wall strain patterns and their association with aneurysm growth.

articles.title: Editor's Choice - Five Year Follow Up of Mechanochemical Ablation for the Treatment of Small Saphenous Vein Incompetence.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to assess the effectiveness of mechanochemical ablation (MOCA) for the treatment of small saphenous vein (SSV) incompetence at three and five years, building on preliminary results that showed feasibility, safety, and high occlusion rates at one year follow up.

METHODS: Sixty patients who underwent MOCA for SSV incompetence at a single centre between January 2017 and December 2019 were included. Clinical and radiological data were reviewed retrospectively from a prospectively maintained database. Primary endpoints were SSV recanalisation and re-intervention at three and five years. Additional outcome measures included Venous Clinical Severity Score (VCSS), quality of life (QoL) using the Aberdeen Varicose Vein Questionnaire (AVVQ) and the visual analogue scale to assess pain during long term follow up, and signs and symptoms of chronic venous disease. Uni- and multivariable analyses were performed to identify risk factors for SSV recanalisation.

RESULTS: Fifty patients completed the full five year follow up. Freedom from recanalisation was 84.7% at three years and 66.5% at five years. Freedom from re-intervention at the same time points was 86.7% and 72.6%, respectively. Although the VCSS and AVVQ scores decreased during the first year, a progressive increase was observed over the follow up period. The median VCSS increased significantly at three and five years. The AVVQ score increased from a median (interquartile range [IQR]) of 5.0 (IQR 3.0, 7.0) at one year to 8.2 (IQR 5.0, 11.0) at three years and 10.1 (IQR 6.0, 14.0) at five years (p < .001). Multivariable analysis identified body mass index > 25 kg/m2 and pre-operative SSV diameter > 6 mm as significant risk factors for SSV recanalisation.

CONCLUSION: Treatment of SSV incompetence with MOCA had high five year recanalisation and re-intervention rates. Additionally, a progressive decrease in QoL and deterioration of patient reported outcomes over time were found, as reflected by rising VCSS and AVVQ scores.
articles.englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to assess the effectiveness of mechanochemical ablation (MOCA) for the treatment of small saphenous vein (SSV) incompetence at three and five years, building on preliminary results that showed feasibility, safety, and high occlusion rates at one year follow up. METHODS: Sixty patients who underwent MOCA for SSV incompetence at a single centre between January 2017 and December 2019 were included. Clinical and radiological data were reviewed retrospectively from a prospectively maintained database.

articles.title: Intimo-Intimal Intussusception during Endovascular Repair of Type B Aortic Dissection.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Stent graft induced aortic intimo-intimal intussusception (SAoII) during thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) of type B aortic dissection (TBAD) is a rare complication. This study aimed to report reliable imaging features of SAoII to avoid such a potentially catastrophic event. This retrospective, multicentre observational analysis was registered as a Chinese Clinical Trial (ChiCTR2300073780).

METHODS: Patients undergoing TEVAR for TBAD in three centres were reviewed from January 2014 to December 2022. SAoII was defined as intra-procedural partial or circumferential disruption of the aortic intima because of TEVAR, excluding those created by natural disease progression. The imaging features and management of SAoII were summarised.

RESULTS: 1 643 patients undergoing TEVAR for TBAD were reviewed. Among them, SAoII was observed in 20 patients (mean age, 44.5 ± 11.8 years; 16 men). TEVAR was performed in the acute phase (eight of 20), subacute phase (11 of 20), or chronic phase (one of 20). Imaging features including displacement of the intima, wire, or delivery system were observed in eight (40%), floating endograft in 17 (85%), intussusception of the intima layer in 13 (65%), true lumen occlusions and visceral artery loss in three (15%), and a single lumen without intimal septa in three (15%) patients. SAoII was observed in 60% (12 of 20) after deployment of the stent graft, in 20% (four of 20) after introduction of a stent graft delivery system, and in 20% (four of 20) after the introduction of a super stiff wire. All patients who developed SAoII were endovascularly managed by an additional stent graft; no aortic related death was observed among these patients with SAoII during the median follow up of 51.5 months.

CONCLUSION: SAoII is a rare but potentially fatal iatrogenic complication during or after TEVAR; endovascular interventions could be effective to manage this acute complication. Timely and accurate identification of decisive imaging features are key to successful treatment.
articles.englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Stent graft induced aortic intimo-intimal intussusception (SAoII) during thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) of type B aortic dissection (TBAD) is a rare complication. This study aimed to report reliable imaging features of SAoII to avoid such a potentially catastrophic event. This retrospective, multicentre observational analysis was registered as a Chinese Clinical Trial (ChiCTR2300073780).

articles.title: Editor's Choice - Clinical Impacts of Sodium-Glucose Co-Transporter 2 Inhibitors in Diabetic Patients with Chronic Limb Threatening Ischaemia Undergoing Endovascular Therapy: Results of the SIRIUS Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Although sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors are effective treatments, their use may be associated with increased risk of lower limb amputation. Moreover, no studies have reported on their clinical safety and efficacy in patients with chronic limb threatening ischaemia (CLTI). Therefore, this multicentre retrospective observational study evaluated their clinical efficacy in diabetic patients with CLTI who underwent endovascular therapy (EVT).

METHODS: Eligible patients with diabetes and CLTI were identified retrospectively between January 2021 and December 2023 from a multicentre Japanese EVT registry. The patients were divided into two groups based on whether or not they received treatment with SGLT2 inhibitors. The clinical safety and efficacy of SGLT2 inhibitors was evaluated after propensity score matching (PSM). The primary outcome was freedom from major amputation within one year. Secondary endpoints were amputation free survival, all cause death, wound healing, cardiovascular death, and infection related death within one year.

RESULTS: Among 257 patients, 51 matched pairs were analysed after PSM, with no baseline differences between groups. One year freedom from major amputation was similar (94.0% vs. 86.8%; p = .30), whereas amputation free survival was statistically significantly better in the SGLT2 inhibitor group (88.3% vs. 71.3%; p = .030). The all cause mortality rate was also lower with SGLT2 inhibitors (4.7% vs. 18.7%; p = .030). Wound healing (82.8% vs. 69.7%; p = .49), cardiovascular mortality (0.0% vs. 7.0%; p = .070), and infection related mortality (2.2% vs. 6.1%; p = .31) did not differ statistically significantly between the groups.

CONCLUSION: SGLT2 inhibitors may not be associated with an increased risk of major lower limb amputation in patients with CLTI undergoing EVT. These agents may be associated with improved clinical outcomes in this population.
articles.englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Although sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors are effective treatments, their use may be associated with increased risk of lower limb amputation. Moreover, no studies have reported on their clinical safety and efficacy in patients with chronic limb threatening ischaemia (CLTI). Therefore, this multicentre retrospective observational study evaluated their clinical efficacy in diabetic patients with CLTI who underwent endovascular therapy (EVT).

articles.title: Pedal Artery Angioplasty Increases Wound Recurrence after Complete Wound Healing by Endovascular Therapy in Patients with Chronic Limb Threatening Ischaemia: Results of the SAVEPEDAL Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: In patients with chronic limb threatening ischaemia (CLTI), pedal artery angioplasty (PAA) is widely known to improve wound healing, but inframalleolar revascularisation may worsen arterial lesion morphology and lead to wound recurrence after healing. This retrospective cohort study aimed to clarify the effects of PAA on wound recurrence after wound healing.

METHODS: Consecutive limbs with CLTI (n = 534) secondary to infrapopliteal and pedal artery disease that underwent endovascular therapy (EVT) and achieved complete wound healing at eight cardiovascular centres in Japan were analysed (March 2021 - December 2023). Limbs were divided into two groups according to whether PAA was performed (n = 89) or not (n = 445).

RESULTS: Propensity score matching extracted 160 matched limbs that had no remarkable intergroup differences in patient and lesion characteristics. The wound recurrence rate at one year was statistically significantly higher in the PAA group than in the non-PAA group (51.4% vs. 23.5%; p < .001). Low serum albumin level, haemodialysis, good pedal artery type before EVT, and low small artery disease score showed significant interaction effects on wound recurrence, favouring non-PAA over PAA. Subanalysis of changes in plantar arch artery morphology before EVT and during repeat angiography at the time of wound recurrence showed statistically significantly more frequent deterioration of plantar arch artery morphology in the PAA group than in the non-PAA group (p = .020).

CONCLUSION: This study showed a significantly greater wound recurrence rate and more frequent deterioration of plantar arch artery morphology after PAA than after a non-PAA treatment in patients with CLTI.
articles.englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: In patients with chronic limb threatening ischaemia (CLTI), pedal artery angioplasty (PAA) is widely known to improve wound healing, but inframalleolar revascularisation may worsen arterial lesion morphology and lead to wound recurrence after healing. This retrospective cohort study aimed to clarify the effects of PAA on wound recurrence after wound healing. METHODS: Consecutive limbs with CLTI (n = 534) secondary to infrapopliteal and pedal artery disease that underwent endovascular therapy (EVT) and achieved complete wound healing at eight cardiovascular centres in Japan were analysed (March 2021 - December 2023).

articles.title: Outcomes after Endovascular Arch Repair in Patients with a Native Ascending Aorta Diameter Greater than 38 mm: An Observational Study in Two High Volume Centres.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to evaluate early outcomes of endovascular aortic arch repair using custom made stent grafts in patients with a native ascending aortic diameter > 38 mm.

METHODS: This two centre, retrospective observational study included all consecutive patients who underwent endovascular arch repair with custom made arch branched stent grafts for a native ascending aorta diameter > 38 mm.

RESULTS: From July 2018 to April 2025, 228 patients were treated with an arch branch device; 25 of these patients (median age 68.9 years; 68% men) with a native ascending aorta diameter > 38 mm (mean 41.28 ± 2.94 mm) (14% of total cohort) underwent endovascular arch repair for thoracic aortic aneurysm (n = 19, 76%), aortic dissection (n = 3, 12%), or penetrating ulcer (n = 3, 12%). Nine procedures (36%) were performed under urgent conditions. The mean proximal oversizing was 13%. Technical success was achieved in 96%, with one intra-operative death caused by retrograde type A dissection. No intra-operative stroke or type I or III endoleak was observed. Within 30 days, major and minor strokes occurred in 8% (n = 2) and 12% (n = 3) of patients, respectively. Spinal cord ischaemia and retrograde type A dissection were each observed in three cases. The 30 day mortality rate was 40% (elective 24%, n = 6; urgent 16%, n = 4). Aortic related deaths included retrograde type A dissection (n = 3) and cardiac tamponade (n = 2). Myocardial infarctions (n = 2) were also observed. Additional deaths were attributed to stroke, pulmonary embolism, or unknown causes. Most deaths occurred within the first post-operative week.

CONCLUSION: Endovascular arch repair using custom made branched endografts in patients with a dilated native ascending aorta (> 38 mm) is technically feasible but often performed in urgent settings and associated with substantial early morbidity and mortality. These findings underscore the importance of careful patient selection, meticulous planning, and performance in experienced aortic centres where open repair should be considered when feasible. Continued device optimisation is essential before wider clinical application.

METHODS: This two centre, retrospective observational study included all consecutive patients who underwent endovascular arch repair with custom made arch branched stent grafts for a native ascending aorta diameter > 38 mm. RESULTS: From July 2018 to April 2025, 228 patients were treated with an arch branch device; 25 of these patients (median age 68.9 years; 68% men) with a native ascending aorta diameter > 38 mm (mean 41.28 ± 2.94 mm) (14% of total cohort) underwent endovascular arch repair for thoracic aortic aneurysm (n = 19, 76%), aortic dissection (n = 3, 12%), or penetrating ulcer (n = 3, 12%).

articles.title: A Comprehensive Longitudinal Evaluation of Pre-operative and Post-operative Plasma Matrix Metalloproteinases for Identifying Patients at Increased Risk of Endoleak after Endovascular Aneurysm Repair.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate whether plasma concentrations of a comprehensive panel of matrix metalloproteinases (MMPs), measured at baseline and during follow up, are associated with the development of endoleak after endovascular aortic repair (EVAR), and to establish clinically relevant thresholds for post-operative risk stratification.

METHODS: This was a prospective, single centre, observational cohort study including 100 consecutive patients undergoing elective infrarenal EVAR between July 2022 and July 2024. Plasma levels of nine MMP isoforms (MMP-1, MMP-2, MMP-3, MMP-7, MMP-8, MMP-9, MMP-10, MMP-12, and MMP-13) were quantified using an enzyme linked immunosorbent assay at baseline, seven days, six and 12 months. Endoleak was diagnosed on scheduled computed tomography angiography at one, six, and 12 months, independently adjudicated by two radiologists blinded to biochemical data. Associations between MMP concentrations and endoleak were analysed with independent t tests, effect sizes, and multivariable logistic regression. Predictive accuracy was assessed with receiver operating characteristic curves, and optimal cutoff values were derived using the Youden index.

RESULTS: During follow up, 24 patients developed endoleak. Pre-operatively, MMP-1 and MMP-2 levels were statistically significantly higher in the endoleak group (p < .010). At seven days, MMP-1 and MMP-9 were the strongest discriminators (p < .001), while at 12 months, MMP-9 and MMP-10 remained independently associated with endoleak (p < .010). Combined models consistently outperformed individual biomarkers, with areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.880 (MMP-1 + MMP-2, baseline), 0.827 (MMP-1 + MMP-9, seven days), and 0.861 (MMP-9 + MMP-10, 12 months). Clinically relevant cutoff values were identified: ∼15 μg/mL for MMP-1 at baseline, ∼42 μg/mL for MMP-9 at seven days, and ∼2 μg/mL for MMP-10 at 12 months.

CONCLUSION: A dynamic biomarker profile, MMP-1 and MMP-2 pre-operatively, MMP-1 and MMP-9 early post-operatively, and MMP-9 and MMP-10 at late follow up, accurately identified patients at risk of endoleak. Incorporating MMP measurements into follow up protocols may complement imaging and enable personalised surveillance after EVAR.

METHODS: This was a prospective, single centre, observational cohort study including 100 consecutive patients undergoing elective infrarenal EVAR between July 2022 and July 2024. Plasma levels of nine MMP isoforms (MMP-1, MMP-2, MMP-3, MMP-7, MMP-8, MMP-9, MMP-10, MMP-12, and MMP-13) were quantified using an enzyme linked immunosorbent assay at baseline, seven days, six and 12 months.

articles.title: Endovascular First Approach for Acute Embolic Mesenteric Ischaemia: A 15 Year Single Centre Retrospective Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the outcomes of endovascular treatment as the first line approach for acute mesenteric ischaemia (AMI) caused by embolic occlusion of the mesenteric arteries.

METHODS: This retrospective, single centre study included consecutive patients with occlusive AMI between 2009 and 2024. Patients with acute embolic occlusion of the mesenteric artery were included, whereas patients with thrombotic AMI were excluded. The diagnosis was confirmed by computed tomography, intra-operative findings, or autopsy. The main outcomes included rates of technical success, endovascular procedure related complications, 30 day mortality, laparotomy, and bowel resection.

RESULTS: Of 63 patients with embolic AMI (mean age 79 ± 12 years), 15 were treated without attempted revascularisation, of whom three survived. Forty-eight patients (76%, mean age 79 ± 11 years) underwent endovascular revascularisation as the first line treatment, with technical success in 47 (98%). Mechanical aspiration was performed in 45 patients, with additional balloon angioplasty in four, stenting in nine, thrombolysis in three, and stent retriever thrombectomy in three. Plain stent placement without aspiration was performed in three patients. Laparotomy was performed in 19 patients (40%) undergoing endovascular treatment; six had clinical signs of peritonitis (13%) and 11 (23%) required bowel resection. Seven patients (15%) had endovascular procedure related complications (superior mesenteric artery dissection in five, access site bleeding in one, and access site pseudoaneurysm in another patient). Of the 48 patients treated with endovascular revascularisation, 21 (44%) died within 30 days. Factors prominently associated with early death after endovascular revascularisation in univariable analysis were older age (p = .001), clinical signs of peritonitis (p = .003), decreased bowel wall enhancement (p = .004), increased lactate level (p = .006), low bicarbonate level (p = .008), and low base excess (p = .009).

CONCLUSION: An endovascular first approach was suitable for most patients, with good technical success and acceptable mortality rates considering the high mean age of the non-selected patients with embolic AMI. Forty percent underwent laparotomy after endovascular treatment, whereas all patients would have required laparotomy if treated with open embolectomy.
articles.englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the outcomes of endovascular treatment as the first line approach for acute mesenteric ischaemia (AMI) caused by embolic occlusion of the mesenteric arteries. METHODS: This retrospective, single centre study included consecutive patients with occlusive AMI between 2009 and 2024. Patients with acute embolic occlusion of the mesenteric artery were included, whereas patients with thrombotic AMI were excluded.

articles.title: Anatomic Feasibility of a Specifically Designed Custom Made Device as Off the Shelf Endograft for Urgent Repair of Complex Abdominal Aortic Aneurysm.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the theoretical anatomic feasibility of a specifically designed custom made device with one fenestration for the superior mesenteric artery, two inner branches for the renals, and an incorporated distal bifurcated device (Cook Medical, Brisbane, Australia), to be developed as an off the shelf endograft for endovascular repair of urgent complex abdominal aortic aneurysm (cAAA).

METHODS: This was a retrospective single centre study. Pre-operative computed tomography angiograms (CTAs) of consecutive patients treated for cAAA by open or endovascular repair were reviewed. CTAs were collected and analysed retrospectively. Theoretical feasibility was determined based on pre-determined anatomic inclusion and exclusion criteria for access, aortic (proximal and paravisceral diameter), and target vessel characteristics. A description of the technical feasibility in an urgent real world clinical case is also provided, where the coeliac trunk was bridged through an additional physician modified reinforced fenestration.

RESULTS: A total of 250 CTAs were evaluated, including 92 juxtarenal abdominal aortic aneurysms (JRAAs), 84 pararenal abdominal aortic aneurysms (PRAAs), and 74 extent IV thoraco-abdominal aneurysms (type IV). Overall feasibility was 60.8% (69% in JRAA, 65% in PRAA, and 53% in type IV). Access feasibility was 90.2% and aortic feasibility was 67.2%; target vessel feasibility was 73.2% and when stratified by subgroup it was 77% in type IV, 82% in PRAA, and 79% in JRAA (p = .73). Type IV had lower overall feasibility compared with PRAA and JRAA (p = .030), which was mainly related to a lower aortic feasibility owing to a paravisceral aortic diameter > 40 mm (7%) or diameter of the proximal landing zone > 34 mm (6%).

CONCLUSION: This newly proposed, specifically designed custom made device demonstrated broad versatility for different anatomies improving the theoretical applicability in an extensive cohort of cAAA. Clinical application needs to be developed to evaluate safety and efficacy.

METHODS: This was a retrospective single centre study. Pre-operative computed tomography angiograms (CTAs) of consecutive patients treated for cAAA by open or endovascular repair were reviewed.

articles.title: Mortality Following Recurrent Venous Thromboembolism and Major Bleeding Stratified by Active Cancer Status.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE) and major bleeding are serious complications after acute VTE. However, their independent impact on subsequent mortality in the era of direct oral anticoagulants remains unclear, particularly with respect to differences between patients with and without active cancer.

OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate the associations of recurrent VTE and major bleeding with subsequent mortality in the overall cohort and subgroups stratified by active cancer.

METHODS: We analyzed 5,197 patients with VTE from the COMMAND VTE Registry-2 using multivariable Cox proportional hazards models with recurrent VTE and major bleeding as time-updated covariates.

RESULTS: In the overall cohort, 283 patients developed recurrent VTE, 470 developed major bleeding, and 1,323 died. Recurrent VTE and major bleeding were associated with mortality (adjusted HR: 1.65, 95% CI: 1.28-2.12, P < 0.001; adjusted HR: 3.33, 95% CI: 2.83-3.91, P < 0.001, respectively). Among patients with active cancer, both recurrent VTE and major bleeding were associated with mortality (adjusted HR: 1.95, 95% CI: 1.45-2.62, P < 0.001; adjusted HR: 2.96, 95% CI: 2.42-3.61, P < 0.001, respectively). Among patients without active cancer, only major bleeding was associated with mortality (adjusted HR: 3.78, 95% CI: 2.88-4.97, P < 0.001), whereas recurrent VTE was not associated with mortality (adjusted HR: 0.93, 95% CI: 0.55-1.56, P = 0.78).

CONCLUSIONS: In contemporary real-world patients with VTE in the era of direct oral anticoagulants, major bleeding was associated with increased subsequent mortality in both patients with and without active cancer, whereas recurrent VTE was associated with increased mortality in patients with active cancer, with no significant association observed in those without active cancer.
articles.englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Recurrent venous thromboembolism (VTE) and major bleeding are serious complications after acute VTE. However, their independent impact on subsequent mortality in the era of direct oral anticoagulants remains unclear, particularly with respect to differences between patients with and without active cancer. OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to evaluate the associations of recurrent VTE and major bleeding with subsequent mortality in the overall cohort and subgroups stratified by active cancer.

articles.title: Imaging-Based Assessment of Plaque Modification Following Intravascular Lithotripsy in Femoropopliteal Disease: A Prospective Single-Centre Observational Study.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) is designed to treat calcified peripheral arteries with steno-occlusive disease; however, its effect on plaque morphology remains incompletely understood in vivo. This study evaluated plaque modification and luminal changes following IVL in femoropopliteal disease using computed tomography angiography (CTA) and intravascular ultrasound (IVUS).

METHODS: This was a prospective single centre observational study. Consecutive patients with symptomatic femoropopliteal disease undergoing IVL between December 2024 and October 2025 underwent pre- and post-procedural (within five days) CTA with quantitative plaque analysis. IVUS was performed before and immediately after IVL, prior to drug coated balloon angioplasty (applied in all patients) or stenting (used only as bailout). The primary endpoint was change in calcified plaque volume on CTA. Secondary endpoints included luminal gain, haemodynamic changes, procedural success, and 6 month clinical outcomes.

RESULTS: Thirty nine patients were included; median age was 71 years. Calcified plaque volume showed a modest reduction (median proportional reduction 12.2%, p < .001) on post-procedural CTA. IVL resulted in luminal expansion, with IVUS measured lumen area increasing from 5.78 to 16.11 mm2 (p < .001) immediately after IVL alone and CTA intraluminal volume increasing 52.7% (median). Haemodynamic improvement was observed (ankle brachial index: 0.80 to 1.00 (median); toe brachial index: 0.40 to 0.62 (median); p <.001) between baseline and 30 days. Intra-procedural dissections were detected in 18% of cases on IVUS; only two lesions (5%) were flow limiting and required stenting. At 30 days, no mortality or target lesion revascularisations were observed, while restenosis at 6 months occurred in 5% of cases. Chronic total occlusion was associated with residual stenosis in multivariable analysis (OR 6.2, 95% CI 1.11 - 34.48, p = .038).

CONCLUSIONS: IVL was associated with modest apparent plaque modification and significant luminal gain in calcified femoropopliteal lesions. Combined CTA and IVUS imaging suggest luminal expansion is primarily driven by plaque fracture, altered vessel compliance, and remodelling rather than debulking.
articles.englishSummary: OBJECTIVE: Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) is designed to treat calcified peripheral arteries with steno-occlusive disease; however, its effect on plaque morphology remains incompletely understood in vivo. This study evaluated plaque modification and luminal changes following IVL in femoropopliteal disease using computed tomography angiography (CTA) and intravascular ultrasound (IVUS). METHODS: This was a prospective single centre observational study.

articles.title: Safety of Janus kinase inhibitors, ustekinumab, and anti-interleukin-23 in older patients with immune-mediated diseases.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Data on the safety of newer advanced therapies (AT) for immune-mediated inflammatory diseases (IMIDs) remain limited in older patients, and how the underlying IMID type influences treatment safety is unknown.

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed/MEDLINE and Embase for studies evaluating the safety of anti-IL12/23 and -IL23 agents, and JAKi in older patients with IMIDs, including inflammatory bowel disease, rheumatoid arthritis, and psoriasis. Eligible studies included patients who initiated therapy at age ≥50 years and reported outcomes in comparison with (1) younger patients receiving the same therapy, (2) older patients receiving non-AT, or (3) older patients receiving a different AT. Data on infections, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), venous thromboembolism (VTE), malignancy, and mortality were extracted. Pooled odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated using a DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model.

RESULTS: Seventy-nine studies were included. Compared to other AT, JAKi were associated with a higher risk of infections (OR 1.38; 95% CI, 1.22-1.55) and serious infections (1.27; 1.06-1.52). No increase in MACE, VTE, or malignancy risk was seen overall. Among adults > 60 years, there was an increased risk of VTE in rheumatologic cohorts (3.28; 1.16-9.27) that was absent in IBD (0.99; 0.58-1.70) (p for difference = 0.045). Compared with anti-TNF, Anti-IL-12/23 and -IL-23 agents had a lower risk of serious infections (0.76; 0.68-0.84).

CONCLUSION: In older patients with IMIDs, anti-IL-12/23 and -IL-23 agents had lower serious infection risk while JAKi had an increased risk. JAKi showed a possible disease-specific thromboembolic signal in rheumatologic but not IBD cohorts.

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed/MEDLINE and Embase for studies evaluating the safety of anti-IL12/23 and -IL23 agents, and JAKi in older patients with IMIDs, including inflammatory bowel disease, rheumatoid arthritis, and psoriasis. Eligible studies included patients who initiated therapy at age ≥50 years and reported outcomes in comparison with (1) younger patients receiving the same therapy, (2) older patients receiving non-AT, or (3) older patients receiving a different AT.

articles.title: CDC48 protein regulates the turnover of peroxisomal catalase in tobacco.
articles.abstract: In plant cells, protein homeostasis is tightly regulated to prevent imbalances between protein synthesis and degradation that can lead to proteotoxic stress. Protein turnover is largely maintained by the ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS), with the AAA+ ATPase CDC48 facilitating the extraction and processing of ubiquitinated substrates. Previous studies identified redox-related proteins as plant CDC48 partners. Here, using tobacco cell lines overexpressing CDC48, we identified the peroxisomal catalase CAT1 as a substrate of CDC48-dependent turnover. CDC48 overexpression markedly reduced CAT1 abundance and activity, indicating post-translational regulation. CAT1 undergoes extensive polyubiquitination, and was rapidly degraded in a CDC48-dependent manner. Inhibition of deubiquitinating enzymes or CDC48 ATPase activity both led to the accumulation of ubiquitinated CAT1. Finally, CDC48 overexpression, which leads to reduced CAT1 levels, correlated with impaired peroxisomal function. These findings reveal a role for CDC48 in regulating peroxisomal protein turnover in tobacco.

Protein turnover is largely maintained by the ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS), with the AAA+ ATPase CDC48 facilitating the extraction and processing of ubiquitinated substrates. Previous studies identified redox-related proteins as plant CDC48 partners.

articles.title: Alkaline Phosphatase and Cumulative Vascular Access Burden in Maintenance Hemodialysis: An Exploratory Clinical Study.
articles.abstract: Background: Vascular access dysfunction remains a major challenge in maintenance hemodialysis (HD). Although chronic kidney disease-mineral and bone disorder may contribute to vascular pathology, the relationship between mineral metabolism markers and cumulative vascular access deterioration remains poorly defined. Methods: This retrospective single-center study included 74 patients receiving maintenance HD. Cumulative vascular access burden was defined by reinterventions, definitive access losses, and additional vascular accesses. Associations with parathyroid hormone (PTH), calcium, phosphorus, calcium-phosphorus product, and alkaline phosphatase (ALP) were evaluated using group comparisons, correlation analysis, and logistic regression. Results: Patients with cumulative vascular access burden had higher ALP levels than those without burden (92.0 vs. 78.0 U/L, p = 0.010), whereas PTH, calcium, phosphorus, and calcium-phosphorus product did not differ significantly. ALP correlated with cumulative burden (Spearman's ρ = 0.303, p = 0.009), and this association remained statistically significant after adjustment for age, BMI, PTH, and phosphorus (OR per 10 U/L increase = 1.226, 95% CI 1.059-1.418; p = 0.006). Conclusions: Higher ALP levels were associated with greater cumulative historical vascular access burden after adjustment for selected clinical and biochemical variables. These exploratory findings do not establish the prognostic value of ALP for future vascular access outcomes and require prospective validation.

Although chronic kidney disease-mineral and bone disorder may contribute to vascular pathology, the relationship between mineral metabolism markers and cumulative vascular access deterioration remains poorly defined. articles.title: Chemical Mechanisms of Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury and Neuroprotection in the Thrombectomy Era.
articles.abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy has significantly improved outcomes for patients with large-vessel occlusion stroke. However, restoring the artery does not always re-establish full microvascular blood flow, tissue rescue, or a good neurological outcome. Ischemia-reperfusion injury varies over time, with distinct biochemical mechanisms dominating during ischemia, early reperfusion, and the subsequent hours. During ischemia, factors like adenosine triphosphate (ATP) depletion, ionic imbalance, calcium overload, mitochondrial dysfunction, acidosis, and metabolic changes such as succinate build-up render brain tissue highly vulnerable. When blood flow resumes, oxygen delivery to this stressed tissue can induce rapid mitochondrial redox shifts, electron leakage, reactive oxygen and nitrogen species formation, iron-dependent radical generation, and lipid peroxidation. Damage may then persist for hours through ongoing mitochondrial dysfunction, phospholipid hydroperoxide accumulation, reactive aldehydes, ferroptosis, blood-brain barrier breakdown, microvascular issues, and inflammation. Much of the mechanistic evidence supporting these processes derives from experimental studies, and their relevance to clinical outcomes after thrombectomy requires further validation. This narrative review tracks these chemical changes across the main phases of cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury and connects them to modern thrombectomy practices. It also explores how the timing of each process may inform neuroprotective strategies, drug delivery methods, patient selection via imaging, and future clinical trial approaches.
articles.englishSummary: Mechanical thrombectomy has significantly improved outcomes for patients with large-vessel occlusion stroke. However, restoring the artery does not always re-establish full microvascular blood flow, tissue rescue, or a good neurological outcome. Ischemia-reperfusion injury varies over time, with distinct biochemical mechanisms dominating during ischemia, early reperfusion, and the subsequent hours.

articles.title: Contralateral Major Amputation Following Diabetes- and Peripheral Artery Disease-Related Limb Loss: A Systematic Review and Pooled Meta-Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Major amputation remains a devastating and understudied outcome in patients with peripheral artery disease (PAD), chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), and diabetes mellitus (DM)-related limb disease. Although modern vascular care emphasizes index and symptomatic limb surveillance, the population-level risk of non-index limb (NIL) major amputation remains incompletely defined. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to quantify NIL major amputation incidence and evaluate factors associated with contralateral limb loss.

DESIGN/METHOD: A systematic search of PubMed (MEDLINE), Embase, and Scopus through January 2026 was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. Studies reporting contralateral above- or below-knee amputation in adults with PAD, CLTI, DM-related limb disease, or prior ipsilateral major amputation were included. Single-arm random-effects meta-analysis using the restricted maximum likelihood (REML) estimator was performed with log-transformed effect sizes. Subgroup analyses were conducted by clinical phenotype, geographic location, study era, and DM prevalence. Secondary outcomes included overall mortality, bilateral major amputation, NIL minor amputation, NIL revascularization, and development of NIL CLTI.

RESULTS: Seventeen cohorts encompassing 30,359 patients were included. The pooled incidence of NIL major amputation was 6 per 100 person-years (95% CI, 3-9), with substantial heterogeneity (I2=98.93%). Meta-regression showed no significant differences by clinical phenotype (P=.622), geographic region (P=.662), study era (P=.893), or DM prevalence (P=.127). Clinical phenotypes included CLTI versus non-CLTI PAD or DM versus post-ipsilateral major amputation. Geographic region was divided into United States and international studies. Study era was divided into modern (2010-2025) and legacy (pre-2010) studies. Longer follow-up duration was inversely associated with reported incidence (P<.001). Pooled mortality rate was 38% (95% CI, 30-47%), and the pooled rate of bilateral major amputation was 12% (95% CI, 8-18%). Other secondary outcomes included a pooled NIL minor amputation rate of 11% (95% CI, 3-37%), NIL revascularization rate of 19% (95% CI, 6-47%), and NIL CLTI development rate of 32% (95% CI, 11-64%).

CONCLUSIONS: NIL major amputation remains a persistent risk in PAD and DM-related limb disease. These findings support the need for structured bilateral limb surveillance and early NIL risk stratification to inform comprehensive limb preservation care.

Although modern vascular care emphasizes index and symptomatic limb surveillance, the population-level risk of non-index limb (NIL) major amputation remains incompletely defined. We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to quantify NIL major amputation incidence and evaluate factors associated with contralateral limb loss.

articles.title: Index Below-Knee Endovascular Intervention for Intermittent Claudication Is Associated with Increased Amputation Risk.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Guidelines advise against infrapopliteal peripheral vascular intervention (PVI) for intermittent claudication (IC) due to potential harm with unclear benefit. We hypothesized that below-knee intervention at index PVI for IC confers higher future amputation risk than above-knee-only treatment.

METHODS: From the VQI PVI registry (2015-2025), we identified elective, initial PVIs for IC and compared those patients undergoing above-knee-only treatment (AK) to those having any below-knee intervention (BK). Using our previously described methodology, long-term amputation data were obtained by linking the PVI and amputation registries via unique patient identifiers. Demographic and procedural data were analyzed descriptively. Kaplan-Meier Analysis estimated risk of major and any (major+minor) amputation, with independent predictors of amputation identified by multivariable Firth logistic regression.

RESULTS: Among 92,899 treated limbs (81,338 AK; 11,561 BK), BK patients had increased rates of diabetes (54% vs. 41%), CHF (18% vs. 13%), and ESRD/dialysis (4.7% vs. 1.7%, p<0.001). BK patients were more likely to be Black (21% vs. 13%, p<0.001), Hispanic (8.8% vs. 4.3%, p<0.001), and Asian (1.5% vs. 1.0%, p<0.001). Smoking history predominated in AK (89% vs. 67%, p<0.001). 16,086 limbs required repeat PVI, 13,831 (17%) in the AK group vs. 2,255 (20%) in the BK group (p<0.001). At reintervention, BK patients were more likely to have progressed to CLTI (41% vs. 25%; p<0.001) and undergo ≥2 repeat interventions (32% vs. 27%; p<0.001). Initial below-knee intervention was associated with greater ipsilateral major (OR 2.39;1.70-3.35) and any (OR 2.36;1.75-3.18) amputation. Kaplan-Meier showed increased major [1-year (0.3% vs 0.1%);5-years (0.4% vs 0.1%)] and any amputation risk [1-year (0.5% vs 0.1%); 5-years (0.7% vs 0.2%).

CONCLUSIONS: Index below-knee intervention for IC portends greater risk of progression to CLTI, repeat PVI, and ipsilateral amputation, highlighting the potentially dangerous treatment trap of infrapopliteal intervention in patients with intermittent claudicants.

We hypothesized that below-knee intervention at index PVI for IC confers higher future amputation risk than above-knee-only treatment. METHODS: From the VQI PVI registry (2015-2025), we identified elective, initial PVIs for IC and compared those patients undergoing above-knee-only treatment (AK) to those having any below-knee intervention (BK).

articles.title: Differential Effect of Endovascular Treatment in Medium or Distal Vessel Occlusion: A Distal Secondary Analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with medium or distal vessel occlusion stroke are heterogeneous. Randomized trials show no net benefit of endovascular treatment (EVT) over best medical treatment (BMT) alone, which may mask heterogeneity of treatment effect. We used an externally developed machine learning model to predict excellent early neurological outcome (EENO) with BMT alone and examined whether the effect of EVT differed across predicted risk.

METHODS: A Tabular Prior-Data Fitted Network (TabPFN) model was trained to predict EENO (24-hour National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale [NIHSS] score of 0-2) in patients with medium or distal vessel occlusion treated with BMT alone in a local Bernese Stroke Registry. This model was applied to patients from the DISTAL randomized trial (55 centers and 11 countries), who were randomized to EVT plus BMT or BMT alone. We tested for interaction between predicted EENO and treatment allocation on the primary outcome (90-day modified Rankin Scale shift), repeating this using admission NIHSS alone.

RESULTS: In the development cohort (n=257, 42% female, and mean age 70.4±14.8 years), 54% achieved EENO. In the DISTAL cohort (270 BMT alone, 269 EVT plus BMT, 44% female, and mean age 74.9±12.0 years), the model showed moderate external discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.73). A significant interaction was found between predicted EENO and treatment effect (Pinteraction=0.012): in 152 patients predicted to achieve EENO, EVT was associated with worse 90-day modified Rankin Scale score (common odds ratio, 0.48 [95% CI, 0.27-0.84]), whereas no treatment effect was seen in 387 patients predicted not to achieve EENO (common odds ratio 1.13 [95% CI, 0.79-1.60]). A model using admission NIHSS alone showed comparable discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve 0.71) and a common odds ratio for EVT of 0.47 (95% CI, 0.25-0.89) in patients with an NIHSS score of ≤4 and a common odds ratio of 1.05 (95% CI, 0.75-1.47) in patients with an NIHSS score of >4 (Pinteraction=0.029).

CONCLUSIONS: EVT was harmful in patients with medium or distal vessel occlusion predicted to achieve EENO with BMT alone, and an NIHSS-alone model performed comparably to the multivariable model.

We used an externally developed machine learning model to predict excellent early neurological outcome (EENO) with BMT alone and examined whether the effect of EVT differed across predicted risk.

articles.title: Cardiovascular magnetic resonance reveals stable myocardial tissue characteristics despite cardiac remodelling after transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt in liver cirrhosis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt (TIPS) reduces portal hypertension in liver cirrhosis but acutely increases cardiac preload. The present study aimed to prospectively assess changes in cardiac function, remodelling, and myocardial tissue characteristics after TIPS using cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR).

METHODS AND RESULTS: Of the 45 screened patients with advanced liver cirrhosis, 23 patients [median (IQR) age 65 (56-69) years, 70% male, 87% Child-Pugh class B, MELD score 14 (12-20)] were prospectively included and underwent multiparametric CMR before TIPS implantation (CMR-1), as well as follow-up imaging after 3 (2-4) days (CMR-2, n = 20) and 100 (87-122) days (CMR-3, n = 10). Biventricular end-diastolic volumes increased significantly from baseline to the final follow-up (CMR-3) [left ventricle (LV) +27.2 (20.8-38.6) mL/m2; right ventricle (RV) +26.1 (18.2-38.0) mL/m2; both P < 0.001], accompanied by increased stroke volumes [LV +7.2 (3.6-15.7) mL/m2, RV +9.8 (2.3-15.4) mL/m2; both P < 0.001]. LV mass increased from 32 (30-37) g/m2 to 47 (45-52) g/m2 (P < 0.001). Although extracellular volume (ECV) fraction remained unchanged [27 (23-28) % vs. 25 (23-29) %; P = 0.06], ECV mass increased from 17.1 (14.0-21.8) g to 25.4 (20.7-27.4) g (P < 0.001), reflecting the concomitant increase in LV mass. Myocardial tissue characterization revealed no significant changes in native T1 or T2 values during follow-up (all P > 0.05).

CONCLUSION: TIPS implantation induces progressive biventricular dilatation, increased stroke volume, and eccentric remodelling. Despite these marked structural adaptations, myocardial tissue characteristics remained largely unchanged during short- and mid-term follow-up, suggesting predominantly preload-driven cardiac remodelling.

articles.title: Deep inspiration-facilitated stenting for extremely tortuous vertebral artery ostium in a Type III arch.
articles.abstract: Endovascular treatment of vertebral artery ostial (VAO) stenosis can be technically challenging in the presence of severe supra-aortic tortuosity, particularly a Type III aortic arch where stable guide catheter positioning is often difficult to maintain. During device delivery, inadequate proximal support may result in guide catheter prolapse into the aortic arch, compromising procedural success. Although adjunctive support techniques such as the buddy-wire technique may improve system stability, extreme vascular tortuosity can still impede the advancement of balloons or stents.1 A deep inspiration maneuver with transient breath-holding may facilitate device delivery by inducing caudal displacement of the aortic arch and proximal subclavian artery.2 Because the distal vertebral artery remains relatively fixed within the transverse foramina, this maneuver generates temporary axial tension across the V1 segment, partially straightening the tortuous vascular course and improving device trackability.3This technical video (video 1) demonstrates step-by-step endovascular reconstruction of an extremely tortuous right VAO lesion in a patient with prior failed stenting caused by hostile vascular anatomy and subsequent recurrent stenosis. Despite the Type III arch anatomy, a transfemoral approach was mandated over a radial approach due to the acute ostial geometry, providing the necessary antegrade delivery vector. We highlight a dual strategy approach combining distal wire-anchor support to enhance guiding stability and respiratory-induced vascular straightening to facilitate device navigation, ultimately enabling precise stent deployment and complete revascularization.neurintsurg;jnis-2026-025713v2/V1F1V1Video 1.

articles.title: Adipocytokine Profiling and Cardiovascular Risk Stratification in Rheumatoid Arthritis: Literature Review.
articles.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is associated with an increased burden of cardiovascular disease (CVD), reflecting interactions among persistent systemic inflammation, traditional cardiometabolic risk factors, and treatment exposure. Conventional risk scores may underestimate cardiovascular risk in some patients with RA. This narrative review examines the potential role of adipokines in linking synovial inflammation and metabolic dysfunction to vascular disease. It discusses the context-dependent cardiovascular associations of adiponectin, the pro-inflammatory signaling of leptin, resistin, visfatin, and chemerin, and the proposed protective roles of omentin, vaspin, and apelin. Emerging observations connect adipokine profiles with measures of subclinical atherosclerosis and selected clinical outcomes; however, methodological heterogeneity and residual confounding constrain causal and prognostic interpretations. We also consider venous thromboembolism, cardiometabolic multimorbidity, and treatment-related risk, including the clinical safety context of JAK inhibitors. At present, adipokine profiling remains investigational and should complement research, not replace established cardiovascular risk assessment and control of disease activity and conventional risk factors.

articles.title: Extracellular Vesicle-Mediated Angiogenesis in Peripheral Artery Disease: Context-Dependent Effects in Ischemic Limbs and Atherosclerotic Plaques.
articles.abstract: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) is most commonly caused by atherosclerotic arterial stenosis or occlusion, which reduces downstream tissue perfusion and causes tissue ischemia. In response to ischemia, reparative angiogenesis is activated and may support tissue perfusion recovery and skeletal muscle protection. In contrast, neovascularization within atherosclerotic plaques may promote intraplaque hemorrhage and plaque destabilization. Thus, angiogenesis has dual roles in PAD-related ischemia and atherosclerotic plaques. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are membrane-bound particles that carry various cargo, including proteins, lipids, nucleic acids, and metabolites. Through the transfer of bioactive cargo and surface-mediated signaling, EVs can modify recipient-cell functions and thereby influence angiogenic signaling. Investigation of EV-mediated communication may therefore help elucidate the mechanisms underlying angiogenic regulation in vascular disease. In addition, disease-promoting EVs may be therapeutically targeted, whereas engineered EVs may be developed as therapeutic agents or delivery platforms. Recent studies have shown that EVs regulate angiogenic responses in preclinical murine hindlimb ischemia models. However, these effects in ischemic limbs and the potential involvement of EVs in atherosclerotic plaque neovascularization have rarely been reviewed in an integrated manner. This narrative review discusses these contrasting angiogenic processes from a context-dependent perspective. Understanding this context dependency may help develop EV-based strategies that promote functional vascular repair in ischemic tissues while suppressing or normalizing pathological neovascularization in atherosclerotic plaques.

articles.title: GLP-1 Receptor Agonists Decrease the Rate of Rupture, Cardiac Events, and Death in Patients with Abdominal Aortic Aneurysms.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) is a degenerative condition involving several processes including inflammation, matrix remodeling, disruptions of vascular smooth muscle cells, and thrombus formation all leading to progressive dilatation of the aorta and eventual rupture. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) are now considered part of the frontline therapeutic options to treat type 2 diabetes mellitus and have also been validated as having compelling anti-inflammatory and cardiovascular protective properties. Data is limited on the impact of GLP-1RA on outcomes of patients with AAA. The aim of this study is to examine the association and possible impact of GLP-1RA on patients with AAA.

METHODS: Data was sourced from the TriNetX research network, encompassing 123 health care organizations. Utilizing ICD-10 and CPT codes, we identified patients with AAA who received abdominal imaging every six months. Group 1 was comprised of patients who were treated with GLP-1RA while Group 2 patients were not. Propensity-score-matching (PSM) was used in a 1:1 fashion using age, sex, diabetes, metformin use, hypertension, cardiac disease, tobacco use, chronic kidney disease, and pulmonary disease as covariates. Primary outcomes were aneurysm rupture or repair. Secondary outcomes include mortality and major adverse cardiac events (MACE; myocardial infarction, stroke, and heart failure). Standard statistical methods were used as appropriate.

RESULTS: We identified 412,490 patients with diagnosis of AAA who were undergoing 6-month surveillance between June 1, 2010 and April 16, 2024. After PSM, the GLP-1RA group (N=13,722) underwent fewer elective repairs at each timepoint (1.5% vs 2.3% at 2 years, 2.1% vs 3.0% at 5 years, P<.01) and had significantly fewer ruptures at two years (1.1% vs 1.8%, P<.01) and five years (1.6% vs 2.4%, P<.01) when compared to Group 2 (N=13,722). Group 1 also experienced significantly fewer MACE and all-cause mortality at two and five years. On multivariate analysis, GLP-1RA significantly reduced the risk of undergoing elective repair (HR 0.757, 95% CI [0.636-0.902], P<.01), rupture (HR 0.538, 95% CI [0.418-0.691], P<.01), all-cause mortality (HR 0.474, 95% CI [0.439-0.511], P<.001), and MACE (HR 0.825, 95% CI [0.794-0.857], P<.01) at 5 years.

CONCLUSIONS: The use of GLP-1RA in patients with AAA is associated with fewer ruptures, elective repairs, and improved rates of MACE and death. A prospective analysis may further elucidate if GLP-1RA should be prescribed to reduce the rate of aneurysm growth.

Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) are now considered part of the frontline therapeutic options to treat type 2 diabetes mellitus and have also been validated as having compelling anti-inflammatory and cardiovascular protective properties. articles.title: Intraoperative estimated blood loss and perioperative transfusion are independently associated with postoperative morbidity and mortality after lower-extremity bypass.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Intraoperative estimated blood loss (EBL) and need for perioperative packed red blood cell (pRBC) transfusion are common during lower-extremity bypass (LEB) for chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) and have each been associated with adverse postoperative outcomes. However, their joint associations with postoperative outcomes remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of EBL and perioperative pRBC transfusion, individually and jointly, with postoperative morbidity and mortality in patients undergoing LEB for CLTI.

METHODS: A retrospective cohort study was conducted using the Society for Vascular Surgery Vascular Quality Initiative database. Patients undergoing LEB for CLTI between 2014 and 2023 were identified. Receiver-operating characteristic analysis identified an optimal EBL threshold of 225 mL (area under the curve, 0.72) for predicting transfusion, which was used to stratify patients into low-EBL (<225 mL) and high-EBL (≥225 mL) groups. Primary outcomes included myocardial infarction (MI), stroke, 30-day mortality, and a composite end point. Multivariable logistic regression was used to assess adjusted associations across four groups defined by EBL and transfusion status. Separate model was used to evaluate the interaction between EBL and pRBC transfusion.

RESULTS: Among 36,019 procedures, 58.5% had low EBL, and 41.5% had high EBL. Patients who had high EBL and did not require blood transfusion had increased odds of adverse postoperative outcomes, including 30-day mortality [adjusted odds ratio (aOR), 1.26; 95% confidence interval (CI), 1.01-1.59], MI (aOR, 1.88; 95% CI, 1.48-2.39), stroke (aOR, 1.58; 95% CI, 1.09-2.29), and the composite outcome (aOR 1.51, 95% CI, 1.29-1.78). Patients who had low EBL and received blood transfusion had increased odds of 30-day mortality (aOR, 2.46; 95% CI, 1.95-3.10), MI (aOR, 6.57; 95% CI, 5.26-8.21), stroke (aOR, 2.75; 95% CI, 1.84-4.12), and the composite outcome (aOR, 4.08; 95% CI, 3.48-4.78). Patients who had both high EBL and required perioperative blood transfusion demonstrated the highest odds of adverse outcomes, including 30-day mortality (aOR, 2.54; 95% CI, 2.09-3.08), MI (aOR, 7.39; 95% CI, 6.08-8.98), stroke (aOR, 3.79; 95% CI, 2.76-5.21), and the composite outcome (aOR, 4.42; 95% CI, 3.87-5.05). Formal interaction testing demonstrated significant between EBL and transfusion.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients undergoing LEB for CLTI, intraoperative EBL and perioperative pRBC transfusion were both independently and jointly associated with increased postoperative morbidity and mortality. These findings identify EBL and transfusion as markers of perioperative risk and support further investigation of blood-sparing strategies and individualized transfusion practices.

However, their joint associations with postoperative outcomes remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of EBL and perioperative pRBC transfusion, individually and jointly, with postoperative morbidity and mortality in patients undergoing LEB for CLTI.

articles.title: Carotid endarterectomy versus transcarotid artery revascularization for asymptomatic carotid stenosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The treatment for asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis includes a surgical or interventional approach in selected cases. Although endarterectomy should be considered over stenting for selected patients, according to the latest European Society of Vascular Surgery guidelines, the Carotid Revascularization and Medical Management for Asymptomatic Carotid Stenosis Trials suggested that carotid stenting would be associated with low rates of perioperative stroke or death. The transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) technique is a relatively new endovascular method that involves placing a stent at the carotid bifurcation through direct carotid artery access, performed under a flow reversal system. This approach avoids manipulation of the aortic arch, potentially reducing embolic events. The aim of this systematic review is to compare TCAR with carotid endarterectomy (CEA) in asymptomatic patients undergoing carotid intervention. It seeks to evaluate whether TCAR is associated with improved perioperative outcomes, such as lower rates of stroke and death, compared with CEA, given its potentially less invasive approach.

METHODS: The review was performed according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) on the platforms PubMed/MEDLINE, OVID/Embase, and Scopus. The following MeSH terms were used: "asymptomatic carotid stenosis" AND "carotid endarterectomy," "transcarotid artery revascularization" OR "TCAR." Full-text screening and data extraction were performed with the support of the COVIDENCE platform. Six studies were selected for this systematic review, comprising a total of 132,684 patients (30,581 undergoing TCAR and 102,103 undergoing CEA). Statistical analysis was performed using R software.

RESULTS: The selected studies for this systematic review showed similar results in terms of perioperative stroke and death for asymptomatic patients who underwent carotid endarterectomy and TCAR.

CONCLUSIONS: Our results suggest that there are no significant differences between CEA and TCAR for the treatment of asymptomatic patients who require a surgical or interventional approach. Further studies are necessary to provide more robust data in this field.

The transcarotid artery revascularization (TCAR) technique is a relatively new endovascular method that involves placing a stent at the carotid bifurcation through direct carotid artery access, performed under a flow reversal system.

articles.title: Inflammation and thrombosis: from pathophysiology to future treatments.
articles.abstract: Inflammation and coagulation are tightly interconnected host-defense systems that, when dysregulated, promote pathological thrombosis. This narrative review examines mechanisms, clinical settings, and therapeutic implications of thromboinflammation (TI) across venous, arterial, and microvascular thrombosis, with particular attention to the differences in clinical translation among vascular territories. Endothelial activation, tissue factor expression, platelet-leukocyte interactions, neutrophil extracellular traps, complement activation, inflammasome signalling, and impaired fibrinolysis converge to generate a procoagulant phenotype. These mechanisms modify Virchow's triad and contribute to venous, arterial, and microvascular thrombosis, although their relative importance varies across vascular territories. Clinically, TI is relevant in inflammatory bowel disease, rheumatologic and other immune-mediated disorders, sepsis, coronavirus disease 2019, clonal haematopoiesis, complement-mediated diseases, and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. TI offers a unifying framework for mechanistic risk assessment and therapeutic development. In atherothrombosis, randomised trials have demonstrated that selective modulation of inflammatory pathways, particularly the NLRP3-interleukin-1β-interleukin-6 axis and colchicine-sensitive pathways, can reduce recurrent cardiovascular events. By contrast, the role of inflammation-targeted therapies for primary or secondary prevention of VTE remains uncertain. Future studies should identify disease-specific biomarkers and test targeted anti-inflammatory or immunothrombotic strategies, alone or alongside anticoagulation, to prevent thrombosis without compromising haemostasis effectively.

articles.title: Maternal Obesity Is Associated With Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes in Inflammatory Bowel Disease: A Matched Electronic Health Record Cohort Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: We sought to define the prevalence of obesity in the first trimester of pregnancy among women with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and evaluate its association with adverse pregnancy outcomes.

METHODS: First-trimester body mass index (BMI) was assessed in pregnancies with and without IBD. Pregnancies reaching 24 weeks were propensity-score matched 1:6 by maternal age, BMI, smoking status and gravidity to assess whether IBD conferred additional pregnancy risk.

RESULTS: Overall, 22.6% (64/283; 95% CI 17.7%-27.5%) of pregnancies in women with IBD met ethnicity-adjusted criteria for obesity. Increasing obesity class was associated with stepwise increases in gestational diabetes, pre-eclampsia, venous thromboembolism (VTE), emergency caesarean section and high birthweight. Matching yielded 177 IBD pregnancies and 1062 controls. Obesity was independently associated with the composite adverse pregnancy outcome (OR 1.63; 95% CI 1.15-2.33; p = 0.007), whereas no statistically significant additional association was identified for IBD diagnosis alone (OR 0.74; 95% CI 0.53-1.03; p = 0.073). Among IBD pregnancies, aspirin was recommended in 39.3% (86/219). Low-molecular-weight heparin (LMWH) was prescribed in 21.6% (19/88) of pregnancies classified post hoc as intermediate or high VTE risk.

CONCLUSION: More than one in five pregnancies in women with IBD were complicated by obesity. Obesity was strongly associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes, whereas this study did not identify a significant additional effect attributable to IBD diagnosis alone. Preventive prescribing with aspirin and LMWH represents an opportunity for improved antenatal care.

Pregnancies reaching 24 weeks were propensity-score matched 1:6 by maternal age, BMI, smoking status and gravidity to assess whether IBD conferred additional pregnancy risk.
