articles.title: Development of a machine learning model to predict venous thromboembolism risk in women using combined oral contraceptives.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality, with combined oral contraceptives (COCPs) being a modifiable risk factor. Existing clinical tools have limited ability to capture complex predictor interactions. This study aimed to develop and evaluate machine learning (ML) models to predict VTE risk among COCP users.

METHODS: This study was conducted using data from the Saudi Real-World Evidence Network (2016–2023). The primary outcome was the first VTE event within 2 years of COCP initiation. Following data partitioning, feature selection was performed on the training set. Elastic-net logistic regression, random forest (RF), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), one-class support vector machine and Isolation-Forest were trained on original and resampled datasets. Performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and F1 score.

RESULTS: The cohort included 24 518 treatment episodes (n=17 512, VTE events=52). After handling class imbalance, RF and XGBoost were the best-performing models (F1: 84.3% and 81.6%; AUROC: 59.6% and 69.2%, respectively), compared with other models (F1: 2.6%–55.3%, AUROC: 54.2%–68.4%). Key predictors included age, glucocorticoid use and rheumatic, renal and thyroid diseases.

DISCUSSION: ML shows potential for VTE risk detection despite low event rate and class imbalance. However, findings suggest synthetic sample overfitting, and external validation is warranted before clinical deployment. Identified predictors reinforce the role of metabolic and inflammatory factors in VTE susceptibility among COCP users.

CONCLUSION: ML models, particularly XGBoost and RF, demonstrated moderate predictive ability for VTE among COCP users, supporting their use in individualised risk assessments, though external validation is warranted.

Existing clinical tools have limited ability to capture complex predictor interactions. This study aimed to develop and evaluate machine learning (ML) models to predict VTE risk among COCP users.

articles.title: Vascular surgery is over-represented by multiple medical societies compared with its peers.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Medical societies play an important role in representing physicians and their interests. The study aimed to compare the number, size, and fiscal strength of vascular societies with those of other cardiovascular specialties.

METHODS: Information was found via a systematic Internet search and with publicly available data (ie, www.aamc.org). Medical societies representing vascular surgery (VS), cardiology (CARD), cardiothoracic surgery (CTS), and interventional radiology (IR) in the United States were compared. Board-certified physicians (www.abms.org) and publicly available financial information (www.ProPublica.org) were tabulated.

RESULTS: Board-certified vascular surgeons (n = 4464) could join 30 VS societies (4 national, 10 regional, 12 city/state, and 4 other). In comparison, 12 societies (2 national) represent CTS (n = 5869) and 16 (1 national) represent IR (n = 4032) physicians. Cardiologists (n = 22,843) are represented by 14 societies (5 national) and an additional 27 chapters of a parent national society. The available number of vascular surgeons per national society was markedly lower than that of the comparative specialties. Vascular societies generated $23 million in revenue compared to $52 million for CTS, $6 million for IR, and $1.03 billion for CARD. CARD societies accounted for 93% of the total revenue across the four specialties and generated 52 times the revenue of VS societies.

CONCLUSIONS: Compared with similar specialties, VS has relatively few surgeons, but a high number of medical societies. This segmentation may dilute the educational, governmental, societal, and patient advocacy impact of VS compared with that of its peers.

articles.title: Ultrasound-guided selective nerve block promotes perioperative vascular remodeling and early maturation of radiocephalic arteriovenous fistulas.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autogenous arteriovenous fistula (AVF) is the preferred vascular access for maintenance hemodialysis, but its successful maturation depends on adequate perioperative vascular remodeling. We evaluated whether ultrasound-guided selective nerve block (SNB) promotes vascular remodeling and improves AVF maturation after radiocephalic AVF creation.

METHODS: This was a retrospective analysis based on a prospectively-maintained single-center vascular access clinical follow-up database. We included 163 patients with stage 5 chronic kidney disease undergoing primary radiocephalic AVF creation between January 2023 and January 2024. Patients received ultrasound-guided SNB (n = 72) or local infiltration anesthesia (LA, n = 91). Perioperative changes in radial artery and cephalic vein diameters were evaluated, postoperative brachial artery blood flow was recorded, and AVF maturation was assessed at 1, 2, and 3 months. Linear mixed-effects models and multivariable logistic regression were used for analysis.

RESULTS: Compared with LA, SNB significantly increased radial artery and cephalic vein diameters after anesthesia, whereas both vessels constricted in the LA group (both P < .001). Linear mixed-effects analysis demonstrated significant time effects and group-by-time interactions for both vessels, whereas a significant group effect was observed only for the cephalic vein (all P < .001). Postoperative brachial artery blood flow was significantly greater in the SNB group (P < .001). The 2-month AVF maturation rate was significantly higher in the SNB group than in the LA group (60% vs 35%; P = .002), whereas no between-group differences were observed at 1 or 3 months. Younger age, larger preoperative radial artery diameter, and SNB were independent predictors of AVF maturation.

CONCLUSIONS: Ultrasound-guided SNB promotes perioperative vascular remodeling, increases postoperative blood flow, and independently facilitates early AVF maturation after radiocephalic AVF creation. These findings support SNB as a promising perioperative strategy to optimize vascular access outcomes in patients undergoing AVF creation.

articles.title: Machine learning models for predicting futile recanalisation after endovascular treatment in patients with large core infarction.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Predicting futile recanalisation following endovascular treatment (EVT) in patients with large core infarctions is crucial for guiding clinical decisions, optimising perioperative management and improving healthcare resource allocation. This study aimed to compare four machine learning (ML) algorithms and identify the most effective model for preinterventional prediction of futile recanalisation.

METHODS: Patients achieving successful reperfusion (expanded Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction Score≥2b) from the EVT in Acute Anterior Circulation Large Vessel Occlusive Patients With a Large Infarct Core trial were stratified into two groups: no-futile recanalisation (90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS) 0–3) and futile recanalisation (mRS 4–6). The least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression method was used for feature selection, and four ML algorithms, including logistic regression, support vector machine (SVM), decision tree and random forest, were applied. Model performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic curves, calibration plots and decision curve analysis. Feature importance was ranked using SHapley Additive exPlanation (SHAP) values.

RESULTS: Among 146 patients, 74 experienced futile recanalisation. Eight predictors were identified and ranked by SHAP analysis from highest to lowest importance: sex, age, National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale, glucose, systolic blood pressure, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, fibrinogen and occlusion site. Among the four models, the SVM model achieved the highest area under the curve of 0.891 (95% CI 0.837 to 0.945), along with good calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow test, p=0.103) and clinical utility.

CONCLUSION: The SVM model emerges as the optimal predictive tool for futile recanalisation following EVT in patients with large core infarction. Nevertheless, external validation is required to confirm its performance before clinical application.

articles.title: Factors associated with infarct volume growth after mechanical thrombectomy in large core infarction: ANGEL-ASPECT insights.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Infarct volume growth (IVG) correlates with outcomes and may represent a prognostic imaging biomarker in acute ischaemic stroke due to anterior circulation large vessel occlusion (LVO). This study aims to identify factors associated with IVG after mechanical thrombectomy (MT) in patients with large core infarction.

METHODS: This is a post hoc analysis of the Endovascular Therapy in Anterior Circulation Large Vessel Occlusion with a Large Infarct randomised trial. IVG was calculated as final infarct volume minus baseline infarct volume (BIV). The optimal IVG threshold for predicting 90-day favourable outcomes (modified Rankin Scale score 0–3) was determined using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, maximising both sensitivity and specificity. Factors associated with IVG were identified using multivariate logistic regression analyses.

RESULTS: Among 228 included patients, ROC analysis identified an optimal IVG threshold of 105 mL for predicting favourable 90-day outcomes (area under the curve=0.71; specificity=0.85, sensitivity=0.53). Patients were stratified into mild (IVG <105 mL, n=150) and severe (IVG ≥105 mL, n=78) groups. Multivariate logistic regression identified BIV (OR 1.02, 95% CI 1.00 to 1.03; p<0.01), admission blood glucose (OR 1.20, 95% CI 1.04 to 1.37; p=0.01), time from puncture to recanalisation (OR 1.01, 95% CI 1.00 to 1.02; p=0.049) and recanalisation at 36 hours (±12 hours) (OR 0.19, 95% CI 0.05 to 0.72; p=0.01) as independent factors associated with IVG.

CONCLUSION: IVG after MT significantly correlates with clinical outcomes. Identification of modifiable IVG determinants after MT may inform periprocedural management strategies in patients with large infarct due to LVO.

articles.title: The Need for Device-Specific Training Before Handheld Ultrasound Use: Agreement and Repeatability of Simulated Aortic Aneurysm Diameter Measurements by Senior Sonography Students on a Familiar Conventional and an Unfamiliar Handheld System.
articles.abstract: Background: Ultrasound measurement of abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) diameter guides screening and surveillance, but whether students' measurement competence on a conventional system transfers to an unfamiliar handheld device has rarely been assessed. Methods: Twenty-seven senior sonography students made three anteroposterior outer-to-outer measurements of two water-filled balloons embedded in gelatin (reference diameters 3.53 and 5.88 cm, calculated from the circumference before embedding), first on the familiar cart-based conventional system and then, in a fixed, non-randomised order, on a handheld system with which they had no prior hands-on experience. The primary outcomes were bias against the calculated reference, with equivalence testing (±5%), and the paired between-system difference, with Bland-Altman analysis; repeatability was assessed with repeatability coefficients. Results: Conventional measurements were equivalent to the calculated reference within ±5% (bias -0.09 cm, 95% CI -0.16 to -0.02; +0.07 cm, 95% CI -0.05 to +0.19). Handheld measurements were higher (+0.17 and +0.33 cm; both p < 0.001) and failed equivalence; the mean between-system difference was +0.26 cm (95% CI 0.18-0.34), without proportional bias. Single-reading repeatability coefficients were 0.31-0.67 cm. Conclusions: Students' conventional-system measurements agreed closely with the calculated reference, although this reference was not verified after embedding. Because device type was confounded with operator inexperience and with a fixed testing order, which introduces an unquantifiable learning or fatigue effect, the 0.26 cm value is an observed between-system difference under the study conditions and cannot be attributed to the handheld device itself. Measurement competence did not transfer automatically to a new device, underlining the critical need for device-specific training before handheld systems are used for aortic measurement. These implications are educational and technical; phantom findings do not support clinical surveillance recommendations without confirmation in patients.

articles.title: An asymptomatic pulmonary arteriovenous fistula presenting with a Campylobacter rectus brain abscess as the initial manifestation: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Brain abscess is a severe infectious disease of the central nervous system associated with high rates of mortality and morbidity. Pulmonary arteriovenous fistula (PAVF) is a rare but important cause of cryptogenic brain abscesses. The pathogens associated with PAVF-related brain abscesses are typically oral anaerobes or facultative anaerobes, most commonly non-hemolytic streptococci and Streptococcus intermedius. To our knowledge, no case of a monomicrobial Campylobacter rectus (C. rectus) brain abscess in a patient with asymptomatic PAVF has been reported.

CASE PRESENTATION: Herein, we report the case of a 57-year-old man with a C. rectus brain abscess in association with an asymptomatic PAVF. The patient presented to our hospital with fever and headache. Magnetic resonance (MR) imaging revealed a 5 × 2 cm brain abscess in the right temporal and occipital lobes, surrounded by extensive edema. Enhanced computed tomography (CT) scanning of the lungs revealed both nodules and PAVF. Blood culture and cardiac ultrasound failed to detect any abnormalities. Piperacillin-tazobactam and meropenem were administered for anti-infection, although the headache persisted. He was subsequently transferred to neurosurgery to resect the abscess by craniotomy; postoperative pus culture confirmed the presence of C. rectus.

CONCLUSIONS: For brain abscesses caused by oral anaerobes such as C. rectus, screening for right-to-left shunting diseases such as PAVF may be considered when no other source is identified.

articles.title: Survey of the human proteostasis network: translation, protein folding, and organelle-specific systems.
articles.abstract: The condition of having a healthy, functional proteome is known as protein homeostasis, or proteostasis. Maintaining proteostasis is the province of the proteostasis network, which consists of the cellular components that regulate protein synthesis, folding, localization, and degradation. The proteostasis network is a fundamental functional unit in biology with relevance to many diseases. Despite its importance, the human proteostasis network has until now lacked a precise definition, limiting our ability to interrogate proteostasis, integrate multiomic datasets, compare results across studies, or model proteostasis dysfunction in disease. To address this limitation, we have operationally defined the human proteostasis network by providing a comprehensive, annotated, and manually curated list of its components classified into nine Branches based on their function and localization - cytonuclear proteostasis, ER proteostasis, mitochondrial proteostasis, nuclear proteostasis, proteostasis network regulation, translation, extracellular proteostasis, the autophagy-lysosome pathway, and the ubiquitin-proteasome system - which we present in a series of three manuscripts of which this is the first. Overall, the proteostasis network annotation encompasses 3,151 components described by 4,043 annotations. Here, we present the 1,190 components that make up the first seven of these Branches, which comprise the compartment-based proteostasis network (cytonuclear, ER, mitochondrial, nuclear, and extracellular proteostasis), proteostasis network regulation, and translation. These Branches include chaperones, folding enzymes, systems for trafficking proteins, organelle-specific degradation systems, and the cell's translation machinery. This work provides a framework that will facilitate insights into how proteostasis is preserved in health, lost in aging and disease, and how it could be restored through pharmacological intervention.

articles.title: Venous thromboembolism reporting in fusion-positive NSCLC treated with tyrosine kinase inhibitors: A systematic review of safety reporting and protocol-level provisions in phase I-IV clinical trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is increasingly recognized as a clinically relevant complication in patients with fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the completeness and consistency of thromboembolic safety reporting in clinical trials of tyrosine kinase inhibitors remain poorly characterized.

METHODS: We performed a systematic review of phase I-IV clinical trials evaluating targeted therapies in fusion-positive NSCLC. Protocols, publications, and online trial registry updates were systematically reviewed to assess thromboembolic event ascertainment, reporting practices, protocol-level anticoagulant therapy provisions, and VTE-related eligibility criteria.

RESULTS: A total of 108 reporting sources from 61 study entries (58 unique trials) were reviewed. Pulmonary embolism and deep vein thrombosis were the predominant reported events. VTE-related information was highly fragmented across reporting sources: 14 study entries reported events exclusively through full-text publications, 19 exclusively through online trial updates, and 15 through both sources. Study protocols rarely prespecified thromboembolic events as dedicated safety outcomes, more commonly addressing them in eligibility criteria, anticoagulant therapy provisions, or differential diagnosis guidance. More than 40% of study entries lacked protocol-level anticoagulant therapy provisions and nearly 60% lacked VTE-related eligibility restrictions. Marked heterogeneity was observed in event definitions, reporting practices, safety ascertainment, and observation periods.

CONCLUSIONS: In fusion-positive NSCLC trials, heterogeneity in event ascertainment and reporting, rather than a true scarcity of thromboembolic events, represents a major limitation of the available evidence. Greater standardization of safety reporting and integration of trial registry and publication data may improve the completeness, comparability, and interpretability of future studies.

METHODS: We performed a systematic review of phase I-IV clinical trials evaluating targeted therapies in fusion-positive NSCLC.

articles.title: Plasma Proteomics Enhances Genetic Risk Prediction and Biological Understanding of Venous Thromboembolism.
articles.abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a leading cause of morbidity and the third most common vascular cause of death globally. While clinical and genetic risk factors have improved VTE risk stratification, they do not fully capture underlying disease biology. We hypothesized that integrating large-scale plasma proteomics with a validated polygenic risk score (PRSVTE) would reveal novel biological understanding and improve risk stratification. In 44,138 UK Biobank participants, we examined associations between PRSVTE and 2911 plasma proteins using multivariable linear regressions. We evaluated proteins as predictors of incident VTE using Cox regression models. We employed bidirectional Mendelian randomization (MR) using cis-acting protein quantitative trait loci (cis-pQTLs) instruments and genome-wide association summary statistics to infer potential causality. A protein-based risk score (ProteinRS) was developed with Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) logistic regression and compared against a clinical risk model. PRSVTE associated with 265 proteins after false discovery rate correction (FDR <0.01). Pathway enrichment analysis of these proteins highlighted cell adhesion, cell-junction organization, and transmembrane receptor signaling. Time-to-event analyses identified 354 proteins that predicted incident VTE (FDR <0.01). MR implicated 14 proteins in potential causal pathways to VTE, while genetic liability to VTE affected the levels of 44 proteins. A 60-protein ProteinRS improved discrimination beyond clinical factors (area under the curve (AUC) 0.664 versus 0.647; p = 0.024). Participants above the 80th percentile of ProteinRS had a 49% higher hazard of VTE (hazard ratio (HR) = 1.49, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.17-1.90) and those below the 20th percentile had a 48% lower hazard (HR = 0.52, 95% CI: 0.34-0.79) relative to the 20-80th percentile. Integrating genetic and proteomics data uncovered molecular pathways that link genetic susceptibility to VTE, highlighted actionable protein targets, and modestly enhanced risk prediction. Plasma proteomics therefore hold promise for precision prevention of VTE.

articles.title: Long-term patency outcomes after first autogenous arteriovenous fistula creation in patients aged 80 years or older: A competing-risk analysis.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Whether chronological age predicts arteriovenous fistula (AVF) durability remains uncertain. We compared primary patency between patients aged ≥80 and <80 years using competing-risk analysis and examined relevant vascular characteristics.

METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included 416 consecutive patients undergoing first autogenous AVF creation between 2017 and 2020, with follow-up through March 2025. Intraoperative vessel diameters, macroscopic arterial atherosclerosis and preoperative ankle-brachial and toe-brachial indices were prospectively recorded. Death before primary patency loss was treated as a competing event. Cumulative incidence was estimated using Aalen-Johansen and compared using Gray test. Associations were assessed using Fine-Gray and cause-specific Cox regression, with age modeled continuously in a sensitivity analysis.

RESULTS: Among 416 patients, 109 (26.2%) were aged ≥80 years. Median follow-up was 48 months. Older patients had more macroscopic arterial atherosclerosis (67.0% vs 47.9%; P < .001), lower ankle-brachial (1.09 vs 1.16; P < .001) and toe-brachial indices (0.69 vs 0.76; P = .002), and more venous diameters <2.5 mm (22.0% vs 13.4%; P = .030). The cumulative incidence of primary patency loss did not differ between groups (Gray P = .710), with 36-month estimates of 43.2% and 38.0%. Age ≥80 years was not independently associated with primary patency loss [subdistribution hazard ratio (sHR), 1.12; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.74-1.70], whereas each 10-year increase was associated with higher risk in a sensitivity analysis (sHR, 1.20; 95% CI, 1.04-1.39). Proximal anastomosis was associated with lower risk (sHR, 0.57; 95% CI, 0.37-0.88), and venous diameter <2.5 mm with higher risk (sHR, 1.70; 95% CI, 1.05-2.75). Assisted primary and secondary patency did not differ. Fewer than 10% of fistulas were permanently abandoned by 60 months in either group, and 60-month survival among older patients was 82.0%.

CONCLUSIONS: Among patients selected for autogenous AVF creation, age ≥80 years was not independently associated with primary patency loss, whereas a continuous-age sensitivity analysis suggested a modest increase in risk per decade. These findings suggest that an age threshold alone should not determine AVF candidacy in otherwise suitable patients, although interpretation is tempered by loss to follow-up.

articles.title: Insulin dependence erodes the cardiac and survival advantage of asymptomatic status after carotid revascularization.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is associated with adverse outcomes after carotid revascularization, with insulin dependence conferring risk beyond DM alone. How this risk varies by symptom status and intervention type remains unclear. We evaluated the independent association of insulin-dependent DM (IDDM) and non-IDDM with 30-day and 1-year outcomes after carotid endarterectomy, transcarotid artery revascularization, and carotid artery stenting, stratified by symptom status.

METHODS: The Vascular Quality Initiative registry was queried for carotid interventions performed between January 2005 and January 2025. Patients were stratified by insulin-dependence and symptom status at presentation. End points were 30-day and 1-year myocardial infarction (MI), ipsilateral stroke, all-cause mortality, ipsilateral stroke or death, and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE; MI, ipsilateral stroke, or mortality). Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for demographic, clinical, and procedural covariates estimated odds ratios (ORs).

RESULTS: Of 275,668 patients meeting inclusion criteria, 73,582 (26.7%) had DM: 44,041 (59.9%) non-IDDM and 29,541 (40.1%) IDDM. At 30 days, there were 1645 MIs, 2051 ipsilateral strokes, 1806 deaths, 3626 strokes or deaths, and 5029 MACE; at 1 year, 2378 MIs, 2924 ipsilateral strokes, 8269 deaths, 10,750 strokes or deaths, and 12,646 MACE, respectively. Controlling for comorbidities and procedure type, IDDM was independently associated with elevated odds of 30-day MI (OR, 1.63), ipsilateral stroke (OR, 1.24), mortality (OR, 1.19), and MACE (OR, 1.19), but not ipsilateral stroke or death. Excess IDDM risk was concentrated among asymptomatic patients (30-day MACE: OR, 1.35 vs 1.07 in symptomatic patients; interaction P < .001). Asymptomatic IDDM patients had higher 30-day MI odds (OR, 1.54; P < .001) than symptomatic patients without DM, with equivalent 30-day MACE (OR, 1.05; P = .41) and higher 1-year MACE (OR, 1.19; P < .001). Relative to carotid endarterectomy, transcarotid artery revascularization, and carotid artery stenting were associated with higher 30-day ipsilateral stroke odds (OR, 2.10 and 1.93, respectively; P ≤ .01 for both) without differences in MI or mortality; an interaction with insulin dependence was nonsignificant for every end point.

CONCLUSIONS: Insulin-dependent, diabetes was independently associated with substantially elevated odds of MI, ipsilateral stroke, mortality, and MACE after carotid revascularization, with risk sustained at 1 year. For cardiac and survival end points, asymptomatic patients with IDDM occupied a risk stratum comparable with symptomatic patients without diabetes. Asymptomatic status may therefore not confer the same composite risk advantage in insulin-dependent patients, with the excess being cardiac- and survival-driven. These findings support more cautious, individualized counseling and shared decision-making for asymptomatic patients with IDDM and identify insulin dependence as a clinically important, currently underemphasized modifier of perioperative risk.

articles.title: Femoral artery access outcomes and technical considerations in vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Femoral artery access in vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (VEDS) poses unique technical challenges due to structurally fragile arteries. This study evaluated femoral access-related complications in patients with genetically confirmed-VEDS and sought to identify procedural and biologic factors that may inform access planning for endovascular procedures.

METHODS: A cross-sectional analysis of patients with pathogenic/likely pathogenic COL3A1 variants who underwent endovascular procedures requiring femoral artery access. Data were obtained from the global genetically confirmed-VEDS Natural History Study and a retrospective single center cohort. Demographics, genotype, procedural indication, access and closure techniques, access-related complications, and outcomes were abstracted from clinical record. Major access-related complications were defined as femoral artery dissection, pseudoaneurysm, rupture, or closure device failure requiring open operative repair.

RESULTS: A total of 117 femoral artery access sites were used in 105 endovascular interventions among 60 patients between 1989 and 2025. Median age at intervention was 39 years, and 53.3% of patients were male. Among 99 procedures with known access modality, 84 were performed percutaneously and 15 involved planned open femoral exposure. Manual compression was used in 33 percutaneous access sites, with no major access-related complications. Percutaneous closure devices were used in 39 access sites; major complications occurred in five access sites across five procedures, all requiring unplanned surgical exposure and repair. One additional percutaneous access site required unplanned open repair for access-related arterial injury and external iliac artery dissection before any closure device was attempted. Of percutaneous closure device failures, Perclose ProGlide (Abbott Vascular, Inc.) and StarClose (Abbott Vascular, Inc.) had the highest rate of failure (18.8% and 33.3%, respectively). Three of four affected patients had large amino acid substitutions or exon skip mutations; the remaining patient had a small amino acid substitution but underwent 16F sheath placement. No access-related complications occurred after planned open exposure.

CONCLUSIONS: Femoral artery access in VEDS requires deliberate individualized planning. In this cohort, manual compression for smaller-caliber access (≤6F) was associated with favorable outcomes, whereas major complications occurred predominantly following attempted percutaneous closure. Planned open exposure, despite use in procedures involving larger sheath sizes, was not associated with access-related complications and may warrant consideration in selected circumstances, including procedures requiring larger sheath sizes, known previous closure-related arterial injury, and high-risk genotypes.

articles.title: Contemporary patterns of lower extremity revascularization for chronic limb-threatening ischemia in the United States: 2016-2022.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) is a major contributor to morbidity and mortality. Although revascularization improves limb outcomes in CLTI, contemporary practice patterns and real-world outcomes remain poorly characterized, particularly considering the conflicting evidence from randomized trials regarding the optimal revascularization and nonoperative management strategies. Our study utilized National Inpatient Sample (NIS) data coupled with U.S. Census data to characterize the contemporary trends of incidence, revascularization approach, and in-hospital outcomes for adults hospitalized for CLTI.

METHODS: We utilized NIS data (2016-2022) to generate survey-weighted national estimates of U.S. adult hospitalizations for CLTI. Age-normalized incidence rates per 100,000 person-years were calculated using population denominators from the U.S. Census Bureau. Admissions with secondary diagnoses of trauma or arterial dissection were excluded. We evaluated the incidence of CLTI hospitalizations and the rates of in-hospital revascularization type (open, endovascular, or no revascularization), major amputation, and mortality. Outcomes by revascularization strategies (open vs endovascular) were stratified a priori by sex, frailty (Risk Analysis Index), diabetes status, and clinical presentation subgroups. The Mann-Kendall test was used to determine the monotonic temporal trends.

RESULTS: The analysis included 46,915 adult CLTI hospitalizations (mean age, 69.7 years; 40.0% women; 69.5% White patients). The overall CLTI incidence was 7.28 per 100,000 person-years, initially declining until nadir in 2020 with a reversal and steady increase thereafter. A total of 28,763 (61.3%) CLTI hospitalizations involved revascularization (n = 14,252 [49.5%] open and/or n = 16,950 [58.9%] endovascular). The proportion of open revascularization procedures decreased (Ptrend = 0.016), whereas the proportion of endovascular procedures remained stable (Ptrend = 0.368), and the number of hospitalizations without revascularization increased (Ptrend = 0.016) over time. The rates of endovascular revascularization increased among women, nonfrail patients, and patients presenting with rest pain (all Ptrend > 0.05). Overall, the rates of in-hospital amputation (n = 6270 [13.4%]) and mortality (n = 1086 [2.3%]) remained stable (Ptrend > 0.05). However, the proportion of patients discharged alive and without amputation increased the most substantially among those with hospitalization without revascularization (Ptrend = 0.007).

CONCLUSIONS: This study provides an contemporary analysis of U.S. hospitalizations for CLTI, demonstrating increasing rates following 2020. Overall, the in-hospital rates of open revascularization declined in favor of nonoperative strategies, corresponding with the greatest increase in alive discharges without amputations. The relative selection of endovascular strategies varied notably by sex, frailty, and clinical presentation. Our findings indicate the need for further investigation into the optimal selection of patients with CLTI and the coordinated integration of nonoperative care, including medical optimization, with revascularization strategies.

articles.title: Tumor necrosis factor inhibitors and cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis is associated with persistent systemic inflammation and increased cardiovascular risk.

OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between anti-TNF therapy and clinical cardiovascular outcomes in adults with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis.

METHODS: The authors conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and prospectively registered the protocol in PROSPERO (CRD420251270784). Randomized controlled trials and comparative observational studies evaluating anti-TNF therapy versus placebo, no anti-TNF exposure, topical therapy and/or phototherapy, or non-biologic systemic therapy were eligible. Outcomes of interest were Major Adverse Cardiovascular Events (MACE), myocardial infarction, stroke, cardiovascular death, heart failure, atrial fibrillation, venous thromboembolism, and all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: Fourteen studies were included. In randomized evidence, anti-TNF therapy was not associated with significant differences in the risk of MACE, myocardial infarction, stroke, or heart failure. In observational analyses stratified by comparator, anti-TNF therapy was associated with a lower pooled risk of reported cardiovascular events versus topical therapy, but not versus oral therapy or phototherapy.

STUDY LIMITATIONS: The available evidence was limited by short follow-up in randomized trials, low cardiovascular event counts, wide confidence intervals, and indirect assessment of cardiovascular outcomes, as most trials were designed primarily for dermatologic efficacy and general safety rather than cardiovascular endpoints.

CONCLUSIONS: Anti-TNF agents were not associated with a clear increase in major cardiovascular risk and appear to have an acceptable short-term cardiovascular safety profile. However, current evidence does not establish a conclusive cardioprotective effect, and larger prospective studies with longer follow-up are needed.

articles.title: Revascularization of Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis: Cognitive Results of the CREST-2 Randomized Trials.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Studies show that asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis is associated with diminished cognition. Whether carotid revascularization leads to cognitive improvement is unclear.

OBJECTIVE: To determine whether carotid revascularization improves cognition.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: Prespecified cognitive secondary outcomes of the CREST-2 randomized clinical trials of patients 35 years or older with 70% or greater asymptomatic carotid stenosis. Enrollment was December 2014 through July 2024, and follow-up ended July 2025. Five cognitive tests were administered before treatment and annually up to 4 years. Cognitive performances from 146 clinical sites were centrally assessed by telephone, blinded to treatment.

INTERVENTIONS: Two trials compared carotid stenting plus intensive medical management (CAS + IMM) with IMM alone and carotid endarterectomy plus IMM (CEA + IMM) with IMM alone.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: Five cognitive tests, assessing learning, memory, executive function, attention, and processing speed, administered to all patients, were assessed for unadjusted and adjusted mean z scores using a linear mixed model. The minimal clinically important difference was 0.50 SD between treatment groups. The prespecified primary analysis was the fully adjusted composite z score at 4 years. Secondary analyses assessed the individual tests and at the test intervals.

RESULTS: Among 2366 US study patients, 2165 (91.5%) participated in cognitive assessments, 1078 in the CAS trial (529 CAS + IMM; 549 IMM alone) and 1087 in the CEA trial (543 CEA + IMM; 544 IMM alone); mean age was 70.1 years (SD, 7.7) and 37.8% were female. Following baseline, 4954 test batteries were administered for a mean of 2.24 (SD, 1.09) follow-up years. There were no treatment-related differences in the fully adjusted estimated composite z scores at 4 years for either the CAS trial (CAS + IMM, 0.22 [95% CI, 0.13 to 0.30] vs IMM alone, 0.18 [95% CI, 0.09 to 0.27]; between-group difference, 0.03 [95% CI, -0.09 to 0.15]) or the CEA trial (CEA + IMM, 0.25 [95% CI, 0.17 to 0.33] vs IMM, 0.23 [95% CI, 0.15 to 0.32]; between-group difference, 0.02 [95% CI, -0.09 to 0.14]). There were no significant differences between revascularization plus medical management vs IMM alone for any individual cognitive test.

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In patients with severe asymptomatic carotid artery stenosis, revascularization with either CAS or CEA plus IMM, compared with IMM alone, did not significantly improve cognitive function at up to 4 years of follow-up.

articles.title: Revascularization in Asymptomatic Carotid Artery Stenosis With Hemodynamic Impairment and Cognitive Outcomes: The CREST-H Substudy of the CREST-2 Randomized Clinical Trial.
articles.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Cerebral hemodynamic impairment in patients with asymptomatic internal carotid artery (ICA) stenosis is associated with reduced cognition. It is uncertain whether revascularization might be an effective treatment for cognitive impairment in these patients.

OBJECTIVE: To test whether any cognitive benefit from revascularization of high-grade, asymptomatic ICA stenosis varies based on the degree of baseline cerebral hemodynamic impairment.

DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This substudy was conducted within a multicenter phase 3 randomized clinical trial. Adults (aged 35-86 years) without dementia with eighth-grade education or higher and unilateral asymptomatic ICA stenosis greater than or equal to 70% were enrolled from January 2018 to July 2024 at 61 sites in North America (last follow-up in July 2025). Of 607 participants screened from 2485 in CREST-2, 392 were enrolled. Magnetic resonance or computed tomographic perfusion imaging tested for baseline hemodynamic impairment defined by delayed time-to-peak (TTP) arrival of intravenous contrast in the hemisphere ipsilateral minus contralateral to the stenotic artery.

INTERVENTION: Carotid revascularization (endarterectomy or stenting) plus intensive medical management (IMM) vs IMM alone.

MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the difference in composite cognitive z score over 1 year based on 5 cognitive tests. The primary analysis tested for an interaction between treatment group (revascularization vs IMM alone) and degree of baseline hemodynamic impairment among those with reduced baseline cognition (cognitive z score ≤-1.0 SD).

RESULTS: Of 392 participants enrolled (mean age, 71 years; 125 [32%] females), 61 were excluded for missing baseline imaging and 40 for missing cognitive examinations or other covariates, leaving 291 with complete data. Fifty-one had reduced cognition at baseline (25 in the revascularization group and 26 in the IMM alone group). TTP ranged from no interhemispheric TTP delay to a more-than-2-second delay. Mean (SD) cognitive z scores were -1.36 (0.51) at baseline and -1.17 (0.47) at 1 year in the revascularization group and -1.34 (0.83) at baseline and -1.01 (0.97) at 1 year in the IMM alone group. The primary analysis showed no difference in cognition by treatment group over 1 year, adjusting for treatment group × hemodynamic status interaction and other covariates (adjusted difference in cognitive z score, -0.15 SD [95% CI, -0.54 to 0.24]). The interaction was not significant (β estimate = 0.018 [95% CI, -0.025 to 0.061]; P = .40).

CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: In this substudy of a randomized clinical trial, there was no differential effect of revascularization vs IMM alone on cognition over 1 year by cerebral hemodynamic status among those with baseline reduced cognition, suggesting that revascularization does not improve cognitive dysfunction by restoring flow to the brain in chronic asymptomatic carotid stenosis.

articles.englishSummary: IMPORTANCE: Cerebral hemodynamic impairment in patients with asymptomatic internal carotid artery (ICA) stenosis is associated with reduced cognition. It is uncertain whether revascularization might be an effective treatment for cognitive impairment in these patients. OBJECTIVE: To test whether any cognitive benefit from revascularization of high-grade, asymptomatic ICA stenosis varies based on the degree of baseline cerebral hemodynamic impairment.

articles.title: Performance of Western HA-VTE risk models in East Asian populations: a prospective multicenter study.
articles.abstract: Hospital-associated venous thromboembolism (HA-VTE) causes significant morbidity, but risk prediction models are inconsistently validated, especially in non-Western populations. We prospectively validated 5 HA-VTE risk scores (Caprini, Padua, IMPROVE [International Medical Prevention Registry on Venous Thromboembolism], Kucher, and Intermountain) in a prospective multicenter cohort of 2948 adult inpatients from 17 Chinese hospitals. Symptomatic VTE events were recorded through 3 months of follow-up. The 90-day HA-VTE incidence was 2.54%. All 5 models showed moderate discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC], 0.726-0.759). Caprini, Padua, and Intermountain models did not differ significantly (DeLong test, P> .05). Caprini had the highest sensitivity (0.83) but classified 42.6% of patients as being at high risk. Padua and Intermountain favored specificity (0.75-0.81) with lower sensitivity (0.64-0.67). Clinical model selection should align with specific balances between sensitivity and utility. In surgical inpatients, Caprini performed best (AUC, 0.804; sensitivity, 0.90; negative predictive value, 1.00), although its more than 40 input variables limit practical use. Calibration was generally acceptable. Performance varied across subgroups. The prophylaxis subgroup showed attenuated performance, with reduced discrimination (eg, Caprini AUC decreased to 0.682) and less stable calibration. Western HA-VTE models have moderate predictive value in East Asian inpatient populations. Performance differs across subgroups. Local recalibration and development of simpler, population-specific scores are needed.

articles.title: Surgery Versus Ultrasound-Guided Foam Sclerotherapy for the Treatment of Isolated Anterior Saphenous Vein Incompetence: A Single-Center Randomized Trial.
articles.abstract: Background: Isolated anterior saphenous vein (ASV) incompetence is a clinically relevant source of symptomatic anterior thigh varicose veins, which may cause pain, heaviness, swelling and serious complication such as superficial vein thrombosis. Therefore, targeted management is often required, yet evidence guiding treatment remains limited. This single-center, randomized trial compared high ligation surgery in combination with phlebectomy and ultrasound-guided foam sclerotherapy (UGFS). Methods: Thirty-nine limbs of 35 patients (19 allocated to surgery, 20 to UGFS) were treated and followed up at 1 and 3 years. The primary outcome was ASV-territory recurrence defined as reflux time > 0.5 s along the ASV in the UGFS group or new anterior thigh varicosities connected to the previous saphenofemoral junction in the surgical group at 3 years. Secondary outcomes were the same duplex endpoint at 1 year, recurrence of clinically visible varicose veins, and groin neovascularization at 1 and 3 years. Results: ASV-territory recurrence was numerically higher after UGFS (63% vs. 33%) at 3 years, although the difference was not statistically significant, whereas recurrence was higher after UGFS than surgery at 1 year (65% vs. 11%; p < 0.001). Clinical recurrence rates did not differ significantly between groups at 1 and 3 years. Neovascularization was observed exclusively in the surgery group at 1 year and remained more frequent at 3 years (44% vs. 5%). Conclusions: Our findings suggest better short-term disease control with surgery than with UGFS for isolated ASV incompetence, whereas the prespecified primary endpoint of ASV-territory recurrence at 3-years did not differ significantly between groups. Both surgery and UGFS may therefore be considered for selected patients, with treatment choice guided by patient-centered factors, including vein anatomy, invasiveness, and patient preference.

articles.title: Sequential decision-making in endovascular stroke therapy: benefit and harm of the next retrieval attempt after failed reperfusion.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: After failed reperfusion in endovascular thrombectomy (EVT), interventionalists must outweigh the expected benefit of an additional retrieval attempt with the outcome of the current angiographic result. Framing EVT as an infinite-horizon optimal stopping problem, the present study provides a per-pass evaluation of the expected benefit of EVT continuation versus procedural termination after unsuccessful reperfusion, based on large-scale real-world registry data.

METHODS: Patients from the German Stroke Registry - Endovascular Treatment (GSR-ET) between 2015 and 2023 were screened. Inclusion criteria were (1) age ≥ 18 years, (2) anterior circulation LVO, (3) 1-15 retrieval attempts and (4) availability of relevant clinical data. Primary endpoint was the rate of good functional outcome, defined as modified Rankin Scale (mRS) score 0-2 at 90 days. For each retrieval attempt, patients were stratified into successful reperfusion (mTICI 2b-3) and persistent occlusion (mTICI 0-2a). The net expected benefit of EVT continuation, Δ(k), was defined as the difference between the mRS 0-2 rate at pass k + 1, and the mRS 0-2 rate for unsuccessful reperfusion at pass k. A positive Δ(k) indicates that continuation is favored at that decision node k. The pass at which Δ(k) first becomes non-significant identifies the empirical, optimal stopping threshold.

RESULTS: Among 9,495 included patients, successful reperfusion (mTICI 2b-3) was achieved in 8,405 (89%), and 3,428 (36%) achieved good functional outcome at 90 days. Up to six retrieval attempts, Δ(k) was positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05), indicating that continuation of EVT was associated with superior expected outcome at each of these decision points. At pass seven, Δ(k) became negative and lost statistical significance (p = 0.53), identifying this as the empirical optimal stopping threshold.

CONCLUSION: Continuation of EVT up to six retrieval attempts confers a significant functional benefit over termination after unsuccessful reperfusion. These findings provide a decision-theoretic basis for individualized intraprocedural decision-making and suggest that functional independence can be achieved beyond conventionally assumed pass thresholds.

METHODS: Patients from the German Stroke Registry - Endovascular Treatment (GSR-ET) between 2015 and 2023 were screened.

articles.title: Two-Year Outcomes of the Prospective THRILLER Registry on Popliteal and Infrapopliteal Endovascular Interventions for CLTI.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Over 70% of patients with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI) present with below-the-knee disease, and there is a growing trend towards endovascular revascularization.

OBJECTIVES: The Dutch Chronic Lower Limb-Threatening Ischemia Registry (THRILLER) aimed to provide real-world data on outcomes after popliteal and infrapopliteal endovascular revascularization to guide revascularization strategies.

METHODS: This prospective multicenter registry included consecutive CLTI patients undergoing popliteal or infrapopliteal endovascular revascularization in seven Dutch hospitals. Primary outcomes were limb salvage and amputation-free survival (AFS) at 24 months, estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method.

RESULTS: Between February 2021 and December 2023, a total of 1,119 interventions in 1,060 limbs (938 patients) were included, treating 551 popliteal, 1,352 tibial, and 239 pedal lesions. The median follow-up was 43.6 months (Q1-Q3: 35.5-52.7 months). Overall, 78.4% (831/1,060) of the limbs were Rutherford 5 and 8.1% (86/1,060) were Rutherford 6; 41.3% (382/926) were WIfI (Wound, Ischemia, and foot Infection) stage 4. Technical success was achieved in 92.3% (1,033/1,119). Limb salvage and AFS decreased significantly after technical failure and with increasing WIfI stage and Rutherford category. Compared to Rutherford 5, Rutherford 6 limbs had significantly worse limb salvage (HR: 3.07; 95% CI: 1.89-4.99; P < 0.001) and AFS (HR: 2.07; 95% CI: 1.50-2.86; P < 0.001). For AFS, the excess risk of Rutherford 6 was greatest in the first 3 months (HR: 14.13; 95% CI: 4.94-40.38 vs Rutherford 4; P < 0.001).

CONCLUSIONS: Endovascular revascularization for popliteal and infrapopliteal disease in patients with CLTI is safe and effective in preventing limb loss and mortality at 2 years, although patients with Rutherford 6 limbs face significantly worse outcomes, particularly in the first 3 months.

METHODS: This prospective multicenter registry included consecutive CLTI patients undergoing popliteal or infrapopliteal endovascular revascularization in seven Dutch hospitals.

articles.title: JTH in Clinic: Venous Thromboembolism (VTE) Prophylaxis of Pediatric Patients at Risk of VTE.
articles.abstract: As the incidence of venous thromboembolism (VTE) increases in hospitalized children, there is an urgent need to improve VTE prevention strategies in this population. Implementation of thromboprophylaxis, which includes mechanical and pharmacological interventions, varies in practice due to limited pediatric-specific data and, until recently, a lack of evidence-based guidelines. However, recent randomized clinical trials and well-designed multicenter observational studies have provided improved evidence on the safety and efficacy of anticoagulants for VTE prevention in specific pediatric subpopulations supporting the development of risk assessment models to help identify subgroups of children at high risk for VTE. Based on these data, the American Society of Hematology and International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis recently developed the first evidence-based guideline for anticoagulant prophylaxis in children at risk of VTE. While this guideline is an exciting step towards preventing VTE-associated harm, VTE prevention remains complex due to unique pediatric risk factors and changing physiology with age, resulting in heterogeneous VTE and bleeding risk profiles. In this case-based review, we apply the new guideline and supporting evidence to guide decisions regarding the use of thromboprophylaxis in pediatric cases commonly encountered in clinical practice, highlighting the nuances of VTE prevention in critically ill children. We review the complex decision-making process required prior to initiation of pharmacologic prophylaxis, including assessment of VTE risk, bleeding risk, and shared decision-making with families. Additionally, we highlight the importance of multidisciplinary teams in VTE prevention and anticoagulant stewardship, as well as the similarities and differences in pediatric versus adult practice.

articles.title: Association of completion imaging modalities and carotid endarterectomy outcomes in the Vascular Quality Initiative.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: Completion imaging after carotid endarterectomy (CEA) confirms technical success and identifies defects requiring correction. However, the comparative effectiveness of imaging modalities in detecting clinically significant problems remains unclear. This study evaluated completion imaging patterns, intraoperative re-exploration as a surrogate for detection efficacy, and associated postoperative outcomes.

METHODS: CEAs performed between 2012 and 2024 in the Vascular Quality Initiative were analyzed. Completion imaging was categorized as none, Doppler, duplex ultrasound, or angiography. Intraoperative re-exploration rates were compared across modalities to assess detection of technical defects requiring revision. Postoperative outcomes were analyzed among patients who required re-exploration. Inverse probability weighted logistic regression estimated adjusted odds ratios (aOR). Temporal trends were also analyzed.

RESULTS: Among 208,786 CEAs, 24% had no completion imaging, 48% used Doppler, 24% duplex, and 4% angiography. Angiography had the highest intraoperative re-exploration rate (none, 0.9%; Doppler, 0.9%; duplex, 2.3%; angiography, 3.6%; P < .001). Among the 2723 patients who required re-exploration, postoperative stroke occurred in 8.3% with no imaging, 12.5% with Doppler, 3.7% with duplex, and 22.5% with angiography (P < .001). In inverse probability weighted-adjusted analyses, intraoperative duplex was associated with significant reduction in postoperative stroke compared with: no imaging [aOR, 0.43; 95% confidence interval (CI), 0.27-0.69], Doppler (aOR, 0.28; 95% CI, 0.19-0.40), and angiography (aOR, 0.13; 95% CI, 0.09-0.20), all P < .001. Overall, angiography had the worst stroke outcomes. Doppler and angiography performed worse than duplex across additional end points, including ipsilateral stroke, transient ischemic attack, any neurological event, return to operating room, and 30-day mortality. Despite the stronger safety profile of duplex, it remains underused, as most CEAs performed in the last 15 years have used Doppler or no imaging.

CONCLUSIONS: Re-exploration and stroke outcomes after completion imaging reflect each modality's safety and efficacy in detecting significant technical defects. Duplex ultrasound demonstrated the lowest stroke rates and overall complications compared with angiography, Doppler, and no imaging, suggesting its superior efficacy and safety. Doppler showed intermediate performance, whereas angiography carried the highest risk among patients who required re-exploration. Despite strong evidence favoring duplex, the majority of surgeons performing CEAs still rely on Doppler or omit any completion imaging. Greater use of duplex ultrasound and incorporation of intraoperative duplex assessment into vascular training may improve intraoperative assessment, although further prospective evaluation is warranted.

This study evaluated completion imaging patterns, intraoperative re-exploration as a surrogate for detection efficacy, and associated postoperative outcomes.

articles.title: Risk of Venous Thromboembolism in Kidney Transplant Recipients with Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kidney transplant recipients with autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) may be at higher risk of venous thromboembolism than non-ADPKD recipients.

METHODS: We conducted an observational study of adult kidney transplant recipients at a single center, the University Medical Center Groningen (UMCG; n=1179, 393 with ADPKD), and replicated key analyses in the multicenter Swiss Transplant Cohort Study (STCS; n=4415, 710 with ADPKD). The primary endpoint was time to first venous thromboembolism after transplantation or death related to venous thromboembolism (identified through medical record review), analyzed using Kaplan-Meier estimates and Cox regression. Data were pooled for subgroup analyses and to assess determinants of post-transplant venous thromboembolism risk.

RESULTS: Venous thromboembolism occurred more often in ADPKD than non-ADPKD kidney transplant recipients (log-rank p=0.04 and p<0.001 for UMCG and STCS, respectively). The 10-year cumulative venous thromboembolism incidence was 13.5% [95% CI: 9.4, 17.5], versus 9.6% [95% CI: 7.0, 12.1] in ADPKD versus non-ADPKD recipients in UMCG, and 21.0% [95% CI: 17.0, 24.7] versus 15.1% [95% CI: 13.5, 16.6] in STCS. Median [Q1, Q3] time to venous thromboembolism were similar across cohorts (UMCG: 1.7 [0.4, 4.9], STCS: 1.4 [0.2, 4.8] years). Venous thromboembolism risk was highest in the early (<2 years) post-transplant period. After adjustment for venous thromboembolism risk factors, ADPKD remained independently associated with post-transplant venous thromboembolism in both cohorts (UMCG HR 1.80 [95% CI: 1.21, 2.69]; STCS HR 1.39 [95% CI: 1.13, 1.72]). The association between ADPKD and risk of venous thromboembolism was more pronounced in males. Hemoglobin levels after kidney transplantation were approximately 7.0 ± 0.8% higher in ADPKD recipients, particularly in males, with corresponding higher risks of erythrocytosis during follow-up. Incorporating longitudinal hemoglobin as a time-varying covariate attenuated the association between ADPKD and venous thromboembolism, suggesting that the association was at least partially driven by higher hemoglobin levels.

CONCLUSIONS: Kidney transplant recipients were at high risk for venous thromboembolism, and those with ADPKD are at an even higher risk.

articles.title: Whole-transcriptome single-cell spatial landscape of instability in human carotid atherosclerosis.
articles.abstract:
AIMS: Carotid atherosclerotic plaque instability is a major cause of ischemic stroke. While current clinical guidelines for carotid endarterectomy rely primarily on stenosis severity and patient symptomatology, unstable plaques can cause strokes even with low to moderate stenosis, suggesting that factors beyond plaque stenosis may drive its instability. This study aimed to characterize the cellular and spatial features of plaque instability at both single-cell and subcellular resolution.

METHODS AND RESULTS: single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was performed on carotid endarterectomy samples from patients with clinically and histologically classified stable or unstable plaques, consisting of more than 53,000 cells. Vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs), macrophages, and T-lymphocytes accounted for ∼85% of plaque-resident cells, with unstable plaques showing increased abundance of inflammatory synthetic VSMCs, GZMK+ cytotoxic T-lymphocytes, and antigen-presenting macrophages. In contrast, stable plaques were enriched in contractile and fibroblast-like VSMCs, alongside MRC1+ resident-like macrophages. To then spatially map these populations, CosMx™ high-plex spatial transcriptomics was integrated utilizing the unprecedented whole-transcriptome (∼18,934 targets) Human Discovery RNA panel. This revealed a distinct spatially disorganized plaque architecture in unstable plaques, characterized by infiltration of inflammatory synthetic VSMCs and effector T-lymphocytes distributed across both the fibrotic cap and lipid core, alongside distinct multicellular microenvironments enriched for adaptive immune engagement. This was in contrast to stable plaques, which exhibited more structured, macrophage-dominant spatial microenvironments and neighborhoods. We lastly profiled ∼90,000 paired peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) to assess the plaque macroenvironment. PBMCs surrounding unstable plaques displayed exclusive enrichment of CD14+CD16+ intermediate monocytes and effector T-lymphocytes, which were depleted surrounding stable plaques. Ligand-receptor interaction analyses within CCL and CXCL-mediated pathways revealed enhanced immune-stromal signaling between PBMC-derived monocytes and plaque-resident VSMCs in the unstable plaque group, with coordinated chemokine-driven interactions indicating a shift toward VSMC- and T-lymphocyte mediated recruitment of circulating immune cells.

CONCLUSIONS: These results demonstrate that carotid plaque instability is driven by spatially coordinated expansion of inflammatory VSMCs and effector immune cells within the plaque and from the circulation, with a shift from predominantly innate immune-dominant characteristics in stable plaques toward adaptive immune-enriched responses in unstable conditions. This integrated single-cell and spatial transcriptomic approach refines an integrated immune-stromal framework linking local plaque remodeling with systemic immune activation, highlighting key tissue-resident and circulating contributors to instability and establishing a foundation for mechanism-informed diagnostics and targeted therapeutic strategies beyond stenosis severity.

articles.title: Mechanical Thrombectomy Versus Anticoagulation Alone in Intermediate-High Risk PE: Improved Functional 90-Day Outcomes in STORM-PE RCT.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Up to 50% of pulmonary embolism (PE) survivors experience long-term functional limitations and reduced quality of life (QoL). Reperfusion strategies can rapidly relieve right-ventricular (RV) dysfunction and prevent clinical deterioration or hemodynamic collapse; however, these approaches have never been evaluated in a randomized trial against anticoagulation alone using patient-centered outcomes.

OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate whether mechanical thrombectomy with anticoagulation improves functional, QoL, and safety outcomes compared with anticoagulation alone in patients with acute intermediate-high risk PE over 90 days.

METHODS: STORM-PE enrolled 100 PE patients randomized 1:1 to computer-assisted vacuum thrombectomy (CAVT) with anticoagulation or anticoagulation alone across 22 international sites, with RV-to-left-ventricular (RV/LV) ratio change at 48 hours as the primary endpoint. Secondary endpoints included major adverse events within 7 days, functional and QoL outcomes, mortality, and symptomatic PE recurrence through 90 days.

RESULTS: For all patients, median time from randomization to last follow-up visit was 91.0 days [Q1-Q3: 80.5-100.0]. At 90 days, 66.0% (31/47) of CAVT and 64.2% (34/53) of anticoagulation patients completed the 6-min walk test. The CAVT arm exhibited a longer 6-min walk distance compared with anticoagulation alone (478.7 ± 159.5 m vs 368.0 ± 127.8 m, P = 0.003). More CAVT than anticoagulation patients were NYHA functional class I (97.4% [37/38] vs 75.6% [34/45], P = 0.005) at 90 days. Dyspnea and QoL scores were comparable between groups, with no differences between arms for all-cause mortality, PE-related mortality, and symptomatic PE recurrence within 90 days.

CONCLUSIONS: In STORM-PE, CAVT with anticoagulation resulted in improved functional outcomes at 90 days compared with anticoagulation alone, with equivalent safety rates. This trial supports CAVT as an effective and safe reperfusion strategy for intermediate-high risk PE.

articles.title: Timeless therapeutics: cardiac indications for vitamin K antagonists in clinical practice.
articles.abstract: Anticoagulation is a critical component in the treatment of cardiovascular diseases. Large randomised controlled trials have demonstrated that direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) are effective and safe for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) and treatment or prevention of venous thromboembolism. Nevertheless, for specific cardiac indications and patient characteristics, vitamin K antagonists (VKAs) rather than DOACs are either preferred, or the benefit of DOACs in comparison to VKAs remains uncertain. These include, among others, mechanical heart valves, AF associated with moderate-to-severe mitral stenosis, left ventricular or atrial thrombus, and older patients with frailty. As VKAs will continue to play a vital role in the management of patients with cardiovascular diseases in the foreseeable future, this review discusses cardiac indications and patient characteristics that necessitate the use of VKAs and general management principles of VKA therapy.

articles.title: Structural dynamics of substrate processing by the p97-Ufd1-Npl4-FAF1 machinery.
articles.abstract: The AAA-ATPase VCP/p97 unfolds ubiquitylated proteins in key signaling and cellular homeostasis pathways, yet the mechanisms by which Ufd1-Npl4 and FAF1 adapters handle ubiquitin chains to coordinate substrate loading and processing remain unclear. Our cryo-EM study of p97-Ufd1-Npl4 and FAF1 engaging a substrate reveal interactions that drive substrate processing. While Npl4 is capped by distal ubiquitins, and the initiator ubiquitin can be traced from the Npl4 groove to the ATPase channel at near-atomic resolution, we find that the Npl4 tower adaptively responds to the configurational changes in the ATPase motor's spiral staircase. A helix in FAF1 together with the Ufd1-UT3 domain engage proximal ubiquitins while providing the necessary structural plasticity to accommodate this motion and deliver ubiquitins to Npl4's groove. Our study reveals the intricate, dynamic interplay between p97, Ufd1-Npl4, and FAF1 in efficient processing of ubiquitylated substrates.

articles.title: Atomically dispersed nanoactivators drive innate mitochondrial biogenesis for active neuroprotection in ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Mitigating mitochondrial bioenergetic failure is a pivotal yet formidable neuroprotective goal in treating cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI). However, conventional pharmacological interventions remain largely confined to passive antioxidant defense, which temporarily scavenges reactive oxygen species (ROS) without restoring organelle function. Here, we report a bimetallic nanoactivator (RMV) designed to drive active mitochondrial revival for rescuing ischemic tissues. RMV comprises atomically dispersed ruthenium sites anchored within an oxygen-deficient manganese hydroxide matrix via synergistic Ru-O-Mn bridges. Benefiting from its intrinsic mitochondriotropic properties, RMV effectively intercepts aberrant electron leakage and breaks the self-amplifying cycle of ROS-induced ROS release through cascade multi-enzyme mimetic activities. Importantly, transcriptomic profiling and ultrastructural analysis reveal that RMV transcends passive antioxidant defense by functioning as a bioactive switch. It revives the suppressed SIRT1-PGC1α-TFAM signaling axis, fundamentally driving mitochondrial biogenesis and the reconstruction of functionally intact respiratory chains. In a murine stroke model, RMV treatment induces a 1.52-fold expansion of the neuronal mitochondrial biomass under ischemic stress, thereby suppressing neuronal apoptosis, reducing infarct volumes, and favorably reshaping an M2-polarized neuroimmune microenvironment. These integrated effects yield robust and sustained neurofunctional recovery. Our study shifts the neuroprotective paradigm from reactive damage control to active mitochondrial biogenesis, offering an atomically engineered strategy for ischemic stroke management.

However, conventional pharmacological interventions remain largely confined to passive antioxidant defense, which temporarily scavenges reactive oxygen species (ROS) without restoring organelle function. Here, we report a bimetallic nanoactivator (RMV) designed to drive active mitochondrial revival for rescuing ischemic tissues.

articles.title: Association of Prethrombectomy Hemorrhagic Infarction on MRI With Further Transformation and Functional Outcomes: A Multicenter Study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Mechanical thrombectomy (MT) is the standard of care for acute ischemic stroke from large vessel occlusion (LVO). Although postprocedural parenchymal hematoma (PH) predicts poor outcomes, pretreatment hemorrhagic infarction (HI), defined as petechial bleeding within infarcted tissue, is traditionally viewed as a benign radiologic finding. Its significance on sensitive preintervention MRI remains underexplored. We evaluated whether pretreatment MRI HI is associated with 90-day functional dependence, post-MT PH, and symptomatic intracerebral hemorrhage (SICH).

METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included consecutive patients with anterior circulation LVO undergoing MT at 2 stroke centers (2015-2022). Patients required pre-MT T2*-weighted MRI. HI was graded (types I/II) per European Cooperative Acute Stroke Study III criteria in blinded fashion. The primary outcome was 90-day functional dependence (modified Rankin Scale 3-6). Secondary outcomes were post-MT ipsilateral PH and SICH. We used multivariable Bayesian and frequentist logistic regression to adjust for age, sex, NIH Stroke Scale, baseline disability, comorbidities, infarct volume, and procedural factors.

RESULTS: Among 479 patients (median age 72 years; 46% female; 50% received IV thrombolysis), pretreatment HI was identified in 25 (5.2%), with excellent inter-rater agreement (Cohen κ = 0.9). Functional dependence at 90 days occurred in 47% of the total cohort, ipsilateral PH in 9.4%, and SICH in 3.1%. In multivariable analysis, pre-MT HI was independently associated with 90-day functional dependence (Bayesian adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 6.66, 95% credible interval [CrI] 2.15-24.28, Pr[OR > 1] = 1.00; frequentist aOR 5.95, 95% CI 1.91-18.52, p = 0.002). Pre-MT HI also demonstrated a high posterior probability of association with post-MT ipsilateral PH (Bayesian aOR 2.76, 95% CrI 0.73-9.26, Pr[OR > 1] = 0.94; frequentist aOR 2.84, 95% CI 0.84-9.58, p = 0.091) and SICH (Bayesian aOR 5.59, 95% CrI 0.63-34.92, Pr[OR > 1] = 0.95; frequentist aOR 6.02, 95% CI 1.00-36.11, p = 0.049).

DISCUSSION: HI detected on pretreatment MRI is an independent predictor of poor long-term functional outcomes and correlates with post-MT PH/SICH. Pre-MT HI may reflect significant blood-brain barrier disruption and microvascular fragility, serving as a marker of reperfusion vulnerability. Limitations include the retrospective design and the relatively low frequency of HI, PH, and SICH, which were addressed using Bayesian modeling to quantify uncertainty. Although not a contraindication to MT, identifying HI may aid in periprocedural risk stratification and serve as a candidate marker for future neuroprotective trials.

articles.title: Sex Differences in Blood Pressure Dynamics and Outcomes After Endovascular Thrombectomy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Optimal blood pressure (BP) management after endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) for acute ischemic stroke (AIS) remains controversial, and whether early BP dynamics differentially affect outcomes among female and male participants is unclear.

METHODS: This was an exploratory secondary analysis of ENCHANTED2/MT, a multicenter, open-label, blinded-end point randomized trial conducted in 44 tertiary hospitals in China. Eligible adults had AIS due to large-vessel occlusion, successful reperfusion after EVT, and persistent elevated systolic BP (SBP) within 3 hours after reperfusion. Serial BP measurements obtained during the first 72 hours after randomization were used to estimate patient-specific mean BP trajectories and short-term BP variability with a location-scale mixed-effects modeling approach. Associations of mean BP, BP variability, and randomized intensive vs standard BP lowering strategy with clinical outcomes were examined, with sex being evaluated as an effect modifier. The primary outcome was the 90-day modified Rankin Scale (mRS).

RESULTS: Among 816 patients (mean age 67.6 ± 12.0 years; 38% female), intensive BP management was associated with worse 90-day ordinal mRS outcome among male participants (adjusted common odds ratio [acOR] 1.91; 95% CI 1.29-2.83), whereas the corresponding estimate among female participants was closer to null (acOR 0.94; 95% CI 0.56-1.57; ratio of acORs 0.49; 95% CI 0.26-0.94). In separate postrandomization BP exposure models, each 5 mm Hg higher mean SBP was associated with worse 90-day mRS outcome among male participants (acOR 1.11; 95% CI 1.03-1.20), whereas no clear adverse association was observed among female participants (acOR 0.95; 95% CI 0.85-1.05; ratio of acORs 0.85; 95% CI 0.75-0.97). SBP variability showed weaker and less consistent sex differential associations. Findings across secondary outcomes were directionally similar but exploratory.

DISCUSSION: In this exploratory secondary analysis of ENCHANTED2/MT, randomized BP management strategy and early post-thrombectomy BP dynamics showed sex-stratified associations with outcomes. These associations may reflect biological sex and sex-related differences in baseline clinical and vascular characteristics. These findings are hypothesis generating and should be confirmed in prospectively designed studies before informing sex-specific BP management after EVT.

articles.title: Ferroptosis-related endothelial protection by Danhong injection in cerebral and renal ischemia/reperfusion injury: network pharmacology and validation in endothelial cells.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke and ischemic acute kidney injury are both clinical challenges. Danhong injection (DHI) has been reported to exert protective effects against cerebral and renal ischemic injury. However, the shared therapeutic targets and mechanisms underlying its effects in these two organs remain unclear. Using network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and in vitro experiments, this study investigated shared targets and pathways associated with cerebral and renal ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury and evaluated whether DHI exerted a shared ferroptosis-related endothelial protective effect in bEnd3 cells and mouse renal glomerular endothelial cells (MRGECs) subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R). Network pharmacology suggested that ferroptosis may be involved in the effects of DHI against cerebral and renal I/R injury. Molecular docking predicted potential interactions between selected DHI components and glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) or solute carrier family 7 member 11 (SLC7A11). Molecular dynamic simulations indicated that the selected protein-ligand complexes remained relatively stable, while molecular mechanics Poisson-Boltzmann surface area analyses supported favorable binding free energies. Similar to Fer-1 treatment, DHI improved cell proliferation, reduced Fe2+ levels and lipid peroxidation, and increased GPX4 and SLC7A11 expression in OGD/R-induced bEnd3 cells and MRGECs. In conclusion, DHI attenuated injury in bEnd3 cells and MRGECs subjected to OGD/R, accompanied by reduced Fe2+ accumulation and lipid peroxidation and increased GPX4 and SLC7A11 expression. Together with the shared ferroptosis-related pathways identified by network pharmacology, these findings suggest a common ferroptosis-related endothelial protective response to DHI in cerebral and renal I/R injury.

articles.title: Neutrophil-hitchhiking and microglia-homing liposomes co-delivering artemisinin and edaravone for cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury treatment.
articles.abstract: Clinical outcomes of cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) remain unsatisfactory, largely because the blood-brain barrier (BBB) restricts the delivery of most neuroprotective agents to the brain parenchyma. Although artemisinin (ART) and edaravone (EDV) have shown promising therapeutic potential for CIRI, their clinical application is hindered by their short in vivo half-lives and poor aqueous solubility. Neutrophil infiltration triggered by CIRI provides a unique opportunity for drug delivery across the BBB, whereas targeted modulation of microglia represents a key strategy for mitigating reperfusion-induced injury. However, existing neutrophil hitchhiking delivery systems primarily focus on BBB traversal and generally lack a secondary targeting mechanism to promote preferential drug accumulation within the inflammatory core of the ischemic brain. Here, we developed a dual-modified liposomal system functionalized with sialic acid (SA) and phosphatidylserine (PS) (ART/EDV-PS/SAL) for the co-delivery of ART and EDV. This system enables sequential two-step targeting through SA-mediated neutrophil hitchhiking for BBB traversal, followed by PS-mediated microglial homing within ischemic brain tissue. In a mouse model of CIRI, ART/EDV-PS/SAL markedly reduced cerebral infarct volume, preserved BBB integrity, and significantly improved neurological and behavioral outcomes. Mechanistically, ART/EDV-PS/SAL exerted neuroprotective effects by suppressing NLRP3 inflammasome activation, attenuating pyroptosis, and promoting microglial polarization toward the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype. By harnessing endogenous immune cells to achieve efficient and sequential drug targeting, this study establishes a promising nanodelivery platform for the treatment of ischemic stroke and other neuroinflammatory disorders.
