articles.title: Sustained intestinal hydrogen delivery enhances exercise endurance in mice with coordinated gut-liver-muscle metabolic responses.
articles.abstract: Molecular hydrogen (H2) exerts unique metabolic-modulating effects, yet its clinical translation is hindered by a fundamental pharmacokinetic challenge. Rapid systemic diffusion and short intestinal residence time require frequent dosing regimens to maintain sustained tissue exposure. Here, we demonstrate that sustained intestinal H2 delivery improves exercise endurance and correlates with coordinated metabolic responses across the intestine, liver, and skeletal muscle. Mechanistically, continuous intestinal H2 exposure is associated with reduced intestinal inflammatory and oxidative alterations, increased hepatic FOXO1 and gluconeogenesis-related protein abundance, as well as altered expression of glycolysis- and lactate-handling components in skeletal muscle. These observations support a working model in which sustained intestinal H2 exposure is associated with coordinated gut-liver-muscle metabolic responses during strenuous exercise. Although these coordinated metabolic changes were initially observed using a high-frequency hydrogen-rich water (HRW) gavage protocol, this approach is limited by repeated-administration requirements. To address this translational barrier and prolong H2 exposure duration, we engineered Mg@SiO2@ES, an orally deliverable, intestine-targeted hydrogen-generating micro-reactor. This formulation is designed to resist gastric degradation and enable sustained H2 release selectively within the intestinal lumen. It recapitulates multiple metabolic and exercise-related phenotypes observed with repeated HRW gavage. In murine acute exhaustive-exercise models, a single pre-exercise gavage of Mg@SiO2@ES enhanced exercise performance. This improvement was accompanied by attenuated oxidative stress, lower blood urea nitrogen (BUN) levels, and better preservation of circulating glucose and intramuscular glycogen stores. Collectively, these findings highlight the potential of sustained intestinal H2 delivery to elicit systemic metabolic responses. They also demonstrate bioengineered gas-releasing micro-reactors as a promising strategy for further exploration of targeted H2 delivery in metabolic and exercise-related research.

articles.title: Sequential blood-brain barrier-penetrating and microglial-mitochondria-targeting nanosystem for ischemic stroke therapy.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) causes severe neurological deficits closely linked to microglial overactivation after ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury, a process governed by mitochondrial homeostasis. However, restoring microglial mitochondrial function across the blood-brain barrier (BBB) remains challenging. Here, we report a sequentially targeted nanosystem, M-BPM@TGPB, for I/R injury therapy. It comprises a triphenylphosphonium (TPP)-modified, gadolinium-doped Prussian blue core and a mannose-modified BV2-platelet hybrid membrane shell. This design integrates mannose for BBB penetration, platelet membrane for lesion targeting, BV2 membrane for microglial uptake, and TPP for mitochondrial localization, enabling precise vascular-to-subcellular delivery. In vitro, the nanosystem crossed the BBB, localized to BV2 mitochondria, scavenged reactive oxygen species (ROS), restored mitochondrial function, and inhibited inflammation. In a mouse model of middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R), the intravenously administered nanosystem accumulated in microglial mitochondria, scavenged mitochondrial ROS (mtROS), restored mitochondrial homeostasis, promoted M1-to-M2 polarization, suppressed neuroinflammation, reduced neuronal apoptosis, and promoted angiogenesis, thereby reducing infarct volume from 36.61% to 10.57% and the modified neurological severity score (mNSS) from 14 to 2.5. It also exhibited favorable biocompatibility and enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) contrast. Critically, rather than broadly scavenging ROS, this strategy specifically restores microglial mitochondrial function, shifting the therapeutic focus from general antioxidant approaches to organelle-specific intervention. This work may offer a promising design paradigm for nanotherapies targeting central nervous system disorders in which mitochondrial dysfunction and neuroinflammation are core pathological drivers.

articles.title: NIR-Triggered Photothermal-Gated Microneedle Patch for Stage-Responsive Microenvironment Remodeling in Infected Burn Wounds.
articles.abstract: Achieving precise and effective treatment of infected burn wounds across different healing stages remains a major challenge in current wound management strategies. To address this issue, we developed a near-infrared (NIR)-responsive photothermal-gated hemin-coated polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)/polyacrylamide (PA)/magnesium silicide (Mg2Si) microneedle patch (abbreviated as PPMH), designed to enable spatiotemporally controlled therapeutic gaseous-ionic release for stage-responsive microenvironment remodeling throughout wound healing. The microneedle matrix, constructed from biocompatible polymers, integrates exudate-absorbing components at the base and hydrogen-generating magnesium silicide nanosheets (MN) at the needle tips. A hydrophobic hemin shell serves as a photothermal-responsive gate for on-demand activation. Upon insertion into the wound tissue, the microneedles effectively penetrate biological barriers and establish localized therapeutic interfaces. Upon NIR irradiation, the hemin shell undergoes rapid photothermal conversion, triggering gate opening and controlled hydrogen release within the dermal tissue. During the inflammatory phase, the released hydrogen alleviates oxidative stress and suppresses inflammation, while the photothermal effect of the outer hemin coating exerts potent antibacterial action to clear local bacterial infection. In the subsequent regeneration phase, the sustained release of Mg2+ and Si-containing species promotes angiogenesis and re-epithelialization. Collectively, this system effectively modulates the wound microenvironment in a stage-dependent manner, accelerating tissue regeneration and functional recovery. Therefore, PPMH designed in this study represents a versatile and translational platform for stage-responsive microenvironment remodeling and multi-targeted treatment of complex burn wounds.

The microneedle matrix, constructed from biocompatible polymers, integrates exudate-absorbing components at the base and hydrogen-generating magnesium silicide nanosheets (MN) at the needle tips.

articles.title: Streamlined 2D multimodal fusion framework predicts 90 day functional outcomes in acute ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Functional outcome prediction after endovascular therapy can support early risk stratification in acute ischemic stroke. We developed a 2D multimodal fusion framework using multicenter data from 405 patients with post-interventional cerebral hyperdensity on immediate non-contrast CT. Radiomic and deep transfer learning features were extracted from the single CT slice showing the largest hyperdensity area and combined with clinical variables using an Extra Trees classifier. In the external test cohort, the fusion model predicted unfavorable 90-day outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score greater than 2, with an AUC of 0.803, specificity of 88.0%, positive predictive value of 93.3%, and sensitivity of 60.9%. SHAP analysis identified malignant cerebral edema, age, baseline NIHSS, reperfusion status, and imaging intensity descriptors as influential factors. By reducing dependence on 3D segmentation, this framework provides an early phase (within 5 days) prognostic assessment tool for individualized in-hospital risk stratification after thrombectomy.

articles.title: GRSF1 Ameliorates Neurological Impairment in Cerebral Ischemia/Reperfusion Mice via Regulating Mul1/Mfn2-Mediated Mitochondrial Dynamics and Bioenergetics.
articles.abstract: Guanine-rich RNA sequence binding factor 1 (GRSF1), a mitochondrial RNA-binding protein, plays a critical role in maintaining mitochondrial homeostasis and mitigating oxidative DNA damage. Whether GRSF1 contributes to cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury (CIRI) by regulating mitochondrial dynamics remains to be elucidated. Male C57BL/6 J mice underwent middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) to induce CIRI. Principal component analysis and enrichment analysis were employed to validate impairment in mitochondrial dynamics in CIRI mice. GRSF1 was then evaluated for its effects on neurological function and histology. The role of GRSF1 on mitochondrial dynamics following CIRI was examined through enrichment analysis, electron microscopy, and respiratory chain complex activity assays. The relationship between GRSF1 and mitofusin 2 (Mfn2) in mitochondrial fusion was further investigated. The regulatory mechanism of mitochondrial E3 ubiquitin protein ligase 1 (Mul1) on Mfn2 was assessed using co-immunoprecipitation and denaturing immunoprecipitation assays. CIRI mice were characterized by disrupted mitochondrial dynamics, and restoring this balance ameliorates pathological progression. GRSF1 improved neurological function in CIRI mice, an effect confirmed to associate with maintenance of neuronal mitochondrial dynamics. Mechanistically, GRSF1 promoted mitochondrial fusion by suppressing the expression or activity of Mul1, thereby reducing Mul1-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of Mfn2. Ultimately, GRSF1 attenuated CIRI by inhibiting neuronal mitochondrial dynamic imbalance via the Mul1/Mfn2 pathway. It uncovers GRSF1 as a novel neuroprotective regulator in CIRI and identifies the Mul1/Mfn2 pathway as a critical mechanistic pathway underlying its protective effects. Targeting GRSF1 may hold therapeutic potential by modulating mitochondrial dynamics in CIRI.

Male C57BL/6 J mice underwent middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) to induce CIRI.

articles.title: Disrupting the interaction between T lymphocytes and microglia: Mechanism of Huanglian Jiedu Decoction in the treatment of ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Our previous studies have shown that Huanglian Jiedu Decoction effectively suppresses central immune-inflammatory responses, modulates peripheral inflammatory mediators, reduces the infiltration of peripheral T lymphocytes into the central nervous system, and promotes the conversion of infiltrated T lymphocytes in the brain into Treg cells. However, whether Huanglian Jiedu Decoction can influence M2 microglial polarization by regulating T-lymphocyte phenotypic transformation and thereby modulate neuroinflammation after ischemic stroke remains unclear. This study focused on Treg-mediated microglial polarization to investigate the potential of Huanglian Jiedu Decoction to modulate interactions between T lymphocytes and microglia in the treatment of ischemic stroke. We established a rat model of middle cerebral artery occlusion, an inflammatory model of Jurkat T cells stimulated with phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate and ionomycin, and a Transwell co-culture model of T lymphocytes and HMC3 microglia. The results showed that Huanglian Jiedu Decoction effectively alleviated cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury in a rat model of middle cerebral artery, inhibited central inflammatory responses, and promoted the polarization of microglia toward the M2 phenotype. Huanglian Jiedu Decoction also promoted the conversion of CD4+ T cells in brain tissue into regulatory T cells and regulated regulatory T cells through the interleukin-10/Janus kinase 1/signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 pathway, thereby promoting the activation of M2 microglia. These findings suggest that Huanglian Jiedu Decoction, which has heat-clearing and detoxifying properties, can regulate immune homeostasis, inhibit secondary neuroinflammation associated with ischemic stroke, and exert neuroprotective effects. Huanglian Jiedu Decoction may therefore treat ischemic stroke by modulating the interaction between T lymphocytes and microglia, providing a traditional Chinese medicine-based strategy for the treatment of ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Effects of Exercise Preconditioning on Promoting Endogenous Recovery Responses After Ischemic Stroke in Late-Adult Mice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke causes substantial neurological impairment, and although poststroke rehabilitation can support recovery, neurological deficits often limit the feasibility of exercise in clinical settings. Prestroke exercise has emerged as a potential strategy to enhance resilience to ischemic injury, but most preclinical studies have relied on young adult rodents, in which spontaneous recovery can sometimes obscure clinically meaningful functional effects. However, the impact of exercise preconditioning in later stages of adulthood remains insufficiently characterized. Here, we investigated whether a treadmill exercise preconditioning regimen confers neuroprotection and improves recovery-related responses in late-adult mice subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion.

METHODS: Eight-month-old male mice were assigned to sedentary or exercise groups. Following 5 weeks of treadmill running (5 days per week after 1 week of acclimatization), mice underwent 45 minutes of middle cerebral artery occlusion and reperfusion. Behavioral assessments and body-weight monitoring were performed before and after middle cerebral artery occlusion. Infarct volume and cellular responses were evaluated 14 days after stroke.

RESULTS: Fourteen days after stroke, lesion volume was significantly reduced in the exercise group compared with sedentary controls. Exercise preconditioning enhanced neurogenesis, oligodendrogenesis, and CD31-positive vascular responses while suppressing reactive astrocyte activation. Functional improvements were consistently observed across multiple behavioral assays in late-adult mice.

CONCLUSIONS: Preconditioning with treadmill exercise provides neuroprotection against ischemic stroke in late-adult mice by reducing infarct volume and promoting recovery-associated cellular responses. These findings demonstrate that the functional benefits of prestroke exercise extend beyond the young adult stage and support the potential value of regular physical activity as a strategy to mitigate ischemic brain injury later in adulthood.

Prestroke exercise has emerged as a potential strategy to enhance resilience to ischemic injury, but most preclinical studies have relied on young adult rodents, in which spontaneous recovery can sometimes obscure clinically meaningful functional effects. However, the impact of exercise preconditioning in later stages of adulthood remains insufficiently characterized.

articles.title: Cucurbitacin B inhibits the P2RY2/MYC transcriptional axis to disrupt ATP-mediated neuroinflammatory amplification loops.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sustained microglial activation drives neuroinflammation in cerebral ischemia. Cucurbitacin B (CuB), a naturally occurring tetracyclic triterpenoid compound mainly found in Cucurbitaceae, exerts anti-neuroinflammatory effects, yet its precise mechanism remains unclear. The aim of this study was to elucidate the self-amplifying circuit perpetuating neuroinflammation and to determine how CuB disrupts it.

METHODS: The anti-inflammatory effects of CuB were assessed in LPS-stimulated BV-2 microglia. Untargeted metabolomics (UHPLC-QTOF-MS) was employed to characterize metabolic alterations. Molecular mechanisms were further investigated in LPS- or ATP-stimulated BV-2 microglia using siRNA knockdown, overexpression, dual-luciferase assays, chromatin immunoprecipitation followed by quantitative PCR (ChIP-qPCR), electrophoretic mobility shift assay (EMSA) and specific pharmacological inhibitors. The pathophysiological relevance and neuroprotection were validated in a rat middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R) model.

RESULTS: CuB suppressed inflammatory mediator expression and cytokine secretion in LPS-stimulated microglia. Metabolomics in LPS-stimulated microglia revealed profound dysregulation across eight interconnected metabolic modules, including purinergic signaling and calcium homeostasis. Mechanistically, danger-associated ATP activated P2Y2 receptors, triggering PLC/IP3R-mediated Ca2+ overload that stimulated calcineurin to induce MYC. MYC in turn bound the P2RY2 promoter (confirmed by ChIP-qPCR and EMSA) to drive its transcription, establishing a pathogenic ATP/P2RY2/Ca2+/calcineurin/MYC feedforward loop. CuB disrupted this circuit at multiple nodes by reducing ATP release, blocking P2RY2, suppressing Ca2+ overload, inhibiting calcineurin-MYC, and normalizing metabolic dysregulation. In vivo, MYC/P2RY2 upregulation coincided with glial activation, inflammatory cytokine production and infarct expansion.

CONCLUSIONS: This work identifies an ATP/P2RY2/Ca2+/calcineurin/MYC feedforward loop that amplifies neuroinflammation. CuB acts as a multi-target circuit breaker, offering a novel therapeutic strategy for ischemic stroke.
articles.englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Sustained microglial activation drives neuroinflammation in cerebral ischemia. Cucurbitacin B (CuB), a naturally occurring tetracyclic triterpenoid compound mainly found in Cucurbitaceae, exerts anti-neuroinflammatory effects, yet its precise mechanism remains unclear. The aim of this study was to elucidate the self-amplifying circuit perpetuating neuroinflammation and to determine how CuB disrupts it.

articles.title: Targeting Fibroblast Foxc2 Promotes Neurovascular Recovery by Suppressing Sdc4 After Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke remains a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability, with current reperfusion therapies limited by narrow therapeutic windows and inability to promote sustained neurovascular repair. Here, we developed YZD-27, a rationally designed Tanshinone IIA (TSA) derivative with improved druggability, and show that it remains therapeutically effective when administered up to 24 h after ischemic injury in transient and permanent middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO and dMCAO) mouse models. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and cell-cell communication analysis revealed broad cellular responses to YZD-27 and identified fibronectin-1 (Fn1)/syndecan-4 (Sdc4) as a predicted endothelia-fibroblast ligand-receptor interaction. Mechanistically, YZD-27 directly binds forkhead box protein C2 (Foxc2), enhances its protein stability by limiting proteasomal degradation, and increases its occupancy at the Sdc4 promoter, thereby repressing Sdc4 transcription in fibroblast. Fibroblast-conditioned medium experiments further supported a role for Foxc2/Sdc4 regulation in modulating endothelial barrier-related protein expression. These findings identify Foxc2/Sdc4 signaling as a regulatory mechanism associated with the therapeutic effects of YZD-27, and establish YZD-27 as a promising neurovascular therapeutic candidate for ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Echinocystic acid alleviates cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury through PPARγ-dependent modulation of microglial polarization and pyroptotic signaling.
articles.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) worsens outcomes after ischemic stroke, yet effective pharmacological interventions remain limited. Echinocystic acid (EA), a pentacyclic triterpenoid isolated from the fruits of Gleditsia sinensis Lam., has shown neuroprotective activity in CIRI, but its direct molecular target and underlying mechanism remain unclear. In this study, using network pharmacology, molecular docking, surface plasmon resonance, and subsequent validation in middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) mice and oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R)-treated BV2 cells, we identified peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor γ (PPARγ) as a potential target of EA and provided evidence supporting direct binding between EA and PPARγ. EA significantly reduced infarct volume and brain edema while improving neurological outcomes in MCAO mice, and also attenuated OGD/R-induced injury in BV2 cells. Mechanistically, EA restored PPARγ expression, promoted microglial M2 polarization, reduced IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α levels, increased IL-10 production, and attenuated NLRP3/Caspase-1/GSDMD-associated pyroptotic signaling in both in vivo and in vitro models. These effects were largely reversed by the PPARγ antagonist GW9662. Collectively, these findings indicate that EA protects against CIRI, at least in part, through a PPARγ-dependent mechanism involving promotion of microglial M2 polarization and attenuation of NLRP3/Caspase-1/GSDMD-associated pyroptotic signaling, highlighting the therapeutic potential of EA in CIRI.

articles.title: Ultrasound-Responsive Iron-Barium Titanate Schottky Heterojunction-Embedded Hydrogel Accelerates Burn Wound Healing through Bidirectional Hydrogen-Piezocatalytic Redox Modulation.
articles.abstract: Burn wound healing is regulated by a spatiotemporal redox hierarchy, where early reactive oxygen species (ROS) overload drives inflammation, while late ROS deficiency hinders regeneration. Programming this bidirectional sequence requires time-phased, counter-directional ROS control. Herein, we report a nanocomposite hydrogel that integrates hydrogen therapy with piezocatalytic therapy, enabling on-demand redox programming across the entire healing cascade. The system constructs a metal-semiconductor Schottky heterojunction derived from the in situ reduction of Fe2+ within the mesopores of barium titanate. The mesoporous confinement and interfacial coupling program the hydrolysis of nanoscale zero-valent iron for sustained, early-stage hydrogen delivery to scavenge toxic ROS, while the established Schottky barrier efficiently suppresses charge recombination, thereby executing ultrasound-triggered piezoelectric polarization and charge separation for on-demand ROS generation in later-stage pro-regenerative signaling. Embedded within a polyacrylamide/carboxymethyl chitosan double-network hydrogel with inherent antibacterial activity, the resulting system exhibits superior antioxidant capacity and piezocatalytic responsivity, as well as promotion of fibroblast migration, angiogenesis, and M2 macrophage polarization. In a mouse burn model, this redox-programmable platform orchestrates phased healing, attenuating early inflammation, sustaining neovascularization, and suppressing late fibrosis, achieving accelerated wound closure. Collectively, this work establishes a redox programming paradigm via heterojunction catalysis, coupling spatiotemporal ROS scavenging and generation for dynamic tissue regeneration.

articles.title: Localized Hydrogen Release Driven by Mg-Pd Microgalvanic Cells from 3D-Printed Microneedles Reverses Redox Homeostasis for Psoriasis Treatment.
articles.abstract: Psoriasis therapy faces multiple challenges, including refractory, recurrence, and various comorbidities, attributed to its complex pathogenesis driven by aberrant keratinocyte proliferation, oxidative stress imbalance, and inflammation. These three factors form a vicious cycle, and cycle disruption holds great therapeutic potential for psoriasis. However, current therapies merely focus on symptom relief or anti-inflammatory effects alone with ignoring the essential cycle. To address the issues, a magnesium (Mg)-palladium (Pd) micro-galvanic cell (MP) with spontaneous electrochemical corrosion was constructed. MP released hydrogen (H2), inhibiting keratinocyte hyperproliferation, scavenging reactive oxygen species (ROS) and •OH, activating KEAP1‑NRF2 antioxidant signaling pathway, while generated Mg2+ exerted anti‑inflammatory effects. Furthermore, hollow microneedles loaded with MP (MP-MN) were fabricated via 3D printing to penetrate the stratum corneum for deep H2 delivery. In the imiquimod-induced psoriatic mouse model, MP‑MN topical treatment restored skin thickness, ameliorated oxidative stress, decreased splenic Th17/Treg ratio, and lowered both local and systemic pro‑inflammatory cytokine levels. Collectively, MP‑MN presented a comprehensive strategy for anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and immune-regulatory effects in psoriasis, broadening the applications of H2 and micro-galvanic cells in skin disorders.

articles.title: Cerebral Blood Flow-Derived Myogenic Dynamics Reveal Impaired Postischemic Cerebrovascular Recovery in Experimental Stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Restoration of cerebral blood flow (CBF) after ischemic stroke does not necessarily indicate recovery of cerebrovascular regulation. We tested whether myogenic-band dynamics derived directly from CBF signals provide information beyond mean perfusion during cerebral ischemia and after acute stroke.

METHODS: Transient focal cerebral ischemia was induced in 29 Sprague-Dawley rats using middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion. Bilateral laser-Doppler flowmetry (LDF)-derived CBF signals were decomposed using empirical mode decomposition and Hilbert transform, and myogenic-band activity (0.15-0.4 Hz) was quantified by absolute and relative power. Cross-validated logistic regression models were used to evaluate whether myogenic-band power provided discriminative information beyond mean CBF alone.

RESULTS: Ipsilateral mean CBF fell from 73.5±51.8 p.u. at baseline to 52.2±38.0 p.u. during late ischemia (P=0.0088), then increased to 126.6±91.5 p.u. after 3 hours of reperfusion (P=0.0050 versus baseline). Relative myogenic-band power decreased from 37.43±14.65% to 13.35±7.51% during ischemia (P<0.0001) and remained below baseline after reperfusion (20.74±12.02%, P=0.00033 versus baseline); contralateral relative power was comparatively preserved. Combining mean CBF and myogenic-band power improved discrimination of baseline from late ischemia (AUC, 0.99 versus 0.70 for mean CBF alone) and late reperfusion (AUC, 0.88 versus 0.70).

CONCLUSIONS: Frequency-specific analysis of LDF-derived CBF reveals persistent, lateralized abnormalities in myogenic-band dynamics that are not captured by mean perfusion alone. The persistence of depressed myogenic activity despite restored or elevated mean CBF demonstrates incomplete recovery of frequency-specific oscillatory dynamics after reperfusion. These findings support myogenic-band power as a potential functional measure of persistent postischemic cerebrovascular dysfunction.

articles.title: Rescue treatment for medium vessel occlusion by intra-arterial tenecteplase: the RESCUE-TNK randomized clinical trial.
articles.abstract: In patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by medium vessel occlusion (MeVO), intra-arterial tenecteplase may offer a targeted strategy to improve recanalization; we hypothesized that intra-arterial tenecteplase would increase successful reperfusion compared with standard care with a comparable safety profile. This phase 2, prospective, randomised, open-label, blinded-endpoint, multicentre study aims to assess the efficacy and safety of intra-arterial tenecteplase for patients with acute ischemic stroke caused by MeVO. Patients with MeVO were randomly (1:1) assigned to receive intra-arterial tenecteplase or standard care. The primary outcome was successful reperfusion of medium vessel occlusion. A total of 80 patients were randomized to either the tenecteplase group (n = 41) or control group (n = 39). Successful reperfusion reached 61.0% (25/41) in the tenecteplase group versus 28.2% (11/39) in the control group (unadjusted odds ratio 3.98, 95% CI 1.56-10.16; P = 0.004). Symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage within 24 h was similar between the tenecteplase and control groups. This work suggests that intra-arterial tenecteplase significantly increased the probability of successful reperfusion compared with standard care, with a comparable safety profile in this stroke population. articles.title: Adjunctive intra-arterial thrombolysis with endovascular thrombectomy for acute large-vessel occlusion stroke: a network meta-analysis of randomized trials.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) is standard care for acute ischemic stroke due to large vessel occlusion (AIS-LVO), but nearly half of patients with successful reperfusion do not achieve functional independence. Adjunctive intra-arterial thrombolysis (IAT) aims to address residual distal thrombi and microcirculatory impairment; however, the efficacy and safety of IAT in comparison with other thrombolytics remain uncertain.

METHODS: We conducted a network meta-analysis (NMA) of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing EVT alone vs. EVT combined with IAT using alteplase (ALT), tenecteplase (TNK), or urokinase (UK) in AIS-LVO patients. Primary outcomes were excellent clinical outcome (mRS 0-1) and functional independence (mRS 0-2) at 90 days. Safety outcomes included symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage (sICH) and all-cause mortality.

RESULTS: Eight RCTs involving 2,564 patients were included. For excellent clinical (mRS 0-1), EVT + IA-ALT ranked highest [surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) 96.2%], followed by EVT + IA-TNK (59.8%). Both showed significant benefits over EVT alone [EVT + IA-TNK vs. EVT: RR 1.20, 95% CI 1.05-1.39. EVT + IA-ALT vs. EVT: RR 1.40, 95% CI 1.21-1.63 and EVT + IA-TNK (0.125 mg/kg) vs. EVT: RR 1.54, 95% CI 1.07-2.20. EVT + IA-ALT (0.225 mg/kg) vs. EVT: RR 1.40, 95% CI 1.21-1.63]. For functional independence (mRS 0-2), EVT + IA-ALT also ranked highest, but no combination strategy showed a statistically significant benefit over EVT alone in pairwise comparisons. Regarding safety, point estimates for sICH risk did not differ significantly between combination strategies and EVT alone. However, EVT + IA-TNK demonstrated a statistically significant advantage over EVT + IA-ALT in terms of lower all-cause mortality (RR 1.58, 95% CI 1.01-2.46).

CONCLUSIONS: EVT + IA-ALT and EVT + IA-TNK may improve excellent clinical outcome without a statistically significant increase in sICH; however, clinically important bleeding risk cannot be excluded. In exploratory indirect comparisons, EVT + IA-TNK was associated with lower all-cause mortality than EVT + IA-ALT, although this finding is based on sparse evidence and should be interpreted with caution.

articles.title: Stage-Associated Efficacy of Systemically Administered Neural Stem Cell-Derived Exosomes in Ischemic Stroke through the Prevention of Cx43 Degradation.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke pathology is highly dynamic, making the optimal timing for biological interventions highly elusive. This study investigated the stage-associated therapeutic efficacy of neural stem cell-derived exosomes (NSC-Exos) for cerebral ischemia-reperfusion. The in vivo evaluations identified a restricted therapeutic window closely associated with the temporal evolution of the ischemic microenvironment. Early exosome intervention (4 or 24 h post-ischemia) significantly reduced infarct volume, restored blood-brain barrier integrity, and improved neurological functional recovery. In contrast, delayed administration (48 h) failed to reduce the mortality rate and provide meaningful neuroprotection. To examine the molecular basis of this time dependence, we integrated temporal proteomic profiling of the ischemic penumbra with small RNA sequencing of NSC-Exos. The analytical and functional data suggest that early NSC-Exo delivery transfers miR-9-5p to suppress Nedd4 expression, thereby restoring the Connexin 43 protein pool and stabilizing the astrocytic network to halt initial microenvironmental collapse. Collectively, this study underscores the critical importance of intervention timing and provides a potential translational strategy for utilizing NSC-Exos as a targeted, stage-specific therapy in acute ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Research progress on neurovascular and neuroimmune interactions during thrombolysis and reperfusion in acute ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) remains a leading cause of adult mortality and lasting disability worldwide. Although intravenous thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy have established the reperfusion era, a substantial proportion of patients fail to achieve favorable functional outcomes because macrovascular recanalization does not guarantee effective perfusion at the tissue level. This review systematically examines the neurovascular unit (NVU) and the expanded neurovascular immune network as integrated frameworks for understanding brain injury following reperfusion. We delineate the temporal cascade of pathophysiological events, beginning with acute ischemic energy failure, excitotoxicity, and innate immune sensing by cerebral microvascular endothelial cells and microglia. We then focus on the reperfusion phase as the critical window of neuroimmune interaction, characterized by reactive oxygen species burst, nod-like receptor family pyrin domain containing 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome activation, neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) formation, and matrix-metalloproteinase (MMP) mediated disruption of the blood-brain-barrier (BBB). The chronological infiltration and phenotypic transitions of peripheral immune cells, including neutrophils, classical monocytes, and T lymphocytes, are analyzed in relation to biphasic dynamics of the BBB and evolving therapeutic time windows. Furthermore, we evaluate translational advances in combination strategies that pair agents with anti-inflammatory properties and thrombolysis, interventions targeting NETs, blood brain barrier protection, and immunomodulation strategies tailored to specific time windows, alongside emerging biomarkers and novel delivery technologies. This review aims to provide a framework grounded in evidence for mechanistic understanding and therapeutic optimization toward comprehensive neurovascular and neuroimmune repair in the reperfusion era. Unless otherwise specified, mechanistic findings cited in this review derive predominantly from experimental rodent models (mainly transient middle cerebral artery occlusion, tMCAO) or in vitro studies, and human evidence is explicitly indicated where available.

articles.title: Traditional Chinese medicine interventions and mitochondrial communication in myocardial and cerebral ischemia: a critical review.
articles.abstract: Myocardial infarction and ischemic stroke share mitochondrial disturbances, but evidence that traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) interventions regulate mitochondrial communication rather than general mitochondrial injury remains uncertain. This critical review evaluates that distinction. A structured search of PubMed, Lens Scholarly Search, and CNKI from inception to 28 August 2026 identified 1,663 records; 29 reports (24 preclinical/mechanistic and 5 clinical or systematic-review reports) informed the focused evidence map. We organized the evidence across four levels: intramitochondrial coordination, communication among mitochondria, contacts between mitochondria and other organelles, and intercellular mitochondrial signaling. Selected formulations, botanical drugs, and plant metabolites were associated most consistently with calcium-redox balance, bioenergetics, mitochondrial dynamics, mitophagy, and immune-metabolic responses. However, most studies measured static proteins or downstream injury markers, used preventive dosing or poorly defined exposure, and did not test direct target engagement. Evidence for altered organelle contacts or transfer of intact mitochondria was sparse. Clinical studies of selected standardized commercial Chinese polyherbal preparations reported possible functional benefits, but product heterogeneity, trial limitations, and the absence of mitochondrial pharmacodynamic biomarkers preclude mechanistic attribution. We therefore distinguish communication-specific evidence from pathway association and appraise product identity, exposure plausibility, causal validation, methodological quality, and clinical relevance. Future studies should use taxonomically authenticated and chemically characterized preparations, clinically achievable dosing, dynamic communication-specific assays, causal perturbation, and prospectively defined mitochondrial biomarkers. Current evidence supports mitochondrial communication as a useful hypothesis-generating framework, but not yet as an established clinical mechanism of TCM in myocardial or cerebral ischemia.

articles.title: Immunothrombosis Biomarkers and Multi-Omics Profiles After Successful Recanalization in Patients Receiving Ischemic Postconditioning: An Exploratory Analysis of the INSPIRE Trial.
articles.abstract: Successful recanalization after endovascular thrombectomy does not always restore microvascular perfusion, highlighting the need for adjunctive strategies. Ischemic postconditioning (IPostC) involves brief, controlled​ cycles of flow interruption and restoration at the onset of reperfusion to attenuate ischemia-reperfusion injury. In the parent INSPIRE trial, IPostC, delivered in situ as four cycles of 2-minute balloon inflation followed by 2-minute deflation at the previously occluded arterial segment immediately after successful recanalization, reduced infarct growth from baseline to 48 h. This exploratory secondary analysis included all 60 randomized patients. We investigated whether IPostC was associated with early changes in immunothrombosis, coagulation, and microvascular transit and explored associated plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiles. Arterial blood obtained approximately 15 min after successful recanalization was analyzed using flow cytometry and thromboelastography. Quantitative digital subtraction angiography-derived microcirculation time was analyzed in 55 patients, and plasma proteomic and metabolomic profiling was performed in 29 patients. Compared with controls, patients receiving IPostC had lower neutrophil CD11b expression (median, 52.15 versus 64.27 mean fluorescence intensity ×10²; P = 0.011), a lower thromboelastography α-angle (65.15° versus 67.95°; P = 0.037), and shorter microcirculation time (2.11 versus 3.03 s; P = 0.020). Longer microcirculation time was associated with greater infarct growth (r = 0.533; P < 0.001). Proteomic and metabolomic analyses identified signals involving blood-brain barrier and extracellular-matrix organization and mitochondrial bioenergetics. Biomarker comparisons were not adjusted for multiple comparisons; in the omics analyses, no protein and 17 metabolites remained significant after false discovery rate correction. In summary, IPostC was associated with lower neutrophil activation, slower clot propagation, and faster microvascular transit after recanalization, and multi-omics profiling pointed to blood-brain barrier integrity and mitochondrial bioenergetics as candidate pathways. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in larger studies. Trial registration: NCT06545734, registered 9 August 2024.

articles.title: Outcomes of Intra-Arterial Urokinase After Endovascular Reperfusion for Acute Ischemic Stroke Due to Cardioembolism: A Secondary Analysis of the POST-UK Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether adjunctive intra-arterial thrombolysis improves outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the efficacy and safety of adjunctive intra-arterial urokinase in patients with acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism who achieved near-complete to complete reperfusion.

METHODS: This study was a secondary analysis of the POST-UK (Adjunctive Intra-Arterial Urokinase After Near-Complete to Complete Reperfusion for Acute Ischemic Stroke) trial, which was conducted from November 15, 2022, to March 29, 2024. Patients were randomly assigned to the intra-arterial urokinase group or the control group. The primary outcome was disability-free survival at 90 days, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score of 0 to 1. Safety outcomes included 90-day all-cause death, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage and any intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours.

RESULTS: Among 209 patients with cardioembolism (median age 73 [interquartile range, 63-81] years; 45.9% men), 106 were assigned to the control group and 103 to the intra-arterial urokinase group. Compared with the control group, adjunctive intra-arterial urokinase significantly increased the odds of disability-free survival at 90 days (adjusted risk ratio, 1.49 [95% CI, 1.08-2.06]; P=0.01; inverse probability of treatment weighting adjusted risk ratio, 1.47 [95% CI, 1.04-2.09]; P=0.03). No significant differences were found between groups in 90-day mortality rate, symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage, or any intracranial hemorrhage within 48 hours.

CONCLUSIONS: In patients with acute ischemic stroke due to cardioembolism who achieved near-complete to complete reperfusion, adjunctive intra-arterial urokinase significantly improved disability-free survival at 90 days without increasing the risk of death or intracranial hemorrhage.

articles.title: Thrombus stiffness depends on occlusion site and influences thrombectomy outcomes in acute ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Only 60% of patients with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) achieve successful reperfusion after the first endovascular thrombectomy (EVT) attempt. In vitro studies have shown that thrombus stiffness influences thrombus-device interaction and retrieval efficacy. This prospective observational study investigates how thrombus stiffness relates to clinical factors, thrombus imaging characteristics and histological composition. It further explores the association between thrombus stiffness and EVT success, as measured by the modified first-pass reperfusion (mFPR).

PATIENTS AND METHODS: A total of 281 thrombus samples were collected from 51 AIS patients undergoing EVT. Thrombus stiffness was quantified using compressive mechanical testing, composition from histological staining and radiological characteristics from pre-interventional non-contrast computed tomography (CT) and CT angiography. Statistical analysis was performed using linear and logistic mixed-effects regression models.

RESULTS: Thrombi retrieved from the proximal M2 segment of the middle cerebral artery showed significant lower stiffness (0.236 kPa, 95% CI, 0.136-0.409) compared to those from the M1 segment (0.760 kPa, 95% CI, 0.492-1.174) and from the ICA (1.106 kPa, 95% CI, 0.558-2.192). Occlusion location was the strongest clinical marker of thrombus stiffness. Adjusted mFPR probability was 40.4% (95% CI, 24.5-67.0) for thrombi retrieved from the ICA, 89.7% (95% CI, 79.5-97.0) for M1 occlusions, and 53.0% (95% CI, 30.8-84.7) for M2 occlusions.

CONCLUSION: Thrombi in distal vessels of the anterior cerebral circulation are significantly softer than those in proximal intracranial arteries. First-pass EVT success is lower for the stiffest thrombi from the ICA and for the softest thrombi from M2, providing a foundation for future biomechanically informed thrombus removal strategies to optimise AIS treatment.

articles.title: Intranuclear localisation of KLF3-AS1 under the balance of histone acetylation and methylation in BMSCs ameliorates cerebral ischaemia‒reperfusion injury by preserving microglial mitochondrial function and inhibiting inflammatory polarisation.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischaemic stroke occurs when blood flow to the brain is obstructed. Rapid restoration of blood supply frequently induces cerebral ischaemia‒reperfusion injury (CIRI). Bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC)-derived exosomes exhibit promising therapeutic potential for CIRI. In-depth exploration of their therapeutic mechanisms holds crucial significance for CIRI management.

METHODS: The middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO) model was established in mice. An in vitro ischaemic stroke model was established by treating BV-2 cells with oxygen‒glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R). Exosomes were isolated from BMSCs and intranasally administrated into mice or added into BV-2 cells. Neurological deficits, grasping and coordination function were evaluated. Cell viability, apoptosis, proliferation and migration were examined. The localisation of KLF3-AS1 was examined by combined staining of immunofluorescence and fluorescence in situ hybridisation. Intracellular Ca2+ and adenosine triphosphate levels, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species and membrane potential were assessed.

RESULTS: KLF3-AS1 enhanced BMSC viability, proliferation and migration, accompanied by epigenetic reprogramming at its promoter characterised by increased H3K27 acetylation (H3K27Ac) and decreased H3K27 trimethylation (H3K27Me3). BMSC-derived KLF3-AS1-enriched exosomes indicated therapeutic efficacy in both in vivo and in vitro models of cerebral ischaemia. In MCAO-induced mice, these exosomes alleviated neurological deficits and shifted microglial polarisation from pro-inflammatory M1-like to anti-inflammatory M2-like phenotypes. Similar effects were observed in OGD/R-treated BV-2 microglia, where KLF3-AS1-enriched exosomes attenuated oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction while upregulating Silent Information Regulator 3 (SIRT3) expression. Mechanistically, KLF3-AS1 facilitated ETS Variant Transcription Factor 4 (ETV4) nuclear translocation to activate SIRT3 transcription in microglia, and inhibition of SIRT3 abolished the neuroprotective effects of exosomal KLF3-AS1.

CONCLUSION: BMSC-derived exosomes delivering KLF3-AS1 ameliorates CIRI by preserving microglial mitochondrial function and inhibiting inflammatory polarisation, highlighting KLF3-AS1 as a critical epigenetic regulator and exosome-mediated therapeutic agent for CIRI through the ETV4/SIRT3 axis.

KEY POINTS/HIGHLIGHTS: KLF3-AS1 enhances bone marrow mesenchymal stem cell (BMSC) function via promoter H3K27Ac/H3K27Me3 reprogramming. KLF3‑AS1 directly binds ETS Variant Transcription Factor 4 (ETV4) to activate Silent Information Regulator 3 (SIRT3), preserving mitochondrial integrity. BMSC‑derived exosomal KLF3‑AS1 promotes M2 microglial polarisation and ameliorates cerebral ischaemia-reperfusion injury.

articles.title: Translating Stroke Microenvironment Cues Into Materials Design: Intelligent Nanomaterials for Ischemic Stroke Therapy.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS), caused by cerebral blood vessel occlusion, leads to ischemia, hypoxia, and irreversible brain tissue damage. Current treatments primarily rely on thrombolytic agents like alteplase, urokinase, and streptokinase for rapid reperfusion. However, these therapies are limited by narrow therapeutic windows, rapid clearance, poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration, off-target effects, and the complex ischemic microenvironment. These have led to increased interest in nanomaterial-based platforms to improve the precision and efficacy of IS treatment. The IS microenvironment, characterized by oxidative stress, inflammation, ionic imbalance, acidosis, and BBB disruption, provides valuable cues for designing responsive nanomaterials. Nanomaterials engineered to respond to reactive oxygen species, pH, enzymes, light, ultrasound, or magnetic fields can enable targeted drug delivery, controlled release, and multi-modal interventions, enhancing therapeutic precision. This review discusses the IS microenvironment, limitations of traditional therapies, recent advances in intelligent nanomaterials for IS treatment, and the major barriers that currently limit clinical translation.

articles.title: Current and emerging neuromodulation techniques for motor recovery after ischemic stroke: a 2026 update.
articles.abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Neuromodulation technologies have emerged as promising tools to enhance motor recovery following ischemic stroke. Acute reperfusion therapy remains highly time-dependent, underscoring the need for interventions that augment post-stroke neuroplasticity. Brain stimulation techniques aim to modulate cortical excitability and promote adaptive reorganization of motor networks during the critical recovery period after stroke.

AREAS COVERED: The authors review recent advances in neuromodulation strategies for post-stroke motor recovery, as well as the key principles underlying neuromodulation. Major noninvasive modalities, including transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), and low-intensity focused ultrasound stimulation (LIFUS), are reviewed alongside emerging applications of invasive techniques such as deep brain stimulation (DBS) and vagus nerve stimulation (VNS). Recent randomized clinical trials and translational studies are also highlighted. This article is based on literature obtained through PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov searches for content published between 1 January 2020 and 30 March 202630 March 2026 and was supplemented by earlier landmark studies relevant to stroke recovery and neuromodulation.

EXPERT OPINION: Although neuromodulation technologies demonstrate encouraging safety profiles, clinical trial results feature notable neutral results. Future studies bear the burden of refining stimulation paradigms, patient selection, and rehabilitation dosing, possibly leveraging personalized, biomarker-driven patient selection.

articles.title: Extracellular lactate enhances IL-10 transcription via H4K5 lactylation and promotes an A2-like reactive-astrocyte phenotype after ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke triggers a rapid rise in lactate levels in the brain tissue. The neuroprotective role of exogenous lactate administered during the reperfusion phase has recently garnered attention. A neuroprotective A2 phenotype of reactive astrocytes (RACs) is characterized by interleukin-10 (IL-10) upregulation, which mitigates neuroinflammation. However, whether exogenous lactate drives A2-like polarization of RACs remains unknown. This study aimed to elucidate the mechanism by which lactate regulates this process.

METHODS: Rat middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) and in vitro primary RACs models were established. Western blotting, immunofluorescence staining, and RT-qPCR were used to assess A1/A2 polarization markers, IL-10 expression, histone lactylation, and related neuroimmune signaling molecules. Ubiquitination, chromatin immunoprecipitation, and dual-luciferase reporter assays were performed to clarify the mechanism by which lactate regulates IL-10 expression and A2-like polarization of RACs.

RESULTS: Our results demonstrated that increased lactate levels after ischemic stroke correlated with A2 polarization of RACs. Lactate treatment significantly enhanced A2 polarization and reduced infarct volume in the rat MCAO model. Mechanistically, lactate activated signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3) signaling while suppressing sirtuin 1 (SIRT1) expression and synergistically enhancing H4K5 lactylation (H4K5la) and IL-10 expression, thereby driving RACs toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype.

CONCLUSIONS: This study revealed that elevated extracellular lactate in the acute phase of ischemic stroke drove RACs toward an A2-like phenotype through the Yes-associated protein 1 (YAP1)/STAT3/IL-10 and YAP1/SIRT1/H4K5la signaling axes. These findings provide a theoretical basis for targeting RAC lactylation as a potential therapeutic strategy to limit inflammatory damage after stroke.

articles.title: Mitochondria-associated ferroptosis in ischemic stroke: Pathophysiological evolution, interorganelle crosstalk, and therapeutic targeting.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) results from an acute interruption of cerebral blood flow and the ensuing collapse of energy metabolism. Although vascular recanalization can salvage the ischemic penumbra, its overall benefit remains constrained by a narrow therapeutic window and reperfusion injury. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation, contributes to neuronal injury after IS and can amplify ischemia/reperfusion injury. By integrating energy metabolism, iron homeostasis, and redox balance, mitochondria can shape ferroptosis susceptibility within the energy-depleted, iron-dysregulated, and oxidatively stressed ischemic brain. However, most studies have examined iron metabolism and lipid peroxidation at the whole-cell level, leaving the temporal and interorganelle dimensions of mitochondrial regulation of ferroptosis insufficiently integrated. Here, we organize mitochondria-associated ferroptosis across the pathological course of IS, from metabolic reprogramming and substrate accumulation during ischemia to the reverse electron transport-associated reactive oxygen species burst during early reperfusion and subsequent disruption of mitochondrial quality control. We further examine mitochondrial crosstalk with the endoplasmic reticulum, lysosomes, lipid droplets, and nucleus, compare ferroptosis susceptibility across neurovascular unit cell populations, and map these mechanisms onto pharmacological interventions and mechanistically plausible therapeutic windows. Finally, we assess barriers to the clinical translation of mitochondria-targeted therapies and provide a stage-resolved framework for developing neuroprotective strategies in IS.

articles.title: Activatable MRI-Trackable Spherical Nucleic Acids for Idebenone Delivery Against Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
articles.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) is a key driver of poor prognosis in ischemic stroke. Idebenone (IDBN) shows promise for mitigating IRI, but its efficacy is limited by poor brain accumulation. Moreover, IDBN cannot be visually tracked, making it difficult to confirm whether it reaches the ischemic brain and exerts therapeutic effects. Here, IDBN functionalized with a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-cleavable bond is grafted onto phosphorothioate-modified DNA strands and co-assembled with ultrasmall superparamagnetic iron oxide (USPIO) to form USPIO-IDBN-SNAs, where SNAs stands for spherical nucleic acids. Exploiting upregulated class A scavenger receptors, USPIO-IDBN-SNAs target the ischemic area without targeting modifications and increase local IDBN concentration. Hydrophobic IDBN inside the SNAs limits water access to USPIO clusters, suppressing their contrast-enhancing ability. Under oxidative stress, IDBN is rapidly released and exerts remarkable protection. This release allows USPIO clusters to re-establish contact with water, activating their contrast-enhancing ability on T2-weighted imaging. Collectively, USPIO-IDBN-SNAs provide significant neuroprotection against IRI and offer a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-visible platform to monitor IDBN release in the ischemic brain, presenting a promising theranostic approach for precise, trackable stroke therapy.

articles.title: Deterioration of Peri-Infarct Microvascular Hemodynamics Following Successful Reperfusion in Acute Ischemic Stroke Predicts Infarct Growth.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Microvascular hemodynamic deterioration is a proposed mechanism underlying the no-reflow phenomenon in acute ischemic stroke. Experimental studies suggested that relative heterogeneity of capillary transit time (RTH) is a potential imaging biomarker of microvascular impairment. We investigated the relationship between peri-infarct RTH and infarct growth, measured on immediate post-thrombectomy (PT) perfusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and functional outcomes in patients with acute ischemic stroke with successful reperfusion.

METHODS: In this retrospective case-control study from the University of California, Los Angeles, patients with acute ischemic stroke from 2015 to 2020 were included if they had excellent reperfusion (modified Thrombolysis in Cerebral Infarction score ≥2c) and diffusion- and perfusion-weighted MRIs at baseline, immediately PT, and 24 to 48 hours after thrombectomy. Peri-infarct regions were defined as time to maximum ≥6-second regions on baseline MRI that were not infarcted on immediate PT MRI. Following image coregistration, quantitative values of perfusion parameters, including RTH, were obtained from peri-infarct regions on immediate PT MRI. Two primary outcomes were assessed: (1) infarct growth ≥10 mL and (2) poor functional outcome (90-day modified Rankin Scale score >2). Associations between clinical and imaging parameters and outcomes were evaluated using univariate analysis. Age, sex, and covariates that were significant in univariate analysis were included in logistic regression analyses.

RESULTS: Among 47 patients included in the analysis (62% women; mean age, 72±13 years; median National Institutes of Health Stroke Scale score, 14), 20 (43%) patients had substantial infarct growth and poor functional outcome. Peri-infarct RTH was significantly (P=0.005) higher in patients with infarct growth >10 mL than those without and remained as an independent predictor (odds ratio, 1.4 per 10% increase [95% CI, 1.0-2.0]; P=0.04). Similarly, the peri-infarct RTH was significantly higher (P<0.001) in patients with poor functional outcomes than those with good functional outcomes and remained as a significant predictor of poor functional outcome (odds ratio, 1.4 per 10% increase [95% CI, 1.0-1.9]; P=0.03).

CONCLUSIONS: Increased peri-infarct RTH on immediate PT MRI predicts substantial infarct growth and poor functional outcomes in successfully reperfused patients with acute ischemic stroke. Results highlight the role of microvascular dysfunction depicted by elevated RTH as a potential marker of no-reflow phenomenon despite excellent macrovascular reperfusion.

articles.title: Global Burden of Pediatric Stroke (1990-2023): A Shift From Mortality Toward Disability.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pediatric stroke is a significant cause of long-term disability worldwide, with outcomes influenced by age, stroke subtype, and access to care. Our objective was to define the global burden of pediatric stroke by its impact on mortality and disability.

METHODS: The Global Burden of Disease study uses advanced statistical modeling to analyze health across locations, synthesizing data on mortality, morbidity, and risk factors. We examined 2023 data from the study to assess deaths, years of life lost, and years lived with disability during 3 eras (1990-2001, 2002-2013, and 2014-2023) across high-income and low- and middle-income countries. We stratified the analysis by sex, age group, and stroke subtype. We calculated the proportion of burden attributable to disability (years lived with disability/[years lived with disability+years of life lost]) to assess shifts from fatal to nonfatal disease over time.

RESULTS: Between 1990 and 2023, global age-standardized pediatric stroke incidence declined only modestly, whereas age-standardized years of life lost rates declined significantly, indicating that the lower mortality burden reflected better survival rather than a large reduction in disease occurrence. Because years lived with disability rates remained comparatively stable as mortality declined, the proportion of disease burden attributable to disability rose from 14.6% (1990-2001) to 21.7% (2014-2023). This transition was uneven across settings: high-income countries achieved faster mortality declines and reached a higher disability share, whereas low- and middle-income countries retained a higher mortality burden, reflecting a dual burden of ongoing premature death and rising disability. These patterns were consistent across age and sex strata.

CONCLUSIONS: These data indicate that pediatric stroke is undergoing an epidemiological transition from a mortality-dominant burden to one increasingly driven by disability, reflecting improved survival but with uneven distribution worldwide. Reducing the disability burden, through better stroke recognition education and expanded access to prevention, acute stroke care systems, reperfusion, and rehabilitation, particularly in low- and middle-income countries, should be prioritized alongside efforts to close persistent global inequities in outcomes.
articles.englishSummary: BACKGROUND: Pediatric stroke is a significant cause of long-term disability worldwide, with outcomes influenced by age, stroke subtype, and access to care. Our objective was to define the global burden of pediatric stroke by its impact on mortality and disability. METHODS: The Global Burden of Disease study uses advanced statistical modeling to analyze health across locations, synthesizing data on mortality, morbidity, and risk factors.

articles.title: Hydrogen Bonding Denticity Governs Surface Modulation in Inorganic Perovskite Nanocrystals.
articles.abstract: All-inorganic CsPbI3 perovskite nanocrystals (PNCs) have emerged as promising emitters for optoelectronic applications owing to their high color purity, tunable bandgap, and high photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY). However, dynamic surface ligands, abundant trap states, and rapid halide ion migration limit their emission efficiency and operational stability. Here, methylammonium (MA+), formamidinium (FA+), and guanidinium (GA+) were systematically investigated as surface modulators for PNCs via an anti-solvent-assisted post-treatment strategy. Spectroscopic analyses and density functional theory calculations reveal that the passivation efficacy is determined by the strength and denticity of hydrogen-bonding interactions between the organic cations and the PNC surface. Among the three candidates, GA+ exhibits the highest efficacy owing to its trifunctional N─H groups, which enable robust multidentate surface interactions that suppress trap formation and halide ion migration. As a result, GA-treated PNCs achieve a PLQY of 99.3% and retain ∼80% of their initial PLQY after 9 days under ambient conditions. The resulting perovskite light-emitting diodes deliver a maximum external quantum efficiency of 10.2% and a maximum luminance of 473 cd m-2, representing a significant improvement over pristine devices. These findings identify molecular hydrogen-bonding geometry as a key design parameter for surface engineering of efficient and stable PNC-based optoelectronic devices.

articles.title: Nrsn1-Smarcc1 Coupling Regulates Neural Stem Cell Differentiation and Chronic-phase Recovery After Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract: Stroke remains a leading cause of long-term neurological disability worldwide, largely due to irreversible neuronal loss and the limited regenerative capacity of the adult mammalian brain. Neural stem cells (NSCs) in the adult brain possess the potential to generate new neurons after injury, yet the molecular mechanisms regulating their neuronal differentiation following ischemic insult remain incompletely understood. Here, integrating single-cell multi-omics analyses with spatial transcriptomics, we systematically delineated cell type-specific spatiotemporal dynamics in the striatum of a mouse model of ischemia-reperfusion injury. We identified Neurensin 1 (Nrsn1) as a gene markedly upregulated during NSC-derived neuronal differentiation in the recovery phase. Mechanistically, Foxa2 directly activates Nrsn1 transcription, whereas Nrsn1 promotes neuronal differentiation by facilitating the nuclear translocation of the chromatin-remodeling factor Smarcc1 in vitro. In vivo, both endogenous NSCs and transplanted NSCs overexpressing Nrsn1 significantly enhanced neuronal regeneration and improved functional recovery in mice subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion and reperfusion (MCAO/R). Collectively, these findings identify Nrsn1 as a key regulator of NSC neuronal differentiation and uncover a Nrsn1-Smarcc1 coupling mechanism that promotes neural regeneration after ischemic brain injury, highlighting a potential molecular target for strategies aimed at enhancing post-stroke recovery.

articles.title: Poly (Lipoic Acid) Nanoparticles With High Blood-Brain Barrier Permeability and Enhanced Anti-Ferroptotic Activity for Ischemic Stroke Treatment.
articles.abstract: Lipoic acid (LA) scavenges free radicals and was clinically tested for ischemic stroke. However, the short half-life and weak efficacy in penetrating the blood-brain barrier (BBB) limit its use in the brain. Here, we developed poly (lipoic acid) nanoparticles (pLANs) with a half-life of more than 15 h and a high efficiency to penetrate the BBB for ischemic stroke treatment. With intraperitoneal injection, imaging studies using fluorescently labelled pLANs of different sizes revealed that 30 nm pLANs entered the brain most rapidly and provided the strongest protection against ischemic injury. In vitro, 30 nm pLANs significantly prevented cell death induced by oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD), reduced total ROS and lipid peroxides, and inhibited GPX4-dependent ferroptosis. In rat models of cerebral ischemia/reperfusion, 30 nm pLANs extended the therapeutic window by 3 h relative to LA monomer and prevented neuronal damage effectively at only half the dose. These findings demonstrate that 30 nm pLANs effectively cross the BBB, sustain drug levels in blood, and protect against neuronal death by suppressing ferroptosis, offering a promising strategy for ischemic stroke and other neurological disorders associated with oxidative stress.

articles.title: Protocatechuic acid protects neural stem cells against cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury by suppressing JAK2/STAT3 signaling and restoring mitophagy.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Neural stem cells (NSCs) are important for endogenous brain repair but are highly vulnerable to mitochondrial dysfunction during cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI). Preliminary bioinformatics analysis suggested that immune microenvironment remodeling and JAK/STAT signaling activation are involved in CIRI pathology. This study investigated whether protocatechuic acid (PCA) protects NSCs after ischemia-reperfusion injury and explored the underlying mechanisms focusing on the JAK2/STAT3 pathway and mitophagy.

RESULTS: Bioinformatics analysis identified JAK/STAT signaling as a potential regulatory node in CIRI. Transcriptome sequencing further showed that PCA markedly altered the gene expression profile of NSCs, with differentially expressed genes enriched in the JAK/STAT pathway. In vitro, PCA suppressed OGD/R-induced JAK2/STAT3 activation, restored mitochondrial membrane potential, reduced DCFH-DA and MitoSOX Red oxidation-sensitive fluorescence signals, promoted TOMM20/LC3 colocalization, enhanced PINK1/Parkin-related mitophagy, and improved NSC survival. Co-treatment with the JAK2 inhibitor AG490 further supported the protective and pro-mitophagic effects of PCA, whereas co-treatment with the JAK/STAT pathway activator RO8191 weakened PCA-mediated mitochondrial protection and mitophagy restoration. In vivo, PCA improved neurological function, reduced infarct volume, attenuated hippocampal neuronal injury, preserved endogenous NSCs and NeuN-positive cells, and enhanced mitophagy-related signals in MCAO/R rats. Importantly, in vivo Western blot analysis showed that PCA suppressed MCAO/R-induced JAK2/STAT3 phosphorylation, whereas RO8191 co-treatment attenuated this inhibitory effect and weakened the protective effects of PCA, supporting the involvement of JAK2/STAT3 inhibition in PCA-mediated neuroprotection.

CONCLUSION: PCA alleviates CIRI and protects NSCs partly by suppressing JAK2/STAT3 activation, restoring mitochondrial function, and promoting PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy. These findings provide experimental evidence supporting mitochondrial quality control and NSC protection as potential therapeutic targets for ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Microglial SREBP2 regulate cholesterol-related lipid metabolism and inflammatory levels following ischemic stroke via the autophagy pathway.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dysregulated lipid metabolism and inflammation exacerbate brain injury, with abnormal cholesterol metabolism playing a role in stroke condition. SREBPs are key transcription factors regulating lipid synthesis, and their activation is linked to autophagy. It remains unclear whether autophagy clears lipids and modulates inflammation after ischemic stroke, and whether SREBP2 affect cholesterol metabolism and inflammation via autophagy. This study aims to investigate the role of SREBPs and the mediating mechanism of autophagy in post-ischemic stroke lipid dysregulation and inflammation.

METHODS: In vivo mice models of ischemic stroke (middle cerebral artery occlusion, MCAO) and in vitro neuronal oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) models were employed. Through interfering with SREBP2, combined with autophagy inhibitor/activator treatment, we detected cholesterol and cholesteryl ester in microglia and brain tissue, the expression levels of inflammatory factors, and the expression changes of autophagy-related proteins (LC3, p62) and SREBP downstream lipid metabolism-related genes.

RESULTS: After ischemic stroke, the expression of SREBP2 in brain tissue was significantly upregulated, the autophagy pathway was activated, accompanied by cholesterol and lipid accumulation and increased expression of inflammatory factors. Interfering with SREBP2 expression significantly inhibited the excessive activation of the autophagy pathway, reduced the content of cholesterol-related lipids in brain tissue and neurons, decreased the release of inflammatory factors, and alleviated cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. In microglia-neuron co-culture experiments, SREBPs interference in microglia significantly improved the survival rate of OGD/R-induced injured neurons and reduced neuronal apoptosis, while behavioral tests revealed that SREBP2 interference remarkably promoted neural function recovery in MCAO mice.

CONCLUSION: SREBP2 regulate the autophagy pathway to affect the balance of cholesterol-related lipid metabolism and the intensity of inflammatory responses after ischemic stroke, thereby participating in the pathophysiological process of cerebral ischemic injury, which provides a new target and theoretical basis for the treatment of ischemic stroke.

articles.title: Morphology matters: Spherical versus rod-shaped selenium nanoparticles exert divergent neuroprotection after cerebral ischemia/reperfusion via redox reprogramming and mitochondrial bioenergetics.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke is a leading cause of death and disability, with reperfusion injury-driven oxidative stress representing a key therapeutic target. Selenium nanoparticles (SeNPs) show neuroprotective potential, yet the influence of nanoparticle morphology remains poorly understood.

OBJECTIVE: To compare the neuroprotective effects of spherical (Sph) versus rod-shaped (Rods) SeNPs in models of cerebral ischemia/reperfusion, focusing on redox modulation, mitochondrial bioenergetics, and functional outcomes.

METHODS: Primary rat cortical neuron-astrocyte co-cultures were exposed to Sph or Rods (1-10 μg/mL). ROS production, mitochondrial membrane potential, cell viability, gene expression, and neurite outgrowth were assessed. In vivo, transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) was induced in rats, followed by intraperitoneal injection of Sph or Rods (1 μg/g) 1 h post-reperfusion. Neurological outcomes and infarct volume were evaluated at 24 and 48 h.

RESULTS: Low concentrations (1-5 μg/mL) of both morphologies upregulated antioxidant genes, suppressed pro-apoptotic factors, enhanced Bcl2 expression, and promoted neuritogenesis without cytotoxicity. High concentration (10 μg/mL) induced pro-oxidant shift, with Sph triggering early apoptosis and Rods causing late apoptosis/necrosis. Both SeNPs restored CO-induced ΔΨm collapse and normalized respiratory chain function. In vivo, Sph improved motor coordination without reducing infarct volume, whereas Rods significantly reduced infarct size but showed less sustained behavioral improvement.

CONCLUSIONS: Nanoparticle morphology critically dictates therapeutic strategy: spherical SeNPs prioritize functional preservation, whereas nanorods confer structural tissue salvage. These findings establish morphology as a key determinant of SeNPs bioactivity and provide a rationale for morphology-guided design of nanotherapeutics for ischemic stroke.

Selenium nanoparticles (SeNPs) show neuroprotective potential, yet the influence of nanoparticle morphology remains poorly understood. articles.title: Hydrogen reshapes the senescent microenvironment of callus to enhance the healing of anti-osteoporotic-drug-induced atypical femoral fracture.
articles.abstract: Long-term bisphosphonates (BPs) are widely used to treat osteoporosis, however, they are paradoxically associated with the development of atypical femoral fractures (AFFs), which often characterized by impaired healing. In this study, we induced an AFF model using zoledronate (ZOL) administration in ovariectomized (OVX) osteoporotic rats, following a unilateral femoral fracture. Here we identified that a local pro-senescent microenvironment causes persistent inflammation and impairs effective regeneration in rat AFFs. Molecular hydrogen has demonstrated anti-senescence and anti-inflammatory properties, yet its effects on AFF healing remain unexplored. Therefore, we treated the AFF rats with hydrogen rich water (HRW). The outcomes were assessed by radiographs, histology, micro-CT, and biomechanical tests. The fracture microenvironment was analyzed based on the indicators of senescence, fibrosis, macrophage polarization, cytokine expression, and angiogenesis. We found that HRW significantly promoted callus bridging and resolved the non-union gap in ZOL-induced AFFs, whereas the ZOL group exhibited persistent fibrous tissue. Micro-CT and biomechanical tests confirmed that HRW did not compromise the mechanical strength of the bone mass elevated by BPs. Instead, HRW specifically attenuated the local senescent microenvironment, with a reduction in both SA-β-gal activity and the expression of p16, p21 within the fracture gap. This was accompanied by clearance of pathological fibroblasts, a shift from pro-inflammatory M1 to anti-inflammatory M2 macrophages, a rebalanced cytokine profile, and restored formation of osteogenesis-coupled type-H vessels. Our findings confirm that molecular hydrogen facilitates AFFs healing by locally reversing the senescent microenvironment, rather than boosting systemic bone formation. This creates a favorable niche for callus bridging, representing a novel therapeutic strategy for fracture delayed union or non-union.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal Core-Shell Microspheres Enable Hydrogen-Mediated Redox Priming and Kartogenin-Induced Cartilage Regeneration for Osteoarthritis Bio-Rescue.
articles.abstract: The effective management of osteoarthritis (OA) remains a formidable clinical challenge due to a chronically inflamed joint microenvironment and the limited self-regenerative capacity of articular cartilage. To address these barriers, we developed an ultrasound-responsive core-shell microsphere platform engineered via a customized microfluidic capillary device. This system features a kartogenin (KGN)-loaded poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) (PLGA) core encapsulated within a sodium alginate shell enriched with tin disulfide (SnS) nanosheets (SSN). Following intra-articular injection, non-invasive ultrasound stimulation triggers the localized SSN to generate low-concentration hydrogen gas (H2). This in situ H2 generation rapidly scavenges excess reactive oxygen species to restore redox homeostasis, thereby mitigating mitochondrial dysfunction and preserving chondrocyte viability. Consequently, this targeted antioxidative intervention suppresses pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion and polarizes synovial macrophages toward a pro-regenerative M2 phenotype. Within this newly stabilized microenvironment, the sustained release of KGN from the PLGA core successfully reverses extracellular matrix metabolic imbalances to promote cartilage repair. In a rat model of OA, this dual-functional, spatiotemporally controlled platform profoundly halted joint degeneration and preserved histological cartilage integrity. Collectively, this ultrasound-triggered core-shell microsphere system offers a highly promising, disease-modifying strategy for comprehensive OA therapy.

articles.title: Chemical Mechanisms of Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury and Neuroprotection in the Thrombectomy Era.
articles.abstract: Mechanical thrombectomy has significantly improved outcomes for patients with large-vessel occlusion stroke. However, restoring the artery does not always re-establish full microvascular blood flow, tissue rescue, or a good neurological outcome. Ischemia-reperfusion injury varies over time, with distinct biochemical mechanisms dominating during ischemia, early reperfusion, and the subsequent hours. During ischemia, factors like adenosine triphosphate (ATP) depletion, ionic imbalance, calcium overload, mitochondrial dysfunction, acidosis, and metabolic changes such as succinate build-up render brain tissue highly vulnerable. When blood flow resumes, oxygen delivery to this stressed tissue can induce rapid mitochondrial redox shifts, electron leakage, reactive oxygen and nitrogen species formation, iron-dependent radical generation, and lipid peroxidation. Damage may then persist for hours through ongoing mitochondrial dysfunction, phospholipid hydroperoxide accumulation, reactive aldehydes, ferroptosis, blood-brain barrier breakdown, microvascular issues, and inflammation. Much of the mechanistic evidence supporting these processes derives from experimental studies, and their relevance to clinical outcomes after thrombectomy requires further validation. This narrative review tracks these chemical changes across the main phases of cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury and connects them to modern thrombectomy practices. It also explores how the timing of each process may inform neuroprotective strategies, drug delivery methods, patient selection via imaging, and future clinical trial approaches.
