articles.title: Remote ischemic preconditioning protects against cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury through lactate-dependent AMPK/ULK1 signaling and autophagy.
articles.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury is a major contributor to ischemic cerebral damage and poor functional outcomes following ischemic stroke, and effective neuroprotective strategies remain limited. Remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC) has emerged as a promising, noninvasive approach; however, its underlying mechanisms are incompletely understood. Here, we investigated whether lactate serves as a key metabolic mediator linking RIPC to neuroprotection through regulation of autophagy. Using an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) model in PC12 cells and a middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model in rats, we demonstrate that I/R impairs autophagic flux, as evidenced by p62 accumulation and reduced LC3-II and Beclin-1 expression, leading to increased cellular apoptosis and injury. Lactate supplementation restored autophagic flux, enhanced cell viability, and suppressed apoptosis under OGD/R conditions. Mechanistically, lactate activated the AMPK/ULK1 signaling pathway, whereas pharmacological inhibition of AMPK or ULK1 attenuated lactate-induced autophagy and cytoprotection. In vivo, RIPC elevated plasma and cerebral lactate levels, activated AMPK/ULK1 signaling, promoted autophagy, reduced infarct volume, and improved acute neurological outcomes. Notably, blockade of lactate transport or inhibition of AMPK/ULK1 signaling attenuated these protective effects. Collectively, our findings suggest that lactate serves as an important mediator of RIPC-induced neuroprotection and reveal a novel lactate-AMPK/ULK1-autophagy axis that mitigates cerebral I/R injury. These results provide mechanistic insight into RIPC and suggest potential therapeutic targets for ischemic stroke.
articles.englishSummary: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion (I/R) injury is a major contributor to ischemic cerebral damage and poor functional outcomes following ischemic stroke, and effective neuroprotective strategies remain limited. Remote ischemic preconditioning (RIPC) has emerged as a promising, noninvasive approach; however, its underlying mechanisms are incompletely understood. Here, we investigated whether lactate serves as a key metabolic mediator linking RIPC to neuroprotection through regulation of autophagy.

articles.title: The RETRIAD Study: Comparative First-Pass Reperfusion Performance of EmboTrap III, Trevo NXT, and APERIO Stent Retrievers in Acute Large-Vessel Occlusion Stroke: A Single-Center Retrospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Background/Objectives: Contemporary stent retrievers differ in design, yet direct comparative evidence regarding their first-pass reperfusion performance using a standardized endpoint remains limited. This study compared first-pass reperfusion outcomes among APERIO, Trevo NXT, and EmboTrap III. Methods: In this exploratory, single-center retrospective cohort study, 200 patients were screened between 1 March 2024 and 1 August 2026. Forty patients had not completed 90-day follow-up at the time of the initial data analysis. An additional 104 patients were excluded because of tandem occlusion (n = 29), recanalization after intravenous thrombolysis before thrombectomy (n = 8), distal vessel occlusion (n = 30), or successful direct aspiration without stent-retriever deployment (n = 37). The final cohort comprised 56 patients treated with first-line combined stent-retriever and aspiration thrombectomy using APERIO (n = 28), Trevo NXT (n = 14), or EmboTrap III (n = 14). The primary endpoint was strict first-pass effect (FPE), defined as first-pass expanded Treatment in Cerebral Ischemia (eTICI) grade 2c-3. Results: Strict FPE was achieved in 16/28 (57.1%), 9/14 (64.3%), and 9/14 (64.3%) patients, respectively (global exact p = 0.879). Both comparisons with APERIO yielded an absolute risk difference of +7.1 percentage points (95% CI, -23.2 to +33.6). Exploratory adjusted analyses yielded imprecise estimates. Heidelberg-classified symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage occurred in zero, three, and two patients, respectively. Conclusions: No statistically detectable difference in strict FPE was demonstrated among the three device-based treatment strategies. However, the small sample size, wide confidence intervals, and nonrandomized treatment allocation preclude conclusions regarding device equivalence or causal effects.

articles.title: Diffusion-weighted imaging reversal after reperfusion therapy in acute ischemic stroke: associations with white matter hyperintensities and cerebral microbleeds.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: White matter hyperintensities (WMH) and cerebral microbleeds (CMBs) are common MRI markers of chronic small-vessel brain injury and have been associated with adverse outcomes after ischemic stroke. However, whether these markers influence early ischemic tissue reversibility following reperfusion therapy remains unclear. We therefore investigated their associations with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) lesion reversal, hemorrhagic complications, and short-term functional outcome after MRI-guided reperfusion therapy.

METHODS: In this retrospective single-center study, consecutive patients with acute ischemic stroke undergoing MRI-guided intravenous thrombolysis, with or without additional mechanical thrombectomy, were included. According to the institutional protocol, follow-up MRI was planned 24 ± 6 h after treatment to assess DWI lesion evolution, WMH volume, and CMBs. DWI reversal was defined as a reduction of ≥ 25% in baseline DWI lesion volume. Multivariable regression analyses were performed to identify predictors of DWI reversal, intracerebral hemorrhage, and functional outcome at hospital discharge.

RESULTS: Among 345 patients (median age 74 years [IQR 63-82], 48.1% female), 45 (13%) additionally underwent mechanical thrombectomy. DWI reversal occurred in 76 patients (22.0%) and was not associated with baseline WMH volume, CMBs, initial infarct volume, treatment modality, or thrombolysis time window. Higher baseline NIHSS and modified Rankin Scale scores were associated with lower odds of DWI reversal, whereas hypercholesterolemia was independently associated with increased odds of DWI reversal. We found no evidence of an association of WMH burden or CMB presence with intracerebral hemorrhage or of an independent association with functional outcome. Fourteen patients (4.1%) developed new CMBs on follow-up MRI.

CONCLUSIONS: We found no evidence of an association between baseline WMH volume or CMB presence and early DWI lesion reversal or hemorrhagic complications following reperfusion therapy in this cohort. These findings provide no evidence that these two chronic MRI markers are major determinants of early infarct tissue reversibility. Larger multicenter studies incorporating comprehensive small-vessel disease phenotyping and long-term follow-up are warranted.

We therefore investigated their associations with diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) lesion reversal, hemorrhagic complications, and short-term functional outcome after MRI-guided reperfusion therapy.

articles.title: Panax notoginseng-Derived Carbon Quantum Dots as a Novel Administration Strategy for Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury Therapy.
articles.abstract: The present study aimed to synthesize Panax notoginseng-derived carbon quantum dots (PN-CDs) and explore their role in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI). PN-CDs were synthesized by the hydrothermal method, and characterization and biocompatibility were assessed. Next, CIRI models were established using SH-SY5Y cells, primary neurons were treated with oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R), and rats were subjected to middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion (MCAO/R). After PN-CDs treatment, inflammation, apoptosis, and oxidative stress were detected in neuronal cells and rats using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, quantitative reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction, flow cytometry, Western blot, and 2',7'-dichlorodihydrofluorescein diacetate probe. Meanwhile, 2,3,5-triphenyltetrazolium chloride, terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick end labeling, Nissl, and hematoxylin and eosin staining were employed to measure the pathological damage of rats. Additionally, CIRI rats were administered with PN-CDs, Panax notoginseng saponins (PNS), Panax notoginseng (PN), or edaravone to investigate whether PN-CDs had the best effect. The findings revealed that PN-CDs exhibited favorable biocompatibility and crossed the blood-brain barrier. In vitro, PN-CD treatment inhibited oxidative stress, apoptosis, and inflammation, as evidenced by the decrease of interleukin-1β (IL-1β), IL-6, Bax, C-caspase-3, tumor necrosis factor-α, malondialdehyde, and reactive oxygen species and the increase of superoxide dismutase, Bcl-2, and glutathione. In CIRI rats, PN-CDs improved pathological damage and suppressed inflammation, apoptosis, and oxidative stress. The therapeutic effect of PN-CDs on CIRI was distinctly better than that of PNS and PN, and comparable to that of the first-line drug edaravone. In short, PN-CDs, a novel and efficient administration strategy, alleviates CIRI by inhibiting apoptosis, oxidative stress, and inflammation.

articles.title: Scutellarin as a multi-target neuroprotective agent: Analytical evidence, pharmacokinetic insights and translational strategies across neurodegenerative disorders.
articles.abstract: Neurodegenerative disorders are a leading cause of disability and mortality globally, but effective disease-modifying therapeutic strategies are still largely unavailable. Scutellarin is a flavonoid glycoside extracted from Erigeron breviscapus (Vant.) Hand-Mazz. It has been widely studied in preclinical models of neurodegenerative disorders. In this study, we performed a systematic review of preclinical animal studies. We combined comprehensive database retrieval with quantitative synthesis of eligible outcomes. The pooled results demonstrated that scutellarin significantly reduced cerebral infarct volume and improved neurological deficit scores in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion models. It also ameliorated learning and memory impairments in experimental Alzheimer's disease (AD) models. Consistent neuroprotective effects were also found in models of depression, anxiety, Parkinson's disease, etc. Mechanistic analysis indicated that scutellarin produces multi-level neuroprotective effects. It acts by reducing oxidative stress, inhibiting neuroinflammation, suppressing apoptosis, stabilizing the neurovascular unit and other neurobiological processes. This review first evaluated the preclinical efficacy of scutellarin through systematic review and meta-analysis. It then integrated cross-disease mechanisms with network pharmacology, reverse virtual screening and molecular docking to identify computationally predicted targets. Although scutellarin shows promising preclinical effects, its clinical translation faces major limitations. These limitations include low oral bioavailability, poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) penetration and insufficient data on brain exposure. Overall, scutellarin is a multi-target neuroprotective candidate. Future studies should focus on target validation, exposure-response modeling, delivery optimization and clinically relevant translational evaluation.

articles.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveal mesenchymal stem cell-associated neuroimmune and neuronal signaling patterns after ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke induces coordinated yet spatially heterogeneous neuroimmune and neuronal responses that shape secondary injury and tissue remodeling. However, how intranasal mesenchymal stem cell administration is associated with these cell type-specific responses remains incompletely understood. Here, we integrated single-cell RNA sequencing of the ipsilateral cerebrum on days 1, 7, and 14 after middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion with spatial transcriptomic profiling on day 7. A total of 55,520 high-quality single-cell transcriptomes were obtained from control, middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion, and mesenchymal stem cell-treated samples. In this exploratory dataset, the middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion samples showed relatively greater representation of inflammatory and antigen-presenting microglial states and elevated expression of selected microglial state-associated genes, including Slfn4, Apoe, and Gpnmb. In the corresponding exploratory comparison, the mesenchymal stem cell-treated sample showed relatively greater representation of homeostatic-associated and Lgals3/Spp1-enriched microglial states and lower expression of several inflammatory-associated genes. Spatial mapping further revealed regionally restricted expression of microglial and neuronal markers within the injured tissue. Excitatory neurons displayed preliminary mesenchymal stem cell-associated transcriptional patterns involving mitochondrial transcripts, oxidative phosphorylation, synaptic signaling, calcium-related functions, and apoptosis/autophagy-associated pathways. CellChat analysis computationally predicted relatively high levels of tumor necrosis factor, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand, and complement signaling in the middle cerebral artery occlusion/reperfusion sample, whereas the mesenchymal stem cell-treated sample had relatively high levels of predicted activity of neuregulin, pleiotrophin and selected semaphorin. Together, these integrated datasets provide a hypothesis-generating framework linking microglial state remodeling, neuronal metabolic and synaptic programs, and predicted neuroimmune communication patterns after ischemic stroke. Because each omics condition or time point was represented by one biological sample, all the transcriptomic findings should be considered preliminary and exploratory and should be validated in independently replicated cohorts.

articles.title: Engineering a Translational Human Thrombus Platform to Evaluate Clinical Therapies in Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recanalization failure after ischemic stroke remains a major clinical challenge, partly because cerebral thrombi display marked spatial heterogeneity that is poorly reproduced by experimental models. Here, we engineered a translational human blood-based thrombus platform that recapitulates key histological features of patient-derived stroke clots.

METHODS: Under controlled conditions, the platform generated reproducible thrombi with pronounced interthrombus and intrathrombus heterogeneity, including alternating red blood cell-rich and platelet-rich territories. Multiscale structural and biochemical analyses confirmed the successful replication of the clinical biphasic organization associated with resistance to rtPA (recombinant tissue-type plasminogen activator): a compact outer fibrin shell containing focal accumulations of plasminogen activator inhibitor-1, and a dense inner core further stabilized by neutrophil extracellular traps.

RESULTS: Functional thrombolysis assays demonstrated that this architecture directly dictates lytic susceptibility. Specifically, artificially breaching the outer fibrin shell (halved thrombi) significantly accelerated early rtPA-mediated lysis, proving its role as an effective physical barrier. Furthermore, lytic response was inherently linked to clot composition: platelet-rich thrombi with dense plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 and neutrophil extracellular trap networks exhibited profound resistance to standard rtPA compared with red blood cell-rich clots. Supporting the platform's translational relevance, this structural resistance was successfully overcome by clinically relevant strategies, including tenecteplase and adjunctive DNAse, consistent with observations from human stroke cohorts.

CONCLUSIONS: By accurately reproducing the spatial organization and differential thrombolytic responses of human cerebral thrombi, this translational framework provides a robust preclinical tool to dissect lytic resistance and evaluate next-generation precision reperfusion therapies. Furthermore, developing robust ex vivo human platforms is increasingly critical to align with the replacement, reduction, refinement ethical guidelines for animal research.

articles.title: Intranasal Delivery of an Antioxidant Nanoassembly for Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury via Drd2/β-arrestin2/ERK Signaling.
articles.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) is caused by reduced cerebral blood flow, leading to excessive oxidative stress and neurological deficits. Curcumin (Cur) is a promising therapeutic agent, but its antioxidant activity is limited by low bioavailability and poor brain penetration. Herein, an intranasal delivery strategy using a tetrahedral framework nucleic acid (tFNAs)-Cur nanoassembly (tFNAs-Cur) was employed for CIRI treatment. tFNAs-Cur was synthesized through self-assembly, achieving a high Cur loading efficiency of 87% and exhibiting potent scavenging activity against reactive oxygen species (ROS) including O2·-, ·OH, and H2O2. In vitro studies showed that tFNAs-Cur inhibited oxygen glucose deprivation/reoxygenation-induced ROS elevation of cytoplasm and mitochondria, and enhanced proliferation and migration of SH-SY5Y cells. In vivo studies demonstrated that intranasal administration of tFNAs-Cur reduced cerebral infarct volume, enhanced neuronal survival, and improved neurological and behavioral outcomes in middle cerebral artery occlusion rats. Further mechanistic investigation using RNA sequencing revealed that tFNAs-Cur exerted its effects by activating the Drd2/β-arrestin2/ERK signaling, thereby improving mitochondrial function and upregulating BDNF levels. Furthermore, hemolysis assays, serum biochemical measurements, and histopathological analyses demonstrated that tFNAs-Cur possessed a favorable biosafety profile both ex vivo and in vivo. This study provides an intranasal antioxidant nanoassembly strategy for CIRI and holds potential for clinical translation.

articles.title: Mechanism of Shanhu Qishiwei pills in regulating endoplasmic reticulum stress through GRP78/CHOP signaling pathway for the treatment of cerebral ischemia.
articles.abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Stroke, a prevalent cerebrovascular condition, is characterized by high occurrence, disability, mortality, and recurrence rates. Shanhu Qishiwei pills (བྱུར་དམར་བདུན་ཅུ།, SHQSWP) are a Tibetan prescription, which were included in the national drug standard ZZ-8432 of the National Food and Drug Administration with approval number Z54020114. SHQSWP can relieve palpitation, tranquilize, and arrest convulsion and is mainly used for cerebral thrombosis, cerebral hemorrhage, and coronary heart disease. This study aimed to investigate the mechanism of SHQSWP for the treatment of cerebral ischemia.

AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aimed to screen the differential proteins of SHQSWP for the treatment of cerebral ischemia and verify its mechanism in regulating the endoplasmic reticulum stress signaling pathway.

MATERIALS AND METHODS: Triple quadrupole liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (HPLC-QqQ-MS) was to quantitatively detect 25 chemical components in SHQSWP. TTC staining, HE staining, Nissl staining, and TUNEL staining were used to verify the effectiveness of SHQSWP for the treatment of cerebral ischemia in middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model rats. Deferentially expressed proteins were screened using a protein chip, and the potential targets and signaling pathways of SHQSWP in the treatment of cerebral ischemia were visually screened using protein-protein interaction (PPI) network analysis. Molecular docking technology was used to predict the binding affinity and binding mode of the key compounds in SHQSWP with related target proteins. RT-qPCR, WB and IF were used to verify the signaling pathways and targets regulated by SHQSWP in the treatment of cerebral ischemia.

RESULTS: HPLC-QqQ-MS was used to determine the contents of 25 chemical components in SHQSWP, including neochlorogenic acid, isorhamnetin, chlorogenic acid, gallic acid, hydroxysafflor yellow-A, and crocin I. Each SHQSWP dose can reduce the rate of cerebral infarction in MCAO rats, improve neurobehavioral and pathological changes in the cortical area of brain tissues, increase the number of Nissl bodies in the cortical area, and reduce the rate of positive apoptotic cells in the cortical area. Protein chip prediction showed that SHQSWP may play a therapeutic role by regulating EPhA5, IL-1α, fractalkine, IL-10, IL-7, and IL-3 proteins. Molecular docking revealed that GRP78 may be the common dominant target of 15 components in SHQSWP, and Rutin may be the representative component with the strongest binding force with 7 key targets. SHQSWP can significantly increase the mRNA expression levels of PARP1 and XBP1 in the brain tissue of MCAO rats, significantly reduce the protein expression levels of CHOP, GRP78 and BAX, and increase the protein expression level of XBP1. A medium SHQSWP dose can reduce the fluorescence intensity of NLRP3, BAX, and CHOP in rat brain tissues and enhance the fluorescence intensity of XBP1.

CONCLUSIONS: SHQSWP can inhibit endoplasmic reticulum stress-mediated apoptosis by regulating key proteins such as BAX, CHOP, GRP78, and XBP1, thus playing a neuroprotective role in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury.

articles.title: RIC-specific cytoprotective profile mediated by microglia in a mouse model of acute ischaemic stroke.
articles.abstract: Background: Remote ischaemic conditioning (RIC) is an endogenous neuroprotective strategy involving repeated, transient occlusion of a limb artery to reduce ischaemic injury at a distant site. We investigated the effects of RIC in a mouse model of focal cerebral ischaemia induced by distal transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO). Animals were randomised into three groups: Stroke (tMCAO, 60 min), Stroke+remote ischaemic preconditioning (RIPerC) (RIC applied during ischaemia) and Stroke+remote ischaemic postconditioning (RIPostC) (RIC initiated 10 min after reperfusion). The RIC protocol consisted of three cycles of 5-minute hindlimb ischaemia followed by 5-minute reperfusion. Results: At 72 hours postischaemia, both RIPerC and RIPostC significantly reduced the infarct volumes in male and female mice. In males, infarct size decreased from 6.31 ± 0.28% (Stroke) to 3.77 ± 0.47% (RIPerC, p<0.0025) and 4.00 ± 0.40% (RIPostC, p<0.0061). However, the RIPerC+RIPostC group significantly increased the infarct volume compared with the Stroke group (8.41± 0.72%). In females, reductions were greater: from 6.69±0.46% (Stroke) to 2.95 ± 0.34% (RIPerC, p<0.0001) and 2.96 ± 0.32% (RIPostC, p<0.0001). Functional recovery was improved, particularly with RIPostC, correlating with infarct size reduction (Pearson’s r=0.5505 in males, r=0.7313 in females). Apoptosis was reduced by over 50% with both treatments, and microglial phagocytic activity (cluster of differentiation 68+/Iba1+ (ionised calcium binding adaptor molecule 1)) increased significantly. Microglial depletion using PLX3397 (71.3% reduction in Iba1+ cells) worsened ischaemic injury, yet RIC preserved its protective effects, suggesting additional microglia-independent mechanisms. Furthermore, RIC enhanced neurogenesis in the subventricular zone and infarct core (doublecortin marker+ cells doubled versus Stroke), with a marked proliferative response in female hippocampi (Ki67+ cells increased by 127%). Conclusion: These findings reveal sex-specific efficacy of RIC, with mechanistic insights obtained in male animals suggesting a dual mode of action via modulation of microglial function and promotion of endogenous neurorepair pathways.

articles.title: Beyond Blood-Brain Barrier Crossing in Reperfusion-Era Ischemic Stroke: Interface-Matched Active-Entity Delivery and Translational Product Design.
articles.abstract: Reperfusion therapy has transformed acute ischemic stroke care, yet large-vessel recanalization does not ensure capillary reperfusion, preservation of the blood-brain barrier and neurovascular unit (BBB/NVU), or durable neurological recovery. Nanomedicine is still commonly judged by BBB crossing or ischemic-hemisphere accumulation, although vascular access, tissue viability, transport phenotype, thromboinflammation, and standard treatment change rapidly during the lifetime of a formulation. This narrative review proposes a conceptual framework that matches the reperfusion state and pathological interface to the compartment in which the therapeutically active entity must act. The framework is intended to organize preclinical evidence and generate testable translational hypotheses; it has not yet been clinically validated. Persistent occlusion may favor intravascular targets, whereas recanalization with no-reflow creates a distinct microvascular delivery problem. Early reperfusion injury may prioritize BBB/NVU stabilization, while later biological contexts may require selective immune, regenerative, or organelle-directed interventions. These contexts may coexist spatially, vary across vascular territories, and shift during treatment; they should therefore not be interpreted as a mandatory chronological sequence. We distinguish BBB crossing, controlled barrier modulation, and BBB/NVU repair as separate therapeutic tasks, and introduce transport attrition as a practical explanation for why sequential targeting, transcytosis, cellular uptake, endosomal escape, and organelle localization can yield little final active-entity exposure despite strong tissue imaging. Recent predominantly preclinical examples illustrate how thrombus-targeted rtPA systems, neutrophil-intercepting particles, NET-degrading polymersomes, lesion-targeted nanoplatforms, and mitochondrial nanomedicines may fit different delivery topologies. Translational credibility requires topology-resolved exposure, target engagement in viable tissue, hemocompatibility under antithrombotic treatment, state-appropriate models, function-linked manufacturing controls, and compatibility with thrombolysis and thrombectomy.

articles.title: Mitochondrial cristae remodeling in ischemic stroke: mechanisms and therapeutic perspectives.
articles.abstract: Mitochondrial cristae arrange the respiratory machinery within the inner membrane and change as ischemia gives way to reperfusion. Their organization depends on mitochondrial contact site and cristae organizing system assemblies, optic atrophy 1, adenosine triphosphate synthase, and cardiolipin. Disruption of these systems can impair energy production, facilitate neuronal death, and expose mitochondrial DNA to inflammatory sensors. This review brings structural work together with experimental stroke studies to examine how crista remodeling contributes to injury and recovery. Genetic manipulation of selected regulators has preserved mitochondrial structure and reduced injury in neurons and microglia. Most of these interventions preceded ischemia, leaving the speed and feasibility of repair after stroke onset uncertain. Pharmacological modulation and mitochondrial delivery offer ways to address this gap, particularly around reperfusion. Emerging strategies combine modulation of crista protein assemblies with cardiolipin directed treatment, mitochondrial antioxidant nanomedicine, organelle delivery, and control of local drug exposure. Their therapeutic evaluation can be aligned with distinct opportunities at reperfusion and during subsequent tissue recovery. Progress toward treatment will require evidence that a candidate reaches the affected brain cells, modifies the intended membrane assembly, and produces lasting neurological benefit. The available studies place crista remodeling within neuroprotective pathways and identify the experimental steps needed to evaluate it as a therapeutic target.

articles.title: Characterization and treatment of ischemic stroke in patients with infective endocarditis: a meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ischemic stroke is a common and serious complication of infective bacterial endocarditis. This study aimed to characterize the frequency, clinical and pathological features, treatment strategies, and outcomes of patients with stroke due to infective endocarditis.

METHODS: We systematically searched PubMed from database inception to October 2022 for studies reporting on stroke in patients with infective endocarditis and performed a meta-analysis.

RESULTS: A total of 122 studies comprising 270,211 patients with infective endocarditis were included. Ischemic stroke occurred in 21% and hemorrhagic stroke in 5% of patients. Stroke was observed in 32% of patients with mitral valve endocarditis, 25% with aortic valve, and 11% with tricuspid valve endocarditis. Stroke was associated with significantly higher mortality (OR 2.35; 95%CI 1.74-3.16). Staphylococcus and Streptococcus species were most frequently associated with stroke (33% and 25%, respectively). The risk of stroke did not differ significantly between patients with and without pre-existing antithrombotic therapy (37% vs. 24%; OR 1.24, 95%CI 0.75-2.06). Successful reperfusion was achieved in 80% of patients undergoing mechanical thrombectomy, although mortality remained high at 49%.

CONCLUSIONS: Stroke is a common complication of infective bacterial endocarditis and has a substantial impact on patient outcomes. It occurs most frequently in patients with mitral valve endocarditis and in those with infections caused by staphylococcal pathogens. Stroke risk was not reduced in patients with pre-existing antithrombotic therapy, supporting discontinuation where no other indication exists. Mechanical thrombectomy in patients with endocarditis-related large vessel occlusion achieves high recanalization rates; however, overall clinical outcomes remain poor in this population.

articles.title: Cavitation jet treatment-assisted glycosylation of hemp seed protein: Structural regulation and emulsion stability.
articles.abstract: This study employed cavitation jet treatment to facilitate the effective glycosylation of hemp seed protein (HSP) with chitosan (CS). Initially, the treatment disrupted intra- and inter-molecular hydrogen bonds, inducing HSP structural unfolding. This critical conformational transition exposed internal reactive amino groups, enabling them to interact with CS carbonyl groups and achieving a maximum grafting degree of 34.54%. Consequently, the secondary structure of HSP was reorganized from an ordered state into a more relaxed, disordered configuration. The subsequent covalent attachment of hydrophilic CS chains effectively shielded exposed hydrophobic regions, significantly enhancing the complex's water affinity. Therefore, overall functional performances were markedly improved: solution properties were enhanced through increased solubility and decreased turbidity, while emulsion performance was optimized, evidenced by a superior EAI (55.89 m2/g), an extended ESI (84.35 min), and improved apparent viscosity and viscoelasticity. This approach provides a practical strategy for the high-value utilization of hemp by-products.

articles.title: Sex dimorphism in vascular trajectories after living-donor kidney transplantation: a prospective exploratory cohort study.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiovascular risk remains high after kidney transplantation, reflecting pre-transplant early vascular aging. Arterial stiffness generally improves, but the trajectory of microvascular endothelial function, and its dependence on recipient's biological sex and donor matching, is unclear.

METHODS: In 71 living-donor kidney transplant recipients, microvascular endothelial function (reactive hyperemia index, lnRHI) and arterial stiffness [augmentation index at 75 bpm (AI@75)] were measured before transplantation and at a median of 24.6 months. Forty-six of their donors were assessed identically before donation, providing a healthy reference of the same sex. Resistance arteries from 37 recipients and 46 living donors underwent wire myography.

RESULTS: AI@75 improved overall (-5.7%; P = .003), whereas microvascular function declined in men but not women (male ΔlnRHI -0.149, P = .002; sex × time interaction β = -0.19, P = .026), stable in direction across 11 specifications including tacrolimus exposure and graft function. The greater AI@75 improvement with sex-matched transplantation (P = .020) did not survive adjustment for baseline stiffness (P = .32). Ex vivo, endothelial relaxation showed no detectable sex difference in recipients (P = .83) or donors (P = .94), whereas passive stiffness was higher in female recipients (P = .048).

CONCLUSIONS: After living-donor kidney transplantation, arterial stiffness improved in both sexes, while microvascular endothelial function declined in men and not in women. Referenced to healthy donors of the same sex, arterial stiffness in men remained abnormal at follow-up. Sex-matched transplantation conferred no independent vascular benefit. These findings are exploratory and require confirmation in larger cohorts.

Arterial stiffness generally improves, but the trajectory of microvascular endothelial function, and its dependence on recipient's biological sex and donor matching, is unclear. METHODS: In 71 living-donor kidney transplant recipients, microvascular endothelial function (reactive hyperemia index, lnRHI) and arterial stiffness [augmentation index at 75 bpm (AI@75)] were measured before transplantation and at a median of 24.6 months.

articles.title: Endohepatology in the Management of Portal Hypertension in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease.
articles.abstract: Portal hypertension is the principal driver of decompensation in advanced chronic liver disease, yet in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) it deviates from the classical sinusoidal paradigm. Growing evidence points to a mixed sinusoidal-presinusoidal phenotype in which the hepatic venous pressure gradient (HVPG) may underestimate true portal pressure, and in which decompensation and varices can occur at lower HVPG values than in viral cirrhosis. This biology is compounded by a diagnostic gap: non-invasive tests such as liver stiffness by vibration-controlled transient elastography, FIB-4, ANTICIPATE-NASH, spleen stiffness and the NICER model, are degraded by obesity through technical limitations and altered diagnostic thresholds, even when test discrimination is preserved. Moreover, no non-invasive rule-in for clinically significant portal hypertension reaches a 90% positive predictive value in obese MASLD, leaving a clinically meaningful grey zone. Endohepatology addresses these diagnostic limitations by providing complementary hemodynamic, elastographic, and histological information. Within a single sedated session, EUS-guided shear-wave elastography and EUS-guided liver biopsy can adjudicate F2-F3 fibrosis when treatment eligibility is uncertain; EUS-guided portal pressure gradient measurement can provide a direct gradient when HVPG or non-invasive tests are discordant with the clinical phenotype; and EUS-based vascular assessment can characterize collateral and variceal anatomy. The same platform extends to therapy, including EUS-guided gastric variceal obliteration and pre-bariatric risk stratification. Current evidence is largely early-phase and requires prospective validation. Rather than replacing established tools, endohepatology offers an integrated pathway tailored to the diagnostic and therapeutic problems most characteristic of MASLD.

articles.title: Uncovering the transcriptional hallmarks of endothelial cell aging via integrated single-cell analysis.
articles.abstract: Endothelial cells (ECs) are critical regulators of vascular function and exhibit tissue-specialized roles. During aging, these cells become dysfunctional, resulting in increased susceptibility to cardiovascular disease. Although single-cell transcriptomics has revealed extensive endothelial heterogeneity, a comprehensive atlas of human EC transcriptomes over the course of the adult human lifespan has been lacking. Here, we present the Human Aging Endothelial Cell Atlas (HAECA), a harmonized single-cell transcriptomic compendium of over 375,000 ECs from 12 human tissues throughout adulthood. We identified age-associated transcriptional shifts, including a decline in angiogenic gene expression in venous ECs and widespread alterations in extracellular matrix and mechanotransduction-associated signatures. Furthermore, we uncovered a p21-linked transcriptional program in ECs, which we linked to cellular senescence in both in vitro and in vivo models. Together, our study provides a high-resolution transcriptomic reference of the human endothelium across tissues and age.

articles.title: Increased Disarray of Extracellular Matrix Collagen-I Fiber Network and Compromised Biomechanics in Aortae From Marfan-Syndrome Mice Assessed Through Combined Opto-Biomechatronics.
articles.abstract: Fibrillin‑1 (FBN1) mutations lead to extracellular matrix (ECM) defects with progressive aortic dilation in Marfan's syndrome (MFS). MFS thoracic aortas have increased stiffness, but how visco-elastic and microstructural abnormalities affect in vivo hemodynamics remains inconclusive. We applied ex vivo uniaxial visco-elasticity stress-relaxation testing and simultaneous 3D collagen Second Harmonic Generation (SHG) imaging to MFS and wt littermate linearized aortic strips with in vivo vascular function. MFS mouse (Fbn1mgR/mgR) aortas were stiffer and more viscous. SHG imaging revealed MFS ECM disorganization at rest and stronger collagen-alignment strain response than wt strips, indicating greater fibrillar straightening capacity. in vivo, MFS mice developed early, progressive aortic dilation. Pulse wave velocity was elevated in young MFS mice pre-dilation but declined as aneurysms formed. Female MFS aortic peak pressure and velocity were normal, but reduced in MFS-males vs. wt. Ex vivo perfused wt carotid arteries were highly compliant. Female MFS carotids were stiffer, had reduced radial strain, a right‑shifted pressure-strain curve and minimal wall‑thickness changes. MFS carotids did not recover baseline diameter after perfusion, indicating impaired visco-elastic recoil. We demonstrate early visco-elastic MFS aortic dysfunction and ECM disorder. Mechanistically, the larger collagen-straightening capacity in MFS cannot compensate for the increased visco-elasticity during a beat-to-beat cycle.

articles.title: Magnetoactive Hydrogels to Probe Curvature-Directed Endothelial Cell Mechanosensing.
articles.abstract: The vascular system exhibits complex, nonplanar geometries that become further distorted during pathological remodeling, including arterial tortuosity and aneurysms. Although hemodynamic shear stress is a well-established regulator of vascular function, the direct effects of curvature as an intrinsic geometric cue remain poorly defined. This is largely because existing in vitro models are static and fail to capture the dynamic changes that accompany disease progression. To address this gap, we used a magnetoactive hydrogel platform that enables real-time, on-demand curvature of endothelial monolayers to reproduce clinically established tortuosity metrics. Using this system, we found that elevated curvature increased nuclear localization of Yes-associated protein (YAP), with the strongest response in convex relative to concave regions of highly tortuous endothelial monolayers. This mechanosensitive response was accompanied by reduced VE-Cadherin junctional thickness and increased membrane localization of endothelial nitric oxide synthase. These findings identify local curvature, independent of shear stress, as a regulator of endothelial cell mechanosensing and function, and establish a dynamic hydrogel platform for isolating geometric regulation from shear stress inputs in vascular mechanobiology.

articles.title: Transcription factor EB as a novel target for dimethyl fumarate to restore endothelial function in diabetes.
articles.abstract: Diabetes mellitus-associated endothelial dysfunction represents a pivotal early event in diabetic vasculopathy, linking metabolic derangements to vascular injury. Dimethyl fumarate (DMF), an FDA-approved drug for multiple sclerosis and psoriasis, exhibits potent anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties, yet whether it protects against diabetic endothelial dysfunction and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Here, diabetic db/db mice and the non-diabetic db/m+ littermates were treated with DMF (100 mg·kg-1·d-1) or vehicle for 4 weeks, and vascular function in aortic and mesenteric artery rings was assessed by wire myography. Human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) and endothelial cell (EC)-specific Tfeb knockout (TfebECKO) mice were employed to investigate the target of DMF in vitro and in vivo. DMF restored the impaired endothelium-dependent relaxations (EDRs) in db/db mouse aortas and insulin-induced relaxations in mesenteric arteries, improved glucose tolerance, reduced aortic endothelial mitochondrial ROS (mito-ROS) accumulation, and lowered the expression of inflammatory markers. IL-1β induced phosphorylation and cytoplasmic retention of TFEB (indicative of TFEB inhibition), mito-ROS production, and inflammatory responses in HUVECs and mouse aortas, all of which were reversed by DMF pretreatment. These protective effects of DMF were largely reversed by TFEB knockdown in HUVECs or in aortas of TfebECKO mice. RNA sequencing data analysis revealed a substantial overlap between DMF-regulated and TFEB-overexpression transcriptional profiles, implicating a role of TFEB in DMF-induced suppression of inflammatory and oxidative pathways. Together, DMF ameliorates endothelial dysfunction in diabetes by inhibiting TFEB phosphorylation and restoring TFEB nuclear activity. Endothelial TFEB represents a critical mediator responsible for the vaso-protective effects of DMF and a promising therapeutic target for the treatment of diabetic vascular complications.

articles.title: Computational modeling of bioresorbable flow-diverting stents: Insights into approaches for coupling hemodynamics and material degradation.
articles.abstract: Bioresorbable flow diverters (BRFDs) represent an emerging treatment for intracranial aneurysms (IAs) that reduces complications associated with permanent flow diverters, as BRFDs-due to their temporary nature-restore native blood flow following degradation. The therapeutic efficacy of BRFDs depends on material degradation, hemodynamics, thrombosis, and endothelialization. To this end, computational models enabling a holistic evaluation of the interplay between these processes could provide considerable insight into optimizing BRFD designs. This review summarizes degradation modeling approaches for bioresorbable metals, including continuum damage mechanics (CDM), mechanochemical phase-field, and reaction-diffusion models. It evaluates the suitability of each framework for integration with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) for guiding BRFD design. CDM approaches focus on the degradation of mechanical integrity and do not directly consider electrochemical transport, whereas mechanochemical models account for mechanical, chemical, and electrochemical processes, providing detailed information on localized corrosion, albeit at a higher computational cost. Reaction-diffusion models are the most practical option for coupling with CFD, offering a balance between accuracy in describing key mechanisms and computational feasibility, although the most suitable approach ultimately depends on how each metal degrades. Critical gaps in BRFD models include the limited modeling of iron, zinc, and molybdenum, and specific aspects of blood chemistry. Additionally, since no standardized validation protocol currently exists for computational models of BRFDs, we recommend a staged pathway: a framework integrating material degradation and hemodynamics and considering thrombosis and endothelialization, validated against in vitro and/or in vivo data, will be essential for advancing the design and therapeutic efficacy assessment of BRFDs. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: Bioresorbable flow diverters (BRFDs), when compared to permanent flow diverters, allow mitigation of long-term complications in treating intracranial aneurysms, but their development remains limited by an incomplete understanding of the interaction between material degradation, blood flow, and biological responses such as thrombosis and aneurysm healing. The design choices of FDs ultimately depend on this interplay, yet no computational framework currently exists to guide it. This review is the first of its kind to systematically evaluate the use of degradation models for coupling with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to elucidate physiologically relevant information of aneurysm healing with BRFDs. Coupling these frameworks provides a practical guide to accelerate the translation of bioresorbable devices from conceptualization, design, and development to clinical use.
articles.englishSummary: Bioresorbable flow diverters (BRFDs) represent an emerging treatment for intracranial aneurysms (IAs) that reduces complications associated with permanent flow diverters, as BRFDs-due to their temporary nature-restore native blood flow following degradation. The therapeutic efficacy of BRFDs depends on material degradation, hemodynamics, thrombosis, and endothelialization. To this end, computational models enabling a holistic evaluation of the interplay between these processes could provide considerable insight into optimizing BRFD designs.

articles.title: Functional Biomaterials for Vascular Healing After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: From Surface Engineering to Clinical Translation.
articles.abstract: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) creates a dynamic blood-material-tissue interface in which thrombosis, inflammation, smooth muscle cell proliferation, and endothelial recovery evolve simultaneously. This narrative review examines coronary biomaterials using a healing-centered translational framework that links material properties to molecular and cellular responses, tissue-level healing, measurable structural and functional phenotypes, and clinical outcomes. We review the evolution from bare-metal and drug-eluting stents to polymer-free systems, drug-coated balloons (DCBs), bioresorbable scaffolds, and bioactive or biomimetic surfaces. Particular emphasis is placed on strut geometry, polymer chemistry and degradation, drug-release kinetics, surface properties, corrosion behavior, endothelial barrier function, macrophage responses, thrombogenicity, and neointimal growth. Structural coverage on intravascular imaging is distinguished from functional endothelial recovery, which requires complementary biological or physiological assessment. Randomized evidence is interpreted at the level of the tested device, formulation, lesion, and procedural strategy; newer platforms are not assumed to confer class-wide superiority. Future progress will require multifunctional, healing-responsive platforms that integrate antithrombotic, pro-endothelial, immunomodulatory, and controlled-delivery functions while demonstrating mechanical durability, comparative clinical effectiveness, manufacturability, and cost-effective scalability.
articles.englishSummary: Percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) creates a dynamic blood-material-tissue interface in which thrombosis, inflammation, smooth muscle cell proliferation, and endothelial recovery evolve simultaneously. This narrative review examines coronary biomaterials using a healing-centered translational framework that links material properties to molecular and cellular responses, tissue-level healing, measurable structural and functional phenotypes, and clinical outcomes. We review the evolution from bare-metal and drug-eluting stents to polymer-free systems, drug-coated balloons (DCBs), bioresorbable scaffolds, and bioactive or biomimetic surfaces.

articles.title: Electrodeposited Heterostructured Fe-Zn Alloy Microtubes for Vascular Stents: Achieving Enhanced Strength, Ductility, and Uniform Degradation.
articles.abstract: To synergistically enhance the strength-ductility trade‑off and achieve uniform degradation in Fe-Zn alloys, heterostructured alloy microtubes were fabricated via layer‑by‑layer electrodeposition on a rotating soluble aluminum mandrel. Microstructural characterization revealed a columnar‑layered architecture with coherent interfacial bonding after annealing, free of delamination or defects. The heterostructured sample containing ten alternating soft layers (FZ10) exhibited an ultimate tensile strength of approximately 605 MPa and an elongation of about 17.3%, both superior to those of the single-layer alloy. The loading-unloading-reloading (LUR) experiments demonstrated pronounced hetero-deformation induced (HDI) strengthening and HDI strain-hardening effects, indicating the critical role of interfacial constraints in deformation coordination. Electrochemical and simulated body fluid (SBF) immersion tests showed that the heterostructure promoted faster and more uniform corrosion, with an average degradation rate of approximately 0.135 mm·y- 1 after 56 days, suppressing localized pitting. XPS and FTIR analyses identified the corrosion products as Fe/Zn oxides and Ca-P compounds, forming a bilayer degradation film with a dense inner layer and a loose outer layer. Additionally, heterostructured Fe-Zn alloy microtubes exhibited favorable cytocompatibility. These heterostructured microtubes integrate high strength, ductility, and controlled and uniform degradability, making them promising candidates for further development as biodegradable vascular stent materials.

Microstructural characterization revealed a columnar‑layered architecture with coherent interfacial bonding after annealing, free of delamination or defects. articles.title: Nonlinear radial force attenuation and stress-corrosion-crack induced fracture of biodegradable Zn alloy stents under vascular bioreactor conditions.
articles.abstract: Zinc alloy vascular stents have emerged as promising candidates in the development of biodegradable stents in recent years. However, due to the complexity of the in vivo environment and the high cost of animal experiments, robust experimental evidence regarding stent degradation-induced radial support loss and the underlying failure mechanisms remains lacking. In this study, a bioreactor system capable of simulating both physiological chemical conditions and pulsatile hemodynamics was developed to investigate the degradation behavior and mechanical evolution of Zn alloy stents. The results revealed a pronounced nonlinear relationship between radial force attenuation and mass loss. Specifically, the radial force decreased by >50% when the mass loss was only approximately 25%, demonstrating a distinct "cliff-like" failure pattern. This rapid deterioration was mainly attributed to stress corrosion cracking (SCC) occurring in the V-shaped load-bearing regions of the stent. During expansion, severe stress concentration and high plastic strain developed in these regions, which, combined with micro-galvanic corrosion, promoted crack initiation and propagation. These experimental findings verify that the mechanical failure of Zn alloy stents is dominated by local structural vulnerability rather than uniform degradation, suggesting that geometric optimization of critical regions is more effective than overall material enhancement for improving long-term structural reliability. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: This research has revealed a pronounced non-linear relationship between radial force attenuation and mass loss in biodegradable Zn alloy vascular stents via a customized bioreactor system. The stents exhibited a distinct "cliff-like" failure pattern, which is primarily dominated by stress corrosion cracking (SCC) localized within the V-shaped load-bearing regions of the stent. This finding indicates that geometric optimization of critical high-stress regions is far more effective for ensuring long-term structural reliability than overall material alloying alignment.
articles.englishSummary: Zinc alloy vascular stents have emerged as promising candidates in the development of biodegradable stents in recent years. However, due to the complexity of the in vivo environment and the high cost of animal experiments, robust experimental evidence regarding stent degradation-induced radial support loss and the underlying failure mechanisms remains lacking. In this study, a bioreactor system capable of simulating both physiological chemical conditions and pulsatile hemodynamics was developed to investigate the degradation behavior and mechanical evolution of Zn alloy stents.

articles.title: The paradigm evolution of biliary stents: from passive drainage to intelligent diagnostic-therapeutic platforms.
articles.abstract: The clinical management of biliary obstruction has long relied on mechanical drainage provided by stents, yet the inherent risks of re-occlusion, infection, and migration underscore the fundamental limitations of this passive support paradigm. This review proposes a four-stage paradigm evolution framework for biliary stent technology, demonstrating a shift from "passive physical support" to an "active therapeutic platform." The first stage, represented by plastic and self-expandable metallic stents, established anatomical drainage but is limited by biofilm deposition, tumor ingrowth, and migration. The first paradigm shift introduced functionalized stents incorporating drug-eluting, radionuclide, or photothermal/photodynamic coatings, transforming stents into active therapeutic carriers. The second paradigm shift emphasizes bio-adaptation through fully biodegradable stents achieving "temporary support followed by disappearance," alongside cell/matrix coatings to promote tissue regeneration. A third paradigm shift is emerging, focusing on intelligent responsiveness and personalization through closed-loop systems integrating biosensors, wireless communication, and artificial intelligence for real-time monitoring and on-demand therapy, combined with 3D/4D printing for patient-specific adaptation. Through critical assessment of each stage, this review dissects translational challenges including evaluation standards, long-term safety, cost-effectiveness, and regulatory complexities. Ultimately, we present a clinical decision-oriented technological spectrum delineating stent positioning across benign and malignant biliary diseases, envisioning future dynamic platforms integrating diagnosis, treatment, and monitoring to advance biliary intervention into an era of data-driven precision therapy. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: This review establishes, for the first time, a four-stage paradigm evolution framework for biliary stent technology-from passive mechanical support to active functionalized intervention, bio-adaptive scaffolds, and ultimately intelligent diagnostic-therapeutic platforms. By systematically dissecting the irreconcilable contradictions inherent to each paradigm, this framework provides a design-philosophy navigational map that transcends conventional chronological classifications. The integration of materials science mechanisms, cross-technology quantitative comparisons, and evidence-based clinical decision pathways offers both clinicians and biomaterials researchers a comprehensive reference for understanding the past trajectory and future direction of biliary stenting.

articles.title: PDA-Engineered 3D-Printed Polymer-ZrO2 Hybrid Scaffolds Enabling Enhanced Radiopacity, Photothermal Therapy, and Cell Migration Modulation.
articles.abstract: The clinical translation of bioresorbable polymer scaffold is limited by radiolucency, insufficient mechanical strength, and the absence of post-implantation therapeutic control. This study introduces a multifunctional scaffold that addresses these challenges through a polymer-ceramic nanocomposite architecture and bioinspired surface modification. ZrO2 nanoparticles are uniformly embedded into poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) via solution blending and fabricated into vascular scaffold by fused deposition modeling, yielding improved elastic modulus and radial strength while preserving elastic recovery. The ceramic phase provides intrinsic and sustained x-ray visibility in vitro, in vivo, and during 100-day perfusion, outperforming conventional contrast-agent-based strategies. A subsequent polydopamine (PDA) coating step enables efficient near-infrared (808 nm) photothermal functionality, which was leveraged for photothermal therapeutic modulation and repeatable, pulse-controlled release of paclitaxel. Cellular evaluation of vascular smooth muscle cell viability and migration underscores the therapeutic relevance of this externally triggered strategy for restenosis prevention. Overall, by integrating mechanical reinforcement, x-ray imaging capability, and remote therapeutic activation within a single PCL-based hybrid platform, this system addresses the long-standing clinical limitations of polymeric vascular scaffolds and offers a promising strategy for next-generation theranostic vascular implants.
articles.englishSummary: The clinical translation of bioresorbable polymer scaffold is limited by radiolucency, insufficient mechanical strength, and the absence of post-implantation therapeutic control. This study introduces a multifunctional scaffold that addresses these challenges through a polymer-ceramic nanocomposite architecture and bioinspired surface modification. ZrO2 nanoparticles are uniformly embedded into poly(ε-caprolactone) (PCL) via solution blending and fabricated into vascular scaffold by fused deposition modeling, yielding improved elastic modulus and radial strength while preserving elastic recovery.

articles.title: Underlying Plaque Type and Neoatherosclerosis After ST-Segment Elevation Myocardial Infarction - Serial Optical Coherence Tomography Substudy of the CONNECT Trial.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The relationship between underlying plaque type and the development of neoatherosclerosis remains uncertain.

METHODS AND RESULTS: This was a secondary analysis of the CONNECT trial, which randomized 239 patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) to receive biodegradable polymer or durable polymer everolimus-eluting stents. Patients with serial optical coherence tomography (OCT) were included and post-procedural OCT frames that corresponded to segments showing neoatherosclerosis at the 3-year follow-up (NA-leading segments) were identified by manual frame matching. At the frame level, we compared post-procedural OCT findings in NALS to 2 comparators: non-NA-leading lesions (lesions without neoatherosclerosis); and non-NA-leading segments within NA-leading lesions. Of 144 lesions with serial OCT, neoatherosclerosis occurred in 17 (11.8%). In NA-leading segments, compared to non-NA-leading lesions and non-NA-leading segments within NA-leading lesions, the proportion of frames with lipid-rich plaque was higher (71% vs. 54% [odds ratio (OR) 2.72; 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.23-6.01] and 58% [OR 2.62; 95% CI 0.99-6.96], respectively). Similarly, the mean (±SD) in-stent atherothrombotic material area was larger in NA-leading segments (0.41±0.39 vs. 0.24±0.31 [geometric mean ratio (GMR) 2.00; 95% CI 1.21-3.29] and 0.16±0.16 mm2[GMR 2.33; 95% CI 1.26-4.31], respectively).

CONCLUSIONS: Underlying lipid-rich plaque and a higher burden of in-stent atherothrombotic material were associated with neoatherosclerosis at 3 years in STEMI patients, indicating that plaque composition at the time of DES implantation may critically influence neoatherosclerosis formation.
articles.englishSummary: BACKGROUND: The relationship between underlying plaque type and the development of neoatherosclerosis remains uncertain. METHODS AND RESULTS: This was a secondary analysis of the CONNECT trial, which randomized 239 patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) to receive biodegradable polymer or durable polymer everolimus-eluting stents. Patients with serial optical coherence tomography (OCT) were included and post-procedural OCT frames that corresponded to segments showing neoatherosclerosis at the 3-year follow-up (NA-leading segments) were identified by manual frame matching.

articles.title: Neurovascular coupling in simultaneous EEG-fNIRS studies: A scoping review of analytical frameworks and clinical applications.
articles.abstract: Simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) have been used across cognitive and physiological states and in diverse clinical populations. However, the interpretation of cross-modal coupling remains difficult because findings from different analytical frameworks, populations, and experimental conditions have not been systematically mapped. This scoping review followed the Arksey and O'Malley framework and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, EBSCO, and IEEE Xplore were searched through February 10, 2026, for studies that quantitatively related simultaneously recorded EEG and fNIRS signals. Two reviewers independently screened the records. Findings were synthesized narratively, and analytical pipelines were mapped across the signal domain, feature extraction, coupling metric, and temporal lag handling. Fifty-seven studies were included. Amplitude-based studies related event-related potentials and oscillatory EEG features to focal hemodynamic responses, with associations varying across electrophysiological features, cortical regions, and task conditions. Frequency- and scale-specific analyses identified band-dependent relationships, while coupling at ultra-slow scales showed sensitivity to vascular and systemic physiological influences. Studies that explicitly modeled timing identified several-second offsets in some paradigms, while directional estimates varied across tasks and recording states. Network analyses showed partial and context-dependent correspondence between EEG- and fNIRS-derived measures, while model-based approaches characterized multivariate and predictive cross-modal relationships. Across frameworks, observed coupling differed with recording state, frequency band, cortical region, and temporal lag handling rather than representing a single quantity. Clinical findings were heterogeneous, and most condition-specific patterns were supported by small and methodologically diverse evidence bases. These findings support framework-matched analysis and pipeline-explicit reporting when interpreting EEG-fNIRS coupling.
articles.englishSummary: Simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG) and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) have been used across cognitive and physiological states and in diverse clinical populations. However, the interpretation of cross-modal coupling remains difficult because findings from different analytical frameworks, populations, and experimental conditions have not been systematically mapped. This scoping review followed the Arksey and O'Malley framework and the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR).

articles.title: Electrophysiological and computational analyses of anethole-induced inhibition of L-type calcium channels in rat tracheal smooth muscle.
articles.abstract: Anethole, a naturally occurring phenylpropanoid, is a major constituent of several essential oils and exhibits a broad spectrum of pharmacological activities, including reduction of neuronal excitability, antispasmodic effects, and inhibition of Ca2+ influx. To elucidate the mechanism underlying calcium current inhibition, we investigated the effects of anethole on voltage-dependent calcium channels (VDCCs) in rat tracheal smooth muscle myocytes. Whole-cell patch-clamp recordings in dissociated tracheal myocytes were combined with molecular docking analyses. Ba2+ was used as the charge carrier because it generates larger and more stable inward currents through L-type VDCCs than Ca2+. At 0.67 mM (approximately the IC₅₀ for inhibition of tracheal contraction induced by 60 mM K+), anethole reduced the peak current density from -3.58 ± 0.39 to -1.53 ± 0.26 pA/pF (n = 18). In addition, anethole shifted the half-activation voltage (V1/2) from -6.46 to +1.41 mV and the half-inactivation voltage from -25.38 to -36.42 mV, indicating depolarizing and hyperpolarizing shifts in the steady-state activation and inactivation curves, respectively. Both effects reduced channel availability and favored inhibition of IBa. Computational analyses identified preferential interaction regions within the pore-forming and voltage-sensing domains of the channel, providing a plausible structural basis for both current inhibition and voltage-dependent modulation. Collectively, the electrophysiological and computational findings indicate that anethole inhibits VDCCs through complementary mechanisms involving pore interaction together with modulation of channel activation and inactivation. These effects occur at concentrations that also inhibit tracheal smooth muscle contraction, supporting the hypothesis that VDCC inhibition contributes to the antispasmodic action of anethole.
articles.englishSummary: Anethole, a naturally occurring phenylpropanoid, is a major constituent of several essential oils and exhibits a broad spectrum of pharmacological activities, including reduction of neuronal excitability, antispasmodic effects, and inhibition of Ca2+ influx. To elucidate the mechanism underlying calcium current inhibition, we investigated the effects of anethole on voltage-dependent calcium channels (VDCCs) in rat tracheal smooth muscle myocytes. Whole-cell patch-clamp recordings in dissociated tracheal myocytes were combined with molecular docking analyses.

articles.title: Delayed Cerebral Ischemia as Progressive Neurovascular Unit Failure: A Hypothesis-Generating Perspective.
articles.abstract: Despite decades of investigation, delayed cerebral ischemia (DCI) remains the principal cause of secondary neurological injury following aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH). Successive paradigms including angiographic vasospasm, early brain injury, neuroinflammation, blood-brain barrier disruption, cortical spreading depolarization, microvascular dysfunction, oxidative stress, and metabolic failure have each explained important aspects of disease biology. However, these mechanisms have largely evolved as parallel explanations rather than components of an integrated model, leaving the dissociation between vasospasm and DCI, delayed onset, interpatient heterogeneity, and limited efficacy of vasospasm-directed therapies incompletely explained. This perspective proposes, as a hypothesis, progressive neurovascular unit (NVU) failure as a conceptual framework for DCI after aSAH. We integrate experimental, translational, and clinical evidence spanning vascular biology, neuroimmunology, cerebrovascular physiology, electrophysiology, metabolism, biomarker research, and therapeutic trials to develop a hypothesis-generating framework. The established mechanisms of DCI may represent interacting manifestations of progressive disruption of coordinated signaling among endothelial, vascular smooth muscle, pericyte, astrocytic, microglial, and neuronal compartments of the neurovascular unit. Within this framework, early brain injury may initiate NVU dysfunction, which is amplified by interacting vascular, barrier, inflammatory, electrophysiological, and metabolic disturbances, culminating in neuronal metabolic failure and tissue injury. Vasospasm is therefore positioned as one contributor to this process rather than a sufficient explanation for DCI. This framework offers a possible basis for interpreting clinical heterogeneity and therapeutic discordance while generating testable predictions for multimodal biomarker development, biological phenotyping, and mechanism-informed therapeutic strategies. The framework does not introduce new mechanisms; rather, it proposes a testable distinction between compensated NVU dysfunction and NVU failure, frames compartment-specific non-additive interactions as an empirical question, and organizes biomarkers by the NVU compartment they reflect. These proposals remain to be validated.

articles.title: Endothelial Piezo1 Hyperactivity Drives Neurovascular Dysfunction in Hypertension.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hypertension is a major driver of neurovascular dysfunction and cognitive decline, yet the molecular mechanisms linking elevated arterial pressure to impaired cerebral blood flow remain poorly defined. Piezo1, a mechanosensitive cation channel enriched in the brain endothelium, is a candidate mediator of cerebral blood flow deficits during hypertension.

METHODS: Using 2 distinct mouse models of hypertension-BPH/2J mice (genetically hypertensive strain) and angiotensin II-infused C57BL/6J mice-we assessed brain endothelial Piezo1 activity using patch-clamp electrophysiology. Endothelial-specific Piezo1 deletion models were used to evaluate the role of the channel in hypertension-associated cerebrovascular impairment. Cerebral blood flow responses were measured in vivo by laser speckle contrast imaging, and super-resolution nanoscopy was used to quantify Piezo1 nanoscale organization. Behavioral testing was used to assess cognition.

RESULTS: Genetic manipulation of endothelial Piezo1 had minimal impact on baseline blood pressure. However, cerebral endothelial Piezo1 activity was markedly elevated in different hypertension models. Deletion of endothelial Piezo1 protected against hypertension-induced cerebrovascular deficits, including impaired vasomotion, reduced functional hyperemia, and blunted CO2-evoked hyperemia. Super-resolution imaging revealed that hypertension increased Piezo1 clustering, consistent with electrophysiological findings of enhanced channel coupling and open probability. Mechanistically, Piezo1 hyperactivity was PKC (protein kinase C)-dependent, and the PKC-Piezo1 spatial association was enhanced during hypertension. Importantly, PKC inhibition normalized brain endothelial Piezo1 activity, restored cerebral blood flow responses, and rescued cognitive performance.

CONCLUSIONS: Hypertension increased the gain of Piezo1 function in brain endothelial cells, promoting dysfunctional neurovascular signaling and cognitive impairment. Targeting Piezo1 or PKC signaling selectively restored cerebrovascular regulation. This work identifies a mechanosensitive pathway that could be leveraged to protect the hypertensive brain.
